processes.title: Purpose
processes.purpose: The Maaden Safety, Security, Health and Environment Management System (MSHEM) establishes a unified Maaden wide framework for managing environmental, health, safety and security risks throughout the lifecycle of Maaden activities. MSHEM defines the minimum mandatory requirements, controls and required outcomes that enable Maaden to protect employees, contractors, communities, environment, assets and operations, manage EHSS risks, fulfil applicable legal and regulatory obligations, and achieve safe, responsible and sustainable business performance. MSHEM provides a consistent Maaden wide approach to: • Establish EHSS governance, leadership, accountability and responsibilities; • Engage leaders, employees and contractors in managing EHSS risks and improving performance; • Identify, assess and manage EHSS risks and applicable obligations; • Establish, implement and maintain effective preventive and mitigative risk controls; • Integrate applicable EHSS requirements into operations, projects and contractor activities; • Maintain emergency preparedness and response capability for credible emergency situations; • Monitor, evaluate and assure EHSS performance; and • Promote learning, incident prevention and continual improvement. MSHEM establishes consistent Maaden wide requirements and outcomes for managing EHSS risks and performance, while enabling Business Units and Corporate Functions to implement those requirements in a manner that reflects their activities, risks and operating context.

processes.title: Scope
processes.purpose: MSHEM applies to Maaden businesses, functions, sites, operations, projects and activities over which Maaden has management or operational control. MSHEM addresses four integrated EHSS domains: Environment, Health, Safety and Security. The Safety domain encompasses both Occupational Safety and Process Safety. It applies throughout the relevant asset and activity lifecycle, including exploration, project development, design, construction, commissioning, operations, maintenance, modification, closure, post-closure and rehabilitation. MSHEM requirements shall be implemented by Business Units and Corporate Functions through detailed procedures, work instructions, plans, controls and other implementation arrangements. Contractors and other parties performing activities under Maaden's control shall comply with applicable MSHEM requirements relevant to their work.

processes.title: MSHEM Structure
processes.purpose: MSHEM is an integrated management system that enables Maaden to manage EHSS risks, fulfil applicable obligations and support continual improvement in EHSS performance. The system is organized into six integrated Parts that collectively define the framework, governance, processes and performance requirements for effective EHSS management: Part 1 | MSHEM Framework Defines the Purpose, Scope and Structure of MSHEM. Part 2 | EHSS Governance, Risk and Capability Defines the governance, leadership, risk management and organizational capabilities required to support effective EHSS management. Part 3 | EHSS Processes Defines the core EHSS risk control requirements across: • Environment; • Health; • Safety, comprising Occupational Safety and Process Safety; and • Security. Part 4 | Contractor and Project EHSS Management Defines requirements for managing EHSS risks associated with contractor activities and projects. Part 5 | Emergency Management and Response Defines requirements for emergency preparedness, response capability and emergency response resources. Part 6 | EHSS Performance, Assurance and Improvement Defines requirements for incident management, performance evaluation, assurance, management review and continual improvement.

processes.title: MSHEM Governance
processes.purpose: To ensure MSHEM is effectively governed, implemented, maintained, evaluated and continually improved through defined accountabilities, responsibilities, consistent implementation and systematic oversight.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Maaden Business Units, Corporate Functions and activities subject to MSHEM requirements.

clauses.heading: MSHEM Implementation Principles
clauses.text: MSHEM shall establish the minimum Maaden wide EHSS requirements applicable to Business Units and Corporate Functions.

clauses.heading: MSHEM Implementation Principles
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions may establish additional or more stringent EHSS requirements and controls based on their activities, risks, operating conditions and applicable obligations, provided that applicable MSHEM requirements continue to be met.

clauses.heading: MSHEM Implementation Principles
clauses.text: MSHEM shall not replace or reduce compliance with applicable laws, regulations, permits, regulatory directives or other binding obligations. Where multiple applicable requirements address the same matter, the more stringent requirement shall apply.

clauses.heading: Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Executive leadership shall be accountable for the implementation and effectiveness of applicable MSHEM requirements within their areas of responsibility.

clauses.heading: Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall designate responsible people for coordinating and monitoring the implementation of applicable MSHEM requirements.

clauses.heading: Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Roles, responsibilities and authorities relevant to MSHEM implementation shall be defined, documented and communicated by Business Units and Corporate Functions.

clauses.heading: Implementation, Applicability and Deviations
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall implement applicable MSHEM requirements within their areas of responsibility and maintain proportionate documented information sufficient to demonstrate implementation, verify controls, support compliance and inform decision making, without creating duplicate records where equivalent controlled evidence is available.

clauses.heading: Implementation, Applicability and Deviations
clauses.text: Where a MSHEM requirement is determined to be not applicable, the decision and supporting justification shall be documented and approved by the highest EHSS authority of the relevant Business Unit or Corporate Function.

clauses.heading: Implementation, Applicability and Deviations
clauses.text: Where an applicable MSHEM requirement cannot be met, the proposed deviation shall be documented, justified and risk assessed, with alternative controls identified where necessary, and approved by the appropriate management authority in accordance with the assessed risk level.

clauses.heading: Implementation, Applicability and Deviations
clauses.text: A deviation from MSHEM shall not authorize non-compliance with applicable law, regulation, permit, license, approval or regulatory directive.

clauses.heading: Implementation, Applicability and Deviations
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain action plans for identified MSHEM implementation and compliance gaps. Actions shall be assigned, prioritized according to risk where appropriate, tracked and closed within established completion dates.

clauses.heading: Governance Review
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall periodically review the implementation status, effectiveness and compliance of applicable MSHEM requirements within their areas of responsibility in accordance with section 6.3 EHSS Audit and Assurance.

clauses.heading: Governance Review
clauses.text: Corporate EHSS shall periodically review the implementation status, effectiveness and compliance of MSHEM across Maaden in accordance with section 6.3 EHSS Audit and Assurance.

clauses.heading: MSHEM Ownership, Review and Control
clauses.text: Corporate EHSS shall be the owner and custodian of MSHEM and shall establish, maintain, approve, issue, communicate and control MSHEM documentation.

clauses.heading: MSHEM Ownership, Review and Control
clauses.text: Corporate EHSS, supported by relevant Subject Matter Experts, shall evaluate MSHEM requirements at least annually to confirm their continued suitability and effectiveness and identify opportunities for continual improvement.

clauses.heading: MSHEM Ownership, Review and Control
clauses.text: The annual evaluation shall consider changes in Maaden activities and risks, applicable obligations, incidents and lessons learned, audit and assurance findings, performance trends, operating experience, and relevant technical or industry developments.

clauses.heading: MSHEM Ownership, Review and Control
clauses.text: MSHEM shall be revised where annual evaluations or other significant changes identify a need for modification.

clauses.heading: MSHEM Ownership, Review and Control
clauses.text: MSHEM shall undergo a comprehensive review at least every three years to confirm its continued suitability, effectiveness and alignment with Maaden requirements.

clauses.heading: MSHEM Ownership, Review and Control
clauses.text: MSHEM records shall be retained for at least three years unless a longer or shorter retention period is required by applicable legal, regulatory, permit, or specific MSHEM requirements.

processes.title: EHSS Leadership and Accountability
processes.purpose: Leadership at all levels visibly demonstrates commitment to EHSS, establishes clear accountabilities, provides resources, promotes worker engagement and ensures EHSS considerations are integrated into business decisions and operations.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Maaden Business Units and Corporate Functions, and to Maaden employees and contractor personnel working under Maaden’s control.

clauses.heading: Leadership and Commitment
clauses.text: Executive leadership, management and supervisors shall visibly demonstrate commitment to EHSS and lead by example in the implementation of applicable MSHEM requirements.

clauses.heading: Leadership and Commitment
clauses.text: EHSS considerations shall be integrated into business planning, decision-making, change management and operational activities.

clauses.heading: Leadership and Commitment
clauses.text: Leadership shall ensure that resources necessary to implement, maintain and improve MSHEM are available.

clauses.heading: Leadership and Commitment
clauses.text: Leadership shall promote a culture in which personnel are empowered to report hazards, incidents, concerns and improvement opportunities, and to exercise authorized stop-work authority without fear of retaliation, and shall ensure that reported matters are evaluated and addressed.

clauses.heading: Leadership and Commitment
clauses.text: Leadership shall promote and support the recognition of employees and contractor personnel who demonstrate positive EHSS behaviors, contributions or performance that support the objectives and intended outcomes of MSHEM.

clauses.heading: EHSS Accountabilities
clauses.text: EHSS accountabilities, responsibilities and authorities shall be clearly assigned to relevant roles, communicated and periodically reviewed.

clauses.heading: EHSS Accountabilities
clauses.text: Accountability for EHSS performance shall remain with line management and shall not be delegated to EHSS personnel.

clauses.heading: EHSS Accountabilities
clauses.text: EHSS responsibilities applicable to a role shall be incorporated into relevant position descriptions and communicated to affected personnel.

clauses.heading: Worker Participation and Engagement
clauses.text: Employees and contractor personnel shall be provided with opportunities to participate in EHSS activities, consultations, hazard identification, risk assessments, incident investigations and continual improvement initiatives relevant to their work activities.

clauses.heading: Worker Participation and Engagement
clauses.text: Employees and contractor personnel shall comply with applicable EHSS requirements, report hazards, incidents, unsafe acts or unsafe conditions, and shall be authorized and expected to stop or not start work where required controls are absent or ineffective, or where conditions present an unacceptable EHSS risk.

clauses.heading: Visible EHSS Leadership
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement and maintain a visible EHSS leadership program that defines leadership engagement activities, participation expectations, monitoring and follow-up requirements.

clauses.heading: Visible EHSS Leadership
clauses.text: Management shall undertake visible EHSS leadership activities appropriate to their roles and areas of responsibility to engage with personnel, verify the effectiveness of EHSS controls, reinforce desired behaviors, and identify issues and improvement opportunities.

clauses.heading: Visible EHSS Leadership
clauses.text: Visible EHSS leadership activities shall be risk based and consider material EHSS risks, control effectiveness, EHSS performance, serious injury and fatality prevention, and workforce concerns. Significant observations, issues and resulting actions shall be documented, communicated and addressed.

processes.title: EHSS Policy, Objectives and Planning
processes.purpose: Maaden establishes and maintains an approved EHSS Policy and translates its commitments into aligned and measurable EHSS objectives supported by adequately resourced plans that support compliance, EHSS risk reduction and continual improvement of EHSS performance and MSHEM.
processes.scope: This process applies to the development, approval, communication, implementation and revision of the Maaden EHSS Policy, EHSS objectives and associated EHSS objective plans across Maaden Business Units and Corporate Functions.

clauses.heading: Policy Establishment and Approval
clauses.text: Maaden shall establish, implement and maintain an EHSS Policy that is appropriate to Maaden’s purpose and context, and to the nature and scale of its activities and associated EHSS risks and opportunities.

clauses.heading: Policy Establishment and Approval
clauses.text: The EHSS Policy shall be approved by the Chief Executive Officer and shall provide the framework for establishing EHSS objectives and performance improvement initiatives.

clauses.heading: Policy Establishment and Approval
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall apply the approved Maaden EHSS Policy and shall not establish or use a separate EHSS policy.

clauses.heading: Policy Commitments
Policy Communication and Review
clauses.text: EHSS Policy shall be maintained as documented information, communicated to employees and contractor personnel, and made available to relevant interested parties.

clauses.heading: Policy Communication and Review
clauses.text: Corporate EHSS shall review the EHSS Policy at least every three years and revise it where necessary to ensure it remains current, effective and aligned with Maaden's strategic direction, activities, risks and obligations.

clauses.heading: EHSS Objectives Establishment and Alignment
clauses.text: Corporate EHSS shall establish Maaden wide EHSS objectives that support the commitments of the EHSS Policy, align with Maaden’s strategic and business planning processes, and contribute to the intended outcomes of MSHEM.

clauses.heading: EHSS Objectives Establishment and Alignment
clauses.text:
Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish EHSS objectives appropriate to their respective EHSS responsibilities, risks, and operating contexts that:
a. are relevant to their activities and operating context;
b. support applicable Maaden wide EHSS objectives; and
c. address identified EHSS performance and improvement priorities.

clauses.heading: Objective Setting Criteria and Communication
clauses.text: EHSS objectives shall include relevant baselines, measurable targets, defined timeframes, and criteria for evaluating progress and achievement.

clauses.heading: Objective Setting Criteria and Communication
Objective Setting Criteria and Communication
clauses.text: EHSS objectives shall be documented and communicated to personnel responsible for their implementation, monitoring and achievement.

clauses.heading: Resources and Improvement Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain EHSS objective plans to achieve their EHSS objectives.

clauses.heading: Resources and Improvement Planning
clauses.text: Each EHSS objective plan shall define, as a minimum, the required actions, accountable owner, required resources, target completion dates and applicable milestones, and the indicators or other criteria for monitoring progress and evaluating achievement.

clauses.heading: Resources and Improvement Planning
clauses.text: Accountable leaders shall ensure that the human, technical, physical and financial resources necessary to implement approved EHSS objective plans are identified and addressed through applicable business planning and resource allocation processes.

clauses.heading: Resources and Improvement Planning
clauses.text: EHSS objectives and associated EHSS objective plans shall be integrated into applicable strategic, business, project and operational planning processes.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Review and Revision
clauses.text: Progress against EHSS objectives and EHSS objective plans shall be monitored and reported at the frequency defined in the applicable objective plan, using the indicators, milestones and completion criteria established in the plan.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Review and Revision
clauses.text: EHSS objectives and plans shall be formally reviewed at least once annually.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Review and Revision
Monitoring, Review and Revision
clauses.text: Changes to EHSS objectives, EHSS objective plans, responsibilities, resources or target dates shall be appropriately justified and approved, documented and communicated to affected personnel.

processes.title: EHSS Legal and Regulatory Requirements
processes.purpose: Applicable EHSS legal and regulatory requirements are identified, understood, communicated, implemented and periodically evaluated to support and demonstrate compliance.
processes.scope: This process applies to the identification, evaluation, implementation and review of EHSS legal and regulatory requirements applicable to Maaden Business Units and Corporate Functions.

clauses.heading: Identification and Evaluation of Legal and Regulatory Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and maintain access to EHSS legal and regulatory requirements applicable to their activities, facilities, projects and operations.

clauses.heading: Identification and Evaluation of Legal and Regulatory Requirements
clauses.text: EHSS legal and regulatory requirements shall be evaluated to determine their applicability and resulting compliance obligations.

clauses.heading: Identification and Evaluation of Legal and Regulatory Requirements
clauses.text: The identification and evaluation of EHSS legal and regulatory requirements shall be undertaken by competent personnel and supported by specialist expertise where required.

clauses.heading: Identification and Evaluation of Legal and Regulatory Requirements
clauses.text: EHSS legal and regulatory requirements shall be reviewed and updated at least annually, and when new requirements are introduced, existing requirements are amended, or activities or operations change.

clauses.heading: Identification and Evaluation of Legal and Regulatory Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain arrangements to monitor relevant sources for new and amended EHSS legal and regulatory requirements and assess their applicability within defined timeframes that consider effective dates, compliance deadlines and associated EHSS risks.

clauses.heading: Legal and Regulatory Requirements Register
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, maintain and review at least annually a register of applicable EHSS legal and regulatory requirements, including permit conditions, approvals, licenses and regulatory authorizations, identifying their sources or references, associated activities and compliance obligations, responsible functions or roles, established compliance controls, and validity or renewal requirements, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Implementation and Communication
clauses.text: Responsibilities and authorities for implementing and maintaining compliance with applicable EHSS legal and regulatory requirements shall be assigned and communicated to relevant personnel and stakeholders.

clauses.heading: Implementation and Communication
Evaluation of Compliance
clauses.text: Compliance with applicable EHSS legal and regulatory requirements shall be monitored at intervals appropriate to the nature of the obligation, associated risks and applicable permit conditions.

clauses.heading: Evaluation of Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall, as part of the annual review of EHSS legal and regulatory requirements, evaluate compliance with applicable obligations, maintain documented evidence of the evaluation, and identify actions necessary to address any compliance gaps.

clauses.heading: Evaluation of Compliance
clauses.text: Non-compliance with applicable EHSS legal and regulatory requirements shall be documented, evaluated, appropriately escalated and addressed through corrective actions that are tracked to closure. Applicable regulatory notification and reporting requirements shall be fulfilled.

processes.title: EHSS Risk Management
processes.purpose: EHSS risks associated with Maaden activities, facilities, projects, products, services and changes are systematically identified, assessed, treated, monitored and reviewed so that risks are eliminated where reasonably practicable or otherwise reduced and maintained at a level that is As Low As Reasonably Practicable (ALARP).
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden Business Units and Corporate Functions that manage activities, facilities, projects, products, services or changes that may create or modify EHSS risk.

clauses.heading: EHSS Risk Management Framework
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain processes to identify, assess, treat, monitor and review EHSS risks associated with their activities, facilities, projects, products, services and changes.

clauses.heading: EHSS Risk Management Framework
clauses.text: EHSS risks shall be assessed using the approved Maaden EHSS Risk Matrix and a risk assessment methodology selected according to the nature, complexity and credible consequence potential of the matter being assessed.

clauses.heading: EHSS Risk Management Framework
clauses.text: Risk assessment methodologies shall be used in accordance with section 3.47 Process Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment.

clauses.heading: Risk Identification and Assessment
Risk Identification and Assessment
Risk Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Initial risk shall be assessed before credit is given to controls or safeguards intended to prevent the unwanted event or reduce its consequences.

clauses.heading: Risk Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Residual risk shall be assessed after crediting only those controls and safeguards that meet applicable Maaden requirements for effectiveness, independence and reliability.

clauses.heading: Risk Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Risk assessments shall be documented in sufficient detail to support review, approval, implementation, monitoring and reassessment.

clauses.heading: Risk Assessment Triggers
Risk Assessment Triggers
clauses.text: Where findings are not immediately corrected, or where findings may affect similar activities, systems, facilities or operations, a risk assessment shall be performed and risk reduction actions identified.

clauses.heading: Risk Assessment Triggers
clauses.text: An approved Medium, Significant, High or Critical risk shall be reassessed before the approval validity period expires, and earlier where the scope, operating conditions, assumptions, affected people, consequence potential or effectiveness of a credited control change.

clauses.heading: Risk Treatment and Interim Controls
clauses.text: Risk control measures shall be selected and implemented in accordance with the hierarchy of controls to eliminate risks where reasonably practicable or otherwise reduce risks to a level that is As Low As Reasonably Practicable (ALARP).

clauses.heading: Risk Treatment and Interim Controls
clauses.text: Where risks cannot immediately be reduced to ALARP, interim controls shall be identified, implemented and monitored until permanent risk reduction measures are implemented.

clauses.heading: Risk Treatment and Interim Controls
clauses.text: The risk assessment shall specify the performance requirements, verification method and verification frequency for each interim control.

clauses.heading: Risk Treatment and Interim Controls
clauses.text: Where interim controls are not identified, or where interim controls do not reduce the initial risk, risk approval shall be escalated to a higher approval authority.

clauses.heading: Risk Treatment and Interim Controls
clauses.text: EHSS Risks, approved interim controls, operating restrictions, required actions and escalation conditions shall be communicated to affected employees, contractors and other people responsible for implementing or verifying them.

clauses.heading: Competence and Participation
clauses.text: EHSS risk assessments shall be led or facilitated by personnel competent in the selected risk assessment methodology, the use of the Maaden EHSS Risk Matrix and the activities, processes or hazards being assessed.

clauses.heading: Competence and Participation
clauses.text: Risk assessment participants shall collectively possess the operational, technical and EHSS knowledge necessary to identify credible scenarios, evaluate controls and assess risk within the defined scope.

clauses.heading: Risk Approval and Acceptance
clauses.text: Immediately after a Medium, Significant, High or Critical risk is identified, verbal authorization for continued operation or activity shall be obtained from the relevant management authority specified in Table 2.5-1, followed by documented review and approval within the applicable timeframe. No mitigating actions are required to be taken or approved for Low risks.

clauses.heading: Risk Approval and Acceptance
clauses.text: Where immediate verbal authorization is permitted, the decision, approving authority, basis for continuation, interim controls and time of authorization shall be recorded and subsequently completed through the documented approval process.

clauses.heading: Risk Approval and Acceptance
clauses.text:
The minimum approval authority, approval timeframe, and maximum validity period shall be as specified in Table

clauses.heading: Risk Approval and Acceptance
clauses.text: Risk approvals shall only be granted after the risk assessment, interim controls, mitigation actions and required endorsements have been reviewed and determined to be suitable for continued operation or activity.

clauses.heading: Risk Approval and Acceptance
clauses.text: All approved risks shall have defined risk treatment actions, responsible people and target completion dates established to reduce the risk to an acceptable level.

clauses.heading: Risk Approval and Acceptance
clauses.text: Risks that remain open at the end of the approved validity period shall be reassessed, reviewed and reapproved prior to renewal of the risk acceptance.

clauses.heading: Risk Approval and Acceptance

clauses.heading: Risk Registers and Stewardship
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assign a competent EHSS Risk Management Focal Point, or equivalent role, responsible for supporting the quality, maintenance, review and reporting of EHSS risk management outputs.

clauses.heading: Risk Registers and Stewardship
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain risk registers for Medium, Significant, High and Critical EHSS risks through HEMAYA.

clauses.heading: Risk Registers and Stewardship
Risk Registers and Stewardship
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall review the status of Medium, Significant, High and Critical risks and the effectiveness of associated controls, interim controls and risk treatment actions on monthly basis.

clauses.heading: Risk Registers and Stewardship
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall validate at least quarterly the implementation and effectiveness of interim controls and mitigation actions for Critical and High risks, and retain documented evidence supporting decisions to close, extend or renew the risk approval.

clauses.heading: Risk Registers and Stewardship
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that risks from their EHSS risk registers, including risks arising from the failure or degradation of critical controls associated with identified material unwanted events in accordance with section 2.6 Critical Control Management, are reflected in the Business Units or Corporate Functions ERM risk registers .

clauses.heading: Risk Registers and Stewardship
clauses.text: Critical and High Risk status shall be periodically reported to the applicable Maaden executive EHSS governance forum in accordance with section 6.4 Management Review and Continual Improvement.

clauses.heading: Risk Registers and Stewardship
clauses.text: Business Units shall provide quarterly reporting of Critical and High Risks to Corporate EHSS for periodic review and verification.

processes.title: Critical Control Management
processes.purpose: Establish minimum requirements for identifying, implementing, verifying and improving critical controls for fatal hazards and associated material unwanted events.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden controlled activities, facilities, projects and operations where hazards have the potential to result in one or more fatalities or life altering occupational illness or impairment.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Management Framework and Accountability
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement and maintain a Critical Control Management process with reference to the ICMM Critical Control Management Good Practice Guide and applicable Maaden risk management requirements.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Management Framework and Accountability
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and define applicable fatal hazards and associated material unwanted events, including their scope, credible causes and maximum reasonable consequences. Applicability shall be based on the maximum reasonable consequence, considering credible failure of existing controls, and shall not be excluded solely because the likelihood of the material unwanted event is assessed as rare.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Management Framework and Accountability
clauses.text: Critical Control Management shall be led by operational line management. EHSS, Risk and relevant technical functions shall provide governance, facilitation, technical support and assurance without replacing operational accountability.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Management Framework and Accountability
clauses.text: A Risk Owner shall be assigned for each fatal hazard or defined group of related material unwanted events, and a Control Owner shall be assigned for each critical control. Responsibilities for implementing, verifying, evaluating and reporting critical controls shall be defined.

clauses.heading: Fatal Hazards, Material Unwanted Events and Critical Controls
clauses.text: Controls for applicable material unwanted events shall be identified using an appropriate hazard and control analysis methodology, considering the nature and complexity of the hazard.

clauses.heading: Fatal Hazards, Material Unwanted Events and Critical Controls
clauses.text:
A control shall only be designated as a critical control where:
a. it directly prevents a material unwanted event or mitigates its consequences;
b. its absence, degradation or failure would significantly increase the likelihood or severity of the material unwanted event despite other controls; and
c. its required performance can be defined and verified. Critical control selection shall also consider the importance, reliability and contribution of the control relative to other controls.

clauses.heading: Fatal Hazards, Material Unwanted Events and Critical Controls
clauses.text: Supporting activities, including management plans, procedures, risk assessments, training, maintenance and monitoring, shall not be designated as critical controls unless they independently meet the critical control criteria.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Performance Requirements
clauses.text: Each critical control shall have an approved Critical Control Performance Specification, Performance Standard or equivalent documented requirement.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Performance Requirements
Critical Control Performance Requirements
clauses.text: Performance requirements shall reflect the nature of the critical control and, where applicable, the approved design basis, technical standards, operating limits and required human actions.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Implementation
clauses.text: Critical controls and their performance requirements shall be integrated into the applicable processes through which work is designed, planned, authorized, executed, maintained and reviewed.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Implementation
clauses.text: Personnel and contractors exposed to fatal hazards shall understand the applicable material unwanted events, critical controls, their responsibilities, Go/No-Go criteria and required actions where a critical control is absent, degraded or ineffective.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Implementation
clauses.text: Before exposure to a fatal hazard, applicable task dependent critical controls shall be confirmed as in place and meeting the defined Go/No-Go criteria.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Implementation
clauses.text: Work shall not commence or continue where an applicable Go/No-Go criterion is not met. Any temporary substitution, impairment or alternative arrangement affecting a critical control shall be formally assessed and authorized through the applicable MSHEM Risk Management, EHSS Critical Systems Bypass or Management of Change process, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Verification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish a risk-based verification program to determine whether critical controls are in place and meet their approved performance requirements.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Verification
clauses.text: Verification methods, frequencies and responsibilities shall be appropriate to the control type, failure mechanism, consequence of failure and applicable technical, legal, regulatory or manufacturer requirements.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Verification
clauses.text: Critical control verification shall form part of operational line management accountability. Technical specialists shall participate where specialist competence is required, and verification shall not be treated solely as an EHSS, audit or assurance activity.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Verification
clauses.text: Where a critical control is absent, degraded, bypassed, ineffective or does not meet its approved performance requirements, the deficiency shall be addressed and escalated according to its significance. Exposure shall be prevented or stopped where applicable Go/No-Go criteria are not met, and required corrective actions shall be tracked to verified closure.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Verification
clauses.text: Critical control deficiencies shall be assessed for broader applicability where equivalent controls, equipment, locations or activities may be affected.

clauses.heading: Critical Control Verification
clauses.text: Personnel implementing or verifying critical controls shall meet the required competency requirements established as part of section 2.7 EHSS Competency, Awareness and Communication process.

clauses.heading: Evaluation, Reporting and Improvement
clauses.text: Risk Owners, with input from Control Owners and relevant technical specialists, shall periodically evaluate critical control effectiveness considering whether the control is adequately designed to achieve its objective; and whether the control is effectively implemented and operating as required.

clauses.heading: Evaluation, Reporting and Improvement
clauses.text: Critical control evaluation shall consider relevant verification results, incidents and High Potential Incidents, recurring deficiencies, inspection and maintenance results, assurance findings, changes and operating experience.

clauses.heading: Evaluation, Reporting and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall monitor and report the health and effectiveness of critical controls, including significant or recurring deficiencies and corrective actions.

clauses.heading: Evaluation, Reporting and Improvement
clauses.text: Significant or systemic critical control deficiencies shall be escalated through the applicable Business Unit and Corporate governance arrangements, and relevant lessons shall be communicated to personnel and contractors who implement, verify or rely on the affected controls.

clauses.heading: Review and Management of Change
clauses.text: Fatal hazards, material unwanted events, critical controls and associated performance requirements shall be reviewed periodically and following relevant incidents or High Potential Incidents, recurring critical control deficiencies, material changes, or relevant changes in legal, technical or operating knowledge.

clauses.heading: Review and Management of Change
clauses.text: Changes to the approved Critical Control Management scope, fatal hazards, material unwanted events, critical controls or performance requirements shall be controlled through the Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Review and Management of Change
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain controlled documented information sufficient to demonstrate implementation and effectiveness of Critical Control Management.

processes.keywords: Critical Control Management; critical control, MUE, material unwanted event, control verification; Critical Control Management Framework and Accountability; Fatal Hazards, Material Unwanted Events and Critical Controls; Critical Control Performance Requirements; Critical Control Implementation; Critical Control Verification; Evaluation, Reporting and Improvement; Review and Management of Change
processes.trigger: if a fatal or material unwanted event or associated critical control is relevant

processes.title: EHSS Competency, Awareness and Communication
processes.purpose: Personnel are competent, trained, informed and engaged in EHSS matters relevant to their roles and activities through effective competency management, training, awareness and communication processes.
processes.scope: This process applies to the identification, development, implementation, verification, review and maintenance of EHSS competency, training, awareness and communication requirements for employees, contractor personnel and other relevant people undertaking activities on behalf of Maaden.

clauses.heading: Competency Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify the EHSS competencies required for roles that can affect EHSS performance, considering, as a minimum, assigned responsibilities, applicable legal and other requirements, EHSS risks, and operational and emergency response requirements.

clauses.heading: Competency Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain role based EHSS competency requirements, including for safety critical roles, defining applicable competency criteria, required training, assessment or verification methods, proficiency or acceptance criteria, and revalidation requirements commensurate with the risks associated with the role.

clauses.heading: Competency Management
clauses.text: Personnel performing activities that can affect EHSS performance shall be competent based on appropriate education, training, qualifications, experience, or a combination thereof.

clauses.heading: Competency Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess the competency of relevant personnel against established requirements and implement appropriate actions to address identified competency gaps.

clauses.heading: Competency Management
clauses.text: Competency shall be verified before personnel perform critical risk or role specific work and revalidated at defined intervals, with required certifications, licenses and authorizations kept current and valid.

clauses.heading: EHSS Training
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and maintain applicable mandatory EHSS training requirements for employees and contractor personnel, and establish EHSS training programs based on competency requirements, legal obligations, EHSS risks and operational needs.

clauses.heading: EHSS Training
clauses.text: Required EHSS training shall be completed before personnel undertake activities for which specific training or competency is required.

clauses.heading: EHSS Training
clauses.text: The suspension, deferment or significant interruption of mandatory EHSS training or required EHSS awareness programs shall be formally authorized, risk assessed and documented. Interim controls and recovery plans shall be established, including affected priority roles and training requirements, defined responsibilities, completion or reinstatement criteria, monitoring and escalation of outstanding requirements.

clauses.heading: EHSS Training
clauses.text: All EHSS training interventions shall comply with applicable Maaden Learning Center policies, procedures, standards and governance requirements, including its governance and oversight of learning compliance, quality assurance and training record integrity across Maaden.

clauses.heading: EHSS Training
clauses.text: The Maaden Learning Center shall review and endorse, before contract signing, all scopes of work involving external EHSS training providers, consultants, certification bodies, or training interventions to verify alignment with corporate learning standards, competency requirements, quality assurance processes, and governance requirements.

clauses.heading: EHSS Training
clauses.text: Completion and attendance for mandatory EHSS training shall be supported by verifiable evidence. Missed, overdue or expired mandatory training, and approved exceptions, shall be managed through defined arrangements including refresher or makeup training, escalation, monitoring of repeated non-attendance and documented closure.

clauses.heading: EHSS Training
clauses.text: Employees, contractor personnel and visitors shall receive applicable EHSS induction and awareness information before accessing or undertaking activities within Maaden controlled workplaces.

clauses.heading: EHSS Training
clauses.text: The effectiveness of EHSS training shall be evaluated and verified using methods appropriate to the training objectives and associated risks.

clauses.heading: EHSS Training
clauses.text: EHSS training and competency assessments shall be conducted by personnel competent in the applicable subject matter and training or assessment method.

clauses.heading: EHSS Awareness
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall provide employees, contractor personnel and other relevant people with EHSS awareness based on their roles, activities and exposure to risk, including, as applicable, the Maaden EHSS Policy, relevant EHSS risks and controls, individual responsibilities and accountabilities, applicable obligations, incident and emergency reporting requirements, and stop-work authority and responsibilities.

clauses.heading: EHSS communication
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain processes to communicate relevant EHSS information to employees, contractor personnel and other interested parties, as applicable, in a manner and language understood by the intended audience.

clauses.heading: EHSS communication
clauses.text: EHSS communication processes shall support consultation, participation, feedback and the sharing of relevant EHSS information, including incidents, lessons learned, changes in requirements and improvement opportunities.

clauses.heading: Records and Review
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain accurate, complete and current records of required EHSS competency, training, attendance, verification, revalidation, exceptions and certifications. Required records shall be maintained in the designated Maaden Learning Center platforms, with missing, overdue, expired or non-compliant requirements identified, escalated and addressed.

clauses.heading: Records and Review
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall periodically review competency, training, awareness and communication requirements and associated compliance. Requirements shall be updated following significant changes to activities, processes, EHSS risks, applicable obligations, technology, organizational responsibilities, or relevant lessons from incidents and assurance findings.

processes.keywords: EHSS Competency, Awareness and Communication; ehss competency, awareness and communication; Competency Management; EHSS Training; EHSS Awareness; EHSS communication; Records and Review
processes.trigger: if competency, authorization, consultation, awareness or communication is required

processes.title: Life Saving Rules
processes.purpose: The Maaden Life Saving Rules establish clear and consistent non-negotiable requirements for activities and conditions associated with fatal or other high consequence risks and provide a common basis for identifying, reporting and managing Life Saving Rule violations across Maaden.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden employees, contractor personnel and other people performing applicable activities under Maaden operational control, with the Life Saving Rules forming part of the applicable MSHEM risk management, critical control, work planning and operational requirements.

clauses.heading: Maaden Life Saving Rules
clauses.text:
Maaden shall establish and maintain the following nine Life Saving Rules:
a. Permit to Work
b. Confined Space
c. Energy Isolation
d. Line of fire
e. Working at height
f. Mobile equipment
g. Geotechnical Ground Control and Stability
h. Hazardous Materials and Explosives
i. EHSS Critical Systems Bypass

clauses.heading: Maaden Life Saving Rules
clauses.text: Each Life Saving Rule shall have approved Maaden trigger criteria defining the acts, omissions or conditions that constitute an LSR violation.

clauses.heading: Maaden Life Saving Rules
clauses.text: An event shall only be classified as an LSR violation where the applicable approved Maaden LSR trigger criteria are met.

clauses.heading: Maaden Life Saving Rules
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall integrate applicable Life Saving Rules and associated controls into relevant work planning, risk assessment, permit to work, contractor management and other operational arrangements.

clauses.heading: Maaden Life Saving Rules
clauses.text: Personnel and contractors undertaking work to which an LSR applies shall be informed of the applicable Life Saving Rule and its trigger criteria.

clauses.heading: Maaden Life Saving Rules
clauses.text: Where an applicable LSR trigger condition exists, affected work shall not commence or continue until the condition has been made safe and applicable control requirements are satisfied. Life Saving Rules support the Critical Control Management framework and do not replace applicable critical control performance, verification or Go/No-Go requirements under Section 2.6.

clauses.heading: Maaden Life Saving Rules
clauses.text: LSR violations shall be reported, recorded, classified and managed in accordance with Section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship.

processes.keywords: Life Saving Rules; LSR, life saving rule, lifesaving rule, stop work; Maaden Life Saving Rules
processes.trigger: if the activity falls within a Maaden Life Saving Rule or associated stop-work condition

processes.title: Environmental Risk and Impact Management
processes.purpose: Environmental risks, impacts and obligations arising from Maaden activities, products, services and projects are systematically identified, assessed, maintained within acceptable risk tolerance, and considered in operational, project and closure decision making throughout the asset lifecycle.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Maaden Business Units and Corporate Functions. It applies across the lifecycle of an asset including exploration, feasibility, design, construction, operation, closure and rehabilitation.

clauses.heading: Environmental Risk and Impact Identification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify environmental aspects, impacts, environmental hazards and environmental risks associated with activities, products, services, projects and facilities under their control or influence, in accordance with section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Environmental Risk and Impact Identification
clauses.text: Environmental risk and impact identification shall consider all routine activities, non-routine activities, abnormal operating conditions, reasonably foreseeable emergency situations, planned changes and projects, closure and rehabilitation activities, and legacy environmental conditions where applicable.

clauses.heading: Environmental Risk and Impact Identification
clauses.text: Environmental risk and impact identification shall consider the full range environmental hazards and receptors, including land, water, air, acid rock drainage, heavy metals and mercury, hazardous chemicals, biodiversity, waste and tailings, energy, climate, cultural heritage and others.

clauses.heading: Environmental Risk and Impact Identification
clauses.text: Environmental risk and impact identification shall consider information from applicable studies, monitoring data, incidents, audit findings, inspections, permit requirements, stakeholder concerns, regulatory observations, scientific information and operational experience.

clauses.heading: Environmental Risk and Impact Assessment
clauses.text: Environmental aspects and associated impacts shall be evaluated to determine their significance, taking into account applicable legal and permit conditions, the nature and severity of the impact, likelihood, affected environmental receptors, community concerns and relevant stakeholder expectations.

clauses.heading: Environmental Risk and Impact Assessment
clauses.text: Environmental risks arising from identified aspects and impacts shall be assessed and managed in accordance with the section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Environmental Risk and Impact Assessment
clauses.text: Environmental aspects and associated impacts shall be prioritized for avoidance, minimization, or elimination.

clauses.heading: Environmental Risks and Impacts
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish criteria to determine environmental risks and impacts.

clauses.heading: Environmental Risks and Impacts
clauses.text: Environmental risks and impacts shall be documented and maintained in a controlled register.

clauses.heading: Environmental Risks and Impacts
clauses.text: Environmental risks and impacts shall be considered when establishing objectives, plans, operational controls, monitoring programs and improvement initiatives. All critical, high and significant risks and the risk treatment plan shall be communicated to the relevant Business Unit management as well as Corporate environment.

clauses.heading: Environmental Risks and Impacts
clauses.text: Environmental controls shall be maintained for all environmental risks and impacts throughout the asset lifecycle stages.

clauses.heading: Environmental Obligations and Decision Making
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and maintain environmental legal, regulatory, permit and other obligations relevant to identified environmental risks and impacts in accordance with section 2.4 EHSS Legal and Regulatory Requirements process.

clauses.heading: Environmental Obligations and Decision Making
clauses.text: Environmental risks, impacts and obligations shall be considered during project development, operational planning, modification, expansion, closure and rehabilitation decisions.

clauses.heading: Environmental Obligations and Decision Making
clauses.text: Environmental risk assessments shall support permitting, environmental studies, environmental management plans and operational control arrangements where required.

clauses.heading: Environmental Obligations and Decision Making
clauses.text: Where environmental risks or impacts may affect external stakeholders, ecosystems, protected areas or shared resources, the Business Unit shall consider applicable stakeholders and regulatory requirements.

clauses.heading: Review Cycle and Change Management
Review Cycle and Change Management
clauses.text: Changes that may alter environmental risks, impacts, obligations or controls shall be evaluated through the applicable Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Review Cycle and Change Management
clauses.text: Environmental risk and impact information shall be maintained current and reflective of actual operating conditions.

clauses.heading: Monitoring and Verification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall monitor the effectiveness of controls implemented for significant environmental risks and impacts.

clauses.heading: Monitoring and Verification
clauses.text: Monitoring and assurance activities shall verify that identified environmental risks and impacts remain understood, controlled and compliant with applicable obligations.

clauses.heading: Monitoring and Verification
clauses.text: Deficiencies identified through monitoring, audits, inspections, incidents or reviews shall be evaluated and addressed.

clauses.heading: Records and Evidence
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain documented information demonstrating environmental risk and impact assessments, significant environmental risk and impact registers, environmental obligations relevant to identified risks and impacts, reassessments and reviews, and actions arising from identified environmental risks and impacts.

processes.keywords: Environmental Risk and Impact Management; environmental risk and impact management; Environmental Risk and Impact Identification; Environmental Risk and Impact Assessment; Significant Environmental Risks and Impacts; Environmental Obligations and Decision-Making; Review cycle and Change Management; Monitoring and Verification; Records and Evidence
processes.trigger: if the activity creates or changes a significant environmental aspect or impact

processes.title: Environmental Permitting and Compliance
processes.purpose: Environmental legal and regulatory obligations, permits and approvals applicable to Maaden are identified, obtained, maintained, implemented, monitored, verified and managed throughout their lifecycle to maintain compliance and prevent permit breaches, enforcement actions and environmental non-compliance.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Maaden Business Units and Corporate Functions where Maaden activities are subject to environmental permits and approvals or authorizations, legal and regulatory obligations, environmental approval requirements associated with exploration, projects, construction, operation, modification, expansion, closure, rehabilitation or post-closure activities.

clauses.heading: Governance and Lifecycle Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define accountability and responsibility for obtaining, maintaining and complying with applicable environmental permits, approvals and compliance obligations.

clauses.heading: Governance and Lifecycle Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and integrate applicable environmental permit and approval requirements throughout the lifecycle of activities, projects and assets.

clauses.heading: Governance and Lifecycle Management
clauses.text: Required environmental permits, licenses and approvals shall be obtained before the applicable activity begins and maintained throughout their period of applicability.

clauses.heading: Governance and Lifecycle Management
clauses.text: Projects shall follow sustainability requirements provided in the Maaden Capital Investment System (MCIS_TK_0387_Sustainability Requirements Toolkit )for consideration at different stages of the project.

clauses.heading: Governance and Lifecycle Management
clauses.text: Constraints, permitting delays, regulatory actions, or compliance risks shall be escalated through the applicable governance processes and incorporated into the relevant operational and project risk registers.

clauses.heading: Identification and Management of Compliance Obligations
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify applicable environmental laws, regulations, permit and approval conditions, monitoring and reporting requirements, regulatory directions and formally adopted environmental commitments in accordance with section 2.4 EHSS Legal and Regulatory Requirements process.

clauses.heading: Identification and Management of Compliance Obligations
clauses.text: Operational, engineering and administrative controls shall be implemented and maintained to comply with applicable environmental obligations, permit conditions and regulatory commitments. Obligations and related actions shall be assigned to responsible functions and tracked to completion through Hemaya system.

clauses.heading: Change Management and Permit Maintenance
clauses.text: Proposed changes shall be evaluated before implementation to determine their effect on environmental permits, approvals and compliance obligations in accordance with the section 3.52 Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Change Management and Permit Maintenance
clauses.text: Environmental compliance obligations, permit requirements and related controls shall be reviewed and updated following relevant legal, regulatory, permit, project, operational or organizational changes.

clauses.heading: Regulatory Monitoring and Reporting
clauses.text: Environmental monitoring required by environmental permits, regulatory approvals or legal obligations shall be defined and implemented in accordance with section 3.3 Environmental Monitoring process.

clauses.heading: Regulatory Monitoring and Reporting
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that required environmental reports and regulatory submissions, including environmental monitoring reports, permit application packages, environmental impact assessment reports, environmental audit reports and associated studies, are reviewed to identify and address compliance concerns before submission to the relevant authority.

clauses.heading: Regulatory Compliance Verification and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall periodically evaluate compliance with applicable environmental obligations using documented evidence, including permits, approvals, monitoring results, regulatory reporting and adopted commitments.

clauses.heading: Regulatory Compliance Verification and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall be prepared in advance and maintain readiness as per Maaden Regulatory Environmental Inspection Violation Governance Protocols and fully co-operate with regulatory inspections, audits, assessments and compliance verification activities.

clauses.heading: Non-Compliance, Permit Breaches and Corrective Action
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify, report and manage, regulatory requirement deviations, environmental permit breaches, non-compliance events, regulatory findings and observations, regulatory notices of violations, penalties, or other enforcement actions and major noncompliance risks.

clauses.heading: Non-Compliance, Permit Breaches and Corrective Action
clauses.text: Actual or potential environmental non-compliance shall be investigated to determine its causes and required corrective actions, with actions assigned, tracked and verified for effectiveness by the relevant Business Unit.

clauses.heading: Non-Compliance, Permit Breaches and Corrective Action
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall notify and respond to the relevant regulatory authorities within the timeframes and in the manner required by applicable laws, permit conditions or regulatory directions for environmental non-compliance, major environmental incidents, shutdowns, emergencies and other reportable events.

clauses.heading: Records, Review and Improvement
clauses.text: Environmental permitting and compliance records shall be controlled, retained and available in accordance with applicable legal, regulatory and corporate requirements.

clauses.heading: Records, Review and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall periodically review and report environmental permitting and compliance performance in accordance with section 6.4 Management Review and Continual Improvement.

clauses.heading: Records, Review and Improvement
clauses.text: Environmental permitting and compliance arrangements shall be updated following changes, compliance evaluations, regulatory inspections, non-compliance events, findings and relevant lessons learned.

processes.keywords: Environmental Permitting and Compliance; environmental permit, consent, licence, compliance; Governance and Lifecycle Management; Identification and Management of Compliance Obligations; Change Management and Permit Maintenance; Regulatory Monitoring and Reporting; Regulatory Compliance Verification and Assurance; Non-Compliance, Permit Breaches and Corrective Action; Records, Review and Improvement
processes.trigger: if an environmental permit, approval, licence, consent or compliance condition applies

processes.title: Environmental Monitoring
processes.purpose: Environmental monitoring is established and maintained to verify environmental performance, demonstrate compliance with legal, regulatory and permit obligations, and other commitments, and to detect actual or potential environmental harm, and support timely corrective action and continual improvement throughout the lifecycle of applicable sources and assets.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Maaden Business Units and Corporate Functions where environmental monitoring is required by applicable obligations, environmental risk assessments, environmental commitments or Maaden requirements, throughout the relevant lifecycle phases.

clauses.heading: Governance, Accountability and Applicability
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and document environmental monitoring requirements arising from applicable legal and regulatory obligations, permits, approvals, authorizations, environmental assessments, commitments and Maaden internal requirements.

clauses.heading: Governance, Accountability and Applicability
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall determine and document applicable environmental monitoring requirements for relevant project, operational, closure and post-closure lifecycle phases and establish environmental monitoring programs to address those requirements.

clauses.heading: Governance, Accountability and Applicability
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assign competent personnel to implement, review and report on environmental monitoring programs.

clauses.heading: Environmental Monitoring Planning and Implementation
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, maintain and implement a documented environmental monitoring plan to demonstrate compliance with applicable obligations, commitments and Maaden requirements.

clauses.heading: Environmental Monitoring Planning and Implementation
clauses.text: Environmental monitoring plans shall be based on significant environmental aspects and associated risks, relevant receptors and exposure pathways, applicable obligations, operational controls and lifecycle requirements. The plans shall define, as applicable, monitoring locations, parameters, methods, frequencies, limits and trigger levels, and data quality, reporting and escalation requirements.

clauses.heading: Environmental Monitoring Planning and Implementation
clauses.text: Environmental monitoring plans shall be reviewed and updated following significant changes affecting their basis, scope or requirements.

clauses.heading: Environmental Monitoring Planning and Implementation
clauses.text: Environmental monitoring shall be performed using approved or accepted methods and equipment, qualified personnel, authorized service providers and competent laboratories.

clauses.heading: Environmental Monitoring Planning and Implementation
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain the monitoring locations, infrastructure, equipment and supporting systems necessary to implement the environmental monitoring plan.

clauses.heading: Data Quality, Validation and Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish quality assurance and quality control measures to ensure the integrity, traceability and reliability of environmental monitoring data. Records demonstrating monitoring data quality and validation shall be retained.

clauses.heading: Data Quality, Validation and Control
clauses.text: Environmental monitoring data shall be reviewed and validated by competent Business Unit environmental personnel before use for decision-making, performance evaluation or external reporting. Invalid, unreliable or incomplete data shall be investigated and addressed before use.

clauses.heading: Exceedance, Escalation and Corrective Action
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish documented criteria for identifying exceedances of applicable limits or internal trigger levels, adverse environmental trends and monitoring program failures.

clauses.heading: Exceedance, Escalation and Corrective Action
clauses.text: Identified exceedances and actual or potential environmental non-compliance shall be reported, classified, investigated and escalated in accordance with applicable legal, regulatory, permit and section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship requirements.

clauses.heading: Exceedance, Escalation and Corrective Action
clauses.text: Corrective actions addressing the identified causes of exceedances, adverse environmental trends and environmental monitoring program failures shall be implemented and their effectiveness verified.

clauses.heading: Reporting and Regulatory Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify the completeness and accuracy of required environmental monitoring reports and submit them in accordance with applicable legal, regulatory and permit requirements, including content, format and submission timeframes.

clauses.heading: Reporting and Regulatory Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall communicate significant environmental monitoring results, exceedances and compliance issues to relevant internal and external stakeholders, along with justifications and corrective action plans where applicable.

clauses.heading: Verification and Review
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall periodically analyze environmental monitoring results and review monitoring programs to identify trends, emerging risks and improvement opportunities and confirm their continued applicability and effectiveness.

clauses.heading: Verification and Review
clauses.text: Environmental monitoring programs shall be updated where review findings or changes in applicable obligations, environmental risks, operating or lifecycle conditions affect monitoring requirements or program effectiveness.

processes.keywords: Environmental Monitoring; environmental monitoring; Governance, Accountability and Applicability; Environmental Monitoring Planning; Environmental Monitoring Program Implementation; Data Quality, Validation and Control; Exceedance, Escalation and Corrective Action; Reporting and Regulatory Compliance; Verification and Review
processes.trigger: if environmental sampling, monitoring, calibration or data reporting is required

processes.title: Environmental Footprint Management
processes.purpose: Maaden environmental footprint data are complete, accurate, validated, traceable, and consistently consolidated to support internal management, investor reporting, external sustainability disclosures, performance evaluation, target setting, and strategic decision making.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Business Units, Corporate Functions, contractors and third parties that generate or report data contributing to Maaden’s environmental footprint reporting, including greenhouse gas emissions, energy, water, materials and waste data.

clauses.heading: Environmental Footprint Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain an Environmental Footprint Management process for the collection, validation, consolidation, analysis and reporting of environmental footprint data.

clauses.heading: Environmental Footprint Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Corporate Sustainability shall maintain and periodically review the approved Environmental Footprint Technical Guidance Document, including environmental footprint methodologies, indicator definitions, reporting requirements, and reporting protocols.

clauses.heading: Environmental Footprint Aspects and Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and assess aspects that may affect the integrity, accuracy, completeness, consistency or reliability of environmental footprint data.

clauses.heading: Environmental Footprint Aspects and Controls
Environmental Footprint Aspects and Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify, implement and periodically verify controls to prevent, detect and correct environmental footprint data errors and reporting deficiencies that could result in materially incorrect environmental performance information or disclosures.

clauses.heading: Environmental Footprint Aspects and Controls
clauses.text: Environmental footprint risks and controls shall be reviewed following significant changes to activities, assets, reporting obligations, organizational arrangements or reporting methodologies.

clauses.heading: Reporting Boundaries and Data Framework
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain documented environmental reporting boundaries consistent with corporate requirements and applicable reporting obligations provided in the Environmental Footprint Technical Guidance Document.

clauses.heading: Reporting Boundaries and Data Framework
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that environmental footprint data are obtained from identified and authorized sources, remain traceable to supporting source information, and are reported using documented and consistently applied indicators, definitions, units of measure, responsibilities, reporting frequencies and calculation methodologies. Material changes to reporting boundaries, methodologies, inventories or indicators shall be reviewed, approved and documented.

clauses.heading: Environmental Footprint Data Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall collect, maintain and submit environmental footprint data relevant to their activities, products and services in accordance with approved reporting requirements.

clauses.heading: Environmental Footprint Data Management
clauses.text: Missing, incomplete, inconsistent or inaccurate environmental footprint data shall be identified, investigated, corrected and documented.

clauses.heading: Calculation, Estimation and Methodology Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall use approved methodologies, verified emission factors, conversion factors and calculation methods specified in Environmental Footprint Technical Guidance Document.

clauses.heading: Calculation, Estimation and Methodology Control
clauses.text: Estimates or data substitutions shall be used only when valid source data are unavailable or do not meet defined data quality criteria, with their use justified, documented and traceable.

clauses.heading: Calculation, Estimation and Methodology Control
clauses.text: Changes to calculation methodologies, factors, assumptions or estimation methods shall be assessed, approved and documented, including evaluation of the effects of significant changes on reported inventories, historical performance, baselines and targets.

clauses.heading: Data Validation, Quality Assurance and Consolidation
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall validate environmental footprint data and consolidated information before finalization or reporting to confirm completeness, accuracy, consistency and traceability, and investigate, resolve and document identified discrepancies, anomalies or validation failures.

clauses.heading: Performance Indicators, Baselines and Targets
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain applicable environmental footprint performance indicators, baselines and targets aligned with corporate requirements, Maaden strategic objectives and applicable business specific commitments, and monitor performance and progress against them.

clauses.heading: Performance Indicators, Baselines and Targets
clauses.text: Material deviations from approved baselines or targets shall be investigated, documented and escalated in accordance with defined criteria.

clauses.heading: Reporting, Disclosure and Verification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall provide environmental footprint information and data required for corporate reporting and external disclosures in accordance with Environmental Footprint Technical Guidance Document.

clauses.heading: Reporting, Disclosure and Verification
clauses.text: Environmental footprint data, performance metrics and material environmental disclosures shall be reviewed for completeness, consistency and accuracy before external release and shall be supported by documented evidence, traceable source data and Maaden approved methodologies aligned with applicable GRI disclosure requirements and other applicable reporting criteria.

clauses.heading: Reporting, Disclosure and Verification
clauses.text: Independent verification or assurance shall be undertaken where required by legal obligations, adopted standards, certification schemes, stakeholder commitments or corporate requirements.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Escalation and Corrective Action
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall evaluate, at defined intervals, the implementation and effectiveness of environmental footprint management requirements and controls, and escalate legal non-compliance, material misstatements, control failures, overdue actions and significant reporting deficiencies in accordance with section 6.4 Management Review and Continual Improvement.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Escalation and Corrective Action
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and implement environmental footprint reduction and performance improvement plans where environmental footprint performance evaluation identifies adverse trends, unmet objectives or targets, or opportunities for improvement.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Escalation and Corrective Action
clauses.text: Environmental footprint management findings and deficiencies shall be investigated, with corrective actions tracked to verified closure and lessons learned communicated and used to improve controls, competency, methodologies and reporting processes.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Escalation and Corrective Action
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain environmental footprint management records that are controlled, traceable, retrievable and protected from loss, unauthorized alteration or destruction, and shall retain them in accordance with applicable legal and Maaden requirements.
