processes.trigger: if greenhouse-gas, resource, material, water, energy or waste footprint data are managed

processes.title: Air Quality and Emissions Management
processes.purpose: Air quality and emissions are systematically identified, assessed, prevented, controlled, monitored and continually improved to protect environment and community receptors; prevent pollution and adverse impacts on health and ecosystems; maintain compliance with applicable legal and regulatory obligations and sustain responsible environmental stewardship throughout the assets lifecycle.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Maaden Business units and Corporate Functions with activities that may generate air emissions from construction, mining, crushing, screening, conveying, stockpiling, material handling, transporting, manufacturing and materials processing, refining, smelting, power generation, storing, treatment and other operational activities.

clauses.heading: Governance, Accountability and Applicability
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement and maintain an Air Quality and Emissions Management process, aligned with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, permit obligations and other agreed commitments.

clauses.heading: Governance, Accountability and Applicability
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall determine and document the applicability and boundaries of air quality and emissions management for their activities, projects, facilities and assets, including relevant emission sources and categories, air pollutants and potential receptors.

clauses.heading: Governance, Accountability and Applicability
clauses.text: Air quality and emissions management requirements shall be integrated into project development, design, construction, operation, modification, closure and post-closure activities.

clauses.heading: Source Identification and Inventory Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify, document and maintain an inventory of applicable air emission sources, including point sources, flares, mobile sources, fugitive sources, emergency emission sources, wastewater- related sources, storage sources and temporary construction sources.

clauses.heading: Source Identification and Inventory Management
clauses.text: The up-to-date air inventory shall include, but not limited to, location of the emission source, emission flow, air pollutants in emission stream, emission quantities, concentrations of air pollutants, EPO requirements, monitoring requirements and calculation methods, applicable receptors, pollution or emission control equipment.

clauses.heading: Source Identification and Inventory Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain and report inventory of regulated pollutants including particulate matter, sulfur oxides, nitrogen oxides, carbon monoxide, hazardous air pollutants, volatile organic compounds and other pollutants required by regulatory obligations.

clauses.heading: Source Identification and Inventory Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and evaluate air emission sources, pollutants, receptors, applicable obligations and associated risks in accordance with section 3.1 Environmental Risk and Impact Management process, and implement and maintain controls to manage significant air emission risks.

clauses.heading: Air Emissions and Air Quality Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify air emission sources and activities that could affect air quality, people, communities or environmental receptors, and establish and maintain controls to comply with applicable obligations and emission limits and to prevent or minimize adverse air quality impacts.

clauses.heading: Air Emissions and Air Quality Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain programs to monitor, assess and verify air emissions and air quality performance where required by applicable obligations, permits, environmental risks or management system requirements.

clauses.heading: Fugitive Emissions and Dust Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and control applicable sources of fugitive emissions and dust, including volatile organic compounds, hazardous air pollutants and other relevant pollutants, to prevent or minimize adverse impacts.

clauses.heading: Fugitive Emissions and Dust Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall implement monitoring, inspection, verification and leak detection and repair programs where required by applicable obligations, permits or risk assessments, and investigate and address significant fugitive emission and dust events and odor complaints.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain air quality and emissions monitoring programs, evaluate results and trends against applicable limits, permit conditions and internal criteria, and address identified exceedances and control failures.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify and submit required air quality and emissions reports, retain associated records in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements, and evaluate at defined intervals the effectiveness of air quality and emissions management to determine required updates to assessments, inventories, controls, monitoring programs and plans.

processes.keywords: Air Quality and Emissions Management; air quality, emissions, stack, fugitive dust; Governance, Accountability and Applicability; Source Identification and Inventory Management; Air Emissions and Air Quality Management; Fugitive Emissions and Dust Management; Monitoring, Verification and Improvement
processes.trigger: if air emissions, fugitive dust, stack releases or ambient-air impacts may occur

processes.title: Waste Management
processes.purpose: Manage all applicable waste throughout its lifecycle from generation to final recovery, treatment or disposal in a manner that prevents environmental harm, supports resource efficiency and circularity, maintains legal compliance, and provides demonstrable traceability and control.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Maaden Business Units and Corporate Functions that generate or manage waste throughout its lifecycle, including storage, handling, transport, recovery, recycling, treatment and disposal. It covers industrial, municipal, medical, laboratory, construction and demolition wastes, contaminated materials, wastewater residues and other applicable waste streams. This process does not apply to Tailings, Waste rock, Ore Rejects, Phospho-gypsum, Red mud or bauxite residue, managed under section 3.10 Tailings Management process.

clauses.heading: Establish and Define Waste Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement and maintain a waste management process covering waste generation, classification, storage, collection, transport, recovery, treatment and disposal.

clauses.heading: Establish and Define Waste Management
clauses.text: Business Unit and Corporate Function management shall ensure that responsibilities, competent personnel, resources and waste management arrangements are established and implemented within their areas of control.

clauses.heading: Establish and Define Waste Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify applicable waste management obligations and maintain documented procedures, waste inventories, registers and records appropriate to their waste profile.

clauses.heading: Waste Identification, Characterization and Classification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify, characterize and classify waste streams generated by activities, products, services, projects and facilities under their control using applicable requirements, approved methodologies, process knowledge and analytical data where required.

clauses.heading: Waste Identification, Characterization and Classification
clauses.text: Hazardous waste and waste of uncertain classification shall be managed as hazardous in accordance with applicable requirements until its classification has been verified.

clauses.heading: Waste Identification, Characterization and Classification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain a waste inventory and register that identifies waste types, classifications, quantities, sources and management pathways.

clauses.heading: Waste Identification, Characterization and Classification
clauses.text: Waste characterization and classification shall be reviewed whenever changes occur that may affect waste properties, classification or management requirements.

clauses.heading: Waste Identification, Characterization and Classification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions that generate or control radioactive waste shall establish and maintain a radioactive waste management program in accordance with applicable Nuclear and Radiological Regulatory Commission (NRRC) requirements, including inventory, traceability, recordkeeping and regulatory reporting.

clauses.heading: Waste Impact Assessment and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and assess waste management impacts associated with generation, handling, storage, transport, recovery, treatment and disposal activities.

clauses.heading: Waste Impact Assessment and Planning
clauses.text: Waste impact assessments shall consider, where applicable; misclassification, incompatible mixing, container and secondary containment failure, labelling deficiencies, storage failures, uncontrolled accumulation, fire and explosion, hazard exposure, waste transport incidents, spill and release events, contamination, unauthorized disposal, biodiversity impacts and contract absence or failures.

clauses.heading: Waste Impact Assessment and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall develop and implement waste management plans that apply the waste hierarchy in the following order of preference: avoid, reduce, reuse, recycle, recover, treat and dispose.

clauses.heading: Waste Impact Assessment and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall minimize waste generation through project development, procurement, operational planning, process improvement, material efficiency initiatives, shutdowns, decommissioning and closure, and establish objectives and actions for significant waste streams.

clauses.heading: Waste Impact Assessment and Planning
clauses.text: Waste shall be treated or disposed of only where it cannot reasonably be avoided, reduced, reused, recycled or recovered, using methods compatible with its classification and applicable requirements.

clauses.heading: Waste Segregation, Handling and Storage
clauses.text: Waste shall be segregated at or as close as reasonably practicable to the point of generation, with hazardous waste separated from non-hazardous waste and incompatible waste streams to prevent reactions, releases, contamination or exposure.

clauses.heading: Waste Segregation, Handling and Storage
clauses.text: Waste shall be handled and stored in identified and labelled containers and designated storage areas that are compatible with the waste characteristics and intended management pathway and provide controls against releases, unauthorized access and other applicable risks, including secondary containment, inspection access and emergency response provisions where required.

clauses.heading: Waste Segregation, Handling and Storage
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall control waste accumulation and apply additional hazard specific and regulatory controls to medical, laboratory, chemical and other waste streams requiring special management. Anticipated accumulation beyond applicable storage limits or capacity shall be subject to contingency arrangements and required regulatory authorization.

clauses.heading: Waste Transport, Transfer and Service Providers
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall use approved and legally authorized service providers for waste transport, transfer, recovery, treatment and disposal and verify that the providers and receiving facilities are authorized to manage the relevant waste streams.

clauses.heading: Waste Transport, Transfer and Service Providers
clauses.text: Waste movements shall be traceable from the point of generation to confirmed receipt, recovery, treatment or disposal using applicable manifests, transportation documents or equivalent tracking systems, with waste service providers managed in accordance with section 4.1 Contractor EHSS Management.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Verification and Records
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall inspect and monitor waste management activities, including waste storage areas, at defined intervals and against established criteria to verify the implementation and effectiveness of controls and compliance with applicable obligations and permit requirements.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Verification and Records
clauses.text: Waste management performance indicators, and targets shall be established and periodically reviewed, tracked and reported.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Verification and Records
clauses.text: Legal breaches, failed controls and overdue corrective actions shall be escalated through defined governance arrangements.

processes.trigger: if waste is generated, classified, stored, transported, treated or disposed

processes.title: Water Management
processes.purpose: Water resources, water related infrastructure and water interactions are managed throughout the asset lifecycle to protect people, the environment, communities and operations, comply with obligations, maintain water security, and prevent water depletion, contamination and uncontrolled releases.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Business Units and Corporate Functions involved in water management across the asset lifecycle, from exploration and feasibility through design, construction, operation, closure and rehabilitation, including water abstraction, mine dewatering, receipt, storage, transfer, treatment, use, recycling and discharge.

clauses.heading: Governance and Water Management Framework
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall use this process as the framework for water management and establish, implement and maintain water management procedures aligned with applicable legal, regulatory and permit requirements and the Maaden Corporate Water Management Standard (CWMS)

clauses.heading: Governance and Water Management Framework
clauses.text: Water related projects and water management infrastructure shall be planned, assessed, designed, constructed, commissioned and transferred to operations in accordance with applicable Maaden Capital Investment System (MCIS) requirements.

clauses.heading: Governance and Water Management Framework
clauses.text: Where an applicable requirement of the CWMS or MCIS exceeds or provides additional detail to this process, the applicable CWMS or MCIS requirement shall apply.

clauses.heading: Governance and Water Management Framework
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain a water management framework that addresses; water abstraction and supply, mine dewatering and groundwater management, process and potable water systems, wastewater treatment and discharge, stormwater and seepage management, water reuse and recycling, tailings water management, surface water and groundwater protection and closure and post-closure water obligations.

clauses.heading: Governance and Water Management Framework
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and apply applicable water management obligations and commitments, obtain and maintain required licenses, permits, approvals and authorizations, comply with their conditions, and verify compliance at defined intervals.

clauses.heading: Governance and Water Management Framework
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define, document and communicate responsibilities and authorities for water management and ensure that assigned personnel are competent to fulfil their responsibilities.

clauses.heading: Governance and Water Management Framework
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement and track controls and actions proportionate to identified water related risks and sufficient to meet applicable obligations.

clauses.heading: Water Risk and Impact Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify, assess, manage and review water related risks and impacts across the asset lifecycle in accordance with the Corporate Water Management Standard, including following significant changes affecting water risks, obligations or performance.

clauses.heading: Water Stewardship and Catchment Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions operating in shared catchments or water stressed regions shall identify and evaluate the catchments, groundwater systems and shared water resources that may influence, or be influenced by, their activities.

clauses.heading: Water Stewardship and Catchment Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify water sources and dependent receptors, groundwater and surface water interactions, other significant water users, community water dependencies and catchment level water risks.

clauses.heading: Water Stewardship and Catchment Management
clauses.text: Where water related risks are associated with shared water resources, the assessments shall consider existing water users, foreseeable future water users, water allocation arrangements, sensitive receptors, ecosystem water requirements, high-value water resources, cumulative impacts, and major stakeholder concerns.

clauses.heading: Water Stewardship and Catchment Management
clauses.text: Catchment related assessments and controls shall be reviewed when significant changes occur in water availability, water demand, catchment conditions, regulatory requirements, or foreseeable cumulative impacts.

clauses.heading: Water Stewardship and Catchment Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall evaluate actual and potential impacts on communities, ecosystems, other water users and long-term water availability where their operations may materially influence shared water resources.

clauses.heading: Water Stewardship and Catchment Management
clauses.text: Water related stakeholder concerns, commitments and identified shared water risks shall be considered in water management planning.

clauses.heading: Water Planning and Balance Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain water balances covering material water inputs, outputs, transfers, storage, consumption, reuse, recycling and losses.

clauses.heading: Water Planning and Balance Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall integrate water balances into operational planning, risk management, water stewardship, regulatory compliance and asset lifecycle planning, and review and update them following significant changes affecting water supply, demand, infrastructure, operations or water related risks.

clauses.heading: Operational Water Management Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and implement controls to manage water related activities, infrastructure and facilities throughout the asset lifecycle to achieve compliance with applicable obligations, protect water resources, prevent adverse impacts to people and the environment, and manage water related emergencies.

clauses.heading: Operational Water Management Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that water abstraction, collection, storage, transfer, treatment, use, reuse, recycling, injection and discharge activities comply with applicable legal, regulatory, permit and Maaden requirements.

clauses.heading: Operational Water Management Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain emergency preparedness and response plans for credible water related emergency scenarios, including loss of water supply, pond overtopping, pipeline rupture, water contamination, tailings, phosphogypsum or red mud water releases, extreme weather events, and water treatment system failures scenarios in accordance with section 5.1 Emergency Response Preparedness and Planning.

clauses.heading: Operational Water Management Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions that abstract, dewater, use or may impact groundwater shall establish and implement groundwater protection, abstraction management and aquifer monitoring controls to manage groundwater quantity, groundwater quality, regulatory obligations and potential impacts on environmental receptors.

clauses.heading: Water Quality and Environment Protection
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify water resources, receiving environments, groundwater and surface-water receptors, environmentally sensitive areas, water-dependent ecosystems, people and other water users potentially affected by their activities, and implement controls to prevent or minimize adverse impacts.

clauses.heading: Water Quality and Environment Protection
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify, assess and manage risks associated with wastewater, contaminated water, stormwater, seepage and other water releases, and ensure that authorized discharges comply with applicable legal, regulatory, permit and Maaden requirements.

clauses.heading: Water Monitoring and Performance Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain risk based water monitoring programs to evaluate water related risks, control effectiveness, compliance and performance.

clauses.heading: Water Monitoring and Performance Management
clauses.text: Water related monitoring information and records shall be maintained and reported in accordance with applicable legal, regulatory, permit and Maaden requirements.

clauses.heading: Water Monitoring and Performance Management
clauses.text: Monitoring programs shall be developed based on Corporate Water Management Standard and shall provide minimum information to evaluate; water abstraction, water consumption, water losses, water use efficiency, water reuse and recycling, water quality, water discharge performance, groundwater and surface water impacts, effectiveness of water controls.

clauses.heading: Water Monitoring and Performance Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish measurable water-intensity performance indicators and water efficiency targets, taking into account water availability, operational requirements, water-related risks, significant water uses, legal obligations and opportunities to improve water stewardship.

clauses.heading: Water Monitoring and Performance Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall implement and periodically review water efficiency and water consumption reduction plans to improve performance and support achievement of established objectives and targets.

clauses.heading: Closure, Post-Closure and Long-Term Water Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify foreseeable long-term water related risks, liabilities and obligations and incorporate applicable water quantity, water quality, treatment, storage, discharge, monitoring and maintenance requirements into closure and post-closure planning throughout the asset lifecycle.

clauses.heading: Closure, Post-Closure and Long-Term Water Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall incorporate ongoing post-closure water management requirements, including associated operation, maintenance, monitoring and treatment requirements, into closure plans and financial provisions.

clauses.heading: Verification, Reporting and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify, at defined intervals, the implementation and effectiveness of water management requirements and controls and maintain evidence demonstrating compliance with applicable water related obligations.

clauses.heading: Verification, Reporting and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall report, escalate, investigate and address water related incidents, non- compliances, permit breaches, significant exceedances, control failures and findings in accordance with applicable MSHEM processes.

processes.trigger: if water is abstracted, treated, stored, transferred, discharged or monitored

processes.title: Energy Management
processes.purpose: This process defines Maaden’s minimum corporate requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving energy management across applicable Business Units and Corporate Functions to achieve measurable improvement in energy performance, including energy efficiency, energy use and energy consumption.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Units and Corporate Functions under Maaden’s operational control in Saudi Arabia where activities, assets or decisions affect energy use, consumption, efficiency or performance.

clauses.heading: Governance, Roles, and Accountability
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall be accountable for energy performance, regulatory compliance, resource allocation, implementation of this process, and continual improvement of energy management within their respective areas of control.

clauses.heading: Governance, Roles, and Accountability
clauses.text: Business Unit and Corporate Functions shall appoint competent energy management personnel with clearly defined roles, responsibilities, authority, and reporting lines. Appointed personnel shall have the required competence to implement ISO 50001 requirements and applicable SEEC Framework obligations.

clauses.heading: Governance, Roles, and Accountability
clauses.text: For Growth Projects, Maaden Capital Investment System (MCIS) minimum requirements shall be followed, including the applicable sustainability toolkit requirements under MCIS_TK_0387, to ensure energy efficiency, metering, monitoring, regulatory compliance, and sustainability considerations are embedded during project development, design review, procurement, and approval stages.

clauses.heading: Governance, Roles, and Accountability
clauses.text: Corporate Sustainability shall act as the corporate process custodian for energy management and define minimum requirements, reporting expectations and performance review requirements for Business Units, sites, operations and growth projects.

clauses.heading: Energy Management Framework
clauses.text:
Business Units and Corporate Functions shall integrate energy management into applicable business planning, significant energy use assessment, operational control, performance monitoring and continual improvement processes, in accordance with ISO 50001 principles.
a. Sites that collectively represent at least 90% of the respective Business Unit’s total energy consumption shall be prioritized for ISO 50001 implementation, certification and re-certification.
b. For other sites within each Business Unit, management shall identify Significant Energy Users in accordance with ISO 50001, establish monitoring arrangements, and implement documented action plans to improve energy efficiency and energy performance.

clauses.heading: Energy Management Framework
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify, obtain, maintain, and comply with all applicable energy-related permits, regulatory authorizations, SEEC requirements, utility conditions, and other legally binding obligations relevant to their operations, projects, fuels, utilities, and energy consuming assets.

clauses.heading: Energy Management Framework
clauses.text: New projects, major modifications, replacement equipment, and procurement decisions shall consider best available technology, life-cycle energy performance, energy efficiency specifications, design alternatives, and total cost of ownership, as applicable to the project scope and technical feasibility.

clauses.heading: Energy Management Framework
clauses.text: Energy performance, compliance status, action plan progress, savings verification, key risks, and corrective actions shall be reported at defined intervals to Site, Business Unit, and Corporate Sustainability governance forums, in accordance with section 6.4 Management Review and Continual Improvement process.

clauses.heading: Energy Management Framework
clauses.text: Records shall be retained as auditable evidence, including permits and approvals, legal and regulatory obligation registers, energy reviews, energy baselines, energy performance indicators, metering data, calibration records, operational-control evidence, project design reviews, procurement evaluations, training records, management reviews, internal audits, nonconformities, and corrective actions.

clauses.heading: Energy Management Framework
clauses.text: Internal audits shall be planned and performed periodically to verify conformance with this process, ISO 50001, applicable SEEC requirements, MCIS sustainability toolkit requirements for growth projects, operational controls, monitoring arrangements, reporting obligations, and recordkeeping requirements.

clauses.heading: Energy Management Framework
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall periodically review energy performance, including progress against objectives, targets, action plans, regulatory obligations, and improvement opportunities.

processes.keywords: Energy Management; energy management; Governance, Roles, and Accountability; Energy Management Framework
processes.trigger: if significant energy is consumed, generated, recovered or optimized

processes.title: Biodiversity Management
processes.purpose: Biodiversity and ecosystem service dependencies, impacts, risks and opportunities are identified, assessed and managed throughout the asset lifecycle to prevent or minimize adverse impacts on biodiversity, support ecosystem restoration, realize biodiversity commitments, and achieve agreed biodiversity objectives.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden controlled activities, projects and operations that may affect biodiversity, ecosystems or ecosystem services throughout relevant lifecycle stages, from exploration and design through operation, rehabilitation, closure and post-closure. It also applies to contractors and other value chain parties where Maaden has control or material influence over the relevant biodiversity risks or outcomes.

clauses.heading: Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Maaden shall establish corporate biodiversity governance arrangements defining accountability for biodiversity strategy and biodiversity performance across Maaden Business Units and Corporate Functions.

clauses.heading: Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assign competent personnel and integrate biodiversity risks, opportunities, objectives and controls into business and asset planning and decision making.

clauses.heading: Biodiversity Obligations and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify applicable biodiversity related legal requirements, regulatory requirements, approvals and agreed commitments, and incorporate the resulting obligations and actions into applicable plans and controls.

clauses.heading: Biodiversity Baseline Development and LEAP (Locate, Evaluate, Assess and Prepare) Approach
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall apply the Locate, Evaluate, Assess and Prepare phases to identify biodiversity sensitive locations, evaluate dependencies, assess impacts and risks, and establish actions required to achieve defined biodiversity outcomes.

clauses.heading: Locate
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify relevant national and regional biodiversity plans, legally protected areas and recognized conservation priorities and consider them in project siting, mine planning and design.

clauses.heading: Locate
clauses.text: Maaden shall not conduct exploration or mining within properties inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and manage potential impacts on legally protected areas and other recognized biodiversity sensitive areas affected by their activities.

clauses.heading: Locate
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain biodiversity baselines where biodiversity values, dependencies, impacts or risks could be material. Baselines shall be developed or validated by competent personnel and shall establish measurable reference conditions for evaluating biodiversity losses, gains, rehabilitation and restoration outcomes, and biodiversity objectives.

clauses.heading: Locate
clauses.text: Biodiversity baselines shall include, habitat inventory, flora and fauna inventory, protected species, threatened species, critical habitats, ecosystem services, invasive species, habitat condition protected areas, and community biodiversity values, where applicable.

clauses.heading: Locate
clauses.text: Business Units shall identify and spatially record priority biodiversity locations using Maaden approved geographic information systems or equivalent controlled mapping systems. Priority locations shall include, where applicable, protected areas, key biodiversity areas, critical habitats, biodiversity sensitive ecosystems, biodiversity sensitive catchments, restoration priority areas and areas of biodiversity importance to affected communities.

clauses.heading: Locate
clauses.text: Biodiversity baselines and priority location information shall be reviewed at intervals defined in the applicable Biodiversity Action Plan or monitoring program and when material changes to activities, environmental conditions, available knowledge or applicable obligations occur.

clauses.heading: Evaluate
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify biodiversity and ecosystem service dependencies associated with operations and relevant activities.

clauses.heading: Evaluate
clauses.text: Dependency assessments shall consider water availability, groundwater recharge, climate changes, soil stability and erosion control, closure performance and nature Impacts.

clauses.heading: Assess
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and assess direct, indirect and cumulative biodiversity impacts, including, where applicable, habitat loss, degradation and fragmentation, vegetation clearing, species disturbance, invasive alien species, hydrological alteration and pollution.

clauses.heading: Assess
clauses.text: Assessment outputs shall be incorporated into biodiversity management planning and action plans. Material biodiversity risks shall be managed and escalated in accordance with the section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Prepare
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and implement a Biodiversity Action Plan where significant biodiversity values or sensitive receptors are present, material biodiversity impacts or risks are identified, or an applicable obligation or commitment requires coordinated biodiversity action.

clauses.heading: Prepare
clauses.text: Biodiversity Action Plans shall define, as applicable, relevant baseline and reference conditions; significant biodiversity values and priority risks; applicable obligations and stakeholder commitments; avoidance, minimization, rehabilitation, restoration and offset actions; No Net Loss and Net Gain objectives where required or formally adopted; measurable indicators and success criteria; monitoring and reporting requirements; milestones, responsibilities and resources; and review and adaptive-management arrangements.

clauses.heading: Prepare
clauses.text: Where activities could affect critical habitat, applicable Business Units shall establish specific avoidance, protection and mitigation measures and measurable outcomes for the affected critical biodiversity values.

clauses.heading: Prepare
clauses.text: Where an approved project or expansion is permitted to affect critical habitat, the applicable Business Unit shall establish and monitor measurable Net Gain objectives for the affected critical biodiversity values.

clauses.heading: Prepare
clauses.text: Where No Net Loss, Net Gain or offset outcomes are required or claimed, the applicable Business Unit shall use a documented methodology to quantify and verify biodiversity losses, gains and progress against defined objectives.

clauses.heading: Mitigation Hierarchy and Operational Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall apply the biodiversity mitigation hierarchy by avoiding impacts, minimizing unavoidable impacts, restoring affected biodiversity and considering offsets only for significant residual impacts after the preceding measures have been evaluated.

clauses.heading: Mitigation Hierarchy and Operational Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish controls for land disturbance, vegetation clearing, wildlife interactions, invasive species, habitat protection, erosion and sediment, and topsoil conservation, including limiting disturbance to approved boundaries.

clauses.heading: Restoration, Rehabilitation and Biodiversity Outcomes
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall integrate biodiversity rehabilitation and restoration into project design, development, operation and closure planning and implement progressive rehabilitation where practicable.

clauses.heading: Restoration, Rehabilitation and Biodiversity Outcomes
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish measurable rehabilitation and restoration criteria linked to biodiversity and closure objectives and monitor effectiveness against applicable baseline or reference conditions.

clauses.heading: Restoration, Rehabilitation and Biodiversity Outcomes
clauses.text: New projects and expansions shall establish and implement measures to achieve No Net Loss of significant biodiversity values by closure.

clauses.heading: Restoration, Rehabilitation and Biodiversity Outcomes
clauses.text: Existing operations with material biodiversity impacts shall establish measurable pathways toward No Net Loss where required by applicable obligations or formally adopted Maaden biodiversity objectives.

clauses.heading: Biodiversity Monitoring, Reporting and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall implement biodiversity monitoring programs using indicators relevant to identified biodiversity values, impacts and objectives. Indicators shall be quantitative where practicable and may include habitat disturbance and restoration, rehabilitation success, species abundance and distribution, invasive species occurrence, ecosystem condition and water-related biodiversity indicators.

clauses.heading: Biodiversity Monitoring, Reporting and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall evaluate biodiversity performance and control effectiveness against baseline conditions, defined objectives and success criteria, and use the results to support adaptive management.

clauses.heading: Biodiversity Monitoring, Reporting and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall manage biodiversity incidents, failures, significant deviations and corrective actions in accordance with the section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship process, and escalate material biodiversity issues through applicable management and risk processes.

clauses.heading: Biodiversity Monitoring, Reporting and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain verifiable evidence supporting material biodiversity performance claims and applicable regulatory and sustainability reporting, including Taskforce for Nature Related Financial Disclosures (TNFD) aligned disclosures where adopted by Maaden.

processes.trigger: if land disturbance, water use or other activity may affect biodiversity or ecosystem services

processes.title: Tailings Management
processes.purpose: Tailings storage facilities and associated systems are governed under accountable leadership and are designed, constructed, operated, monitored, modified, closed and managed post-closure throughout their lifecycle to prevent or control credible failure modes, maintain facility integrity and critical controls, protect workers, communities, infrastructure and the environment, and comply with applicable legal, regulatory and approved Maaden requirements.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Units responsible for tailings storage facilities or associated systems throughout their lifecycle, from concept and site selection through design, construction, commissioning, operation, modification, care and maintenance, closure and post-closure. It covers engineered facilities used to contain tailings or mineral-processing residues, including tailings dams, red mud storage facilities, gypsum stack facilities and associated water management, seepage control, diversion, monitoring and containment systems.

clauses.heading: Tailings Management Framework and Application
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish, implement and maintain a performance-based Tailings Management System for each applicable facility in accordance with this process, applicable GISTM requirements, the approved Maaden Corporate Tailings Management Standard (CTMS), and applicable legal, regulatory and permit requirements.

clauses.heading: Tailings Management Framework and Application
clauses.text: Corporate Sustainability shall maintain the CTMS and Maaden’s corporate tailings governance framework and oversee implementation and conformance. Material tailings risks and performance shall be reported through approved governance channels.

clauses.heading: Tailings Management Framework and Application
clauses.text: Critical decisions affecting tailings facility design, construction, operation, expansion, monitoring, risk reduction, closure or post-closure performance shall be supported by documented risk-based decision-making processes consistent with the CTMS and applicable GISTM requirements.

clauses.heading: Tailings Management Framework and Application
clauses.text: The CTMS shall define detailed applicability, roles, competency criteria, technical and operating requirements, review frequencies, mandatory deliverables, conformance evidence and disclosure requirements.

clauses.heading: Tailings Management Framework and Application
clauses.text: Tailings management shall be integrated with applicable MSHEM processes and the Maaden Capital Investment System (MCIS). Capital projects shall apply CTMS requirements from concept and option selection through design, construction, commissioning and handover to operations.

clauses.heading: Management and Governance
clauses.text: Maaden shall maintain a Board approved and publicly available commitment to safe tailings management, emergency preparedness and response, and recovery following failure, consistent with GISTM.

clauses.heading: Management and Governance
clauses.text: An Accountable Executive (AE) shall be designated for each Business Unit with accountability for tailings facility safety, environmental and social performance.

clauses.heading: Management and Governance
clauses.text: Business Units shall appoint a site-specific Responsible Tailings Facility Engineer. The Engineer of Record and Independent Tailings Review Board or senior independent technical reviewer shall also be appointed as required by GISTM and the CTMS and subject to Accountable Executive approval.

clauses.heading: Management and Governance
clauses.text: The Engineer of Record shall be empowered through a written agreement defining the role’s authority and responsibilities and Maaden’s obligations to support its effective performance. Procurement may inform but shall not determine the Engineer of Record selection.

clauses.heading: Management and Governance
clauses.text: Personnel performing tailings safety critical roles shall have defined authority, appropriate competency, sufficient time and resources, independence where required, and succession arrangements.

clauses.heading: Management and Governance
clauses.text: Relevant performance objectives, performance reviews and incentive arrangements shall incorporate public safety and tailings facility integrity. They shall not be compromised by production, schedule, cost or procurement considerations.

clauses.heading: Management and Governance
clauses.text: Tailings facilities and associated systems shall be subject to layered assurance comprising Business Unit and site verification, Corporate assurance and competent independent technical review. Assurance shall include Engineer of Record reviews, Dam Safety Reviews and Independent Tailings Review Board or senior independent technical review, as applicable, at frequencies defined by GISTM and the CTMS.

clauses.heading: Management and Governance
clauses.text: Business Units shall conduct documented assessments of conformance with GISTM, the CTMS and this process. Corporate Sustainability shall arrange independent validation where required. Findings and corrective actions shall be risk-ranked, tracked to closure and verified for effectiveness, with material issues reported through appropriate governance channels.

clauses.heading: Management and Governance
clauses.text: Business Units shall promote early problem recognition, cross-functional collaboration and learning. Workers’ experience-based knowledge and lessons from incidents, non-conformances, reviews, exercises and relevant external events shall be incorporated into planning, design, operations and the TMS. Personnel shall be trained for their responsibilities.

clauses.heading: Management and Governance
clauses.text: The Accountable Executive shall ensure that a formal, confidential and documented process is maintained to receive, investigate and promptly address tailings-related concerns from employees and contractors. People reporting concerns in good faith shall be protected from retaliation.

clauses.heading: Management and Governance
clauses.text: Tailings information and records shall be controlled, retained and accessible throughout the facility lifecycle and post-closure period in accordance with the CTMS and Maaden information-management requirements. Knowledge continuity shall be maintained during organizational changes, changes of Engineer of Record and transfers of ownership or responsibility.

clauses.heading: Integrated Knowledge Base
clauses.text: Each applicable facility shall maintain an interdisciplinary knowledge base covering its technical, environmental, social, human-rights and local economic context. The knowledge base shall include site and material characterization, downstream conditions, climate change and material uncertainties and shall be updated at GISTM and CTMS defined intervals and following material changes.

clauses.heading: Integrated Knowledge Base
clauses.text: Credible failure scenarios shall be supported by documented breach and inundation analyses and assessments of potential human exposure, vulnerability and downstream impacts. These assessments shall be updated following material changes to the facility, its surroundings or the knowledge base.

clauses.heading: Integrated Knowledge Base
clauses.text: Consequence assessments shall consider potential impacts on people, the environment, infrastructure, communities and business continuity and be updated following changes to facility conditions or consequence exposure.

clauses.heading: Integrated Knowledge Base
clauses.text: New facilities shall be supported by documented multi-criteria alternatives and impact assessments. The assessments shall use the knowledge base to select sites, technologies and management strategies that minimize lifecycle risks to people and the environment and minimize the volume of tailings and water placed in external tailings facilities. Impact mitigation shall follow the mitigation hierarchy and consider climate change and safe closure.

clauses.heading: Integrated Knowledge Base
clauses.text: Existing facilities and expansions shall periodically review opportunities to improve tailings technologies, designs and management strategies. Impact assessments shall be updated following material changes.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Business Units shall maintain an inventory of applicable facilities and associated systems and their current consequence classifications. Classifications shall be determined in accordance with GISTM and the CTMS and reviewed following material changes and at CTMS-defined intervals.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Business Units shall maintain multidisciplinary lifecycle risk assessments using FMEA to identify credible failure modes, consequences, uncertainties, control dependencies and required risk-reduction measures under normal, abnormal and extreme conditions, including care and maintenance, closure and post-closure. The assessments shall be reviewed at intervals defined by the CTMS and following material changes.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Risks shall be reduced to ALARP and managed in accordance with section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management and as defined in CTMS.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: For High, Very High and Extreme consequence facilities, the Accountable Executive shall confirm and document that applicable risks have been reduced to ALARP. Reasonable measures to further reduce potential consequences shall be identified and implemented as required by GISTM and the CTMS.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Critical controls associated with catastrophic or other material unwanted events shall be managed in accordance with section 2.6 Critical Control Management process. Their performance requirements shall be defined, monitored and verified, and failures or material deterioration shall be promptly escalated and addressed.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Tailings facilities and associated systems shall be designed by competent people using robust design criteria appropriate to the consequence classification, credible failure modes and all lifecycle stages.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: The Engineer of Record shall prepare and maintain a controlled Design Basis Report. The report shall address the knowledge base, site conditions, geotechnical, hydrogeological, seismic, climate and water-management considerations, operating constraints, staged construction, and closure and post-closure requirements. It shall be reviewed by the Independent Tailings Review Board or senior independent technical reviewer, as required by GISTM and the CTMS.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Where an existing facility cannot meet an applicable GISTM or CTMS design or upgrade requirement, the Engineer of Record shall document the basis. The Independent Tailings Review Board or senior independent technical reviewer shall review the determination.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: The Accountable Executive shall approve measures and timeframes for reducing both the probability and consequences of failure to ALARP.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Construction and commissioning shall comply with approved designs and the CTMS. Appropriate Quality Control, Construction Quality Assurance and Construction versus Design Intent Verification shall be implemented, and controlled construction and as-built records shall be maintained. A facility or construction stage shall not be placed into service until design conformance and readiness for safe operation have been verified and approved.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Each facility shall be operated, maintained and surveilled within its design intent and approved operating limits under a current Operations, Maintenance and Surveillance Manual. Controls shall address, as applicable, tailings deposition, storage capacity, water balance and water management, seepage, containment and prevention of overtopping or uncontrolled releases.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Monitoring and surveillance programs shall be implemented, aligned with facility risks, consequence classification and identified credible failure modes. The Integrated, risk-based monitoring and surveillance shall verify design assumptions, consequence classification, identified credible failure modes, operating controls, critical controls and environmental and social performance.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Monitoring data shall be evaluated for trends and deterioration against defined performance criteria. Trigger Action Response Plans shall be used to manage exceedances and abnormal conditions. Monitoring results shall be reviewed and approved as required by the CTMS.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Changes that could affect facility integrity or risk shall be managed through the Management of Change process and the CTMS. This includes changes to design, construction, operating parameters, deposition, water management, monitoring, closure arrangements or organization. Reviews shall consider cumulative effects and require corresponding updates to risk assessments, designs and facility documentation.

clauses.heading: Design, Construction, Operation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Tailings Storage Facilities and associated structure closure plans and cost estimates shall be integrated into overall mine closure planning and address progressive closure, long-term stability, environmental and social objectives, post-mining land use, performance criteria, monitoring, maintenance and assigned responsibilities.

clauses.heading: Emergency Response and Long-Term Recovery
clauses.text:
Each applicable facility shall maintain a site-specific Emergency Preparedness and Response Plan based on credible failure scenarios, breach analysis and potential consequences. The plan shall be in accordance with section
5.1 Emergency Response Preparedness and Planning process.

clauses.heading: Emergency Response and Long-Term Recovery
clauses.text: Emergency arrangements shall be developed, communicated, resourced, tested and updated with relevant workers, contractors, project-affected people, authorities and emergency services in accordance with the CTMS. External emergency-response capabilities and gaps shall be assessed, and community-focused preparedness measures shall be established.

clauses.heading: Emergency Response and Long-Term Recovery
clauses.text: Arrangements shall address immediate life-saving and environmental response following catastrophic failure. They shall also address medium- and long-term reconstruction, restoration and recovery.

clauses.heading: Affected Communities
clauses.text: Business Units shall respect human rights and conduct human-rights due diligence in accordance with the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights. The due diligence shall inform tailings decisions and address risks arising from credible failure scenarios.

clauses.heading: Affected Communities
clauses.text: Project-affected people shall be meaningfully engaged throughout the facility lifecycle, including in developing the knowledge base and making decisions affecting public safety or tailings facility integrity.

clauses.heading: Affected Communities
clauses.text: Effective grievance and remedy mechanisms shall be maintained for project-affected people. Where applicable, Free, Prior and Informed Consent requirements affecting indigenous or tribal peoples and internationally recognized involuntary-resettlement requirements shall be applied in accordance with GISTM, the CTMS and relevant Maaden processes.

clauses.heading: Public Disclosure and Access to Information
clauses.text: Public and regulatory disclosures and responses to requests for tailings information shall be complete, accurate, timely and authorized in accordance with GISTM, the CTMS, applicable legal and permit requirements and Maaden disclosure requirements. Where a request for information is denied, the reason shall be communicated to the requesting party, subject to applicable legal, security and confidentiality restrictions.

processes.title: Closure and Land Rehabilitation
processes.purpose: Maaden mines and assets are planned, operated, rehabilitated, closed, monitored and relinquished in a manner that protects human health and the environment, fulfils legal and regulatory obligations, supports community transition, maintains financial assurance, achieves the agreed post-closure land use, and leaves sites safe, stable and non-polluting.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Maaden Business Units and relevant Corporate Functions and covers closure, rehabilitation and asset retirement obligations for mines, plants, infrastructure, mineral waste facilities, other assets and disturbed land throughout their lifecycle, from exploration and project development through operation, decommissioning, closure, post- closure monitoring and relinquishment.

clauses.heading: Closure Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish closure governance with defined accountability and multidisciplinary involvement for closure planning, implementation, monitoring and relinquishment.

clauses.heading: Closure Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Business Units shall integrate closure requirements, risks, costs and activities into Life of Asset planning, operational planning, investment plans and other relevant business decisions.

clauses.heading: Closure Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Business Units shall provide the technical capability, personnel and financial resources necessary to fulfil applicable closure, rehabilitation, post-closure and relinquishment obligations.

clauses.heading: Closure Planning and Life of Mine Integration
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish a Mine Closure Plan for each applicable operation during project development, maintain it throughout the Life of Mine, and use the Maaden Closure Planning Toolbox to support closure planning, closure criteria development, progressive closure, closure execution planning, costing, closure assurance and continual improvement.

clauses.heading: Closure Planning and Life of Mine Integration
clauses.text: Mine Closure Plans shall be integrated with mine and asset design, operational planning, mineral waste management, water management, biodiversity management and social performance planning, and shall address progressive closure, temporary closure, unplanned closure, final closure and post-closure requirements.

clauses.heading: Closure Planning and Life of Mine Integration
clauses.text: Business Units shall review and update Mine Closure Plans following material operational, regulatory, environmental, social, financial or closure-risk changes that may affect closure outcomes, liabilities, post-closure land use or closure assumptions.

clauses.heading: Closure Knowledge Base and Studies
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish and maintain the environmental, social, operational, technical, financial and regulatory information, and undertake and maintain the technical studies, necessary to support closure planning, decision- making, closure feasibility and the achievement of closure objectives. Studies shall be reviewed and updated when new information, operational changes or closure performance may affect their outcomes.

clauses.heading: Closure Knowledge Base and Studies
clauses.text: Business Units shall identify, assess and manage material knowledge gaps and uncertainties that may affect closure risks, costs, objectives, post-closure land use or outcomes.

clauses.heading: Closure Vision, Objectives and Post-Closure Land Use
clauses.text: Business Units shall document and maintain the closure vision, closure objectives and intended post-closure land use for each applicable operation or asset, considering applicable legal and regulatory obligations, Maaden commitments and relevant stakeholder input.

clauses.heading: Closure Vision, Objectives and Post-Closure Land Use
clauses.text: Closure objectives shall define the environmental, social, community-transition, safety and financial outcomes to be achieved through closure and post-closure.

clauses.heading: Closure Vision, Objectives and Post-Closure Land Use
clauses.text: Business Units shall demonstrate that the intended post-closure land use is legally permissible, technically feasible, environmentally sustainable and compatible with relevant stakeholder and regional land-use considerations.

clauses.heading: Closure Vision, Objectives and Post-Closure Land Use
clauses.text: Business Units shall document the implications of material changes to the intended post-closure land use and update the Mine Closure Plan, closure objectives and closure cost estimate, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Risk and Opportunity Management
clauses.text: Business Units shall identify, assess, record and manage closure related risks and opportunities throughout the asset lifecycle in accordance with Section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management, considering safety, environmental, social, legal and regulatory, financial and reputational consequences, including climate change, cumulative impacts and long-term residual risks.

clauses.heading: Risk and Opportunity Management
clauses.text: Closure risk assessment outcomes shall determine the prioritization of closure actions, rehabilitation activities, technical studies and resources, and the measures included in closure plans to manage material long-term and residual risks.

clauses.heading: Closure Design and Rehabilitation Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units shall ensure that closure and rehabilitation designs achieve long-term physical and chemical stability, protect human health and the environment, and support the intended post-closure land use and closure success criteria.

clauses.heading: Closure Design and Rehabilitation Requirements
clauses.text: Closure and rehabilitation designs shall address applicable mine features, mineral waste facilities, processing facilities, contaminated areas, water management infrastructure and associated infrastructure.

clauses.heading: Closure Design and Rehabilitation Requirements
clauses.text: Closure and rehabilitation designs shall assess and manage material long-term risks, including acid rock drainage, metal leaching, contaminant migration, surface water, groundwater and other sources of long-term pollution, where applicable.

clauses.heading: Progressive Closure
clauses.text: Business Units shall identify, plan and implement progressive closure opportunities throughout operations and integrate them into Life of Mine plans and operational schedules.

clauses.heading: Progressive Closure
clauses.text: Business Units shall select and prioritize progressive closure activities based on their contribution to risk reduction, closure objectives, post-closure land use, value creation and reduction of closure costs and liabilities.

clauses.heading: Progressive Closure
clauses.text: The funding approach for progressive closure activities shall be determined with consideration of the expected reduction in closure liabilities, closure costs and financial assurance requirements.

clauses.heading: Progressive Closure
clauses.text: Business Units shall monitor progressive closure performance and evaluate its effect on closure outcomes, costs, liabilities and financial assurance requirements, where applicable.

clauses.heading: Social Transition and Stakeholder Engagement
clauses.text: Business Units shall identify stakeholders affected by closure and engage them during relevant stages of closure planning and execution. Relevant stakeholder input shall be documented and considered in closure planning and decision-making.

clauses.heading: Social Transition and Stakeholder Engagement
clauses.text: Business Units shall assess material social transition impacts, risks and opportunities associated with closure, including those relating to the workforce, affected communities, local economies and cultural heritage, where applicable.

clauses.heading: Social Transition and Stakeholder Engagement
clauses.text: Closure plans shall define measures to manage identified material social transition risks and impacts and to support beneficial transition opportunities, where practicable.

clauses.heading: Closure Costing and Financial Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units shall maintain lifecycle closure cost estimates, developed using the support from Maaden Closure Planning Toolbox, covering all material closure obligations, including decommissioning, rehabilitation, post-closure monitoring and maintenance, social transition and residual risk management, where applicable.

clauses.heading: Closure Costing and Financial Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units shall maintain and periodically reassess financial provisions and any required financial assurance to cover closure liabilities in accordance with applicable legal, regulatory, permit and corporate requirements.

clauses.heading: Closure Execution Planning
clauses.text: Before final closure activities commence, Business Units shall establish and maintain a Closure Execution Plan defining the scope, schedule, resources, monitoring and completion requirements, and take necessary approvals.

clauses.heading: Closure Execution Planning
clauses.text: Business Units shall manage closure execution through established project management processes.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Success Criteria and Adaptive Management
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish measurable success criteria linked to closure objectives, activities and the agreed post-closure land use, covering applicable physical, environmental, social and safety outcomes.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Success Criteria and Adaptive Management
clauses.text: Business Units shall monitor and evaluate closure implementation and performance against applicable obligations and success criteria at frequencies determined by legal, regulatory, permit and corporate requirements.

clauses.heading: Monitoring, Success Criteria and Adaptive Management
clauses.text: Business Units shall use monitoring and evaluation results to address performance deviations, implement corrective actions and update closure plans, controls and monitoring programs where required.

clauses.heading: Temporary or Sudden Closure
clauses.text: Business Units shall identify credible temporary suspension and unplanned closure scenarios and incorporate associated preparedness, response, care and maintenance, and cost requirements into closure plans and closure cost estimates.

clauses.heading: Temporary or Sudden Closure
clauses.text: During temporary suspension or transition to unplanned closure, Business Units shall implement care and maintenance arrangements that protect human health and safety, maintain environmental and regulatory compliance, manage security and asset-integrity risks, and support either the safe resumption of operations or progression to final closure.

clauses.heading: Decommissioning, Dismantling and Asset Retirement
clauses.text: Business Units shall identify assets requiring retirement, decommissioning, dismantling, decontamination, remediation or rehabilitation and integrate the applicable requirements and costs into closure plans.

clauses.heading: Decommissioning, Dismantling and Asset Retirement
clauses.text: Business Units shall ensure that retired assets and affected areas are safe, physically and chemically stable, non- polluting and compatible with the agreed post-closure land use and completion criteria, with technically feasible and legally permitted opportunities to reuse, repurpose, recycle or recover assets and materials evaluated before disposal.

clauses.heading: Relinquishment and Liability Transfer
clauses.text: Business Units shall identify, document and maintain the applicable requirements and pathway for closure certification, relinquishment and any associated liability transfer.

clauses.heading: Relinquishment and Liability Transfer
clauses.text: Relinquishment or liability transfer shall not be completed until the Business Unit has demonstrated achievement of applicable closure success criteria, obtained all required legal and regulatory approvals, and retained evidence supporting certification, relinquishment and liability transfer.

processes.title: Occupational Health Risk Assessment and Industrial Hygiene Management
processes.purpose: Identify, assess and prioritize occupational health hazards and exposures throughout the asset lifecycle, establishing a reliable basis for selecting and verifying controls, and uses exposure and health information to prevent occupational illness.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Units, Corporate Functions and controlled workplaces, including employees, contractor personnel and others who may be exposed to occupational health hazards during routine, non-routine, abnormal or foreseeable emergency work throughout the asset lifecycle.

clauses.heading: Governance, Accountability and Competence
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain occupational health risk assessment and industrial hygiene arrangements commensurate with occupational health hazards and exposures arising from their activities, including provision of the resources, information, access and personnel required to implement them.

clauses.heading: Governance, Accountability and Competence
clauses.text: Line management shall ensure occupational health risks, controls and required actions are managed and escalated in accordance with the EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Governance, Accountability and Competence
clauses.text: Personnel conducting or reviewing occupational health risk or exposure assessments shall be competent for the assessment scope. Workers, contractor representatives and other personnel knowledgeable about the work shall participate where relevant.

clauses.heading: Hazard Identification and Exposure Profiling
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify chemical, physical, biological, ergonomic and psychosocial or work organization hazards; their sources; affected areas; exposed people; exposure routes; and potential acute, chronic or long-latency health effects under routine, non-routine, abnormal and foreseeable emergency conditions.

clauses.heading: Hazard Identification and Exposure Profiling
clauses.text: Similar Exposure Groups (SEGs) shall be established and maintained for workers with comparable exposure profiles, with the grouping basis, material changes, relevant Safety Data Sheets and process specific exposure information documented.

clauses.heading: Hazard Identification and Exposure Profiling
clauses.text: Occupational health profiles and assessments shall be completed before commissioning new or modified facilities, equipment or processes; reviewed at intervals not exceeding five years; and revalidated following change, new hazards or information, abnormal results, control failure, occupational illness or health incidents, or substantiated worker concerns.

clauses.heading: Hazard Identification and Exposure Profiling
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall register and assess workplace agents classified by the current International Agency for Research on Cancer Monographs as Group 1, 2A or 2B. Diesel particulate matter shall be treated as a carcinogenic airborne contaminant in underground mining. Exposure shall be eliminated where reasonably practicable and otherwise minimized in accordance with Airborne Contaminants and Chemical Exposure Control.

clauses.heading: Occupational Health Risk and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain baseline occupational health hazard and exposure profiles for applicable activities and Similar Exposure Groups and complete targeted assessments where exposure is material or uncertain, results are abnormal, or required controls are absent, degraded or failed.

clauses.heading: Occupational Health Risk and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Assessments shall evaluate exposure characteristics, health consequences, inherent and residual risk, control effectiveness and uncertainty using Maaden EHSS Risk Management Process. Hazards capable of fatal, irreversible or disabling harm shall be evaluated for inclusion in Critical Control Management.

clauses.heading: Occupational Health Risk and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall implement and maintain a risk based exposure assessment strategy that defines assessment priorities, methodologies, assessment criteria, data quality requirements and response actions.

clauses.heading: Occupational Health Risk and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Qualitative assessments shall characterize potential exposure, identify uncertainty and information gaps, determine interim controls and establish priorities for quantitative monitoring.

clauses.heading: Occupational Health Risk and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Quantitative monitoring shall be conducted when required by law, an applicable MSHEM process, assessment uncertainty, abnormal results or trends, or control-verification needs

clauses.heading: Occupational Health Risk and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Exposure sampling shall represent relevant workers, tasks and operating conditions. Combined exposures, extended work schedules and incomplete sampling coverage shall be evaluated where relevant, and associated uncertainty shall be documented.

clauses.heading: Occupational Health Risk and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Assessment results shall inform Similar Exposure Groups, monitoring and control plans, competency and training, health surveillance, emergency preparedness, design and change-management decisions.

clauses.heading: Exposure Criteria and Assessment Quality
clauses.text: Occupational exposure assessments shall apply the ACGIH Threshold Limit Values (TLVs) and Biological Exposure Indices (BEIs).

clauses.heading: Exposure Criteria and Assessment Quality
clauses.text: Occupational health assessments shall identify credible acute exposure and oxygen displacement scenarios requiring detection, alarms or emergency response and shall provide relevant emergency response requirements to the applicable Emergency Preparedness and Response process.

clauses.heading: Exposure Criteria and Assessment Quality
clauses.text: Occupational health assessments shall identify hazards and Similar Exposure Groups requiring referral to Medical Services and Health Surveillance. Health surveillance and biological monitoring shall reflect the hazard, exposure route, exposure profile and applicable requirements and shall not replace hazard prevention or exposure controls. Relevant exposure information shall be made available to Medical Services as required for health surveillance. Aggregated health-surveillance findings shall be used to review occupational health risks and control effectiveness while maintaining medical confidentiality.

clauses.heading: Exposure Criteria and Assessment Quality
clauses.text: Affected workers shall receive understandable information on occupational health hazards, exposure results, associated health significance, required controls and actions following control failure, in a manner that addresses applicable language, literacy and accessibility needs and protects personal and medical information.

clauses.heading: Contractors, Projects, Performance and Records
clauses.text: Contractor occupational health requirements shall be managed through Contractor EHSS Management. Where Maaden and contractor personnel share or influence an exposure profile, contractor personnel shall be included in Similar Exposure Groups and exposure assessments, and relevant information and controls shall be maintained.

clauses.heading: Contractors, Projects, Performance and Records
clauses.text: Projects shall apply occupational health criteria, assessments and controls through Projects EHSS Management and transfer outstanding occupational health risks and actions through the applicable handover process.

clauses.heading: Contractors, Projects, Performance and Records
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall review occupational health performance at least annually through EHSS Performance Monitoring, Measurement and Evaluation, considering exposure trends, aggregated health findings, occupational illnesses, control effectiveness and outstanding actions. Exposure exceedances, occupational illnesses and material control failures shall be reported through Incident Management and Stewardship when the applicable criteria are met.

clauses.heading: Contractors, Projects, Performance and Records
clauses.text: Occupational health assessment, exposure monitoring and control verification records shall be retained for the life of the facility and for any longer period required by Maaden or applicable law to enable reconstruction of long-latency exposure histories. Exposure records shall be maintained separately from confidential medical records, with access, disclosure and disposal controlled to protect personal and medical information.
