processes.title: Airborne Contaminants and Chemical Exposure Control
processes.purpose: Prevent occupational illness and acute harm arising from airborne contaminants and hazardous chemicals by assessing exposures, applying effective controls and responding to exceedances or control failures.
processes.scope: This process applies where employees, contractors or other people may be exposed to airborne contaminants or hazardous chemicals by inhalation, skin or eye contact, ingestion or injection during routine, non-routine, abnormal or emergency conditions.

clauses.heading: Exposure Hazard Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify airborne contaminant and chemical exposure hazards arising from materials, processes, equipment, tasks and workplace conditions, considering all credible exposure routes and relevant normal, abnormal, non-routine, maintenance, upset and foreseeable emergency conditions.

clauses.heading: Exposure Hazard Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Before disturbing materials, deposits or residues of unknown composition, Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify or sample the material and apply precautionary controls until its hazards and required controls are established under sections 3.12 Occupational Health Risk Assessment and Industrial Hygiene Management and 3.20 Hazardous Materials Management.

clauses.heading: Exposure Hazard Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Hazard identification, Similar Exposure Group determination, exposure assessment, monitoring and control verification shall comply with Process 3.12. Airborne contaminant sampling and analysis shall be performed using validated methods, calibrated equipment and competent laboratories, consistent with applicable requirements of ISO 7708, ISO 13137, ISO 15767, relevant parts of ISO 16000 and the NIOSH Manual of Analytical Methods.

clauses.heading: Exposure Hazard Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall evaluate airborne contaminant exposures and establish control and response actions against the applicable exposure criteria determined through the section 3.12 Occupational Health Risk Assessment and Industrial Hygiene Management process.

clauses.heading: Exposure Hazard Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Exposure evaluations shall apply relevant time-weighted average, short-term exposure and ceiling limits, together with applicable skin, sensitizer and biological exposure criteria, and account for extended shifts and combined exposures. The airborne exposure action level is 50% of the applicable occupational exposure limit. Exposure at or above the action level shall trigger reassessment, representative monitoring, implementation or improvement of controls, and verification of control effectiveness. Biological monitoring shall apply the relevant BEI, determinant, sampling time and background notation.

clauses.heading: Exposure Hazard Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Affected people shall be withdrawn or their exposure stopped where an applicable OEL, short-term exposure limit, ceiling limit or withdrawal criterion is exceeded or likely to be exceeded, with affected work resumed only after controls are implemented and verified as effective and confirmed exceedances reported and investigated in accordance with Process 6.1 Incident Management.

clauses.heading: Exposure Prevention and Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall apply the hierarchy of controls to eliminate or minimize contaminant generation, release, spread and exposure through all credible routes, prioritizing elimination, substitution and engineering controls over administrative controls and personal protective equipment.

clauses.heading: Exposure Prevention and Control
clauses.text: Agent specific controls shall be established for serious, irreversible or uncertain health hazards, including carcinogens, mutagens, reproductive toxicants, sensitizers, respirable crystalline silica, asbestos and other fibrous minerals, toxic metals, welding fumes, diesel particulate matter, acid mists and toxic gases. Work affecting asbestos- containing or other regulator controlled material shall not start until required identification, authorization, competent people, isolation, decontamination, waste and clearance arrangements are confirmed.

clauses.heading: Exposure Prevention and Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that required engineering controls, including suppression, extraction and enclosure systems, have defined performance criteria, are operational before exposure generating work begins, and are commissioned, verified, inspected, tested and maintained based on risk and applicable specifications, with work stopped or restricted whenever a required control is absent, ineffective or impaired until equivalent protection is implemented and verified as effective.

clauses.heading: Airborne Contaminant Controls
clauses.text: Dust generated by drilling, blasting, crushing, screening, cutting, grinding, loading, tipping, conveyor transfer, muck piles, stockpiles and haul roads shall be controlled at source using wet methods, extraction, enclosure, isolation, remote operation, reduced drop heights, stabilized surfaces or other effective controls to prevent hazardous loss of visibility, secondary exposure and re-entrainment.

clauses.heading: Airborne Contaminant Controls
clauses.text: Ventilation and local extraction shall have defined airflow and capture criteria, collect contaminants at or near their source and prevent contaminated air from reaching other work areas or air intakes. Contaminated air shall not be recirculated unless contaminant removal, monitoring and failure controls are designed and verified for the hazard.

clauses.heading: Airborne Contaminant Controls
clauses.text: Operator enclosures used for particulate exposure control shall conform to ISO 23875, maintain the required protective performance and be monitored, inspected and maintained. Use for gases or vapors requires specific design and verification, and loss of protective performance requires affected work to stop until equivalent protection is verified as effective.

clauses.heading: Airborne Contaminant Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall control diesel particulate matter exposure using the hierarchy of controls and the ICMM Diesel Particulate Matter Good Practice Guide, prioritizing electric or low-emission equipment, low-sulfur fuel, engine maintenance and exhaust after-treatment, followed by ventilation, filtered enclosures, remote operation and work planning, with respiratory protection used only as a supplementary or interim control. Underground ventilation shall comply with section 3.36 Underground Mines Ventilation, Fire and Refuge Safety.

clauses.heading: Respiratory Protection and Acute Exposure Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall implement a documented respiratory protection program in accordance with Process 3.31 and applicable ISO/TS 16975-1 requirements where respiratory protection is necessary for residual exposure, temporary control impairment, emergency response or specialized work, and not as a substitute for feasible higher-order controls.

clauses.heading: Respiratory Protection and Acute Exposure Controls
clauses.text: Respiratory protective equipment shall be certified and selected for the applicable contaminant, exposure level, oxygen concentration, task, duration and required protection factor. The respiratory protection program shall address medical suitability, training, equipment issue, inspection, cleaning, storage, maintenance and filter or cartridge replacement. Supplied breathing air shall meet at least Grade D breathing-air quality in accordance with ANSI/CGA G-7.1 or an equivalent adopted standard.

clauses.heading: Respiratory Protection and Acute Exposure Controls
clauses.text: Tight-fitting respirators shall be fit-tested in accordance with ISO 16975-3 before initial use, at least every 12 months and following changes that could affect the seal, with wearers completing a seal check before each use and remaining free from facial hair or other equipment that interferes with the seal.

clauses.heading: Respiratory Protection and Acute Exposure Controls
clauses.text: Respiratory protection areas shall be identified, signposted and access controlled where necessary. Air-purifying respirators shall not be used where oxygen is below 19.5%, the contaminant or concentration is unknown, or the atmosphere is or may become immediately dangerous to life or health (IDLH).

clauses.heading: Respiratory Protection and Acute Exposure Controls
clauses.text: Credible acute exposure scenarios shall have monitoring, alarms, withdrawal, escape, communication and emergency response controls. IDLH entry shall require positive pressure self-contained breathing apparatus or positive pressure supplied air with auxiliary escape.

clauses.heading: Contamination Control and Exposure Response
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall prevent ingestion, skin contact and cross contamination through risk- based hygiene and decontamination arrangements, including changing, washing, laundering, equipment cleaning and contaminated-waste management. Dry sweeping and compressed air shall not be used where they could disperse contamination; wet cleaning or HEPA-filtered vacuum equipment shall be used instead. Eating, drinking, smoking and food storage shall be prohibited in contaminated areas.

clauses.heading: Contamination Control and Exposure Response
clauses.text: Emergency eyewash and shower facilities provided where harmful chemicals could contact the eyes or skin shall comply with ANSI/ISEA Z358.1, be accessible by an unobstructed route within 10 seconds or closer where required, and undergo weekly activation and annual performance testing.

clauses.heading: Contamination Control and Exposure Response
clauses.text: Actual or suspected harmful exposure or failure of a required exposure control shall trigger immediate work controls, decontamination, first aid or medical evaluation, as applicable, and reporting and investigation through Process 6.1 Incident Management.

clauses.heading: Information, Records and Improvement
clauses.text: Affected employees and contractors shall receive understandable information and training covering hazards, exposure routes and criteria, controls, respiratory protection limitations, symptoms, emergency actions and hygiene. Workers shall be consulted during exposure assessment and control review and informed of monitoring conclusions and required actions. Personal exposure information shall be accessible to the individual, and medical information shall remain confidential.

clauses.heading: Information, Records and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain retrievable exposure, monitoring, control verification, exceedance and respiratory protection records for the longest applicable legal, regulatory, permit or Maaden period. As minimum, dust, gas, mist and fume survey records shall be retained for at least 10 years and made available to SAIS when required.

clauses.heading: Information, Records and Improvement
clauses.text: Exposure assessments and controls shall be reviewed, as minimum, following relevant changes, action level or OEL exceedances, control failures, health concerns, new technical information or adverse trends.

clauses.heading: Information, Records and Improvement
clauses.text: Performance monitoring, corrective action and continual improvement shall comply with section 6.2 EHSS Performance Monitoring, Measurement and Evaluation.

processes.trigger: if dust, fumes, vapours, gases, fibres or hazardous chemicals may expose personnel

processes.title: Noise and Hearing Conservation
processes.purpose: Maaden identifies, assess, control and monitor occupational noise exposure to prevent noise induced hearing loss and tinnitus and to maintain personnel ability to communicate and respond to alarms, warnings and operational hazards.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden controlled activities, facilities and work where employees, contractors, visitors or other personnel may be exposed to occupational noise that could damage hearing or interfere with communication, alarms or warnings, including applicable activities, areas, equipment, tasks, routine and non-routine work, and relevant lifecycle stages.

clauses.heading: Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assign accountability and establish a risk-based Noise and Hearing Conservation Program proportionate to its occupational noise exposure profile.

clauses.heading: Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Line management shall implement workplace noise controls, while Industrial Hygiene shall provide technical ownership of noise hazard identification, exposure assessment and control performance verification.

clauses.heading: Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Occupational Health shall manage audiometric surveillance, medical interpretation, confidential follow-up and work- relatedness review through the Medical Services and Health Surveillance process.

clauses.heading: Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Contractor work under Maaden control shall meet the applicable requirements of this process.

clauses.heading: Noise criteria
clauses.text:
Business Units and Corporate Functions shall apply the occupational noise exposure limits and action levels in Table
3.14-1 as minimum Maaden requirements, or lower limits where required by applicable legal, regulatory, permit or authority requirements:
[Table table-55-1.png]

Table 3.14-1. Occupational Noise Exposure Limits and Action levels.

clauses.heading: Noise criteria
clauses.text: Occupational noise exposure shall remain below 100 dBA over 15 minutes and 140 dB linear peak sound pressure level, with exposure at or above the applicable Action Level evaluated and managed through Process 3.12 Industrial Hygiene Management.

clauses.heading: Noise Hazard Identification and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify occupational noise sources, areas, equipment, occupations and tasks and assess representative exposure scenarios for applicable Personnel, Similar Exposure Groups, shifts, operating conditions and routine and non-routine activities through the Occupational Health Risk Assessment and Industrial Hygiene Management processes.

clauses.heading: Noise Hazard Identification and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Exposure assessment shall consider continuous, intermittent, variable and impulsive noise; exposure duration and shift length; representative operating conditions; and combined exposure to noise, ototoxic substances and vibration where interaction is credible.

clauses.heading: Noise Hazard Identification and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Personal noise exposure results shall be evaluated and reported without deducting attenuation provided by hearing protection used by the worker. Exposure characterization, Similar Exposure Group (SEG) classification, and Hearing Conservation Program enrollment shall be based on unprotected noise exposure.

clauses.heading: Noise Hazard Identification and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Exposure shall be reassessed at the interval established by the controlled Industrial Hygiene strategy and following a change, complaint, incident, abnormal surveillance trend or control failure that could materially alter exposure.

clauses.heading: Noise Hazard Identification and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Affected personnel and accountable line management shall be informed of the assessment outcome and the controls applicable to their work.

clauses.heading: Noise Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall eliminate or minimize occupational noise exposure by applying the hierarchy of controls, prioritizing elimination, substitution and engineering controls.

clauses.heading: Noise Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish a documented noise control plan where occupational noise exposure exceeds the applicable exposure limit specified in 3.14.5, required controls are not fully implemented, or existing controls are ineffective.

clauses.heading: Noise Control
clauses.text: The plan shall identify material exposure scenarios, permanent and interim controls, accountable owners, target dates and verification requirements, with interim controls maintained until permanent controls are implemented and verified as effective.

clauses.heading: Noise Control
clauses.text: Noise controls shall be verified under representative operating conditions against defined performance criteria, with failed, degraded, bypassed or ineffective controls reported, risk-assessed and corrected, and unresolved or material failures escalated through the applicable MSHEM process.

clauses.heading: Hearing Conservation Program (HCP) and Noise Hazard Areas
clauses.text: Personnel or Similar Exposure Groups (SEGs) whose occupational noise exposure meets or exceeds the applicable action level specified in 3.14.5, or the applicable 100 dBA or 140 dB peak criterion, shall be enrolled in the Hearing Conservation Program.

clauses.heading: Hearing Conservation Program (HCP) and Noise Hazard Areas
clauses.text: The Hearing Conservation Program shall identify enrolled personnel or exposure groups, designated areas and tasks, exposure information, required controls, hearing protection requirements, occupational health surveillance interfaces, communication requirements and performance measures.

clauses.heading: Hearing Conservation Program (HCP) and Noise Hazard Areas
clauses.text: Areas, equipment and tasks meeting the applicable noise-hazard designation criteria, including those with noise levels of 85 dBA or greater, shall be identified and communicated to affected personnel through applicable warning signs, access controls and hearing-protection requirements.

clauses.heading: Hearing Conservation Program (HCP) and Noise Hazard Areas
clauses.text: Noise area and task designations shall be reviewed and revised when changes to noise exposure, work activities, equipment, controls or applicable criteria could affect the designation.

clauses.heading: Hearing Protection
clauses.text: Hearing protectors shall be selected to maintain protected exposure below the applicable exposure limit, considering measured noise exposure, noise characteristics, device attenuation, compatibility with other personal protective equipment, communication and alarm requirements, task demands and wearer factors.

clauses.heading: Hearing Protection
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall manage hearing protectors through the section 3.31 Personal Protective Equipment process and provide affected personnel with approved, individually suitable devices and instruction on their fitting, inspection, use, care and limitations.

clauses.heading: Hearing Protection
clauses.text: Hearing protectors shall comply with applicable requirements of the SASO Technical Regulation for Personal Protective Equipment and Clothing, have their performance individually verified where required by controlled technical criteria, and be used as dual hearing protection where the 8-hour noise exposure is 110 dBA or greater.

clauses.heading: Hearing Protection
clauses.text: Hearing protection shall be used without replacing feasible and effective higher-order controls, with failed performance verification requiring refitting or replacement, review of exposure controls, and successful reverification before continued reliance on the hearing protector.

clauses.heading: Hearing Protection
clauses.text: Where hearing protection cannot reduce exposure below the applicable exposure limit, additional controls and exposure duration restrictions shall be implemented before work continues.

clauses.heading: Occupational Health Surveillance and Medical Follow-up
clauses.text: Personnel meeting the exposure criteria specified in 3.14.16 or other approved occupational health surveillance criteria shall participate in audiometric surveillance.

clauses.heading: Occupational Health Surveillance and Medical Follow-up
clauses.text: Medical Services and Health Surveillance shall define and maintain requirements for baseline, periodic, job- transfer, exit, repeat and event triggered audiometry, specialist referral, evaluation criteria, follow-up actions and notification timeframes.

clauses.heading: Occupational Health Surveillance and Medical Follow-up
clauses.text: A hearing change meeting approved referral criteria shall trigger Occupational Health review and evaluation of relevant workplace noise exposure, noise controls and hearing protection effectiveness. Suspected work-related hearing conditions meeting the applicable reporting or investigation criteria shall be managed through section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship process.

clauses.heading: Occupational Health Surveillance and Medical Follow-up
clauses.text: Medical information disclosed outside Occupational Health shall be limited to fitness, restrictions, required workplace controls, legally required information and de-identified or aggregated trends.

clauses.heading: Competency, Information and Communication
clauses.text: Personnel conducting, interpreting, approving or supervising occupational noise assessments, exposure controls or hearing protection evaluations shall be competent for their assigned responsibilities.

clauses.heading: Competency, Information and Communication
clauses.text: Personnel exposed to occupational noise shall receive information and training appropriate to their exposure risks, including health effects, workplace noise hazards, required controls, designated noise areas and tasks, hearing protector selection and use, health surveillance, and reporting of concerns or symptoms.

clauses.heading: Competency, Information and Communication
clauses.text: Changes to noise hazards, controls, designated areas or work requirements shall be communicated to affected personnel before work begins under the changed conditions.

clauses.heading: Design, Procurement and Lifecycle Assurance
clauses.text: Projects, procurement activities and changes that could affect occupational noise exposure shall define noise performance criteria, evaluate practicable lower noise options, and require suppliers of noise-significant equipment to provide noise emission data sufficient to verify compliance.

clauses.heading: Design, Procurement and Lifecycle Assurance
clauses.text: Project and commissioning assurance shall verify, under representative operating conditions and before operational acceptance, that specified noise controls and contractual noise performance criteria have been achieved.

clauses.heading: Design, Procurement and Lifecycle Assurance
clauses.text: Changes that could materially affect noise generation, occupational exposure, safety-critical communication, alarms or noise controls shall be managed through section 3.52 Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Performance Review and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall evaluate the effectiveness of the Noise and Hearing Conservation Program at a risk-based frequency, considering exposure results, control verification results, hearing protector performance, aggregated health surveillance trends, incidents, complaints, findings, competency status and overdue actions.

clauses.heading: Performance Review and Improvement
clauses.text: The evaluation shall identify ineffective controls and program arrangements, assign corrective or improvement actions with accountable owners and due dates, and escalate material adverse trends, occupational noise exposure limit exceedances, control failures and overdue risk reduction actions through applicable MSHEM processes.

clauses.heading: Performance Review and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain occupational noise and hearing conservation records in accordance with applicable legal requirements.

processes.title: Thermal Stress and Physical Hazards
processes.purpose: Thermal stress, vibration and workplace illumination exposures shall be identified, assessed and controlled to prevent acute and chronic harm, maintain defined operating limits and verify control effectiveness.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden controlled activities and workplaces where employees, contractors, visitors or other people may be exposed to thermal stress, hand-arm or whole-body vibration, inadequate or disruptive illumination, or other physical agents assigned to this process. It covers thermal stress associated with weather, sunlight, radiant or process heat, cold or refrigerated environments, wet conditions, workload, clothing and PPE.

clauses.heading: Assessment Governance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that physical hazard assessments and monitoring are conducted or technically reviewed by personnel competent in the physical agent and applicable assessment method.

clauses.heading: Assessment Governance
clauses.text: Physical hazard assessments shall comply with applicable legal requirements and technical standards, including ISO 7243 for thermal stress, ISO 5349 for hand-arm vibration, ISO 2631-1 for whole-body vibration and ISO/CIE 8995 for workplace illumination, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Assessment Governance
clauses.text: Instruments used for quantitative assessments shall be suitable for the applicable method, maintained, calibrated or verified at specified intervals, and function checked before use where required.

clauses.heading: Physical Agent Identification and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify physical agent sources, affected people and foreseeable exposure scenarios and assess exposure magnitude, frequency, duration and variability, considering operating and environmental conditions, existing controls, combined exposures and foreseeable higher exposure conditions.

clauses.heading: Physical Agent Identification and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Quantitative monitoring shall be conducted where required by applicable obligations or Maaden adopted criteria, or where qualitative assessment cannot reliably exclude overexposure, using sampling strategies representative of affected people, tasks and operating conditions.

clauses.heading: Physical Agent Identification and Exposure Assessment
clauses.text: Assessment and monitoring results shall be evaluated against applicable exposure limits, action levels and technical criteria, considering exposure variability and measurement uncertainty, and reviewed following material exposure changes, exceedances, control failures, reported symptoms, incidents or occupational illnesses.

clauses.heading: Exposure Control
clauses.text: Physical hazard exposure shall be eliminated where reasonably practicable or otherwise reduced to within applicable exposure criteria using the hierarchy of controls, prioritizing higher order controls over administrative controls and PPE.

clauses.heading: Exposure Control
clauses.text: Where exposure limits or action levels are exceeded, permanent controls are delayed, or exposure may change, documented control and trigger action arrangements shall define interim and permanent controls, monitored conditions, trigger levels, responsibilities, work restrictions, verification requirements and restart criteria.

clauses.heading: Exposure Control
clauses.text: Work shall be stopped or restricted where applicable exposure limits are exceeded, required controls or monitoring are unavailable or ineffective, or changed conditions have not been assessed, and can resume only after the conditions are reassessed and required controls are verified as effective.

clauses.heading: Thermal Stress Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Thermal stress assessments shall consider heat and cold sources, environmental conditions, metabolic workload, exposure duration, clothing and PPE, acclimatization and foreseeable changes in work or environmental conditions.

clauses.heading: Thermal Stress Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Heat stress screening shall use Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) measurements representative of actual workplace conditions and consider workload, clothing, PPE and acclimatization in accordance with ISO 7243 criteria and recognized assessment methods. Weather or forecast data may support planning but shall not replace workplace measurements where local conditions materially affect exposure.

clauses.heading: Thermal Stress Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Thermal controls shall be established and adjusted before and during work based on documented assessments, forecasts, workplace measurements and observed conditions, using, as applicable, source isolation, shielding, ventilation, cooling or heating, workload reduction, scheduling, work-rest arrangements, hydration, recovery facilities, clothing, personal protective equipment, worker observation and emergency arrangements.

clauses.heading: Thermal Stress Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Work rest arrangements shall be based on the thermal exposure assessment under 3.15.11 and include specified rest periods, hygienic potable water and suitable recovery facilities. Direct-sun work shall comply with applicable Saudi requirements, including any authorized exemptions or alternative arrangements.

clauses.heading: Thermal Stress Assessment and Control
clauses.text: New, returning or non-acclimatized personnel shall complete a supervised acclimatization or re-acclimatization process with defined progression, monitoring and completion criteria before full thermal exposure.

clauses.heading: Thermal Stress Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Cold-stress controls shall address wet, refrigerated, cryogenic and adverse weather conditions and foreseeable loss of heating, shelter, protective clothing or other required controls.

clauses.heading: Thermal Stress Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Work shall be stopped or restricted when thermal strain symptoms or defined stop-work conditions occur, with affected personnel removed from exposure and referred for site medical response where heat- or cold-related illness is suspected.

clauses.heading: Thermal Stress Assessment and Control
clauses.text: High risk, lone or remote thermal work shall provide appropriate worker monitoring, reliable communication, emergency access and a means to summon assistance.

clauses.heading: Vibration Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify sources and tasks exposing people to hand-arm (HAV) or whole-body vibration (WBV).

clauses.heading: Vibration Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Vibration exposure assessments shall consider the vibration characteristics, actual exposure duration, operating conditions and all significant sources during the work period, with daily exposure evaluated over an eight-hour reference period, A(8), in accordance with ISO 5349 for HAV and ISO 2631-1 for WBV.

clauses.heading: Vibration Assessment and Control
clauses.text:
A documented vibration control plan shall be implemented where an applicable exposure action value is reached or exceeded, and exposure shall not exceed the applicable exposure limit value. Unless more stringent applicable legal requirements apply, the following criteria shall be used:
a. Hand-arm vibration exposure action value: 2.5 m/s² A(8).
b. Hand-arm vibration exposure limit value: 5.0 m/s² A(8).
c. Whole-body vibration exposure action value: 0.5 m/s² A(8).
d. Whole-body vibration exposure limit value: 1.15 m/s² A(8).

clauses.heading: Vibration Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Vibration exposure shall be eliminated or reduced using the hierarchy of controls, including equipment selection or substitution, isolation, damping, maintenance, surface and roadway improvement, vehicle or seating improvements, operating practices and exposure duration controls. Equipment with defective, missing or ineffective vibration controls shall be removed from use unless verified interim controls prevent unacceptable exposure.

clauses.heading: Vibration Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Design, procurement, hire, inspection and maintenance of vibration generating equipment, tools and vehicles shall apply defined vibration performance and acceptance criteria. Where manufacturer vibration data is used for exposure assessment, its applicability to actual Maaden operating conditions shall be technically verified.

clauses.heading: Vibration Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Vibration controls and exposure conditions shall be reassessed following changes in equipment, vehicles, road or work surface conditions, work practices, exposure duration, reported symptoms or evidence that existing controls are no longer be effective.

clauses.heading: Illumination Assessment and Control
clauses.text:
Workplace illumination shall meet task- and location-specific requirements established in accordance with applicable Saudi requirements and ISO/CIE 8995. The minimum maintained illuminance values specified below shall apply unless a higher level is required by an applicable obligation, task assessment or specific visual condition.
a. Access and movement areas – 100 lux: walkways, corridors, stairs, circulation routes and areas primarily used for movement.
b. General operational areas – 200 lux: plant areas, equipment rooms, warehouses and general operating locations where limited visual detail is required.
c. Routine work and monitoring – 300 lux: routine operational checks, surveillance or monitoring activities, reading clear displays and similar activities.
d. Detailed work – 500 lux: maintenance activities, instrument or panel reading, normal inspection, workshops, reading, writing and similar detailed tasks.
e. Fine or precision work – 750 to 1,000 lux: fine inspection, precision activities or tasks involving small or low- contrast detail, unless a task-specific assessment determines a higher requirement. Where a task does not clearly fall within these categories or requires specialized visual performance, the required illumination shall be determined using ISO/CIE 8995 standard and task-specific assessment.

clauses.heading: Illumination Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Illumination assessments shall consider the task and operating conditions, illuminance at the relevant work or travel surface, lighting type, contrast, shadows, reflections, glare, transitions between lighting levels, color recognition, emergency routes and foreseeable deterioration, with measurements conducted where compliance has not been verified, conditions have changed, lighting contributed to an incident or task error, or visual difficulty has been reported.

clauses.heading: Illumination Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Lighting deficiencies affecting safe work, access, vehicle interaction or emergency egress shall be corrected before affected activities continue, unless verified interim controls provide an acceptable level of safety, with areas remaining restricted until suitable illumination is restored.

clauses.heading: Illumination Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Lighting systems shall be inspected and maintained, and their performance verified after installation, modification or repair and thereafter at intervals based on deterioration, contamination, environmental conditions, task criticality and operating experience.

clauses.heading: Information, Health and Worker Participation
clauses.text: Affected people shall be informed of applicable physical hazards, exposure criteria, controls, work restrictions, reportable symptoms, stop-work conditions and emergency actions, and consulted on exposure scenarios and the practicality and effectiveness of controls.

clauses.heading: Information, Health and Worker Participation
clauses.text: Personnel requiring medical evaluation, health surveillance, fitness for work assessment or work restrictions following physical agent exposure shall be referred through the Medical Services and Health Surveillance process. Only necessary work restrictions and de-identified health information shall be communicated to relevant functions, with findings indicating possible control failure used to review the applicable exposure assessment and controls.

clauses.heading: Design, Change and Monitoring
clauses.text: Projects, designs, modifications and procurement shall identify foreseeable thermal stress, vibration and illumination exposures and incorporate higher order controls and defined performance criteria before approval or acquisition.

clauses.heading: Design, Change and Monitoring
clauses.text: Changes that could affect physical agent exposure shall be managed in accordance with Section 3.52 Management of Change, with required controls and monitoring verified through applicable project, commissioning or pre-startup reviews before startup, return to service or exposure.

clauses.heading: Design, Change and Monitoring
clauses.text: Risk-based verification shall confirm that physical hazard controls remain effective, applicable exposure criteria are met and affected people understand required controls and actions. Deficiencies shall be corrected or escalated in accordance with section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management.

clauses.heading: Design, Change and Monitoring
clauses.text: Exposure limit or trigger-level exceedances shall result in immediate controls, communication to affected personnel and supervisors, and management of related incidents, suspected occupational illnesses and other reportable events in accordance with Section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship.

processes.title: Radiation Management
processes.purpose: Radiation sources and exposures are identified, authorized, controlled, monitored and managed throughout their lifecycle to protect workers, the public and the environment, prevent loss of control, and meet applicable regulatory requirements.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Units and Corporate Functions whose activities, facilities, equipment, materials or contracted services involve, or could result in exposure to, ionizing radiation or radioactive material. This includes radiation sources and radiation producing equipment, naturally occurring radioactive material (NORM), technologically enhanced naturally occurring radioactive material (TENORM), radioactive contamination and waste, materials with credible radiological potential, contracted radiation services, and radioactive or nuclear materials subject to applicable regulatory controls. It applies to employees, contractors, visitors, outside workers and members of the public who could be affected by Maaden controlled activities.

clauses.heading: Governance and Authorization
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify radiation sources, facilities and activities subject to regulatory control, determine the applicable Nuclear and Radiological Regulatory Commission requirements, and obtain and maintain the required authorization, permit, approval or exemption before commencement and throughout the applicable lifecycle.

clauses.heading: Governance and Authorization
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall remain accountable for radiation protection, source security and regulatory compliance, including activities performed by contractors.

clauses.heading: Governance and Authorization
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain a risk proportionate Radiation Protection Program covering applicable responsibilities, authorizations, source control and security, exposure management, monitoring, source integrity, radioactive waste management, emergency preparedness and response, competency, incident management, reporting and records.

clauses.heading: Governance and Authorization
clauses.text: Where required by regulation or authorization conditions, an NRRC-certified Radiation Safety Officer shall be appointed with documented responsibilities and authority, including liaison with regulators and the authority to stop unsafe or unauthorized radiation activities.

clauses.heading: Governance and Authorization
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall comply with applicable NRRC safeguards requirements for nuclear material and uranium- or thorium-bearing ore.

clauses.heading: Source Inventory and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain a current, controlled and periodically verified inventory of radiation sources and generators, with their acquisition, movement, transfer, use and disposal authorized, documented and traceable throughout the lifecycle in accordance with NRRC requirements.

clauses.heading: Source Inventory and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish authorized arrangements for the return, transfer or disposal of radioactive sources at end of life and manage changes affecting radiation sources, facilities, activities or controls through the section 3.52 Management of Change process, obtaining required NRRC approvals before implementation.

clauses.heading: Radiation Risk Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess and manage radiation risks in accordance with Section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management before introducing or modifying radiation sources, facilities, activities, materials or services and following changes, including risks from radon, contamination, NORM and TENORM.

clauses.heading: Radiation Risk Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Radiation risk assessments and controls shall address applicable exposures, affected people, materials, operating conditions, security considerations and lifecycle stages; apply the principles of justification, dose limitation and optimization; and prioritize elimination and engineering controls over administrative controls and personal protective equipment. Assessments shall be performed or approved by a qualified person.

clauses.heading: Dose Constraints and Dose Limits
clauses.text:
Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish dose constraints, operational limits, investigation levels and work controls, where required, to support dose optimization and prevent exceedance of applicable dose limits in accordance with NRRC requirements.
[Table table-63-1.png]

Table 3.16-1. NRRC-R-01 dose limits for planned exposure situations.

clauses.heading: Dose Constraints and Dose Limits
clauses.text: For declared pregnancy or breastfeeding, the embryo, fetus or infant dose shall not exceed 1 mSv.

clauses.heading: Dose Constraints and Dose Limits
clauses.text: People under 16 years of age shall not be occupationally exposed to ionizing radiation. People under 18 years of age can enter controlled areas only under supervision for approved training or study.

clauses.heading: Dose Constraints and Dose Limits
clauses.text: Dose compliance assessments shall include external exposure and committed intake dose using NRRC specified criteria, factors and reference values.

clauses.heading: Design, Procurement and Commissioning
clauses.text: New or modified radiation facilities, equipment and installations shall incorporate radiological protection, security, maintainability and failure prevention requirements.

clauses.heading: Design, Procurement and Commissioning
clauses.text: Radiation sources, equipment and associated services shall be procured from authorized suppliers and shall meet applicable technical, quality, safety, security and lifecycle management requirements, including end of life arrangements where applicable.

clauses.heading: Design, Procurement and Commissioning
clauses.text: New, relocated or significantly modified radiation sources, equipment and installations shall be tested and verified before operation or return to service, including verification of radiological conditions, area classification and affected safety functions, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Area Classification, Access and Work Control
clauses.text: Areas where radiological hazards exist shall be classified, documented and maintained as controlled or supervised areas based on radiological risk and applicable requirements.

clauses.heading: Area Classification, Access and Work Control
clauses.text: Controlled and supervised areas shall have defined boundaries, signage, access controls, monitoring arrangements and other protective measures commensurate with the level of radiological risk.

clauses.heading: Area Classification, Access and Work Control
clauses.text: Area classifications and associated controls shall be reviewed periodically and following changes that affect radiological conditions or exposure risks.

clauses.heading: Area Classification, Access and Work Control
clauses.text: Radiation work shall be performed only by authorized and competent personnel under documented work authorization and controls proportionate to the radiological risks, including for temporary and field activities where applicable.

clauses.heading: Workplace and Individual Monitoring
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain risk-based workplace and individual radiation monitoring arrangements that define the objectives, methods, frequencies, action levels and records required by the NRRC and applicable authorization conditions.

clauses.heading: Workplace and Individual Monitoring
clauses.text: Radiological surveys and monitoring shall be conducted before initial operation and following changes that affect radiological conditions, occupational exposure or control effectiveness, using workplace monitoring, individual monitoring or a combination of both based on radiological risk and applicable NRRC requirements.

clauses.heading: Workplace and Individual Monitoring
clauses.text: Workers shall be subject to individual dose monitoring where required by the NRRC or applicable authorization conditions, using NRRC recognized dosimetry services and methods commensurate with the nature, magnitude and pathways of potential exposure. Where individual monitoring is not feasible, dose assessment shall use methods approved by the NRRC and representative workplace or worker exposure information.

clauses.heading: Workplace and Individual Monitoring
clauses.text: Monitoring equipment shall be fit for purpose and maintained, calibrated or verified, with monitoring results and exposure records made available to affected workers and abnormal results, limit or action level exceedances and monitoring deficiencies investigated and corrected.

clauses.heading: Public Exposure and Radiological Environmental Protection
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess actual and potential public exposure from Maaden activities in accordance with applicable NRRC requirements, considering the representative person, relevant exposure pathways, foreseeable changes, future exposures and uncertainties, and demonstrate compliance with applicable dose limits and authorization conditions.

clauses.heading: Public Exposure and Radiological Environmental Protection
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall implement engineering, operational and access controls to protect the public from radiological hazards and ensure that visitors entering radiologically controlled areas receive applicable information, precautions, supervision and access control based on the radiological risk.

clauses.heading: Public Exposure and Radiological Environmental Protection
clauses.text: Source and environmental monitoring shall be implemented where required by the NRRC or the public-exposure assessment to verify radiological conditions and control effectiveness, with abnormal results, unexpected increases and actual or potential limit exceedances assessed, recorded and reported in accordance with applicable requirements.

clauses.heading: Public Exposure and Radiological Environmental Protection
clauses.text: New installations and significant modifications that could affect public exposure shall obtain required NRRC approval before commissioning or operation.

clauses.heading: Health Surveillance and Special Protection
clauses.text: Radiation workers shall participate in health surveillance and fitness assessments in accordance with NRRC requirements and applicable Occupational Health requirements.

clauses.heading: Health Surveillance and Special Protection
clauses.text: Suspected abnormal exposure, dose limit exceedance, pregnancy or breastfeeding considerations shall be managed through medical assessment and follow-up actions in accordance with NRRC requirements.

clauses.heading: Health Surveillance and Special Protection
clauses.text: An exposure investigation shall be initiated if an occupationally exposed individual receives, during a single dosimetry reporting period: an effective dose greater than 2 mSv, an equivalent dose to the lens of the eye greater than 1.5 mSv; or an equivalent dose to the skin, hands or feet greater than 40 mSv.

clauses.heading: Source Integrity and Control Verification
clauses.text: Radiation sources, equipment and critical controls shall be inspected, tested, maintained, calibrated and verified at defined frequencies and following acquisition, installation, relocation, maintenance or other activities that could affect integrity, with traceable records maintained.

clauses.heading: Source Integrity and Control Verification
clauses.text: Defective, damaged, leaking, compromised or missing radiation sources and failed critical radiation controls shall trigger immediate cessation of affected activities, source security, assessment, escalation and applicable regulatory notification until an authorized disposition or approved alternative controls are implemented.

clauses.heading: Radioactive Material Security and Waste Management
clauses.text: Radioactive sources and materials shall be protected throughout their lifecycle against unauthorized access, removal, loss, theft, damage, misuse, sabotage and other malicious acts through security controls proportionate to the associated risks and in accordance with applicable NRRC requirements.

clauses.heading: Radioactive Material Security and Waste Management
clauses.text: Radioactive waste and disused sources shall be minimized and managed, stored, transferred, transported, released, discharged or disposed of only in accordance with applicable NRRC authorizations and requirements.

clauses.heading: Radioactive Material Security and Waste Management
clauses.text: Suspected orphaned, abandoned or uncontrolled radioactive material shall be isolated, secured, assessed and reported to the NRRC before further handling.

clauses.heading: Competence and Radiation Work Coordination
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that personnel and contractors performing radiation related activities are appropriately authorized and competent for their assigned duties, with competence verified before independent work and maintained through applicable education, training, qualifications and experience.

clauses.heading: Competence and Radiation Work Coordination
clauses.text: Radiation work involving contractors or outside workers shall be planned and coordinated to define responsibilities and maintain applicable exposure controls, dose management and exposure records in accordance with Maaden and applicable legal, regulatory and permit requirements.

clauses.heading: Radiation Emergency Preparedness and Response
clauses.text: Radiation emergency scenarios shall be identified and addressed through applicable emergency preparedness and response arrangements, including response actions, responsibilities, communication, NRRC notification, medical support, radiation monitoring, security, recovery, testing and applicable external contacts.

clauses.heading: Radiation Emergency Preparedness and Response
clauses.text: Radiation events shall be promptly controlled, escalated, investigated and reported in accordance with applicable NRRC requirements and section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship process.

clauses.heading: Radiation Emergency Preparedness and Response
clauses.text: Emergency worker exposures shall be planned, controlled, assessed and recorded in accordance with NRRC-R-01, with exposure above 50 mSv limited to circumstances permitted by NRRC-R-01 and involving informed, trained and consenting volunteers, applicable medical evaluation and communication of dose information.

processes.title: Ergonomics and Work Design
processes.purpose: Maaden work systems, tasks, equipment, workplaces and organizational work arrangements are designed, selected, operated and reviewed to eliminate or reduce ergonomic risks and prevent work-related musculoskeletal disorders and other adverse health effects arising from poor work design.
processes.scope: This process applies throughout relevant Maaden lifecycle stages to activities and workplaces where ergonomic risks can arise from work demands, work organization, workplace or equipment design, tool or vehicle use, vibration, or changes that can affect ergonomic exposure.

clauses.heading: Ergonomics Governance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement and maintain a process to identify, assess, control and review ergonomic risks associated with activities, roles and work environments that can cause work-related musculoskeletal disorders or other ergonomic related adverse health outcomes.

clauses.heading: Ergonomics Governance
clauses.text: Ergonomic risks shall be considered in applicable risk assessments, work and project design, operational planning and management of change, with changes assessed before implementation where they could introduce or alter ergonomic risks in accordance with section 3.52 Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Ergonomics Governance
clauses.text: Contractors and other people performing work on behalf of Maaden shall comply with the ergonomic risk management requirements applicable to their work.

clauses.heading: Ergonomic Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall conduct ergonomic assessment where identified risk factors, injury or illness information, personnel reports, occupational health findings, design reviews, workplace observations, risk screening or assurance findings indicate that ergonomic risk require further evaluation.

clauses.heading: Ergonomic Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Ergonomic assessments shall consider relevant task, exposure, equipment, environmental and individual factors, including force, frequency, duration, posture, manual handling, vibration and human-machine interaction.

clauses.heading: Ergonomic Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Ergonomic assessments shall be reviewed when changes, incidents, injuries, illnesses, occupational health findings, personnel reports, workplace observations or assurance findings indicate that the assessment, risk level or controls are no longer be valid or effective.

clauses.heading: Ergonomic Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Personnel performing or familiar with the assessed work shall be consulted during ergonomic assessments, workplace design reviews and the evaluation of ergonomic controls.

clauses.heading: Ergonomic Design and Work Design Requirements
clauses.text: Ergonomic requirements shall be incorporated into the design, selection, procurement and modification of workplaces, facilities, tools, equipment, workstations and vehicles before acquisition, installation or implementation.

clauses.heading: Ergonomic Design and Work Design Requirements
clauses.text: Work shall be designed or modified to eliminate or reduce ergonomic risks associated with manual handling, repetitive work, force, sustained or awkward postures, excessive reach and vibration.

clauses.heading: Ergonomic Design and Work Design Requirements
clauses.text: New facilities, projects and major modifications shall evaluate ergonomic risks sufficiently early in the project and engineering lifecycle to influence design, procurement and commissioning decisions and reduce lifecycle ergonomic risk.

clauses.heading: Ergonomic Design and Work Design Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall review and modify workload, staffing, task allocation and work-rest arrangements where they contribute to ergonomic risk.

clauses.heading: Ergonomic Risk Control
clauses.text: Ergonomic risks shall be eliminated or, where elimination is not reasonably practicable, reduced through the hierarchy of controls, giving priority to substitution, engineering and design solutions that control exposure at source and avoiding sole reliance on administrative controls where higher order controls are reasonably practicable.

clauses.heading: Manual Handling and Physical Work Demands
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall screen manual handling activities and assess tasks involving potential musculoskeletal injury risks.

clauses.heading: Manual Handling and Physical Work Demands
clauses.text: Manual handling risks shall be eliminated or reduced through work design and the hierarchy of controls, including mechanical assistance, team handling and improvements to workplaces, storage, equipment, work processes and material flows.

clauses.heading: Equipment, Tools, Vehicles and Workplace Design
clauses.text: Workplaces, equipment and workstations shall be designed, selected or adjustable to accommodate the expected user population and applicable accessibility requirements.

clauses.heading: Equipment, Tools, Vehicles and Workplace Design
clauses.text: Tools and equipment shall be selected and maintained to minimize force requirements, awkward postures and hand-arm vibration exposure throughout their intended use.

clauses.heading: Equipment, Tools, Vehicles and Workplace Design
clauses.text: Mobile equipment and vehicle operator environments shall be designed and maintained to reduce ergonomic risks associated with posture, visibility, access and egress, seating, control layout and whole-body vibration.

clauses.heading: Equipment, Tools, Vehicles and Workplace Design
clauses.text: Control rooms, offices, laboratories and other fixed workstations shall be designed to support safe posture, visibility, reach, accessibility and effective human-machine interaction.

clauses.heading: Reporting and Early Intervention
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall evaluate reports and health findings indicating potential work-related musculoskeletal or other ergonomic health effects, assess contributing workplace factors, and implement corrective actions.

clauses.heading: Competency and Awareness
clauses.text: Personnel exposed to ergonomic risks shall receive relevant information and training before starting work and following changes affecting the risks or controls.

clauses.heading: Competency and Awareness
clauses.text: Ergonomic assessments shall be conducted by personnel competent in the methods used.

clauses.heading: Performance Monitoring and Continuous Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall monitor ergonomic performance using relevant assessment results, health and incident information, exposure data, personnel feedback, corrective actions and assurance findings, and use identified trends and lessons to improve ergonomic risk management.

clauses.heading: Performance Monitoring and Continuous Improvement
clauses.text: Ergonomic controls shall be verified after implementation and reviewed at risk-based intervals and following changes, incidents, health findings or other indications of reduced effectiveness, to confirm the intended risk reduction and identify any additional risks.

processes.title: Fitness for Work, Fatigue and Wellbeing Management
processes.purpose: Ensure workers are fit to safely perform assigned work, with fatigue, impairment and work-related psychosocial risks effectively managed to protect health, safety and wellbeing.
processes.scope: This process applies to all people working under Maaden’s operational control where being unfit for work, fatigue, impairment or work-related psychosocial risks could affect health, safety, the environment or operational integrity. Includes safety critical roles, physically or cognitively demanding work, and other roles or circumstances where fitness for work determination is required by applicable obligations or documented risk-based criteria.

clauses.heading: Governance and Responsibilities
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define responsibilities and authorities for managing fitness for work, fatigue, impairment and work-related psychosocial risks, including authority to apply interim controls and stop, restrict or reassign work, with clinical fitness determinations made by the authorized medical function.

clauses.heading: Governance and Responsibilities
clauses.text: People assigning or supervising work shall ensure assigned work is consistent with the worker’s current fitness status and functional restrictions.

clauses.heading: Governance and Responsibilities
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall provide workers with access to confidential methods for reporting fatigue, impairment, fitness for work or wellbeing concerns and shall not discourage good faith reporting.

clauses.heading: Governance and Responsibilities
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall consult affected workers when assessing fatigue and work-related psychosocial risks and reviewing related controls.

clauses.heading: Safety Critical Work and Fitness Criteria
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify safety critical roles and tasks where reduced fitness could contribute to fatality, serious injury, significant environmental impact, loss of operational control or failure of emergency response.

clauses.heading: Safety Critical Work and Fitness Criteria
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define fitness criteria for safety critical roles and tasks based on the physical, sensory, psychological and cognitive capabilities required for safe performance and provide the authorized medical function with current information on relevant work demands, hazards, exposures and operating conditions.

clauses.heading: Safety Critical Work and Fitness Criteria
clauses.text: Safety critical roles, tasks and fitness criteria shall be reviewed following changes that could affect fitness requirements or applicable obligations.

clauses.heading: Fitness Assessment and Work Status
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that workers requiring formal fitness determination are assessed through medical services established under section 3.19 Medical Services and Health Surveillance.

clauses.heading: Fitness Assessment and Work Status
clauses.text: Fitness determinations shall specify the worker’s fitness status, applicable work restrictions and review date, where required, and be communicated to the worker and relevant persons responsible for assigning or controlling work without disclosing diagnoses or clinical records unless authorized by applicable legal and Maaden privacy requirements.

clauses.heading: Fitness Assessment and Work Status
clauses.text: Workers shall be assigned only to work consistently with their current fitness status and restrictions, with restricted work arrangements reviewed by the specified date and following changes affecting the worker’s ability to perform the assigned work. A worker assessed as Not Fit can resume affected work only after a revised fitness determination permits it.

clauses.heading: Fitness Assessment and Work Status
clauses.text: Contractors shall verify that their personnel meet applicable fitness requirements before assignment and provide Maaden with only the fitness status and restrictions necessary to verify compliance.

clauses.heading: Fitness for Work and Impairment Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define triggers, responsibilities and actions for responding to reported or observed potential impairment, including immediate removal from affected safety critical work and control of associated driving or travel risks until an authorized assessment permits the work or suitable alternative duties are assigned.

clauses.heading: Fitness for Work and Impairment Controls
clauses.text: Potential impairment and fitness determinations shall be managed with respect for safety, dignity, privacy and medical confidentiality and consider fatigue, acute illness or injury, medication, alcohol or other substances, and physical, psychological or cognitive factors affecting safe performance.

clauses.heading: Fitness for Work and Impairment Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall provide workers with confidential access to authorized medical advice where medication could affect safe performance, requiring workers to seek advice before performing affected safety critical work and preventing supervisors from diagnosing medical conditions or advising changes to medication.

clauses.heading: Fitness for Work and Impairment Controls
clauses.text: Alcohol and other drug controls shall comply with applicable Saudi legal and regulatory obligations and approved Maaden Human Resources, privacy and medical requirements.

clauses.heading: Fatigue Risk Assessment and Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess fatigue risks arising from work arrangements, task demands, operating conditions, travel and accommodation, including before changes that could affect alertness, sleep opportunity, recovery or safe performance.

clauses.heading: Fatigue Risk Assessment and Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish risk-based work-hour, roster, rest and recovery requirements that comply with the Saudi Labor Law and implementing requirements, define fatigue escalation and stop-work criteria, and prioritize work design, staffing, scheduling, engineering and organizational controls over reliance on worker self-management or training.

clauses.heading: Fatigue Risk Assessment and Controls
clauses.text: Overtime, call-outs, shutdowns, turnarounds and other extended or unplanned work shall be assessed and controlled, with safety critical work reassigned, restricted or stopped where fatigue risk remains uncontrolled and necessary rest, recovery or safe transport provided.

clauses.heading: Fatigue Risk Assessment and Controls
clauses.text: Contractor fatigue arrangements and exceptions to work-hour, roster, rest or recovery requirements shall be risk- assessed, documented, approved by the designated authority, time-limited and monitored, without overriding applicable Saudi Labor Law, other legal requirements or a worker’s fitness status.

clauses.heading: Wellbeing and Psychosocial Risk Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and assess work-related psychosocial hazards, considering work design and workload, role clarity, organizational change, remote or isolated work, critical or traumatic events, harmful interpersonal conduct, organizational support and fatigue-related work arrangements.

clauses.heading: Wellbeing and Psychosocial Risk Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall manage work-related psychosocial risks through work design, work organization, leadership practices and operational controls, without relying primarily on individual awareness, resilience or wellbeing initiatives.

clauses.heading: Wellbeing and Psychosocial Risk Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall provide workers with confidential health and wellbeing support and implement needs-based initiatives, with participation and health information protected and effectiveness evaluated using worker feedback and aggregated information.

clauses.heading: Wellbeing and Psychosocial Risk Controls
clauses.text: Workers exposed to critical or traumatic events shall be offered confidential support and, where determined by the authorized medical function, have their fitness reviewed before returning to safety critical work.

clauses.heading: Wellbeing and Psychosocial Risk Controls
clauses.text: Contractors shall assess and manage work-related psychosocial risks affecting their personnel and subcontractors and provide confidential health and wellbeing support consistent with applicable Maaden and contractual requirements.

clauses.heading: Competence, Awareness and Communication
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify that workers exposed to fatigue or impairment risks, or subject to fitness requirements, can recognize and report concerns that could affect safe performance and apply the controls relevant to their work.

clauses.heading: Competence, Awareness and Communication
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify that supervisors and other people with work-control authority can respond to reported or observed concerns, apply required interim controls and escalate matters to the authorized medical or management function.

clauses.heading: Competence, Awareness and Communication
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify that people whose planning or scheduling decisions could affect fatigue risk can assess and control that risk within their authority.

clauses.heading: Monitoring and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall monitor and document the implementation and effectiveness of fitness for work, fatigue, psychosocial risk and wellbeing arrangements at defined risk-based intervals, considering compliance, approved exceptions, interventions, contractor conformance, worker feedback, field verification findings, and relevant incident and health trends.

clauses.heading: Monitoring and Improvement
clauses.text: Incident investigations shall consider fatigue, reduced fitness for work and other impairment as possible causal or contributing factors where relevant to the event.

clauses.heading: Monitoring and Improvement
clauses.text: Monitoring and reporting information shall be aggregated or de-identified unless individual identification is necessary and authorized for a defined purpose, with identifiable information limited and handled in accordance with applicable obligations and Maaden privacy requirements.
