processes.title: Medical Services and Health Surveillance
processes.purpose: Define the requirements for risk-based medical services and health surveillance to protect worker health, support medical and emergency response, identify potentially work-related health effects, evaluate exposure control effectiveness and protect confidential medical information.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Units and Corporate Functions requiring medical services or health surveillance based on occupational health risks, workforce needs, operating conditions, emergency scenarios or applicable obligations. It covers medical needs assessment, emergency medical care at Maaden workplaces, determination of service levels and coverage, occupational health surveillance, and protection of confidential medical information.

clauses.heading: Medical Services Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assign accountability for medical services and health surveillance.

clauses.heading: Medical Services Governance and Planning
Medical Services Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define the required medical services, health-surveillance programs, coverage, resources, emergency arrangements, patient referral and transport, contingencies, readiness verification, and coordination with relevant internal and external services based on the needs assessment.

clauses.heading: Medical Service Capability and Access
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall provide access to medical services with the availability, coverage and capability determined by the needs assessment.

clauses.heading: Medical Service Capability and Access
clauses.text: Medical services shall assess, treat and, where required, stabilize occupational injuries and acute illnesses within their authorized clinical scope, and arrange referral, transport and clinical handover when required care exceeds available capability.

clauses.heading: Medical Service Capability and Access
clauses.text: Medical services shall provide or support applicable occupational examinations, health surveillance and work- related case management, and contribute medical expertise to emergency planning and exercises.

clauses.heading: Medical Service Capability and Access
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify the authorization, capability, availability and response times of external medical providers and establish arrangements for their activation, patient referral and transfer.

clauses.heading: Medical Service Capability and Access
clauses.text: Remote or access constrained operations shall establish medical first-response, communication, stabilization, patient transport and escalation arrangements based on the needs assessment.

clauses.heading: Medical Service Capability and Access
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall inform personnel how to obtain medical assistance and report occupational injuries, illnesses and exposure concerns through applicable reporting arrangements.

clauses.heading: Medical Facilities, Personnel and Service Providers
clauses.text: Medical facilities and clinical work areas shall be authorized, equipped, maintained and operated within their approved service scope by personnel who hold the qualifications, licenses, registrations, clinical privileges and competencies required under applicable MOH regulations for their assigned duties and credible medical emergencies.

clauses.heading: Medical Facilities, Personnel and Service Providers
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall manage contracted medical service providers through the Contractor Management process and verify required provider and personnel authorizations before service delivery and before their expiry.

clauses.heading: Medical Facilities, Personnel and Service Providers
clauses.text: Medical services shall maintain clinical governance and quality assurance arrangements that define clinical decisions, referral, escalation, emergency response, health surveillance and medical information authorities and address clinical protocols, patient safety, diagnostic and laboratory quality, adverse events, complaints, provider performance and corrective actions.

clauses.heading: Medical Facilities, Personnel and Service Providers
clauses.text: Medical equipment, medicines, consumables and patient transport resources shall be available, secured where required, maintained and controlled for functionality, authorization, inspection, testing, calibration, storage conditions, expiry, damage and recall, with authorized contingencies established for unavailable or defective medical-emergency resources and affected work stopped unless the contingency meets the needs-assessment criteria.

clauses.heading: Medical Facilities, Personnel and Service Providers
clauses.text: Medical facilities shall control infection risks, segregate medical waste at the point of generation, and manage medical waste in accordance with applicable obligations and section 3.6 Waste Management process.

clauses.heading: Health Surveillance Program
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish health surveillance where required by applicable obligations or indicated by occupational health risk or exposure assessments, work-related symptoms, suspected occupational illness, exposure control failure or an occupational exposure event.

clauses.heading: Health Surveillance Program
clauses.text: Health-surveillance protocols shall be linked to identified hazards, relevant exposures and applicable Similar Exposure Groups and use exposure information to define worker inclusion, assessment timing, result interpretation, follow-up, delayed health effects and hazard specific obligations.

clauses.heading: Health Surveillance Program
clauses.text: An authorized occupational health physician shall approve a protocol for each applicable hazard or exposure group that defines covered people and inclusion criteria; baseline, periodic and exit assessments, including applicable tests and frequencies; authorized providers and laboratories; interpretation and communication of results; clinical follow- up and referral; and work restrictions and return-to-exposure criteria.

clauses.heading: Health Surveillance Program
clauses.text: Health surveillance shall be implemented in accordance with the approved protocol and applicable obligations and not replace hazard elimination or exposure controls.

clauses.heading: Health Surveillance Program
clauses.text: Workers included in health surveillance shall be informed of the relevant hazard, surveillance purpose and requirements, confidentiality protections, results and required follow-up.

clauses.heading: Health Surveillance Program
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define responsibilities for contractor health surveillance, maintain current surveillance coverage and completion status, review surveillance requirements following changes to hazards, exposures or applicable obligations, and prevent or restrict exposure when required surveillance is incomplete.

clauses.heading: Management of Health Surveillance Findings
clauses.text: An authorized occupational health physician shall interpret health surveillance results and obtain specialist occupational medicine advice where required.

clauses.heading: Management of Health Surveillance Findings
clauses.text: Workers shall be informed of their health surveillance results, their significance and required follow-up.

clauses.heading: Management of Health Surveillance Findings
clauses.text: When results are abnormal or indicate a potentially work-related health effect, the applicable Business Unit or Corporate Function shall arrange clinical follow-up, implement required work restrictions, review relevant exposures and controls, assess the need for surveillance of similarly exposed workers, and complete applicable internal and regulatory reporting.

clauses.heading: Management of Health Surveillance Findings
clauses.text: Medical recommendations provided to management shall state work restrictions, review conditions and reassessment requirements without disclosing the diagnosis or other medical information not required to control work-related risk. Further medical information shall be disclosed only when authorized or required by applicable obligations.

clauses.heading: Management of Health Surveillance Findings
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall analyze de-identified health-surveillance and exposure data, identify trends, implement and verify preventive actions, and provide workers with a process to review or appeal health- surveillance findings, work restrictions and return to exposure decisions.

clauses.heading: Medical Emergency Interface
clauses.text: Medical response arrangements shall be integrated with the applicable emergency response plan and credible emergency scenarios.

clauses.heading: Medical Emergency Interface
clauses.text: Medical response arrangements shall address activation, communication, escalation, triage, stabilization, casualty collection, patient transport and evacuation, clinical handover, remote medical advice, specialist consultation, receiving facility coordination, alternative referral and transport arrangements and multiple-casualty contingencies, as applicable to the needs assessment.

clauses.heading: Medical Emergency Interface
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall test medical response arrangements through exercises and following changes that can affect medical response capability, evaluate findings and track resulting actions to verified closure.

clauses.heading: Medical Emergency Interface
clauses.text: Responders shall have access to the emergency medical information and resources required for their roles while protecting personal medical information from unnecessary disclosure.

clauses.heading: Medical Information, Records and Reporting
clauses.text: Medical and occupational health records shall be accurate, traceable, protected from unauthorized access or alteration, and include relevant work and exposure history, surveillance results, clinical recommendations, work restrictions, and the identity and assessment date of the authorized healthcare professional.

clauses.heading: Medical Information, Records and Reporting
clauses.text: Medical information shall be collected, accessed, used, disclosed and transferred securely in accordance with applicable privacy, consent and legal requirements.

clauses.heading: Medical Information, Records and Reporting
clauses.text: Medical and occupational health records shall be retained for the longest period required by applicable obligations, exposure specific requirements, and, for radiation exposed workers, applicable NRRC regulations and authorization conditions, with authorized disposal preventing unauthorized access or recovery.

clauses.heading: Medical Information, Records and Reporting
clauses.text: Workers shall have access to their medical information as legally permitted, while management reporting shall use aggregated or de-identified information unless identifiable information is legally required or necessary to implement a work restriction.

processes.title: Hazardous Material Management
processes.purpose: Hazardous materials are identified, approved and controlled throughout their lifecycle to prevent harmful exposure, fire, explosion, incompatible reactions, loss of containment and environmental release.
processes.scope: This process applies to hazardous materials that Maaden procures, introduces, generates, stores, handles, uses or transfers, including raw materials, products, process intermediates, by-products and residual materials. Explosives, radioactive materials, hazardous waste and the transportation of dangerous goods are governed by their respective MSHEM processes. Relevant hazardous material requirements continue to apply where these materials or activities interface with this process.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Material Governance and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assign accountability and authority for hazardous material management throughout the applicable lifecycle and coordinate controls at interfaces with related MSHEM processes.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Material Governance and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall determine and control hazardous materials subject to regulatory thresholds, approvals, notifications, declarations or reporting requirements and ensure required submissions are complete, accurate and made within the applicable timeframes.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Material Governance and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: Hazardous materials shall be introduced, generated, stored, handled, used, transferred, discontinued and removed only when authorized and when the applicable lifecycle controls have been established.

clauses.heading: Identification, Classification and Hazard Information
clauses.text: Hazardous materials, including process intermediates and by-products, shall be identified and classified for applicable physical, health and environmental hazards using applicable classification requirements and documented, traceable information. The classification shall be reviewed when the material’s composition, properties or hazard information changes.

clauses.heading: Identification, Classification and Hazard Information
clauses.text: Material whose identity or hazards cannot be reliably confirmed shall be secured against use, transfer or unintended interaction and treated as hazardous until its identity, hazards and classification are established through documented technical evaluation, supported by testing or analysis where available information is insufficient.

clauses.heading: Approval and Introduction of Hazardous Materials
clauses.text: Hazardous materials shall be evaluated and approved before first procurement, introduction to a site, generation by a new or modified process, or use for a new or modified purpose.

clauses.heading: Approval and Introduction of Hazardous Materials
clauses.text: The evaluation shall address intended use, quantity, location, restrictions, hazards, elimination or substitution, exposure and release pathways, lifecycle controls, competency and applicable process safety and change management interfaces.

clauses.heading: Approval and Introduction of Hazardous Materials
clauses.text: Hazardous materials shall not be accepted for storage or use unless their identity, hazards and controls are established, approval and receipt requirements are verified, and a current compliant safety data sheet is available.

clauses.heading: Approval and Introduction of Hazardous Materials
clauses.text: Prohibited materials shall not be procured, introduced or used unless legally authorized and formally approved by Maaden. Temporary, trial, sample, research and vendor supplied materials shall have risk-based approval defining quantity, location, duration, accountability and disposition.

clauses.heading: Approval and Introduction of Hazardous Materials
clauses.text: Damaged, leaking, rejected, unidentified or otherwise nonconforming hazardous-material deliveries shall be isolated and controlled pending safe return, transfer or disposition.

clauses.heading: Risk Assessment and Operational Control
clauses.text: People who handle hazardous materials shall be competent and, where required, authorized for their assigned activities.

clauses.heading: Risk Assessment and Operational Control
clauses.text: Hazardous material risks shall be assessed before handling or use and reassessed following a relevant change, new hazard information, an incident or evidence that a control is ineffective.

clauses.heading: Risk Assessment and Operational Control
clauses.text: The assessment shall consider, as applicable, the material hazards, incompatibilities and potential hazardous reactions or decomposition; quantity, concentration and physical form; operating conditions and states; potential exposure and release pathways; people, the environment and assets that may be affected; and credible failures and their consequences.

clauses.heading: Risk Assessment and Operational Control
clauses.text: Controls shall be selected and implemented in accordance with the hierarchy of controls, prioritizing elimination, substitution, inherently safer design and engineering controls. Controls identified as critical under section 2.6 Critical Control Management shall be managed in accordance with that process.

clauses.heading: Risk Assessment and Operational Control
clauses.text: Hazardous material activities shall not begin or continue unless the applicable hazards, operating conditions and limits have been assessed and the required controls are available and effective.

clauses.heading: Inventory, Safety Data Sheets and Hazard Communication
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain an accurate, current and traceable hazardous material inventory identifying each material’s identity, classification, source, location, quantity, Safety Data Sheet, restriction status and responsible area, with discrepancies investigated and corrected or controlled.

clauses.heading: Inventory, Safety Data Sheets and Hazard Communication
clauses.text: Current Safety Data Sheets and control information shall be available at or near hazardous material storage and use areas and accessible to personnel and emergency responders, including during electronic system outages, with obsolete information removed from use and retained where required.

clauses.heading: Inventory, Safety Data Sheets and Hazard Communication
clauses.text: Containers, tanks, vessels, pipelines and hazardous material storage areas shall be legibly labelled to identify their contents and hazards, using material identification and NFPA 704 markings for tanks and vessels and ASME A13.1 identification for pipelines, including direction of flow.

clauses.heading: Inventory, Safety Data Sheets and Hazard Communication
clauses.text: Hazard information shall be communicated to affected personnel in an understandable form and language and updated following changes affecting Safety Data Sheets, inventories, labels, risk assessments or controls.

clauses.heading: Storage, Containment and Transfer
clauses.text: Hazardous material storage and transfer systems shall be compatible with their contents and operated to prevent loss of containment, incompatible interaction, fire, explosion, exposure and environmental release. Materials shall be segregated and maintained within defined storage conditions, with access for inspection and emergency response.

clauses.heading: Storage, Containment and Transfer
clauses.text: Secondary containment, leak detection, overfill protection and drainage isolation shall be provided where required by applicable obligations, permits, approved design criteria or risk assessment. Containment shall be compatible with the materials present, sized for the credible release and maintained with sufficient available capacity in accordance with SAF-08 requirements.

clauses.heading: Storage, Containment and Transfer
clauses.text: Hazardous material transfers shall begin only after the material, source, destination, available receiving capacity, transfer route, connections, containment and emergency arrangements are verified, with engineered controls or independent verification used where transfer errors could result in serious consequences.

clauses.heading: Storage, Containment and Transfer
clauses.text: Ignition sources shall be controlled where hazardous materials could create a fire or explosion risk, and containers shall remain closed when not in use unless equivalent protection is provided.

clauses.heading: Storage, Containment and Transfer
clauses.text: Temporary hazardous material storage shall meet the applicable control requirements for permanent storage.

clauses.heading: Contractors, Transportation and Lifecycle Disposition
clauses.text: Contractors and other external parties shall disclose hazardous materials before site introduction and obtain the approvals required by this process.

clauses.heading: Contractors, Transportation and Lifecycle Disposition
clauses.text: Current hazard, handling and emergency information shall be provided to parties receiving hazardous materials from Maaden. Transportation classified as dangerous goods shall comply with section 3.43 Transportation of Dangerous Goods and Materials process.

clauses.heading: Contractors, Transportation and Lifecycle Disposition
clauses.text: Obsolete, expired, deteriorated, surplus or prohibited hazardous materials, and containers or equipment with residual hazardous material contamination, shall remain identified and controlled until approved for reuse, returned to the supplier, decontaminated or managed in accordance with section 3.6 Waste Management process.

clauses.heading: Contractors, Transportation and Lifecycle Disposition
clauses.text: The potential presence of residual hazardous materials shall be assessed before decommissioning, demolition, excavation or other intrusive work. Identified hazards and required controls shall be communicated before disturbance.

clauses.heading: Asbestos Containing Materials
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain an accessible asbestos register and management plan covering known and presumed asbestos containing materials throughout their lifecycle.

clauses.heading: Asbestos Containing Materials
clauses.text: Work that could disturb known or presumed asbestos containing material shall not begin until the asbestos register has been checked, the material’s status has been confirmed or conservatively presumed, and the required controls have been established.

clauses.heading: Asbestos Containing Materials
clauses.text: Asbestos risks, including risks from naturally occurring asbestiform minerals, shall be identified, assessed and controlled during applicable activities, including inspection, maintenance, excavation, disturbance, emergency response, removal, transportation and disposal, in accordance with applicable requirements and section 3.12 Occupational Health Risk Assessment and Industrial Hygiene Management process.

clauses.heading: Asbestos Containing Materials
clauses.text: New asbestos containing materials shall not be procured or installed.

clauses.heading: Emergency Readiness, Verification and Improvement
clauses.text:
Business Units and Corporate Functions shall provide current hazardous material inventory, location, hazard and response information for the development and maintenance of emergency arrangements in accordance with section
5.1 Emergency Response Preparedness and Planning process.

clauses.heading: Emergency Readiness, Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: Hazardous material emergency arrangements shall consider, as applicable, material isolation, initial response, compatible response agents, containment, environmental protection and internal and external response interfaces.

clauses.heading: Emergency Readiness, Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: Hazardous material releases shall be promptly controlled and reported. Subsequent notification, investigation, remediation and management of resulting waste shall comply with the applicable MSHEM processes.

clauses.heading: Emergency Readiness, Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: Hazardous material information and controls shall be inspected or verified at frequencies based on risk and applicable obligations, with findings and operating experience evaluated, deficiencies controlled until resolved, and affected risk assessments, information and controls updated where required.

processes.trigger: Use when hazardous materials are procured, introduced, generated, stored, handled, used or transferred; use the specialist processes for explosives, radiation, hazardous waste and dangerous-goods transport.

processes.title: Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment
processes.purpose: Hazardous, non-routine and permit controlled work is planned, risk assessed, authorized, coordinated, performed, monitored, suspended when conditions change, and closed under controlled conditions that protect people, the environment, assets and operations.
processes.scope: This process applies to work performed by Maaden employees, contractors and subcontractors at locations, projects, facilities and activities under Maaden operational or project control where a Permit to Work or Task Risk Assessment is required.

clauses.heading: Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment System
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement and maintain a Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment process for work within their operational or project control.

clauses.heading: Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment System
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define competency, assessment, authorization and reauthorization requirements for personnel who prepare, issue, receive, authorize, suspend, revalidate, monitor and close permits. Authorized personnel shall perform only those Permit to Work roles, permit types, locations and activities included within their authorization.

clauses.heading: Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment System
clauses.text: A Permit Issuer and Permit Receiver shall be different authorized people. People performing Permit to Work responsibilities shall have the authority, operational knowledge and competency necessary for their assigned role.

clauses.heading: Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment System
clauses.text: Contractors and subcontractors assigned Permit to Work responsibilities shall meet the applicable Maaden competency and authorization requirements.

clauses.heading: Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment System
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish arrangements to ensure that Permit to Work activities are adequately resourced and that the number and complexity of permits controlled by an individual Permit Issuer do not compromise worksite verification, coordination, monitoring or effective control of the work.

clauses.heading: Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment System
clauses.text: Where electronic Permit to Work systems are used, controls shall be established to prevent unauthorized issue or alteration, preserve required worksite verification and approvals, communicate changes to affected people, maintain permit availability at the work location, and provide appropriate contingency arrangements for system unavailability.

clauses.heading: Permit to Work Applicability
Permit to Work Applicability
Permit to Work Applicability
clauses.text: A Permit to Work shall not normally be required for a routine operational task performed within the approved scope, conditions and controls of a current and approved Standard Operating Procedure, or for a routine maintenance task performed within the approved scope, conditions and controls of a current and approved Standard Maintenance Procedure in a designated maintenance workshop.

clauses.heading: Permit to Work Applicability
Permit Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Every Permit to Work shall be supported by an approved Task Risk Assessment completed before the permit is issued.

clauses.heading: Permit Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Before issuing a permit, the Permit Issuer and Permit Receiver shall verify at the work location that the work scope is correctly defined, worksite conditions have been assessed and required controls have been implemented and are effective.

clauses.heading: Permit Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: The verification shall address, as applicable, hazardous energy isolation, atmospheric conditions, safe access and egress, working surfaces, area controls, interactions with operating equipment or other work, and emergency arrangements.

clauses.heading: Permit Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Each permit shall clearly define the authorized work scope, location and equipment boundaries, date and authorized validity period, required controls, associated certificates, responsible people, validity conditions and conditions requiring suspension, revalidation or cancellation.

clauses.heading: Permit Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Permit requirements shall not be bypassed through generic, blanket or area wide permits that do not adequately define and control the work.

clauses.heading: Permit Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: The Permit to Work process shall define arrangements for permit preparation, issue, acceptance, execution, monitoring, handover, suspension, revalidation, cancellation and closure.

clauses.heading: Permit Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Before permitted work starts, the Permit Receiver shall ensure that affected members of the work party are briefed on and understand the authorized work scope, applicable hazards, required controls, permit limitations, simultaneous operations, emergency actions and conditions requiring work to stop. Changes affecting the work shall be communicated before work continues.

clauses.heading: Permit Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Permitted work shall be subject to field verification during execution at a frequency proportionate to the hazards, complexity, duration, and changing worksite conditions, with identified deviations or ineffective controls corrected before work continues and the permit suspended where safe conditions cannot be maintained.

clauses.heading: Interfaces and Simultaneous Operations
clauses.text: The Permit to Work system shall define and control interfaces with applicable processes, including Hot Work and Ignition Source Control, Energy Isolation and Control of Stored Energy, Working at Height, Confined Space Entry, Lifting Operations, Excavation and Trenching, Radiation Management and Electrical Safety.

clauses.heading: Interfaces and Simultaneous Operations
clauses.text: Interactions between concurrent or simultaneous activities shall be identified, assessed and coordinated by the permit issuer where they could create additional hazards, impair required controls or increase risk.

clauses.heading: Interfaces and Simultaneous Operations
clauses.text: Where multiple permits or Permit to Work systems apply to the same work activity, a responsible person shall be designated to coordinate and control the interfaces between them.

clauses.heading: Interfaces and Simultaneous Operations
clauses.text: The Permit to Work system shall maintain a current record of active and suspended permits and their status, including associated isolations where applicable. Current permits and supporting Task Risk Assessments shall be readily accessible at the work location and to the responsible operating or coordinating authority.

clauses.heading: Permit Handover, Suspension and Completion
clauses.text: A formal handover and revalidation shall be completed where permitted work continues across a shift or where responsible Permit to Work personnel change. The incoming responsible people shall verify that the work scope, worksite conditions, isolations, Task Risk Assessment and required controls remain valid before accepting responsibility.

clauses.heading: Permit Handover, Suspension and Completion
Permit Handover, Suspension and Completion
clauses.text: Suspended work shall not resume until the conditions have been reassessed, required controls restored or revised and the permit revalidated by an authorized person.

clauses.heading: Permit Handover, Suspension and Completion
clauses.text: Before permit closeout, the Permit Issuer and Permit Receiver shall verify that the work is complete or left in a defined safe condition; affected equipment and the work area are safe; personnel, temporary equipment and materials are accounted for; and associated permits, certificates and isolations have been reconciled.

clauses.heading: Permit Handover, Suspension and Completion
clauses.text: Equipment or systems shall not be reinstated, energized, pressurized, or returned to service until operational acceptance requirements are completed.

clauses.heading: Task Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Task Risk Assessment shall provide the overarching framework for identifying, assessing and controlling hazards associated with work tasks in accordance with Section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management.

clauses.heading: Task Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish Task Risk Assessment methods and selection criteria proportionate to the hazards, complexity, credible consequences, worksite conditions and interfaces associated with the task.

clauses.heading: Task Risk Assessment
clauses.text:
The framework shall include, as applicable:
a. A Last Minute Risk Assessment (LMRA) for simple, routine tasks where hazards and required controls are well understood and none of the JSA criteria in 3.21.31 apply; and
b. A team based Job Safety Analysis (JSA) for tasks requiring step by step assessment, greater assessment rigor, specialized knowledge or multidisciplinary participation.

clauses.heading: Task Risk Assessment
Task Risk Assessment
Task Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Risk identified through a Job Safety Analysis shall be rated using the Maaden EHSS Risk Matrix. Required risk review and approval shall be based on the residual risk level in accordance with section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Task Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Personnel performing the work shall be involved in the Task Risk Assessment where their knowledge or experience is necessary to identify task-specific hazards, work conditions and controls.

clauses.heading: Task Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Before work begins, the work party shall be briefed on and understand the planned work scope, applicable hazards, required controls, emergency arrangements and stop-work conditions. The briefing shall be repeated where significant changes occur, or new personnel join the work party.

clauses.heading: Task Risk Assessment
clauses.text: A previous Job Safety Analysis shall only be reused after competent review confirms its applicability to the current task, hazards, worksite conditions and interfaces. Generic or unreviewed assessments shall not be used to authorize work.

clauses.heading: Task Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Where required controls cannot reduce risk to an acceptable level in accordance with Section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management, the task shall be stopped and escalated through the EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Monitoring and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define and implement risk-based frequencies for verifying Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment arrangements, considering the hazards and complexity of work, credible consequences, permit volume, simultaneous operations, changing worksite conditions and previous verification results.

clauses.heading: Monitoring and Assurance
clauses.text: Findings shall be documented, assigned and tracked to closure. Relevant incidents, observations, findings and performance trends shall be used to improve the Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment process.

clauses.heading: Monitoring and Assurance
clauses.text: Completed, cancelled and expired permits, associated certificates and task risk assessments shall be retained for at least three months.

processes.title: Hot Work and Ignition Source Control
processes.purpose: Prevent fires, explosions and other ignition related incidents by eliminating hot work wherever a cold work alternative exists and, where hot work or other ignition sources cannot be eliminated, ensuring they are identified, assessed, authorized, controlled and monitored wherever they could cause a fire or explosion.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden controlled work and activities that generate, introduce or create an ignition source where combustible materials, ignitable substances, flammable or explosive atmospheres are present or could credibly arise.

clauses.heading: Hot Work and Ignition Source Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Hot Work shall include welding, cutting, brazing, open flame soldering, gouging, grinding, heat treatment and other work that produces or uses flame, sparks or heat capable of igniting combustible materials or a flammable or explosive atmosphere. Hot Work shall be managed in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements and NFPA 51B, Standard for Fire Prevention During Welding, Cutting, and other Hot Work.

clauses.heading: Hot Work and Ignition Source Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify activities, equipment, materials, locations and conditions that could generate or introduce an ignition source and assess where interaction with combustible materials or an ignitable atmosphere could result in fire, explosion or escalation of another hazardous event.

clauses.heading: Hot Work and Ignition Source Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Potential ignition sources shall include, as applicable, Hot Work, open flames and smoking, spark producing mechanical activities, internal combustion engines and vehicles, electrical or electronic equipment unsuitable for the hazardous area classification, electrical arcs, faults and electrostatic discharge, friction and mechanical heating, and self-heating, spontaneous combustion or exothermic reactions.

clauses.heading: Hot Work and Ignition Source Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Ignition source assessments shall consider the materials and atmospheres present or capable of release, hazardous area classification, potential paths for sparks and heat, adjacent and lower levels, simultaneous activities, changing conditions and the potential for fire or explosion to spread or escalate.

clauses.heading: Hot Work and Ignition Source Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Ignition sources shall be eliminated or substituted wherever reasonably practicable. Where this is not practicable, suitable engineering, isolation and administrative controls shall be implemented. Controls designated as critical controls shall be managed and verified in accordance with section 2.6 Critical Control Management process.

clauses.heading: Hot Work Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Hot work shall be authorized only where the task cannot reasonably be completed using a cold work method or relocated to a designated hot work area.

clauses.heading: Hot Work Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Before authorization, hot work and potentially affected areas shall be assessed for flammable or explosive atmospheres, combustible materials and dusts, process and equipment conditions, openings and potential releases, simultaneous operations, spark and heat travel, hazardous residues or previous contents, environmental conditions, fire protection availability and emergency arrangements, with identified fire and explosion hazards controlled before work begins.

clauses.heading: Hot Work Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Where a flammable or explosive atmosphere is present or could credibly arise, atmospheric testing shall be completed before hot work and continued periodically or continuously as required, with flammable gas or vapor concentrations maintained below 10% of the Lower Explosive Limit and work stopped when this limit is reached or exceeded.

clauses.heading: Hot Work Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Atmospheric testing shall be performed by competent personnel using suitable instruments calibrated in accordance with manufacturer requirements and function tested before use, at locations and frequencies based on the hazards and changing conditions but not exceeding two hours, including tests of affected equipment and adjacent or connected spaces that could contain or receive flammable gases or vapors.

clauses.heading: Hot Work Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Hot work outside a designated hot work area shall require a Hot Work Permit in accordance with section 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment process, except where work remains within the approved activities and conditions of a current designated area assessment, required controls remain effective and no additional hazard requires permit authorization.

clauses.heading: Hot Work Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall designate hot work areas through documented assessment confirming that each area is constructed or protected with non-combustible or fire-resistant materials, separated from fire and explosion hazards, kept free from uncontrolled combustible or flammable materials, provided with suitable firefighting, housekeeping, inspection and supervision arrangements, and reviewed periodically and following relevant changes.

clauses.heading: Hot Work Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Hot tapping and other intentional welding, cutting, drilling or process boundary penetration of in-service equipment or piping containing hazardous substances shall not be treated as conventional Hot Work. Such work shall only be performed under an approved Hot Tapping process or procedure supported by appropriate engineering and risk assessment, and in accordance with API RP 2201.

clauses.heading: Ignition Source and Fire Prevention Controls
clauses.text: Ignition sources not arising from permitted Hot Work shall be controlled through applicable hazardous area classification, design, operation, inspection, maintenance, electrical safety, fire prevention, hazardous material and other relevant MSHEM requirements. Electrical and electronic equipment used in hazardous classified areas shall be suitable for the area classification and conditions of use.

clauses.heading: Ignition Source and Fire Prevention Controls
clauses.text: Business Units shall identify and control ignition risks arising from electrostatic discharge, lightning and stray currents. Required bonding, grounding and other engineered controls shall be designed, installed, inspected, tested and maintained in accordance with the identified hazards and applicable technical standards.

clauses.heading: Ignition Source and Fire Prevention Controls
clauses.text: Smoking, open flames and unauthorized ignition devices shall be prohibited where fire or explosion hazards exist. Internal combustion engines or other potential ignition producing equipment introduced into areas where an ignitable atmosphere is present or could credibly arise shall be assessed and controlled in accordance with the hazardous area classification and applicable Hot Work Permit requirements.

clauses.heading: Ignition Source and Fire Prevention Controls
clauses.text: Coatings, residues and contaminants capable of producing toxic substances or creating an additional fire or explosion hazard shall be identified and removed or controlled before Hot Work. Pyrophoric, water-reactive, self- heating or unstable materials shall be assessed by a competent person and required treatment or controls established before Hot Work is authorized.

clauses.heading: Ignition Source and Fire Prevention Controls
clauses.text: Hot work equipment shall be suitable for its intended use, inspected before use, maintained in safe operating condition, and removed from service when defective or unsuitable.

clauses.heading: Ignition Source and Fire Prevention Controls
clauses.text: Combustible and flammable materials shall be removed from within at least 11 meters of Hot Work in all directions, including adjacent, upper and lower levels. Where removal is not practicable, they shall be protected using suitable fire-resistant covers, blankets, screens or barriers. The controlled distance shall be increased where sparks, slag, heat or other ignition sources could travel beyond 11 meters.

clauses.heading: Ignition Source and Fire Prevention Controls
clauses.text: Openings, gaps, grating, floor and wall penetrations, drains, vents and process release points through which sparks, slag, heat or flammable material could pass to adjacent or lower areas shall be covered, sealed or otherwise effectively controlled before Hot Work begins.

clauses.heading: Ignition Source and Fire Prevention Controls
clauses.text:
Firefighting equipment appropriate to the identified hazards shall be immediately available at the Hot Work location. A Hot Work Permit shall not be issued while fire detection, alarm, fire water or suppression systems serving the area are impaired unless compensatory controls have been assessed and formally approved in accordance with section
5.3 Emergency Response Equipment Maintenance, Testing and Interruption.

clauses.heading: Fire Watch and Post Work Monitoring
clauses.text: A competent fire watch shall continuously monitor hot work outside a designated hot work area in accordance with NFPA 51B, remain free from conflicting duties, have suitable firefighting equipment and emergency communication, understand the applicable alarm procedures, and stop the work when unsafe conditions develop. Additional fire watches shall be assigned where all exposed areas cannot be directly observed.

clauses.heading: Fire Watch and Post Work Monitoring
clauses.text: Fire watch and post-work monitoring shall continue for the periods required by NFPA 51B, the fire hazard assessment and the Hot Work Permit, including at least 60 minutes of fire watch after hot work and up to three hours of additional monitoring where required.

clauses.heading: Competency, Verification and Assurance
clauses.text: People who authorize, supervise, perform, conduct atmospheric testing for, or act as fire watch for Hot Work shall be competent and authorized for their assigned responsibilities. Personnel involved in Hot Work shall understand the applicable hazards, controls, permit requirements, emergency actions and conditions requiring work to stop.

clauses.heading: Competency, Verification and Assurance
clauses.text: Required controls shall be re-verified whenever Hot Work resumes after an interruption and whenever the work scope, atmospheric conditions, process conditions, simultaneous activities or other relevant conditions change. Where a required control is missing, ineffective or invalidated, Hot Work shall stop and shall not resume until conditions have been reassessed, required controls restored or revised and the permit revalidated in accordance with section 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment.

clauses.heading: Competency, Verification and Assurance
clauses.text: The work area shall be inspected after completion of Hot Work to verify that no ignition source, smoldering material or unsafe condition remains.

clauses.heading: Competency, Verification and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall periodically verify the implementation and effectiveness of Hot Work and Ignition Source Control arrangements through risk-based field verification, review of Hot Work activities and designated areas, and applicable assurance activities.

processes.keywords: Hot Work and Ignition Source Control; hot work, welding, cutting, grinding, ignition; Hot Work and Ignition Source Identification and Assessment; Hot Work Planning and Authorization; Ignition Source and Fire Prevention Controls; Fire Watch and Post-Work Monitoring; Competency, Verification and Assurance
processes.trigger: if welding, cutting, grinding, heating or another ignition source is introduced

processes.title: Energy Isolation and Control of Stored Energy
processes.purpose: Establish minimum requirements for identifying, isolating, controlling and verifying hazardous energy before work is performed to prevent unintended energization, start-up, movement, release of stored energy or exposure to hazardous substances.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden controlled activities, facilities, projects, personnel, contractors and subcontractors where hazardous energy or hazardous substances may expose personnel during installation, commissioning, operation, inspection, testing, maintenance, servicing, modification, decommissioning, demolition, breaking containment, confined space entry or similar work.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Energy Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain documented arrangements for identifying, isolating, controlling, verifying and restoring hazardous energy.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Energy Management
clauses.text: Hazardous energy controls shall be implemented in accordance with SAIS SAF-13 and recognized standards including OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 and ANSI/ASSP Z244.1.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Energy Management
clauses.text: All hazardous energy sources, including stored, residual, accumulated or regenerated energy, shall be identified before work begins.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Energy Management
clauses.text: Required isolation and energy control measures shall be authorized in accordance with section 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment process.

clauses.heading: Isolation Selection and Control
clauses.text: Equipment, systems and processes shall be isolated before personnel are exposed to hazardous energy unless an approved alternative method provides equivalent or greater protection and is permitted by applicable requirements.

clauses.heading: Isolation Selection and Control
clauses.text: Isolation methods shall prevent unintended energization, start-up, movement, material release or other exposure to hazardous energy.

clauses.heading: Isolation Selection and Control
clauses.text: Before personnel are exposed, stored, residual, accumulated or regenerated energy shall be dissipated, relieved, blocked, restrained or otherwise controlled to a safe state, with the effectiveness of the isolation verified at the point of work using an appropriate try/test or equivalent method and measures maintained to control any energy that may reaccumulate or regenerate.

clauses.heading: Isolation Selection and Control
clauses.text: The isolation method shall be selected based on the energy source, task, system configuration, hazardous material characteristics, stored energy and credible consequences of isolation failure.

clauses.heading: Isolation Selection and Control
clauses.text: Positive isolation shall be prioritized where failure of a primary isolation could result in serious harm, significant environmental impact or a major process safety event.

clauses.heading: Isolation Selection and Control
clauses.text: Business Unit and Corporate Functions procedures shall define activities and conditions requiring positive isolation, including applicable breaking containment, confined space, hazardous material and process system activities.

clauses.heading: Isolation Selection and Control
clauses.text: Where positive isolation is required but cannot be achieved, the work shall not proceed unless an alternative arrangement is permitted by applicable requirements and supported by documented technical review, risk assessment and authorization.

clauses.heading: Isolation Selection and Control
clauses.text: Isolation points and devices shall be identified, secured and controlled using locks and tags where personnel protection depends on maintaining the isolation.

clauses.heading: Isolation Selection and Control
clauses.text: Where an energy isolating device can be locked, lockout shall be used unless an approved assessment demonstrates equivalent or greater protection from an alternative arrangement.

clauses.heading: Isolation Selection and Control
clauses.text: Isolation methods not addressed by approved procedures or technical standards shall require documented technical or engineering review, risk assessment and authorization before use.

clauses.heading: Energy Isolation Planning
clauses.text: Documented isolation plans shall be established for complex, critical, multipoint or other isolations requiring enhanced planning and verification.

clauses.heading: Energy Isolation Planning
clauses.text: Isolation plans and records shall identify applicable isolation points and devices and provide sufficient information to control installation, verification, transfer, restoration and removal.

clauses.heading: Energy Isolation Planning
clauses.text: Temporary blinds, disconnections and other positive isolation devices shall remain traceable throughout their lifecycle.

clauses.heading: Energy Isolation Planning
clauses.text: Extended isolations shall include defined responsibility, periodic verification, controlled handover and maintenance of isolation integrity.

clauses.heading: Electrical Isolation
clauses.text: Electrical equipment shall be de-energized before work where personnel could be exposed to electrical hazards unless energized work is specifically authorized under section 3.30 Electrical Safety and section 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment processes.

clauses.heading: Electrical Isolation
clauses.text: Electrical isolation shall identify all applicable electrical energy sources, use approved energy isolating devices, secure isolation against unauthorized operation, and verify de-energization before personnel are exposed.

clauses.heading: Electrical Isolation
clauses.text: Control circuits, software controls, selector switches, push buttons or interlocks shall not be used as the only means of electrical isolation.

clauses.heading: Electrical Isolation
clauses.text: Electrical isolation and absence of voltage verification shall be performed by qualified people in accordance with the applicable Electrical Safety requirements, including NFPA 70E and OSHA 29 CFR 1910.333.

clauses.heading: Personal and Group Protection
clauses.text: Each person exposed to hazardous energy shall be protected through a personal lock or an approved group lockout arrangement providing equivalent individual control.

clauses.heading: Personal and Group Protection
clauses.text: Personal locks shall be uniquely identifiable, standardized, distinguishable from locks used for other purposes, and remain under the control of the individual to whom they are assigned.

clauses.heading: Personal and Group Protection
clauses.text: Group lockout arrangements shall provide effective individual protection and shall define responsibility for control, personnel accountability, shift or work group changes and transfer of protection.

clauses.heading: Personal and Group Protection
clauses.text: Personal locks or tags shall normally be removed only by the person who applied them. Emergency removal shall be performed only through an approved authorization process that protects the affected person and verifies that safe removal conditions exist as per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147.

clauses.heading: Personal and Group Protection
clauses.text: A designated authorized person shall control each group lockout, as per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 and ANSI/ASSP Z244.1.

clauses.heading: Personal and Group Protection
clauses.text: Controls shall be established for personnel changes, shift changes, and work group transitions.

clauses.heading: Personal and Group Protection
clauses.text: The Permit To Work Issuer’s isolation control lock shall be the first control lock applied and the last removed. It shall not replace any personal lock.

clauses.heading: Restoration and Re-Energization
clauses.text: Equipment, systems and processes shall not be restored to service until the work is complete and restoration has been authorized in accordance with the LOTO certificate.

clauses.heading: Restoration and Re-Energization
Restoration and Re-Energization
clauses.text: Before re-energization or return to service, personnel involved in or affected by the task shall be notified and the notification recorded on the LOTO Certificate.

clauses.heading: Restoration and Re-Energization
clauses.text: Temporary energization required for testing or positioning shall be specifically authorized and controlled, with personnel cleared before energization and required isolations reapplied and reverified before work resumes.

clauses.heading: Competency and Assurance
clauses.text: Personnel performing, authorizing or verifying hazardous energy isolation shall be trained, competent and authorized for their assigned responsibilities.

clauses.heading: Competency and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify the implementation and effectiveness of hazardous energy control arrangements through documented program monitoring and procedure inspections conducted at least annually by an authorized person other than the person implementing the procedure being inspected, in accordance with OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147(c)(6) and ANSI/ASSP Z244.1.

processes.trigger: if hazardous energy or stored energy must be isolated, controlled or verified

processes.title: Working at Height
processes.purpose: Establish minimum requirements for planning, authorizing and controlling work at height to prevent falls and falling objects and to ensure safe access, suitable equipment, competent personnel and effective rescue arrangements.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden controlled activities, facilities and projects where a person may be exposed to a risk of falling from one level to another during work or access, including elevated or temporary work areas, unprotected edges and gratings opening , fragile surfaces, ladders, scaffolds, mobile elevating work platforms and personal fall protection systems.

clauses.heading: Working at Height Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain arrangements for controlling work at height consistent with applicable legal requirements and ANSI/ASSP Z359.2 requirements.

clauses.heading: Working at Height Management
clauses.text: Roles, responsibilities, authorities and competency requirements for planning, authorizing, supervising, performing, inspecting and supporting work at height shall be defined.

clauses.heading: Working at Height Management
clauses.text: Personnel performing or supporting work at height shall be trained and, where required, formally authorized for their assigned responsibilities.

clauses.heading: Planning and Risk Control
Planning and Risk Control
clauses.text: Fall hazards shall be identified and risk assessed before work begins, including hazards associated with access, working surfaces, edges and openings, fragile surfaces, equipment, falling objects, weather, electrical or process hazards, traffic and simultaneous operations.

clauses.heading: Planning and Risk Control
Planning and Risk Control
clauses.text: Work at height shall be authorized in accordance with Section 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment, where required, and stopped until reassessment and reauthorization are completed where conditions change or required controls become unavailable or ineffective.

clauses.heading: Safe Access, Work Platforms and Openings
clauses.text: Safe access, egress and movement shall be provided and maintained for work at height locations.

clauses.heading: Safe Access, Work Platforms and Openings
clauses.text: Areas where people walk or work shall be stable, capable of supporting the intended loads and maintained in a safe condition.

clauses.heading: Safe Access, Work Platforms and Openings
clauses.text: Open sides, edges, floor or wall openings and fragile surfaces shall be identified and protected against falls of people, tools, equipment and materials.

clauses.heading: Safe Access, Work Platforms and Openings
clauses.text: The creation of a temporary opening, including the removal of grating, floor plates, covers, hatches or sections of a platform, shall be planned, risk assessed and authorized before the opening is created.

clauses.heading: Safe Access, Work Platforms and Openings
clauses.text: Temporary openings shall be continuously protected by secured load bearing covers, guardrail systems or other physical barriers providing equivalent protection, including during the removal and reinstatement of the affected surface.

clauses.heading: Safe Access, Work Platforms and Openings
clauses.text: Removed grating, floor plates and covers shall be controlled against unintended movement and reinstated, secured and verified before the area is returned to normal use.

clauses.heading: Safe Access, Work Platforms and Openings
clauses.text: Where an opening cannot be fully protected by a cover or physical barrier, access shall be restricted and work controlled through an approved fall protection arrangement.

clauses.heading: Ladders, Scaffolds and Elevated Platforms
clauses.text: Ladders and fixed access systems shall meet applicable design, inspection, maintenance and use requirements, including OSHA 29 CFR 1910.23 where applicable. Ladders shall be used only where appropriate for the task and where a safer means of access or working platform is not reasonably practicable.

clauses.heading: Ladders, Scaffolds and Elevated Platforms
clauses.text: Scaffolds and temporary work platforms shall be selected, designed, erected, altered, inspected, used and dismantled by competent or qualified personnel, as applicable to their assigned responsibilities, considering the work, location, configuration, environmental conditions and anticipated loads, and in accordance with OSHA 1926.451 and ANSI/ASSP A10.8.

clauses.heading: Ladders, Scaffolds and Elevated Platforms
clauses.text: Scaffolds shall be provided with a clearly visible identification status at the access points following inspection by a competent person. The system shall identify whether the scaffold is approved for use, subject to restrictions, or prohibited for use in accordance with ANSI/ASPP A10.8.

clauses.heading: Ladders, Scaffolds and Elevated Platforms
clauses.text: Non-standard or complex scaffolds and temporary platforms shall be subject to documented design and approval by a qualified person before use.

clauses.heading: Ladders, Scaffolds and Elevated Platforms
clauses.text: Scaffolds and temporary work platforms shall provide stable foundations or supports, working platforms, safe access, edge protection and falling object controls, and be protected from use when incomplete, defective, overloaded or unauthorized.

clauses.heading: Ladders, Scaffolds and Elevated Platforms
clauses.text: Mobile elevating work platforms and personnel lifting equipment shall be fit for purpose, inspected, maintained, and operated by competent and authorized people.

clauses.heading: Personal Fall Protection
clauses.text: Fall hazards shall be controlled where a person could fall 1.8 m or more to a lower level, or at a lower height where the risk assessment identifies a potential for serious injury. Personal fall protection shall be provided where collective protection does not adequately control the fall exposure.

clauses.heading: Personal Fall Protection
clauses.text: Personal fall protection systems shall be selected and used according to the activity, user, exposure, environmental conditions and available fall clearance, in compliance with applicable OSHA 29 CFR 1910.140 and ANSI/ASSP Z359 requirements.

clauses.heading: Personal Fall Protection
clauses.text: Fall protection components and systems shall be compatible, fit for their intended purpose and connected to anchorages identified and verified before use, with engineered anchorages and fall protection systems designed and approved by qualified personnel.

clauses.heading: Personal Fall Protection
clauses.text: Fall protection equipment shall be removed from service where it is damaged, defective, altered without authorization, involved in a fall or impact loading, overdue for required inspection, or outside its approved service life.

clauses.heading: Personal Fall Protection
clauses.text: Falling object hazards associated with work at height shall be controlled by securing or containing tools, materials and equipment that could fall and protecting areas below or adjacent to overhead work through access control, barricading or other defined controls.

clauses.heading: Rescue and Emergency Arrangements
clauses.text: Before personnel are exposed to a fall hazard, rescue arrangements shall be established based on the location and fall protection system and address required rescue personnel, equipment, communication, access, medical support and protection of rescuers.

clauses.heading: Rescue and Emergency Arrangements
clauses.text: Required rescue capability shall remain available for the duration of the work and be periodically verified based on the risk and complexity of the task.

clauses.heading: Inspection and Verification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain an inspection schedule identifying the inspection types, frequencies, competent roles, acceptance criteria and record requirements for applicable work at height equipment.

clauses.heading: Inspection and Verification
clauses.text: Personal fall protection equipment shall be inspected by the user before each use and undergo a documented inspection by a competent person at least annually, or more frequently where required by the applicable ANSI/ASSP Z359 equipment standard, manufacturer instructions, conditions and frequency of use, environmental exposure or inspection history.

clauses.heading: Inspection and Verification
clauses.text: Scaffolds shall be inspected for visible defects by a competent person before each work shift and shall undergo documented inspection by a competent scaffold inspector at intervals not exceeding two weeks and following erection, alteration, relocation, severe weather, impact, overloading, or any other occurrence that could affect structural integrity, before use or continued use.

processes.title: Confined Space Entry
processes.purpose: Establish minimum requirements for identifying, assessing, authorizing, controlling, and monitoring confined space entry to protect personnel from hazardous atmospheres, energy releases, restricted access, and other safety and health hazards.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Unit and Corporate Functions, employees, contractors, and subcontractors involved in or affected by entry into confined spaces during operations, maintenance, inspection, cleaning, construction, testing, and emergency activities at Maaden controlled sites.

clauses.heading: Confined Space Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain documented arrangements for managing confined space entry in accordance with SAIS SAF-13, OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146 and NFPA 350.

clauses.heading: Confined Space Management
clauses.text: Confined spaces shall be identified, assessed, recorded and clearly marked, with all entry controlled in accordance with section 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment process, and unauthorized entry prevented in accordance with applicable requirements, including OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146.

clauses.heading: Confined Space Management
clauses.text: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities for confined space entry planning, authorization, supervision, atmospheric testing, attendance, entry, and rescue shall be defined.

clauses.heading: Confined Space Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that personnel assigned to confined space responsibilities are trained, competent, qualified and authorized, as applicable to their roles, and that activities involving Maaden personnel, contractors, subcontractors and other affected parties are coordinated.

clauses.heading: Confined Space Management
clauses.text: Changes to a confined space, its use, configuration, hazards, or surrounding conditions shall trigger reassessment and, where necessary, reclassification and revision of entry controls.

clauses.heading: Confined Space Management
clauses.text: Facility and equipment design or modification shall consider eliminating confined spaces or reducing entry hazards in accordance with NFPA 350.

clauses.heading: Hazard Assessment and Entry Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess confined space hazards and prepare a documented entry plan before entry is authorized.

clauses.heading: Hazard Assessment and Entry Planning
clauses.text: The hazard assessment shall consider inherent, introduced, adjacent, and interacting hazards that could affect entrants, attendants, rescuers, or other affected people, including hazardous atmospheres, engulfment, entrapment, restricted access or egress, hazardous energy, process materials, temperature extremes, biological agents, falls, falling objects, and surrounding operations, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Hazard Assessment and Entry Planning
clauses.text: The entry plan shall define the work scope, acceptable entry conditions, required personnel and competencies, isolation, atmospheric testing and controls, access and egress, communication, PPE, tools and equipment, monitoring, supervision, and emergency and rescue arrangements.

clauses.heading: Hazard Assessment and Entry Planning
clauses.text: Hazardous energy and material sources capable of entering or otherwise affecting the confined space shall be identified and controlled through the applicable requirements established in section 3.23 Energy Isolation and Control of Stored Energy process.

clauses.heading: Hazard Assessment and Entry Planning
clauses.text: Confined space entry shall be coordinated with applicable Permit to Work, energy isolation, hot work, line opening, electrical safety, working at height, respiratory protection, lifting, emergency preparedness, and simultaneous operations requirements.

clauses.heading: Hazard Assessment and Entry Planning
clauses.text: The hazard assessment and entry plan shall be reviewed and revised when the work scope, space conditions, hazards, personnel, equipment, or surrounding operations change.

clauses.heading: Entry Authorization and Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall authorize confined space entry through an approved Confined Space Entry Permit, supported by an entry plan that includes ventilation and rescue arrangements, and a Job Safety Analysis along with any other permits or certificates required for the work.

clauses.heading: Entry Authorization and Control
clauses.text: The confined space entry permit shall identify the space, work scope, hazards, controls, authorized personnel, validity period, acceptable atmospheric conditions, communication requirements, and rescue arrangements.

clauses.heading: Entry Authorization and Control
clauses.text: Before authorizing entry, the Permit Issuer and Receiver shall verify that required isolations, atmospheric conditions and controls, access and egress, equipment, communication, PPE, attendant coverage, and rescue arrangements are in place.

clauses.heading: Entry Authorization and Control
clauses.text: Energy, material and process sources capable of entering or otherwise affecting the confined space shall be isolated and the effectiveness of the isolation verified in accordance with the applicable MSHEM Energy Isolation and Control of Stored Energy requirements. Connected material and process sources shall be isolated by blinding or physical disconnection before entry; valve closure alone shall not satisfy this requirement. Any alternative shall only be used where permitted by applicable legal and regulatory requirements and supported by documented technical review, risk assessment and authorization.

clauses.heading: Entry Authorization and Control
clauses.text: A trained, competent and authorized Standby Man shall remain outside at each designated entry point while personnel are inside the confined space, continuously monitor the entry, maintain communication with entrants and other Standby Men, and perform no duty that could interfere with Standby Man responsibilities. Each entrant shall sign in and out for every entry and exit using a controlled entry/exit log, and the Standby Man shall maintain an accurate account of personnel inside the confined space.

clauses.heading: Entry Authorization and Control
clauses.text: Personnel performing entry, attendance, atmospheric testing, entry supervision, or rescue duties shall be competent and authorized for their assigned roles in accordance with ANSI/ASSP Z117.1.

clauses.heading: Entry Authorization and Control
clauses.text: Related permits and simultaneous activities shall be coordinated throughout the entry to prevent interacting or introduced hazards.

clauses.heading: Entry Authorization and Control
clauses.text: Entry shall be suspended and entrants evacuated when acceptable entry conditions are exceeded, a required control or communication system fails, an emergency alarm activates, or any other condition could endanger personnel.

clauses.heading: Entry Authorization and Control
clauses.text: Entry shall resume only after conditions have been reassessed, required controls restored, acceptable entry conditions reverified, and entry reauthorized.

clauses.heading: Atmospheric Control and Safe Entry Operations
clauses.text: The atmosphere of each confined space shall be tested before entry and monitored during entry at frequencies determined by the hazard assessment and entry plan, but not exceeding two hours. Testing shall address oxygen, flammable gases and vapors, toxic contaminants, and other identified atmospheric hazards, and shall be conducted for oxygen first, followed by flammable gases and vapors and then toxic contaminants, in accordance with OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146.

clauses.heading: Atmospheric Control and Safe Entry Operations
clauses.text: Acceptable entry conditions shall include an oxygen concentration from 19.5 to 22 percent, flammable gases and vapors below 10 percent of the lower flammable limit, and airborne contaminants within applicable occupational exposure limits in accordance with section 3.13 Airborne Contaminants and Chemical Exposure Control process.

clauses.heading: Atmospheric Control and Safe Entry Operations
clauses.text: Atmospheric testing and monitoring equipment shall be suitable for the identified hazards, maintained and calibrated in accordance with manufacturer requirements, and used by competent and authorized personnel.

clauses.heading: Atmospheric Control and Safe Entry Operations
clauses.text: Ventilation, purging, cleaning, or other controls shall be used where required to establish and maintain acceptable entry conditions without introducing additional hazards.

clauses.heading: Atmospheric Control and Safe Entry Operations
clauses.text: Inerted or oxygen deficient confined spaces shall be treated as immediately dangerous to life or health and entered only under approved respiratory protection, monitoring, communication and rescue controls.

clauses.heading: Atmospheric Control and Safe Entry Operations
clauses.text: Atmospheric testing and monitoring results shall be documented and communicated to the entry team.

clauses.heading: Emergency, Rescue and Entry Completion
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish entry specific emergency and rescue arrangements (Rescue Plan) before entry begins, based on the confined space, access and egress, identified hazards, number of entrants, and foreseeable emergency conditions.

clauses.heading: Emergency, Rescue and Entry Completion
clauses.text: Confined space rescue services shall be competent, authorized, properly equipped, informed of the space hazards, provided access for planning and preparation, and capable of responding within the time required to protect entrants.

clauses.heading: Emergency, Rescue and Entry Completion
clauses.text: Non-entry rescue shall be used where practicable and where its use does not increase risk, in accordance with OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146.

clauses.heading: Emergency, Rescue and Entry Completion
clauses.text: Internal rescue teams shall practice confined space rescue at least once every 12 months using actual or representative confined spaces in accordance with OSHA 29 CFR 1910.146(k).

clauses.heading: Emergency, Rescue and Entry Completion
clauses.text: Required rescue equipment, communication systems, first-aid capability, and medical support shall remain available throughout the entry.

clauses.heading: Emergency, Rescue and Entry Completion
clauses.text: On completion of the entry, all people shall be accounted for, temporary equipment and materials removed, and the space inspected. Isolations shall be restored under authorization before permit closure and return to service.

clauses.heading: Entry Verification and Program Monitoring
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish risk-based verification arrangements to evaluate compliance with and effectiveness of confined space entry requirements.

clauses.heading: Entry Verification and Program Monitoring
clauses.text: Active confined space entries shall be inspected at defined intervals to verify compliance with the entry permit and required controls, including isolation, atmospheric conditions, entry team responsibilities, and rescue readiness.

clauses.heading: Entry Verification and Program Monitoring
clauses.text: Completed and suspended entries shall be reviewed where deviations, control failures, unexpected hazards, evacuations, incidents, near misses, or rescue activations occurred, and relevant findings communicated to affected parties.

clauses.heading: Entry Verification and Program Monitoring
clauses.text: Confined space events, including unauthorized entries, evacuations, atmospheric deviations, control failures, incidents, near misses, and rescue activations, shall be reported and managed through the section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship process.

clauses.heading: Entry Verification and Program Monitoring
clauses.text: Confined space performance shall be periodically evaluated using the results of entry inspections, permit reviews, atmospheric monitoring, incidents, control failures, rescue events, contractor performance and other relevant assurance activities, with identified deficiencies corrected and used to improve confined space arrangements.

clauses.heading: Entry Verification and Program Monitoring
clauses.text: Confined space permits, atmospheric monitoring results, inspection and review records, and records of significant events and corrective actions shall be maintained.
