processes.title: Lifting Operations
processes.purpose: Lifting operations are planned, authorized, executed and verified so that loads remain controlled, lifting equipment remains within verified capacity and operating limits, and people, structures, plant and the environment are protected from dropped loads, unintended movement, collision, instability and equipment failure.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden owned, operated, managed or leased locations and to Maaden personnel, contractors, subcontractors and service providers involved in lifting operations. It covers lifting machines, lifting accessories, rigging and engineered lifting points used to raise, lower, suspend or support a load.

clauses.heading: Governance and Competency
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain arrangements for managing lifting operations and lifting equipment.

clauses.heading: Governance and Competency
clauses.text: Authority, responsibility and competency requirements shall be defined for personnel who plan, approve, supervise, operate, rig, signal, inspect, maintain or verify lifting operations and equipment.

clauses.heading: Governance and Competency
clauses.text: Personnel shall only undertake a lifting role where they have been assessed as competent and, where applicable, formally authorized for the role and equipment concerned.

clauses.heading: Governance and Competency
clauses.text: Contractor lifting personnel and equipment shall meet applicable Maaden requirements.

clauses.heading: Lifting Equipment
clauses.text: Lifting equipment, accessories and lifting points shall be suitable for their intended duty, load, configuration and operating environment and shall have identifiable rated capacities or working load limits.

clauses.heading: Lifting Equipment
clauses.text: New, hired, contractor provided, modified or relocated lifting equipment shall undergo an acceptance process before first use that verifies conformity with applicable Saudi legal and regulatory requirements, manufacturer requirements, and applicable international standards for the relevant type of lifting equipment including ASME B30 series.

clauses.heading: Lifting Equipment
clauses.text: Custom designed lifting equipment, attachments and lifting points shall be engineered, verified and marked with their rated capacity before use.

clauses.heading: Lifting Equipment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain an inventory of lifting equipment and accessories requiring controlled inspection, testing, examination or maintenance.

clauses.heading: Lifting Equipment
clauses.text: Inspection, testing, examination and maintenance requirements and frequencies shall be established in accordance with applicable legal requirements, adopted technical standards, manufacturer requirements and equipment risk or service conditions.

clauses.heading: Lifting Equipment
clauses.text: Lifting equipment shall be inspected before use and removed from service if it is damaged or defective, has expired inspection or certification, has no identifiable capacity, or has any inoperable safety function.

clauses.heading: Lifting Equipment
clauses.text: Equipment involved in an overload, dropped load, collision, uncontrolled movement or other event that could affect its integrity shall be removed from service until its condition and suitability for return to service have been verified and authorized.

clauses.heading: Lift Assessment and Classification
clauses.text: Each lifting operation shall be assessed before execution to determine the required level of planning, supervision, technical review and authorization.

clauses.heading: Lift Assessment and Classification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish documented criteria for classifying routine, non-routine, complex and critical lifts.

clauses.heading: Lift Assessment and Classification
Lift Assessment and Classification
clauses.text: A change in load, equipment, configuration, work area, personnel, environmental conditions or interacting activities shall trigger reassessment of the lifting classification and plan where the change may affect risk.

clauses.heading: Lift Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: A lifting plan shall be established before lifting begins. The extent and detail shall be proportionate to the lift classification, complexity and credible consequences.

clauses.heading: Lift Planning and Authorization
Lift Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Routine lifting shall be performed under an approved SOP/SMP or repeat lifting plan where the operation remains within its defined equipment, loads, configuration, location and operating limits.

clauses.heading: Lift Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Non-routine, complex and critical lifting operations shall require an activity specific lifting plan reviewed and approved by personnel with appropriate authority and technical competence. As a minimum, lifting plan review and approval shall require Rigger Level 1 competency for Routing Lifts, Rigger Level 2 competency for Non-Routine Simple/Moderate Lifts, and Rigger Level 3 competency for Complex/critical Lifts.

clauses.heading: Lift Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: A lift shall not commence until responsible personnel have verified that the equipment, load, work area and required controls correspond with the approved plan.

clauses.heading: Lift Planning and Authorization
clauses.text: Where conditions deviate from the plan, the lift shall stop until the change is assessed and authorization reconfirmed.

clauses.heading: Operational Controls
clauses.text: Ground, foundations, supporting structures, underground conditions and adjacent slopes that could affect lifting equipment stability shall be assessed before setup.

clauses.heading: Operational Controls
clauses.text: Loads shall be rigged using equipment suitable for the load, lifting points, configuration and planned movement, with the weight, center of gravity, integrity and lifting points established before lifting.

clauses.heading: Operational Controls
clauses.text: Exclusion zones shall be established based on credible movement, swing, overturning, collision and dropped load hazards. Personnel shall not stand, pass or work beneath suspended loads.

clauses.heading: Operational Controls
clauses.text: Lifting operations shall use a defined communication method understood by the lifting team. Loss or misunderstanding of required communication shall result in the lift being stopped.

clauses.heading: Operational Controls
clauses.text: Erection, dismantling, major reconfiguration and relocation of lifting machines shall be performed as per the manufacturer’s requirements or an approved engineered method under the supervision of competent personnel.

clauses.heading: Special and High Consequence Lifting
clauses.text: Critical lifts shall be subject to enhanced technical, operational and authorization controls appropriate to the credible consequences.

clauses.heading: Special and High Consequence Lifting
clauses.text: Personnel shall not be lifted using lifting equipment where a safer means of access is reasonably practicable. Where personnel lifting is necessary, the equipment, carrier, fall protection, rescue arrangements and authorization shall meet comply with applicable legal and technical requirements, including OSHA 29 CFR 1926.1431 and ASME B30.23.

clauses.heading: Special and High Consequence Lifting
clauses.text: Lifting near electrical conductors shall comply with section 3.30 Electrical Safety requirements and applicable minimum approach distances. Electrical lines shall be treated as energized unless confirmed de-energized, isolated and earthed by the owning authority.

clauses.heading: Special and High Consequence Lifting
clauses.text: Lifting over or adjacent to operating plant, hazardous material inventories or critical equipment shall be eliminated where reasonably practicable. Where it cannot be eliminated, the lifting plan shall address the applicable loss of containment consequences, operational restrictions, isolation, process monitoring and emergency arrangements.

clauses.heading: Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: Critical controls for lifting shall be identified, assigned performance and verification requirements and managed in accordance with Section 2.6 Critical Control Management.

clauses.heading: Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: A lift shall not proceed where a required critical control is absent, ineffective or cannot be verified.

clauses.heading: Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify implementation of lifting requirements through field observation, equipment inspections, lifting plan reviews and assurance activities.

clauses.heading: Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: Lifting related defects, dropped loads, overloads, plan deviations, uncontrolled movements, near misses and incidents shall be reported.

processes.title: Mobile Equipment Safety
processes.purpose: Mobile equipment hazards are systematically identified and controlled so that mobile equipment is designed, selected, operated, maintained, inspected and managed to prevent fatalities, serious injuries, equipment related incidents and uncontrolled interactions with people, vehicles, infrastructure and operating areas.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden owned, operated, managed, leased or controlled locations and to Maaden personnel and contractors who operate, maintain, inspect or authorize mobile equipment. It covers heavy mobile equipment across its lifecycle, from selection to disposal.

clauses.heading: Governance and Competency
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain documented arrangements for the selection, acceptance, operation, inspection, maintenance, modification, withdrawal from service and disposal of mobile equipment, proportionate to their equipment types, material risks and operating conditions.

clauses.heading: Governance and Competency
clauses.text: Authority, responsibility and competency requirements shall be defined for personnel who operate, supervise, inspect, maintain, modify, authorize or verify mobile equipment.

clauses.heading: Governance and Competency
clauses.text: Personnel shall only operate mobile equipment where they have been assessed as competent for the equipment category and operating environment concerned and formally authorized, subject to defined review and revalidation criteria in accordance with section 2.7 EHSS Competency, Awareness and Communication.

clauses.heading: Governance and Competency
clauses.text: Mobile Equipment Operators shall receive site specific induction and operating area orientation, and shall meet applicable fitness for work requirements.

clauses.heading: Governance and Competency
clauses.text: Contractor mobile equipment, operators and maintenance arrangements shall meet applicable Maaden requirements.

clauses.heading: Mobile Equipment
clauses.text: Mobile equipment shall be suitable for its intended duty, load, operating environment and terrain, and shall be operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturer requirements unless an approved engineering assessment establishes an equivalent or higher level of risk control. Powered industrial trucks shall comply with applicable requirements of OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178 and ANSI/ITSDF B56.1, or equivalent recognized standards.

clauses.heading: Mobile Equipment
clauses.text: Mobile equipment shall be fitted with the braking, restraint, warning, visibility, emergency control and unauthorized use prevention systems required to control its credible operating hazards, and with collision warning or proximity detection where required by risk assessment.

clauses.heading: Mobile Equipment
clauses.text: Where applicable, earth-moving equipment braking systems shall conform to ISO 3450 or equivalent; roll-over protective structures (ROPS) to ISO 3471 or equivalent; and falling object protective structures (FOPS) to ISO 3449, or ISO 10262 for hydraulic excavators, or equivalent. Safe access and egress shall be provided in accordance with ISO 2867 or equivalent.

clauses.heading: Mobile Equipment
clauses.text: Fire hazards associated with fuels, hydraulic systems, electrical systems, batteries, hot surfaces and combustible materials shall be assessed, and appropriate fire prevention, detection and suppression controls shall be provided based on equipment type and fire risk.

clauses.heading: Mobile Equipment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain a register of mobile equipment identifying equipment category and the safety critical systems and components subject to controlled inspection, testing or maintenance.

clauses.heading: Mobile Equipment
clauses.text: Inspection, testing and preventive maintenance programs shall be established, with frequencies for safety critical components determined based on manufacturer requirements, equipment duty, operating environment and risk, and records retained and readily accessible.

clauses.heading: Mobile Equipment
clauses.text: Mobile equipment shall be withdrawn from service and prevented from use where it is defective or damaged, has an expired inspection or certification, or has an inoperable safety critical system, with controls established for defect classification and return to service.

clauses.heading: Mobile Equipment
clauses.text: Changes to mobile equipment design, safety systems, operating envelope or operating conditions shall be assessed and managed in accordance with section 3.52 Management of Change before implementation, verified before return to service and supported by manufacturer or competent engineering approval where equipment capacity, stability or safety critical systems are affected.

clauses.heading: Assessment and Operating Limits
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess mobile equipment hazards and interactions with people, vehicles, equipment, infrastructure, process facilities, terrain and geotechnical features, and define operating controls addressing equipment fire, loss of load, towing or coupling failure, tyre or wheel failure, uncontrolled movement and other credible hazards.

clauses.heading: Assessment and Operating Limits
clauses.text: Documented safe operating limits and controls shall be established where rollover, collision, engulfment, ground failure, loss of control on grades, impact with structures or contact with energized services is credible.

clauses.heading: Assessment and Operating Limits
clauses.text: Mobile equipment activity falling outside established operating limits, procedures or designated operating areas shall be subject to task risk assessment and authorization in accordance with section 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment.

clauses.heading: Interaction and Area Controls
clauses.text: Interaction between mobile equipment and pedestrians or light vehicles shall be controlled through elimination, physical separation, engineered separation or equivalent verified controls.

clauses.heading: Interaction and Area Controls
clauses.text: Traffic management, route design, speed limits and right of way rules for areas in which mobile equipment operates shall be established in accordance with section 3.29 Traffic and Journey Management process.

clauses.heading: Interaction and Area Controls
clauses.text: Loading, dumping, reversing, parking, refueling and maintenance interface areas shall be designated and controlled.

clauses.heading: Interaction and Area Controls
clauses.text: Where flagman, spotters or ground personnel are used, their responsibilities, positioning, communication method and exclusion zones shall be defined.

clauses.heading: Operational Controls
clauses.text: Mobile equipment shall be inspected before use against defined criteria, with defects reported and any equipment that is unsafe removed from service before operation.

clauses.heading: Operational Controls
clauses.text: Mobile equipment shall be operated only by an authorized operator and only within its established operating limits, rated capacity and designated operating areas.

clauses.heading: Operational Controls
clauses.text: Seat restraints and required operator protection systems shall be used whenever the equipment is capable of movement.

clauses.heading: Operational Controls
clauses.text: Unattended mobile equipment shall be parked and secured against unintended movement using parking and immobilization controls.

clauses.heading: Operational Controls
clauses.text: Mobile equipment and raised implements shall maintain applicable minimum approach distances from energized electrical infrastructure in accordance with section 3.30 Electrical Safety.

clauses.heading: Operational Controls
clauses.text: Mobile equipment maintenance and repair shall be performed with the equipment isolated, stored energy controlled and raised components mechanically supported in accordance with sections 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment and 3.23 Energy Isolation and Control of Stored Energy.

clauses.heading: Operational Controls
clauses.text: Tire and wheel maintenance involving stored energy hazards, including multipiece or split-rim assemblies, shall be performed in accordance with section 3.37 Tire and Rim Management.

clauses.heading: Underground Mobile Equipment
clauses.text: Mobile equipment designed or intended for underground mining shall meet the applicable safety requirements of ISO 19296, Mining — Mobile Machines Working Underground — Machine Safety, or an equivalent recognized standard. Surface designed mobile equipment shall not be introduced underground unless its suitability for the underground environment has been assessed and any required modifications managed in accordance with section 3.52 Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: Critical controls for mobile equipment shall be identified, assigned performance and verification requirements, and managed in accordance with section 2.6 Critical Control Management, with equipment prevented from operation where a required critical control is absent, ineffective or cannot be verified.

clauses.heading: Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify implementation of this process through field observation, equipment inspection, authorization and competency checks and assurance activities.

processes.title: Light Vehicle Safety
processes.purpose: Light vehicles used for Maaden work are fit for purpose, legally compliant and safely maintained, and that people who drive them are competent, fit and formally authorized, to prevent collisions, rollovers, loss of control, injury and property damage.
processes.scope: This process applies to road-going passengers and utility vehicles classified as light vehicles. It covers Maaden owned, leased, rented and contractor provided vehicles, and privately owned vehicles formally authorized for Maaden work, when operated on public roads, Maaden controlled premises or operational areas.

clauses.heading: Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Business Units and sites shall establish risk-based light vehicle safety arrangements that comply with applicable Saudi traffic law and vehicle registration, insurance, periodic technical inspection and SASO/GSO requirements.

clauses.heading: Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Responsibilities shall be assigned for fleet safety, vehicle acceptance and authorization, driver authorization, inspection, maintenance and assurance.

clauses.heading: Governance and Accountability
clauses.text: Contractor arrangements shall be managed through section 4.1 Contractor EHSS Management and verified by the relevant Maaden contract owner.

clauses.heading: Driver Authorization, Competence and Fitness
clauses.text:
A person shall not drive a light vehicle for Maaden work unless they hold a valid driving license legally recognized in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for the relevant vehicle class and have been formally authorized by Maaden. Authorization shall verify:
a. Relevant driving experience and an acceptable driving record.
b. Completion of Maaden and applicable site induction.
c. Defensive driving training and practical competency assessment appropriate to the vehicle and operating environment.
d. Awareness of applicable In-Vehicle Monitoring System (IVMS), traffic and journey management requirements.
e. Additional competence for off-road, remote area or specialized driving.
f. Current fitness to drive.

clauses.heading: Driver Authorization, Competence and Fitness
clauses.text: Training and competency assessments shall be delivered by competent people or approved providers. Renewal and reassessment intervals shall be established, documented and reviewed based on legal, regulatory and certification requirements, the level of risk, the complexity and frequency of the task.

clauses.heading: Driver Authorization, Competence and Fitness
clauses.text: Business Units and contractors shall maintain a current Authorized Driver Register showing permitted vehicle classes, authorization expiry and applicable route, time, operating or fitness related restrictions. Vehicle allocation shall provide traceability between the driver and vehicle used.

clauses.heading: Driver Authorization, Competence and Fitness
clauses.text: Drivers shall meet section 3.18 fitness for work requirements and shall not drive when affected by fatigue, alcohol, drugs, illness, injury, medication or another condition that could impair safe driving.

clauses.heading: Driver Authorization, Competence and Fitness
clauses.text: Driver authorization shall be reviewed, restricted, suspended or withdrawn following license expiry or suspension, a relevant fitness change, a serious or repeated traffic violation, a significant vehicle incident, demonstrated unsafe behavior or an extended absence from driving. Reinstatement shall require completion of specified corrective actions, reassessment where applicable and approval by the designated authority.

clauses.heading: Vehicle Authorization and Safety Requirements
clauses.text: Maaden owned, leased, rented and contractor light vehicles shall not be used for Maaden-controlled work until they have been formally accepted, authorized and recorded. Acceptance criteria shall address vehicle registration, insurance, statutory technical inspection, age, condition, maintenance status, and compliance with applicable Saudi requirements (SASO/GSO) and Maaden vehicle specifications. Authorization shall be reviewed at defined intervals and withdrawn when the acceptance criteria are no longer met

clauses.heading: Vehicle Authorization and Safety Requirements
clauses.text: Light vehicles shall be selected and configured for the intended use, road and terrain conditions, environmental conditions, passenger capacity and load, and shall be operated within manufacturer limitations. Safety critical systems, including brakes, steering, tires, lights, mirrors, warning devices, occupant restraints and manufacturer- fitted protective systems, shall remain functional and shall not be removed, bypassed or defeated. Vehicles used off- road or in remote areas shall have the capability, tires, ground clearance and additional safety features identified through risk assessment.

clauses.heading: Vehicle Authorization and Safety Requirements
clauses.text: Modifications that may affect vehicle safety, structural integrity, handling, occupant protection or load capacity shall be approved by the vehicle manufacturer or assessed, engineered and certified by a competent engineering authority. Additional rollover protection shall only be installed where required by a Maaden specification or documented risk assessment and shall meet the same approval, engineering and certification requirements.

clauses.heading: Vehicle Authorization and Safety Requirements
clauses.text: Maaden owned, leased, rented and contractor light vehicles used for Maaden controlled work shall be fitted with an IVMS meeting Maaden specifications, unless an exception is supported by an approved risk assessment. The IVMS shall identify the driver, monitor the required driving and journey parameters, remain operational during vehicle use, and be protected against unauthorized interference or disabling. IVMS monitoring, alert escalation and response to identified violations shall be managed through section 3.29 Traffic and Journey Management process.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Defect and Maintenance Control
clauses.text: A documented pre-use inspection shall be completed before a vehicle is first used during each shift and following any event or change that may have affected its safe condition. Identified defects shall be reported and assessed before continued use. A vehicle with a safety critical defect shall be removed from service, secured against unauthorized use, and not returned to service until the defect has been corrected and the vehicle has been verified as safe by a competent person.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Defect and Maintenance Control
clauses.text: Vehicles shall be maintained under a preventive maintenance program based on manufacturer requirements, applicable legal requirements and operating conditions. Maintenance and repair work that may affect vehicle safety shall be performed by competent personnel using parts and methods that meet manufacturer specifications. Vehicles shall not be used when overdue for a legally required inspection or safety critical maintenance.

clauses.heading: Safe Vehicle Operation
clauses.text: Drivers shall comply with applicable traffic laws, approved routes, posted speed limits and site traffic rules, and shall adjust speed and vehicle operation to road, traffic, visibility, weather, vehicle and load conditions.

clauses.heading: Safe Vehicle Operation
clauses.text: Drivers and passengers shall occupy designated seats and wear functioning seat belts whenever the vehicle is moving. Seating and load limits shall not be exceeded, people shall not be carried in cargo areas, and cargo or loose items shall be secured so they do not obstruct safe vehicle operation or emergency egress.

clauses.heading: Safe Vehicle Operation
clauses.text: Drivers shall not use mobile phones or undertake other distracting activities while the vehicle is moving. Operational communication systems shall only be used where necessary for safe operations and without handling the device or compromising vehicle control. Other communication device use shall only occur when the vehicle is parked and secured.

clauses.heading: Safe Vehicle Operation
clauses.text: Vehicles shall be parked in authorized locations, secured against unintended movement and positioned without obstructing emergency routes, equipment or access. Before leaving a vehicle unattended, the engine shall be stopped, the parking brake applied and additional securing measures used where conditions require. Vehicles shall not be refueled while the engine is running or where ignition sources could cause a fire or explosion.

clauses.heading: Safe Vehicle Operation
clauses.text: Following a collision, breakdown or vehicle emergency, the driver shall stop safely, request assistance, take reasonable measures to prevent further harm and follow applicable emergency response and security arrangements. Incidents and near misses shall be reported and managed in accordance with section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship.

clauses.heading: Safe Vehicle Operation
clauses.text: Records necessary to demonstrate driver authorization, vehicle fitness and implementation of applicable light- vehicle controls shall be maintained and retained in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

processes.trigger: if light vehicles are driven, inspected, maintained or used for personnel travel

processes.title: Traffic and Journey Management
processes.purpose: Manage risks arising from the movement and interaction of vehicles, mobile equipment and pedestrians, and from work- related road journeys, through effective traffic planning, route controls, journey risk management, monitoring and emergency arrangements.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden Business Units, Corporate Functions and controlled workplaces where light vehicles, road- going trucks, buses, coaches or mobile equipment interact with one another, pedestrians or rail movements. It also applies to work-related road journeys undertaken under Maaden operational control on public roads, site roads, access roads and remote or off-road routes.

clauses.heading: Management Arrangements and Responsibilities
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions that manage workplace traffic, road journeys or land transport activities shall establish risk-based traffic and journey management arrangements applicable to their activities. The arrangements shall comply with applicable Saudi legal and road authority requirements. ISO 39001, IOGP Report 365 and HSE HSG136 shall be considered as technical references.

clauses.heading: Management Arrangements and Responsibilities
clauses.text: Plant roads and access routes shall comply with applicable SAIS SAF-06 requirements; mine and mineral processing facility roads with applicable SAIS SAF-18 requirements; and mining-site traffic controls with applicable provisions of MSHA 30 CFR Part 56, Subpart H for surface mines and Part 57, Subpart H for underground mines, as technical references.

clauses.heading: Management Arrangements and Responsibilities
clauses.text: Responsibilities shall be assigned to competent personnel for road and area ownership, Traffic Management Plan development, approval and implementation, road inspection and maintenance, journey screening, approval and monitoring, overdue journey escalation, corrective action, and traffic controller, spotter and flagger duties.

clauses.heading: Management Arrangements and Responsibilities
clauses.text: Fatal or material unwanted events involving vehicle interaction, loss of control, rollover or work-related journeys and their associated critical controls shall be managed and verified through the applicable MSHEM EHSS Risk Management and Critical Control Management processes.

clauses.heading: Traffic Management Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish documented traffic controls proportionate to its traffic risks. A Traffic Management Plan shall be established where documented risk assessment identifies significant risks from interactions between pedestrians, vehicles, mobile equipment or rail; traffic density, reversing or restricted visibility or clearance; loading, unloading or logistics activities; or temporary or permanent changes to roads, routes or work areas.

clauses.heading: Traffic Management Planning
clauses.text: Traffic Management Plans shall be based on documented risk assessment and developed with input from competent people representing affected operations and relevant engineering, EHSS, security and emergency response functions. Plans shall be approved by the person accountable for the affected site or area, maintained current and communicated to affected employees, contractors and visitors before exposure to the traffic risks.

clauses.heading: Traffic Management Planning
clauses.text: Traffic Management Plans shall define, as applicable, traffic routes, classifications and access restrictions; direction, speed and right of way rules; controls for intersections, crossings, rail interfaces and restricted clearances; separation of pedestrians, light vehicles and mobile equipment; parking, loading, unloading and passenger transfer areas; reversing and communication controls; and emergency access and escape routes.

clauses.heading: Traffic Management Planning
clauses.text: Traffic controls shall prioritize elimination of unnecessary movement and physical separation of pedestrians, light vehicles and mobile equipment. Where physical separation cannot be achieved, the reasons shall be documented and access control, time separation, traffic sequencing or other risk reduction controls shall be implemented.

clauses.heading: Road and Traffic Controls
clauses.text: Roads and traffic routes shall be designed, constructed and maintained for the vehicles, loads and traffic volumes using them. Road design shall address geometry, surface and drainage, visibility, lighting, signs, intersections, clearances and emergency access. Effective edge protection or restraints shall be provided where drop-offs, dumping activities or overtravel could result in a vehicle overturning. Road and rail crossings shall be controlled to prevent collisions.

clauses.heading: Road and Traffic Controls
clauses.text: Roads and traffic routes shall be inspected at defined intervals and after events or changes that could affect their safety, with identified hazards corrected and affected routes restricted or closed until verified safe for use.

clauses.heading: Road and Traffic Controls
clauses.text: Site traffic rules and arrangements shall control speed, right-of-way, direction of travel, parking, overtaking, communication and reversing; provide appropriate traffic signs, signals, road markings and pedestrian crossings; minimize conflicting vehicle, equipment and pedestrian movements; and ensure temporary or materially changed routes are risk assessed, authorized, marked, communicated and verified before use.

clauses.heading: Road and Traffic Controls
clauses.text: Mine traffic arrangements shall establish controls for interactions among heavy equipment, light vehicles and pedestrians and for access to mining areas, haul and service routes, restricted clearance areas, parking and refuge areas, and maintenance or contractor activities. Pedestrians shall only enter mine traffic routes through designated walkways or specifically controlled work arrangements.

clauses.heading: Journey Management
clauses.text: Work-related journeys shall be evaluated to eliminate or reduce unnecessary travel and identify journeys requiring a documented Journey Management Plan. The criteria shall consider remoteness, route familiarity, journey duration, night or off-road travel, adverse conditions, communication and emergency support limitations, lone travel and security risk. Repeated journeys under stable conditions may be managed through a standing journey plan that defines its applicability, controls, review and change triggers.

clauses.heading: Journey Management
clauses.text: A Journey Management Plan shall define the journey, route, driver, vehicle, passengers and load; applicable hazards and controls; driving and rest arrangements; communication and monitoring requirements; and emergency, recovery and overdue journey arrangements. The journey shall be authorized only after confirming that the driver, vehicle, route, conditions and support arrangements meet applicable requirements.

clauses.heading: Journey Management
clauses.text: Drivers shall comply with the authorized route, driving, rest, communication and check-in arrangements. A journey shall not start or continue when conditions exceed established limits or the driver is fatigued or otherwise unable to drive safely. Significant changes or deviations shall be communicated and reassessed before the journey continues, except where immediate action is necessary to reach a safe location.

clauses.heading: Journey Management
clauses.text: Journeys requiring a Journey Management Plan shall be monitored to the level determined by risk, including required check-ins, significant deviations and confirmation of safe arrival. IVMS or another reliable tracking method shall be used where required by the journey risk assessment and shall remain functional and monitored for the duration of the journey. Missed check-ins, overdue arrival, loss of tracking or significant alerts shall trigger defined contact and escalation actions. Remote journeys shall have communication, emergency and recovery arrangements based on the route, environmental conditions and expected response time.

clauses.heading: Emergency, Violation and Performance Management
clauses.text: Traffic and journey emergency arrangements shall address foreseeable vehicle and journey emergencies and align with section 5.1 Emergency Response Preparedness and Planning process. Vehicle recovery shall be planned and controlled to protect people from vehicle movement, stored energy and recovery forces.

clauses.heading: Emergency, Violation and Performance Management
clauses.text: Business Units and sites shall manage traffic violations and IVMS events, including validation, communication and proportionate action. Serious or repeated violations shall trigger review and, where necessary, restriction, suspension or withdrawal of driving or site access authorization. The effectiveness of traffic and journey controls shall be evaluated using relevant inspection, verification, IVMS, journey, incident and violation information.

clauses.heading: Emergency, Violation and Performance Management
clauses.text: Records necessary to demonstrate implementation of traffic and journey controls shall be maintained and retained in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

processes.trigger: if site traffic, public-road travel, journey planning or vehicle–pedestrian interaction is involved

processes.title: Electrical Safety
processes.purpose: Electrical hazards are identified, assessed, and controlled to prevent fatalities, injuries, occupational illnesses, fires, explosions, and asset damage arising from electrical systems, equipment, and work activities.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden owned, operated, managed, leased, or controlled facilities, projects, and activities where electrical systems, equipment, or electrical hazards are present. It applies to employees, contractors, and other people who perform electrical work or may be exposed to electrical hazards under Maaden's control.

clauses.heading: Electrical Safety Governance and Program
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement, maintain, and periodically review an Electrical Safety Program based on the nature and level of electrical risk. The program shall define roles, responsibilities, and authorization requirements, competency requirements, electrical risk controls and safe work requirements, inspection, testing, and maintenance arrangements, and arrangements for evaluating program performance and improving electrical safety.

clauses.heading: Electrical Safety Governance and Program
clauses.text: Electrical hazards shall be identified, assessed, and controlled in accordance with section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Electrical Safety Governance and Program
clauses.text: Electrical work shall only be performed by personnel who are competent and authorized for the type and scope of work.

clauses.heading: Electrical Safety Governance and Program
clauses.text: Changes to electrical systems, equipment, operating conditions, electrical area classifications, procedures, or work practices that may affect electrical risk shall be managed in accordance with section 3.52 Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Electrical Safety Governance and Program
clauses.text: Relevant lessons from electrical incidents, equipment failures, audits, inspections, assessments, and operating experience shall be communicated and incorporated into electrical risk controls and work practices.

clauses.heading: Planning and Control of Electrical Work
clauses.text: Electrical work shall be planned, risk assessed, authorized, coordinated, and supervised based on the nature and level of electrical risk and in accordance with section 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment process.

clauses.heading: Planning and Control of Electrical Work
clauses.text: Electrical equipment and circuits shall be de-energized and placed in an electrically safe work condition before work begins, unless de-energization would introduce a greater hazard or the work cannot be performed in a de-energized state.

clauses.heading: Planning and Control of Electrical Work
clauses.text: Where energized electrical work is permitted, it shall require documented justification, a task specific risk assessment, authorization by designated personnel, and the permits required by section 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment process.

clauses.heading: Planning and Control of Electrical Work
clauses.text: Controls identified through the risk assessment shall be implemented to protect personnel from electric shock, arc flash, arc blast, inadvertent contact, unauthorized access, and other electrical hazards.

clauses.heading: Electrical Isolation and Establishment of an Electrically Safe Work Condition
clauses.text: Electrical work shall be performed with the equipment de-energized and placed in an electrically safe work condition, unless energized work is justified and controlled in accordance with the energized electrical work requirements of this process.

clauses.heading: Electrical Isolation and Establishment of an Electrically Safe Work Condition
clauses.text: Electrical energy isolation shall be performed in accordance with section 3.23 Energy Isolation and Control of Stored Energy process.

clauses.heading: Electrical Isolation and Establishment of an Electrically Safe Work Condition
clauses.text: Electrical equipment shall not be considered to be in an electrically safe work condition until all applicable electrical energy sources have been identified and isolated, stored electrical energy has been controlled, and absence of voltage has been verified. Generated, induced, and back-fed energy, including energy from batteries, uninterruptible power supplies, photovoltaic systems, and capacitors, shall be considered.

clauses.heading: Electrical Isolation and Establishment of an Electrically Safe Work Condition
clauses.text: Temporary protective grounding shall be applied where identified as necessary to control induced voltage, backfeed, residual electrical energy, or inadvertent energization.

clauses.heading: Electrical Hazard Controls
clauses.text: Electrical shock, arc flash, arc blast, fire, explosion, lightning, static electricity, stray current, and other applicable electrical hazards shall be identified and controlled. Electrical hazards shall be eliminated where practicable, with priority given to engineering controls where elimination is not practicable.

clauses.heading: Electrical Hazard Controls
clauses.text: Electrical studies shall be completed for systems where required to identify electrical hazards, evaluate system performance, and determine necessary protective measures. Study scope shall be based on the system characteristics, electrical hazards, operating conditions, and applicable legal, regulatory, and adopted technical requirements.

clauses.heading: Electrical Hazard Controls
clauses.text: Electrical studies shall be reviewed and updated where necessary following changes to system configuration, fault- current levels, protective devices or settings, operating conditions, significant equipment modifications, incidents, equipment failures, or other evidence that the study data or assumptions may no longer be valid.

clauses.heading: Electrical Hazard Controls
clauses.text: Shock protection boundaries and arc-flash boundaries shall be established, maintained, and applied in accordance with NFPA 70E Article 130, including Tables 130.4(E)(a) and 130.4(E)(b) and Article 130.5. Access to exposed energized electrical conductors or circuit parts shall be controlled in accordance with the applicable boundaries.

clauses.heading: Electrical Hazard Controls
clauses.text: Electrical equipment that may expose personnel to electrical hazards shall be identified and labelled or marked in accordance with NFPA 70E and other applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

clauses.heading: Electrical Hazard Controls
clauses.text: Grounding and bonding systems shall be installed, inspected, tested, and maintained. Their integrity and effectiveness shall be verified before initial service, following modifications or conditions that may affect their performance, and at defined intervals.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Areas, Static Electricity, Lightning and Stray Currents
clauses.text: Hazardous area classifications shall be determined, documented, maintained, and reviewed when changes or new information may affect the classification or ignition risk.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Areas, Static Electricity, Lightning and Stray Currents
clauses.text: Electrical and electronic equipment installed or used in hazardous classified areas shall comply with the applicable area classification and operating conditions.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Areas, Static Electricity, Lightning and Stray Currents
clauses.text: Activities involving flammable or combustible materials shall control ignition risks from static electricity and stray currents through bonding, grounding, equipment selection, and operating controls necessary to prevent hazardous electrical discharge.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Areas, Static Electricity, Lightning and Stray Currents
clauses.text: Lightning protection, grounding, and bonding systems shall be provided, inspected, tested, and maintained where required by the risk assessment or applicable legal, regulatory, permit, or Maaden adopted technical requirements.

clauses.heading: Overhead and Underground Electrical Services
clauses.text: Overhead power lines and underground electrical services shall be identified and controlled to prevent electrical contact, encroachment, mechanical damage, and unintended exposure or energization.

clauses.heading: Overhead and Underground Electrical Services
clauses.text: Work involving cranes, mobile equipment, lifting operations, elevated work platforms, scaffolding, temporary structures, or other activities near energized overhead power lines shall be planned and controlled so that no person, equipment, load, attachment, or material encroaches within the applicable minimum clearance distance. For cranes and derricks in construction, minimum clearance distances shall comply with OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart CC and applicable utility owner requirements.

clauses.heading: Overhead and Underground Electrical Services
clauses.text: Where the applicable minimum clearance distance cannot be maintained, the overhead power line shall be de- energized, isolated, verified as de-energized, and grounded where required, or relocated or protected by an approved engineered means before work begins. These controls shall be established in coordination with the utility owner or person responsible for the electrical system.

clauses.heading: Overhead and Underground Electrical Services
clauses.text: Before excavation, trenching, drilling, or other ground disturbance begins, the presence, location, route, and where relevant, status of underground electrical services shall be verified and the services protected from contact or damage in accordance with section 3.34 Excavation and Trenching process.

clauses.heading: Electrical Equipment Management
clauses.text: Electrical equipment, grounding, bonding, lightning protection, and other electrical protective systems shall be inspected, tested, and maintained in accordance with section 3.50 Asset Integrity Management process.

clauses.heading: Tools, Equipment and PPE
clauses.text: Electrical PPE shall be selected for the identified electrical hazards and exposure levels and managed in accordance with section 3.31 Personal Protective Equipment process.

clauses.heading: Tools, Equipment and PPE
clauses.text: Electrical tools, test instruments, and equipment shall be rated for the electrical hazard, intended task, and operating conditions in which they are used.

clauses.heading: Tools, Equipment and PPE
clauses.text: Electrical tools, test instruments and safety equipment shall be inspected, tested, maintained and, where required, calibrated in accordance with manufacturer instructions and adopted electrical safety requirements, with defective or out of calibration items removed from service.

clauses.heading: Competency and Authorization
clauses.text: Personnel shall perform only electrical work for which they are competent, qualified where required, and currently authorized.

clauses.heading: Competency and Authorization
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain a documented electrical authorization system defining work categories, competency and qualification requirements, authorization scope and limits, approval authority, validity, reassessment, suspension and withdrawal.

clauses.heading: Competency and Authorization
clauses.text: Current authorization for the type and scope of electrical work shall be verified before work begins and remain readily available to personnel assigning, supervising or authorizing the work.

clauses.heading: Competency and Authorization
clauses.text: Contractor personnel shall comply with the same competency, qualification and authorization requirements as Maaden personnel for equivalent electrical work.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness
clauses.text: Credible electrical emergency scenarios, including electric shock, arc flash, arc blast, battery incidents and electrical fires, shall be identified and addressed in applicable emergency preparedness and response plans.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness
clauses.text: Personnel who may encounter an electrical emergency shall receive relevant emergency awareness, with personnel assigned response responsibilities trained and competent for their roles.

processes.title: Personal Protective Equipment
processes.purpose: Establish minimum requirements for the assessment, selection, provision, use, care, and control of personal protective equipment to protect people from hazards that cannot be eliminated or adequately controlled by other measures.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden Business Units and Corporate Functions, employees, contractors, subcontractors, visitors, and other personnel required to use personal protective equipment or protective clothing during Maaden controlled activities.

clauses.heading: PPE Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, document, and maintain PPE arrangements that define responsibilities for the assessment, selection, approval, procurement, provision, use, inspection, maintenance, storage, replacement, and control of PPE.

clauses.heading: PPE Management
clauses.text: PPE shall be selected and used in accordance with the hierarchy of controls where hazards or exposures cannot be eliminated or sufficiently controlled through higher level controls.

clauses.heading: PPE Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall provide required PPE to their employees without charge and shall ensure that contractors provide required PPE to their personnel without charge.

clauses.heading: PPE Management
clauses.text: Employees, contractors, subcontractors, visitors, and other affected personnel shall use, inspect, care for, and report defects in PPE in accordance with applicable requirements and provided instructions.

clauses.heading: PPE Management
clauses.text: PPE selection and use shall be coordinated with relevant hazard and exposure assessments, work control processes, contractor arrangements, emergency response requirements, and applicable specialist protection processes.

clauses.heading: PPE Management
clauses.text: PPE arrangements and requirements shall be reviewed and updated when changes, incidents, findings, performance results, or other information indicate that PPE controls may no longer be effective or compliant.

clauses.heading: PPE Hazard Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess workplaces and activities to identify hazards requiring PPE, considering affected personnel, exposed body areas, exposure conditions, and routine, non-routine, emergency, and foreseeable abnormal activities.

clauses.heading: PPE Hazard Assessment
clauses.text: The assessment shall consider applicable physical, chemical, biological, electrical, thermal, radiation, noise, impact, fall, and airborne contaminant hazards.

clauses.heading: PPE Hazard Assessment
clauses.text: Combined hazards and interactions or incompatibilities among required PPE shall be assessed.

clauses.heading: PPE Hazard Assessment
clauses.text: PPE hazard assessments and resulting PPE requirements shall be documented, communicated to affected personnel and relevant functions, and reviewed when changes could affect their validity or effectiveness.

clauses.heading: PPE Selection and Approval
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall select and approve PPE based on the documented hazard assessment, required protection level, and applicable legal, regulatory, and adopted technical requirements.

clauses.heading: PPE Selection and Approval
clauses.text: Selected PPE shall be appropriate for the task, user, hazards, exposure conditions, environment, and duration of use; properly fit the user; be compatible with other required equipment; and not reduce protection, introduce additional hazards, or unreasonably impair safe task performance.

clauses.heading: PPE Selection and Approval
clauses.text: Approved PPE requirements, protection levels, specifications, combinations, and permitted alternatives shall be documented and communicated to affected personnel and relevant functions.

clauses.heading: PPE Selection and Approval
clauses.text: Electrical and arc-rated PPE shall be selected according to the assessed shock and arc-flash hazards in accordance with NFPA 70E, Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace, and applicable adopted ASTM and IEC product standards.

clauses.heading: PPE Selection and Approval
clauses.text: Eye, face, head, hand, foot, and high-visibility PPE shall comply with Saudi legal and regulatory requirements, including applicable SASO technical regulations and standards, and OSHA 29 CFR part 1910 Subpart I.

clauses.heading: PPE Selection and Approval
clauses.text: Respiratory protection, hearing protection, fall protection PPE, chemical and biological protective PPE, and fire and emergency response PPE shall comply with applicable MSHEM processes and adopted technical standards. Any substitution or deviation from an approved PPE specification shall be assessed and approved before use.

clauses.heading: PPE Conformity, Procurement and Acceptance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall procure PPE that meets approved specifications, the applicable SASO Technical Regulation for Personal Protective Equipment and Clothing, and applicable adopted product standards.

clauses.heading: PPE Conformity, Procurement and Acceptance
clauses.text: Before PPE is accepted, compliance with applicable conformity assessment requirements shall be verified through required certificates, declarations of conformity, technical documentation, product markings, labels, warnings, and manufacturer instructions.

clauses.heading: PPE Conformity, Procurement and Acceptance
clauses.text: PPE shall be obtained from approved sources and shall be identifiable and traceable to the manufacturer, supplier, product model, and applicable conformity documentation where required.

clauses.heading: PPE Conformity, Procurement and Acceptance
clauses.text: PPE shall be inspected upon receipt or before acceptance to confirm that it matches the approved specification, is complete and undamaged, is within its usable service life, and has the required documentation and markings.

clauses.heading: PPE Conformity, Procurement and Acceptance
clauses.text: Contractor provided and personally owned PPE shall meet the same applicable selection, conformity, acceptance, and product standard requirements as PPE provided by Maaden.

clauses.heading: PPE Conformity, Procurement and Acceptance
clauses.text: Counterfeit, recalled, expired, unauthorizedly modified, or otherwise nonconforming PPE shall not be accepted, issued, or used and shall be controlled to prevent unintended use.

clauses.heading: PPE Provision, Use and Specialized Protection
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that approved PPE of the required type, protection level, size, and configuration is available before exposure. Work shall not proceed or continue when required PPE is unavailable or unable to provide the required protection.

clauses.heading: PPE Provision, Use and Specialized Protection
clauses.text: PPE shall be individually assigned where hygiene, fit, traceability, or manufacturer requirements prohibit shared use. Where sharing is permitted, PPE shall be cleaned, disinfected, inspected, and controlled before reissue, as applicable.

clauses.heading: PPE Provision, Use and Specialized Protection
clauses.text: Affected personnel shall use, wear, and adjust designated PPE in accordance with established requirements, training, and manufacturer instructions. PPE shall not be shared where prohibited, used for unintended purposes, or modified without approval.

clauses.heading: PPE Provision, Use and Specialized Protection
clauses.text: People responsible for supervising or controlling an activity shall verify throughout the activity that required PPE is available, correctly used, functional, and capable of providing the required protection.

clauses.heading: PPE Provision, Use and Specialized Protection
clauses.text: Specialized PPE shall be provided and used in accordance with the applicable MSHEM processes and adopted technical standards for respiratory, hearing, electrical, arc-flash, fall, chemical, biological, thermal, fire, and emergency response protection.

clauses.heading: PPE Provision, Use and Specialized Protection
clauses.text: Breathing air supplied to respiratory protective equipment shall meet at least Grade D breathing-air quality in accordance with ANSI/CGA G-7.1 or an equivalent adopted standard.

clauses.heading: PPE Training, Inspection and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that personnel are trained and competent before using required PPE. Training shall address when PPE is required, correct fitting and use, limitations, inspection, care, storage, replacement, and disposal, consistent with OSHA 29 CFR 1910.132, General Requirements, manufacturer instructions, and applicable adopted standards.

clauses.heading: PPE Training, Inspection and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: Personnel competence shall be reassessed, and additional training provided where required, when hazards, tasks, PPE, or workplace conditions change, or when inadequate knowledge or incorrect use is identified.

clauses.heading: PPE Training, Inspection and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: PPE shall be inspected before use and at defined intervals based on the PPE type, conditions of use, exposure, manufacturer instructions, and applicable adopted standards.

clauses.heading: PPE Training, Inspection and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: PPE shall be cleaned, decontaminated, maintained, and stored to preserve its hygiene, integrity, and protective performance.

clauses.heading: PPE Training, Inspection and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: PPE subject to identification, inspection status, service life, expiry, component replacement, or consumable requirements shall be controlled to ensure continued protective performance.

clauses.heading: PPE Training, Inspection and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: PPE shall be repaired or modified only where permitted by the manufacturer, applicable product certification, and adopted standards, and through authorized arrangements.

clauses.heading: PPE Training, Inspection and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: Defective, damaged, contaminated, expired, recalled, or otherwise ineffective PPE shall be removed from service, controlled against unintended use, and repaired, replaced, or disposed of as applicable.

clauses.heading: PPE Training, Inspection and Lifecycle Control
clauses.text: Training, competency, inspection, maintenance, repair, and replacement records shall be maintained where required by applicable requirements, manufacturer instructions, adopted standards, or the PPE arrangements.

clauses.heading: PPE Verification and Performance Monitoring
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify before and during work that required PPE is available, suitable for the identified hazard, exposure, task, and user, properly fitted, serviceable, and correctly used.

clauses.heading: PPE Verification and Performance Monitoring
clauses.text: PPE availability, use, contractor compliance, storage, maintenance, inspection, and lifecycle controls shall be monitored at defined intervals based on risk, operating conditions, and performance, with records maintained where required.

clauses.heading: PPE Verification and Performance Monitoring
clauses.text: PPE incidents, exposure events, defects, failures, misuse, incompatibility, recalls and user concerns shall be reported and reviewed, with PPE requirements reassessed where protective performance may be affected and identified deficiencies corrected, tracked and verified for effective closure.

clauses.heading: PPE Verification and Performance Monitoring
clauses.text: PPE performance, monitoring results, recurring deficiencies and management arrangements shall be periodically reviewed to identify improvements and opportunities to eliminate hazards or reduce reliance on PPE through higher level controls.

processes.keywords: Personal Protective Equipment; personal protective equipment; PPE Management; PPE Hazard Assessment; PPE Selection and Approval; PPE Conformity, Procurement and Acceptance; PPE Provision, Use and Specialized Protection; PPE Training, Inspection and Lifecycle Control; PPE Verification and Performance Monitoring
processes.trigger: if PPE is required as part of the selected control measures

processes.title: Hand and Power Tool Safety
processes.purpose: Establish minimum requirements for the selection, acquisition, inspection, maintenance, storage, transport and safe use of hand and power tools to prevent injuries, occupational illnesses, equipment damage and tool related incidents.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Units and Corporate Functions where hand tools or portable power tools are selected, acquired, supplied, inspected, maintained, stored, transported or used. It covers electric, battery-powered, pneumatic and hydraulic tools and their accessories, attachments, guards, power supplies, cords, plugs, batteries, chargers, hoses, fittings and couplings. It applies to Maaden personnel and contractors who select, use, supervise, inspect, maintain or may be exposed to hazards from these tools.

clauses.heading: Hand and Power Tool Management
clauses.text: Hand and power tools, including accessories and attachments, shall be selected and used only when they are compatible, rated for the intended task and operating environment, and used within the limits specified by the manufacturer.

clauses.heading: Hand and Power Tool Management
clauses.text: Tools shall be procured, hired or accepted for use only when applicable product conformity or certification, operating instructions and safety information are available and verifiable.

clauses.heading: Hand and Power Tool Management
clauses.text: Homemade tools and unauthorized modifications to tools, accessories, attachments, guards, controls or safety devices shall be prohibited.

clauses.heading: Hand and Power Tool Management
clauses.text: Before work commences, hazards associated with hand and power tool activities shall be assessed and controlled in accordance with section 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment process. Tools used where electrical insulation, non-conductivity, non-sparking construction or hazardous area certification is required shall meet the applicable requirements for those conditions.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Maintenance and Defect Control
clauses.text: Hand and power tools, including accessories and attachments, shall be inspected before use and periodically inspected, tested and maintained at frequencies based on tool type, risk, service conditions, frequency of use, manufacturer requirements and operating experience.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Maintenance and Defect Control
clauses.text: Tools requiring certification, specialist inspection, testing or other safety critical periodic verification shall be uniquely identified and included in a controlled inventory showing their current status.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Maintenance and Defect Control
clauses.text: Inspections and tests shall verify the condition and operation of components and safety devices that could affect safe use.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Maintenance and Defect Control
clauses.text: Inspection, testing, maintenance and repair requiring specialist knowledge or authorization shall be performed by competent and, where required, authorized personnel.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Maintenance and Defect Control
clauses.text: Defective, damaged, deteriorated, unauthorized, modified or otherwise unsafe tools shall be removed from service and prevented from unintended use until repaired and confirmed safe through the required inspection, testing or recertification.

clauses.heading: Guards, Controls and Accessories
clauses.text: Guards, handles, controls, interlocks, retaining devices and other safety features shall be installed, maintained and used as designed, without being removed, bypassed, defeated or otherwise made ineffective.

clauses.heading: Guards, Controls and Accessories
clauses.text: Abrasive wheels, cutting discs, wire wheels and other rotating accessories shall be compatible with the tool, rated for the intended application, correctly mounted and guarded, and used within manufacturer defined operating limits.

clauses.heading: Guards, Controls and Accessories
clauses.text: Powered tools shall have controls that prevent unintended starting and enable the operator to maintain control during operation.

clauses.heading: Safe Use of Hand and Power Tools
clauses.text: Hand and power tools shall be used in a manner that maintains control of the tool, with workpieces secured where unintended movement, rotation or ejection could expose personnel to moving parts, reaction forces, ejected materials or other tool related hazards.

clauses.heading: Safe Use of Hand and Power Tools
clauses.text: Tools shall be disconnected from their energy source and, where hazardous energy could cause harm, isolated, depressurized or otherwise made safe before maintenance, adjustment, cleaning, repair, clearing blockages or replacing accessories.

clauses.heading: Safe Use of Hand and Power Tools
clauses.text: Tools shall not be operated until guards, controls, accessories and other safety features disturbed during the activity have been correctly restored.

clauses.heading: Electrical, Pneumatic, Hydraulic and Battery-Powered Tools
clauses.text: Electrical hazards associated with portable electric tools and their power supplies shall be controlled in accordance with section 3.30 Electrical Safety process.

clauses.heading: Electrical, Pneumatic, Hydraulic and Battery-Powered Tools
clauses.text: Pneumatic and hydraulic tool systems shall use hoses, fittings, couplings and restraints that are compatible with the system and rated for the maximum operating pressure.

clauses.heading: Electrical, Pneumatic, Hydraulic and Battery-Powered Tools
clauses.text: Pneumatic and hydraulic tool systems shall be configured and used to prevent attachment ejection, hose separation, hose whip and uncontrolled release of pressure.

clauses.heading: Electrical, Pneumatic, Hydraulic and Battery-Powered Tools
clauses.text: Pneumatic and hydraulic energy shall be isolated, and stored pressure shall be safely released, before pressure- containing components or tool attachments are disconnected or changed.

clauses.heading: Electrical, Pneumatic, Hydraulic and Battery-Powered Tools
clauses.text: Batteries and chargers shall be compatible with the tool and managed in accordance with manufacturer requirements to control electrical, thermal, fire, chemical and physical hazards. Damaged, leaking, swollen, overheated or otherwise defective batteries or chargers shall be removed from service and controlled against unintended use.

clauses.heading: Storage, Transport and Personal Protective Equipment
clauses.text: Tools, accessories and attachments shall be stored and transported in a manner that prevents damage, deterioration, unintended movement and unauthorized use.

clauses.heading: Storage, Transport and Personal Protective Equipment
clauses.text: Tools used or placed where they could fall and harm people, damage equipment or affect operating areas shall be secured or otherwise controlled against falling.

clauses.heading: Storage, Transport and Personal Protective Equipment
clauses.text: Personal protective equipment for hand and power tool activities shall be selected and used based on the tool, task, operating environment and assessed hazards, in accordance with section 3.31 Personal Protective Equipment process.

clauses.heading: Competency Requirements and Verification Process
clauses.text: Personnel who select, use, inspect, test, maintain or repair hand and power tools shall be competent for their activities and receive any specialized training or authorization required for the tool or activity.

clauses.heading: Competency Requirements and Verification Process
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall periodically verify compliance with this process and the effectiveness of hand and power tool controls through risk-based inspection, testing, monitoring and review.
