processes.title: Machine Safety and Guarding
processes.purpose: Machinery and powered equipment hazards are identified and controlled throughout the equipment lifecycle to prevent injury from hazardous movement, unexpected energy release, access to danger zones, ejected materials and loss of control.
processes.scope: This process applies to machinery and powered equipment that Maaden owns, controls, supplies, leases or uses, including contractor provided equipment. It applies to fixed, portable, temporary and integrated machinery systems throughout their lifecycle, from design and procurement to decommissioning.

clauses.heading: Governance and Machinery Risk Management
clauses.text: Machinery safety activities requiring specialist knowledge shall be performed or reviewed by competent personnel.

clauses.heading: Governance and Machinery Risk Management
clauses.text: Machinery shall be uniquely identified, with current information maintained on its hazards, operating limits, safeguards, safety functions, and inspection, verification and maintenance requirements.

clauses.heading: Governance and Machinery Risk Management
clauses.text: Machinery safety requirements shall be incorporated into design, procurement, fabrication, installation, commissioning, operation, maintenance, modification, relocation and decommissioning decisions, including the selection and acceptance of contractor provided machinery.

clauses.heading: Governance and Machinery Risk Management
clauses.text: Before machinery is placed into service, a documented machinery safety risk assessment shall be completed, or an existing assessment shall be verified as applicable and current.

clauses.heading: Governance and Machinery Risk Management
clauses.text: The machinery safety risk assessment shall be reviewed when a repair, modification, relocation, change in use, incident, failure or operating experience could affect the machinery hazards, safeguards or safety functions.

clauses.heading: Governance and Machinery Risk Management
clauses.text: The machinery safety risk assessment shall consider the intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse of the machinery; operation, cleaning, inspection, maintenance and other foreseeable interactions; people who may be exposed and their access to danger zones; mechanical and other relevant hazards, including hazardous energy, pressure and the ejection or release of materials; and foreseeable failure, defeat or bypass of safeguards and safety functions.

clauses.heading: Governance and Machinery Risk Management
clauses.text: The risk assessment shall define the required risk controls, safeguards and safety functions, including their performance and acceptance criteria, and the controls required for residual risk.

clauses.heading: Risk Reduction and Safeguarding
clauses.text: Machinery hazards shall be eliminated through inherently safer design where reasonably practicable, with residual risks reduced in accordance with the hierarchy of controls and engineered safeguards prioritized over administrative controls, warnings and personal protective equipment.

clauses.heading: Risk Reduction and Safeguarding
clauses.text: Machinery hazards that could cause injury shall be safeguarded by preventing access while a hazardous condition exists or stopping the hazardous condition before a person can reach the danger zone.

clauses.heading: Risk Reduction and Safeguarding
clauses.text: Hand tools, feeding devices and material removal devices shall only supplement and not replace required safeguards.

clauses.heading: Risk Reduction and Safeguarding
clauses.text: Guards shall be fixed where access is not required during normal operation and interlocked where access is required, with guard locking provided where the hazard cannot stop before a person can reach the danger zone.

clauses.heading: Risk Reduction and Safeguarding
clauses.text: Guards and protective structures shall be securely retained, withstand foreseeable loads, contain or deflect ejected materials where required, and not introduce additional hazards.

clauses.heading: Risk Reduction and Safeguarding
clauses.text: Guard openings, barriers and perimeter safeguarding shall maintain safety distances that prevent access to danger zones and, where whole-body access is possible, provide controlled entry and measures that prevent hazardous operation while any person remains within the safeguarded space.

clauses.heading: Risk Reduction and Safeguarding
clauses.text: Machinery shall be stable and secured against hazardous unintended movement.

clauses.heading: Machine Controls and Safety Functions
clauses.text: Machinery shall have clearly identifiable and accessible controls positioned to prevent unintended operation and hazardous reaching, including an accessible normal stop control that brings hazardous functions to a safe condition.

clauses.heading: Machine Controls and Safety Functions
clauses.text: Machinery shall require a deliberate start command to initiate or resume hazardous operation following energy restoration, control reset, guard closure or restoration of a protective device, unless automatic restart is necessary and demonstrated to be safe through documented risk assessment.

clauses.heading: Machine Controls and Safety Functions
clauses.text: Where required by the machinery risk assessment, emergency-stop devices shall be identifiable, readily accessible and capable of overriding conflicting operating commands. Emergency stopping shall remain effective until manually reset, and resetting shall not initiate machinery operation. Emergency stopping shall not replace safeguarding, normal stopping controls or required energy isolation.

clauses.heading: Machine Controls and Safety Functions
clauses.text: Interlocked guards shall stop the associated hazardous function or prevent its initiation when opened, removed or displaced.

clauses.heading: Machine Controls and Safety Functions
clauses.text: Safety related control systems shall perform reliably, respond safely to faults and prevent foreseeable bypass or manipulation, in accordance with the machinery risk assessment and applicable international standards.

clauses.heading: Machine Controls and Safety Functions
clauses.text: Reset controls shall allow verification that the danger zone is clear before hazardous operation resumes, using an engineered means where direct verification is not possible.

clauses.heading: Machine Controls and Safety Functions
clauses.text: Presence sensing, pressure sensitive and two-hand controls shall be used only where they prevent access to the danger zone or stop the hazardous condition before it can be reached.

clauses.heading: Operation, Intervention and Hazardous Energy
clauses.text: Machinery shall not be operated where any required guard, interlock, emergency stop device or protective device is missing, damaged, bypassed, defeated or ineffective.

clauses.heading: Operation, Intervention and Hazardous Energy
clauses.text: Before a guard is removed or any part of the body enters a danger zone or line of fire, hazardous motion and energy shall be isolated and stored energy controlled in accordance with section 3.23 Energy Isolation and Control of Stored Energy process.

clauses.heading: Operation, Intervention and Hazardous Energy
clauses.text: Where testing, fault finding or commissioning requires temporary energization, access, hazardous motion and machine operation shall be controlled through a documented task-specific risk assessment.

clauses.heading: Conveyors
clauses.text: Conveyors shall meet the applicable requirements of ASME B20.1, Safety Standard for Conveyors and Related Equipment.

clauses.heading: Conveyors
clauses.text: Conveyors shall be guarded at accessible nip points, pulleys, transfer points, counterweights, screw flights and other hazardous parts, with safe walkways, access routes and designated crossovers provided and riding prohibited unless the conveyor is specifically designed for personnel transportation.

clauses.heading: Conveyors
clauses.text: Conveyors shall incorporate controls that prevent hazardous exposure during start-up, provide an effective pre- start warning where the conveyor is not fully visible from the starting control, and provide accessible emergency stop devices or pull cords wherever people may approach an operating conveyor.

clauses.heading: Conveyors
clauses.text: Inclined conveyors shall have backstops, brakes or equivalent protection where unintended reverse movement could create a hazard. Interdependent conveyors shall be controlled to prevent hazardous material accumulation or movement when associated equipment stops.

clauses.heading: Conveyors
clauses.text: Underground belt conveyors shall use fire resistant belting and meet the applicable fire prevention and protection requirements of SAIS SAF-18 and NFPA 122.

clauses.heading: High Pressure Water Jetting
clauses.text: High-pressure water-jetting systems shall comply with AS 4233.1, ASTM E1575 or EN 1829; use compatible components rated for the maximum operating pressure; have hoses and connections protected or restrained against damage, separation and hose whip; and be inspected before use.

clauses.heading: High Pressure Water Jetting
clauses.text: Manual jetting systems shall require continuous deliberate activation, be protected against unintended operation, rapidly stop or release pressure when the operating control is released, and have an independent emergency shutdown operated by a competent person other than the jetting operator.

clauses.heading: High Pressure Water Jetting
clauses.text: Manual jetting shall be conducted within a controlled exclusion zone, with reaction force, operator stability, communication and line of fire hazards assessed and controlled, and mechanically supported or remotely operated equipment used where safe manual control cannot be maintained.

clauses.heading: High Pressure Water Jetting
clauses.text: High-pressure water-jetting work shall be performed with objects securely supported and not hand-held, and with flexible lances fitted with an engineered device that prevents uncontrolled withdrawal or ejection.

clauses.heading: Abrasive Blasting
clauses.text: Abrasive blasting equipment and operations shall comply with applicable legal requirements and ISO 23779 standards.

clauses.heading: Abrasive Blasting
clauses.text: Abrasive blasting equipment shall be compatible with the abrasive and operating conditions, rated for the maximum operating pressure and protected against unintended pressure release, hose whip, coupling separation, static discharge and unintended abrasive flow.

clauses.heading: Abrasive Blasting
clauses.text: Manual abrasive blasting shall use a hold to activate nozzle control that stops abrasive flow when released, is tested before use, and cannot be bypassed, defeated or secured in the operating position, with reliable communication and controls enabling both the nozzle operator and blasting machine attendant to stop abrasive flow when these roles are performed by different people.

clauses.heading: Abrasive Blasting
clauses.text: Abrasive blasting shall be contained and provided with dust extraction where reasonably practicable. Where full containment is not practicable, exclusion zones and access controls shall prevent exposure of unprotected people. Abrasive materials, coatings and substrates shall be assessed for hazardous contaminants, and lower hazard materials and methods shall be used where reasonably practicable.

clauses.heading: Abrasive Blasting
clauses.text: People shall be protected from the abrasive blast stream, airborne contaminants and hazardous movement of objects being blasted.

clauses.heading: Fixed Workshop Machinery
clauses.text: Fixed workshop machinery shall comply with applicable machine specific standards and manufacturer limitations. Rotating parts, tooling, workpieces, protruding stock and ejected materials shall be guarded, contained or segregated to prevent exposure.

clauses.heading: Fixed Workshop Machinery
clauses.text: Measurement, adjustment, cleaning, lubrication, swarf removal and other interventions shall not expose people to hazardous movement. Machinery shall be stopped and, where required, isolated before these activities. Purpose- designed devices shall be used to remove swarf or materials, and rotating components shall not be stopped by hand.

clauses.heading: Fixed Workshop Machinery
clauses.text: Stationary abrasive wheel machinery shall be fitted with guards capable of containing fragments from wheel failure and use correctly rated and inspected wheels, properly adjusted work rests and tongue guards, and spindle speeds within the wheel and manufacturer limits.

clauses.heading: Design, Procurement and Modification
clauses.text: Machinery and safeguarding shall comply with applicable Saudi legal and regulatory requirements, including SASO 33358 where applicable, approved specifications, manufacturer requirements and international standards.

clauses.heading: Design, Procurement and Modification
clauses.text: Suppliers shall provide the information necessary for safe installation, commissioning, operation, isolation, cleaning, maintenance, modification and decommissioning.

clauses.heading: Design, Procurement and Modification
clauses.text: Modifications to machinery, safeguards, safety related control systems or safety software shall be subject to machinery risk assessment and the applicable Management of Change requirements before implementation.

clauses.heading: Verification, Inspection and Competence
clauses.text: New, relocated or modified machinery shall be verified before operational use against approved specifications, identified safety requirements and defined acceptance criteria. Verification shall confirm the installation, safeguards, safety functions, equipment specific controls and communication of residual risks.

clauses.heading: Verification, Inspection and Competence
clauses.text: Safety functions dependent on stopping time, response time, safeguard position or control system reliability shall be validated by a competent person against defined acceptance criteria. Machinery subject to mandatory conformity assessment, certification or third-party validation shall not be placed into service until the required evidence has been accepted.

clauses.heading: Verification, Inspection and Competence
clauses.text: Guards, protective devices and safety related control functions shall be subject to documented inspection, functional testing and preventive maintenance at frequencies based on risk, manufacturer instructions, operating conditions, failure history and previous results. Defects presenting unacceptable risk shall be corrected before operation, and affected safety functions shall be retested after repair, replacement, adjustment or modification.

processes.title: Excavation and Trenching
processes.purpose: Establish minimum requirements for controlling excavation and trenching hazards to prevent injury, asset damage and environmental impact.
processes.scope: This process applies to excavation, trenching and ground disturbance activities controlled by Business Units and Corporate Functions, including manual and mechanical excavation, ground penetration, drilling, pits, trenches, foundations, shafts, grading, utility work and associated contractor activities.

clauses.heading: Excavation and Trenching Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain documented arrangements for managing excavation and trenching activities.

clauses.heading: Excavation and Trenching Management
clauses.text: Roles, responsibilities and authorities for planning, designing, authorizing, performing, supervising, inspecting and closing excavation work shall be defined.

clauses.heading: Excavation and Trenching Management
clauses.text: Personnel shall be competent, qualified and authorized, as applicable to their assigned responsibilities, with an Excavation Competent Person designated where competent-person oversight is required.

clauses.heading: Planning and Risk Assessment
Planning and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: An excavation plan shall be established with detail proportionate to the risk and define the excavation method, required protective systems, access and area controls, spoil management, inspections and emergency arrangements.

clauses.heading: Planning and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Interfaces with Permit to Work, Energy Isolation, Confined Space Entry, Lifting Operations, Electrical Safety, Working at Height, traffic management, environmental controls and emergency response shall be coordinated where applicable.

clauses.heading: Services, Ground and Structural Integrity
clauses.text: Underground and overhead services shall be identified and located before excavation begins through review of available drawings and records, consultation with relevant service owners and appropriate field verification.

clauses.heading: Services, Ground and Structural Integrity
clauses.text: Services shall be located and verified using suitable detection and safe excavation methods before work could expose or damage them, with exposed services protected, supported, isolated or otherwise controlled as required.

clauses.heading: Services, Ground and Structural Integrity
clauses.text: Where an unidentified, incorrectly located or damaged service is encountered, work shall stop, the area shall be made safe and the applicable responsible parties shall be notified before work resumes.

clauses.heading: Services, Ground and Structural Integrity
clauses.text: Ground and soil conditions shall be assessed by a competent person before excavation and following changes that could affect stability.

clauses.heading: Services, Ground and Structural Integrity
clauses.text: Excavations shall be assessed for potential effects on adjacent structures, foundations, roads, equipment and facilities, with qualified engineer review and approval required where engineered support is necessary or structural stability could be affected.

clauses.heading: Services, Ground and Structural Integrity
clauses.text: Applicable structural requirements shall comply with SBC 303-2024 and the approved engineering basis.

clauses.heading: Excavation Authorization
clauses.text: Excavation work shall be authorized in accordance with section 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment only after confirming that the approved scope, risk assessment and required excavation controls are in place.

clauses.heading: Excavation Authorization
clauses.text: Required service controls, protective systems, access, area controls, equipment, competent personnel and emergency arrangements shall be verified before excavation begins.

clauses.heading: Excavation Authorization
clauses.text: Excavation work shall be stopped where changes to the scope, ground conditions, services, adjacent operations or required controls could affect safety, and resumed only after the risk assessment, excavation plan and authorization have been reviewed and updated.

clauses.heading: Excavation Protective Systems
clauses.text: Personnel exposed to cave-in or ground-collapse hazards shall be protected by an approved protective system suitable for the excavation and ground conditions.

clauses.heading: Excavation Protective Systems
clauses.text: Protective systems shall be selected, designed, installed, used, inspected and removed in accordance with applicable Saudi requirements, SBC 303-2024, OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P, approved engineering information and manufacturer requirements.

clauses.heading: Excavation Protective Systems
clauses.text: Protective systems requiring engineering design shall be designed or approved by a qualified engineer and fully installed, inspected and verified as safe before personnel enter the excavation.

clauses.heading: Access, Excavation Edges and Material Control
clauses.text: Safe access, egress and movement shall be provided and maintained for excavations where personnel entry is required.

clauses.heading: Access, Excavation Edges and Material Control
clauses.text: Excavation edges and surrounding areas shall be protected against falls and unauthorized access, with suitable crossings provided where personnel or equipment are required to cross the excavation.

clauses.heading: Access, Excavation Edges and Material Control
clauses.text: Spoil, materials, equipment and surface loads shall be positioned or controlled to prevent material falling into the excavation, overloading excavation sides or adversely affecting stability.

clauses.heading: Access, Excavation Edges and Material Control
clauses.text: A stairway, ladder, ramp, or other safe means of egress shall be provided in trenches 1.22 m or more in depth and positioned so that lateral travel does not exceed 7.62 m.

clauses.heading: Access, Excavation Edges and Material Control
clauses.text: Loose soil, rock, surface encumbrances, and other unstable materials shall be removed, supported, retained, or otherwise controlled.

clauses.heading: Access, Excavation Edges and Material Control
clauses.text: Open excavations shall remain secured and clearly identified during work interruptions, inactivity and darkness, with suitable lighting and warning devices provided where personnel or vehicles may be exposed.

clauses.heading: Equipment, Traffic and Adjacent Operations
clauses.text: Excavation equipment and vehicles shall be suitable for the work, inspected before use and operated by competent and authorized personnel.

clauses.heading: Equipment, Traffic and Adjacent Operations
clauses.text: Equipment movement, traffic and adjacent operations shall be controlled to prevent harm to personnel and adverse effects on excavation stability, services and structures.

clauses.heading: Equipment, Traffic and Adjacent Operations
clauses.text: Personnel shall be separated from operating excavation equipment, vehicle operating areas and suspended loads through exclusion zones or other effective controls.

clauses.heading: Atmospheric and Emergency Controls
clauses.text: Excavations shall be assessed before personnel enter for hazardous atmospheres, confined space conditions, water ingress, flooding, process releases and restrictions that could affect emergency access or escape.

clauses.heading: Atmospheric and Emergency Controls
clauses.text: Atmospheric testing and monitoring shall be performed where a hazardous atmosphere exists or could reasonably occur, at locations and frequencies determined by the risk assessment and changing conditions.

clauses.heading: Atmospheric and Emergency Controls
clauses.text: Excavations deeper than 1.2 m shall be managed in accordance to section 3.25 Confined Space Entry process.

clauses.heading: Atmospheric and Emergency Controls
clauses.text: Personnel shall not enter or remain in an excavation affected by uncontrolled water accumulation, a hazardous atmosphere or any other condition that could prevent safe escape.

clauses.heading: Atmospheric and Emergency Controls
clauses.text: Emergency and rescue arrangements shall be established before entry where excavation conditions could expose personnel to collapse, hazardous atmospheres, flooding, energy or material release, or restricted access or egress.

clauses.heading: Worksite Verification and Inspection
clauses.text: The Excavation Competent Person shall inspect applicable excavations, adjacent areas, protective systems, access arrangements, services, spoil placement and other required controls before each shift and following events or changes that could increase risk.

clauses.heading: Worksite Verification and Inspection
clauses.text: Work shall be stopped and exposed personnel removed where an unsafe condition is identified, with work resumed only after the condition is corrected and required controls are reverified.

clauses.heading: Worksite Verification and Inspection
clauses.text: Excavations shall be backfilled, covered, barricaded, supported or otherwise secured when work is completed or suspended.

clauses.heading: Worksite Verification and Inspection
clauses.text: Before final closure, affected services, structures, drainage and other systems shall be reinstated, tested or accepted as applicable, and the worksite shall be verified safe before the Permit to Work is closed.

clauses.heading: Worksite Verification and Inspection
clauses.text: Newly discovered, relocated or modified services shall be recorded for updating applicable drawings and asset records.

clauses.heading: Worksite Verification and Inspection
clauses.text: Cave-ins, ground movements, utility strikes, flooding, hazardous atmosphere events, protective system failures and relevant near misses shall be reported and addressed in accordance with section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship.

processes.title: Geotechnical and Ground Control Management
processes.purpose: Geotechnical and ground control hazards are identified, assessed and controlled throughout the mine lifecycle so that ground instability, falls of ground, slope failure, structural collapse, subsidence and other geotechnical events do not create unacceptable risk to people, the environment, assets or operations.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden owned, managed or controlled surface and underground mining activities and mine related projects throughout planning, design, construction, operation, modification, temporary closure and final closure where geotechnical or ground control hazards may exist. It applies to excavations, slopes, mine workings, ground support systems, shafts, waste dumps, stockpiles, engineered ground structures, natural or man-made voids and other areas where ground instability could create EHSS risk.

clauses.heading: Governance, Accountability and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units shall define responsibilities, accountabilities and interfaces for geotechnical and ground control management across relevant technical, operational and EHSS functions.

clauses.heading: Governance, Accountability and Compliance
clauses.text: Geotechnical and ground control arrangements shall comply with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, including applicable requirements of SAF-18 Mines and Mineral Processing Plants. Relevant requirements of 30 CFR Part 56 – Safety and Health Standards for Surface Metal and Nonmetal Mines and 30 CFR Part 57 – Safety and Health Standards for Underground Metal and Nonmetal Mines shall be considered as recognized technical guidance for surface and underground mining, respectively, where relevant and consistent with applicable Saudi requirements.

clauses.heading: Geological, Geotechnical and Hydrogeological Information
clauses.text: Before applicable mine or ground control design is undertaken, sufficient geological, geotechnical, hydrogeological, structural and, where relevant, seismic information shall be collected, analyzed and interpreted by qualified personnel. Documented geological, geotechnical and hydrogeological models and databases shall be established and maintained throughout the mine lifecycle.

clauses.heading: Geological, Geotechnical and Hydrogeological Information
clauses.text: Geotechnical investigation, testing and modelling shall use recognized engineering practices and defined quality control arrangements. Data sources, assumptions and material limitations shall be documented and considered in design and risk decisions.

clauses.heading: Geological, Geotechnical and Hydrogeological Information
clauses.text: Where groundwater, surface water, pore pressure or seismicity could contribute to a credible ground control failure mechanism, assessment, modelling, monitoring and response arrangements proportionate to the identified risk shall be established and integrated into geotechnical design and ground control management.

clauses.heading: Geotechnical Risk Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Each applicable mine or operation shall conduct and maintain a documented geotechnical and ground control risk assessment in accordance with Section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management.

clauses.heading: Geotechnical Risk Assessment and Control
Geotechnical Risk Assessment and Control
clauses.text: Geotechnical critical controls shall be managed in accordance with section 2.6 Critical Control Management, with their performance and verification requirements incorporated into applicable inspection, monitoring and Trigger Action Response Plans.

clauses.heading: Ground Control Management Plan
clauses.text: Each mine shall establish, implement and maintain a Ground Control Management Plan (GCMP) proportionate to its geotechnical risk profile and covering applicable surface and underground ground control hazards throughout the mine lifecycle. The GCMP shall be technically reviewed by a qualified geotechnical professional and approved by the mine manager.

clauses.heading: Ground Control Management Plan
clauses.text: The GCMP shall integrate the applicable requirements of this process, including the technical basis for ground control decisions, geotechnical risks and controls, design requirements, inspection and monitoring arrangements, Trigger Action Response Plans, operational ground control requirements, competency and emergency response interfaces.

clauses.heading: Ground Control Management Plan
clauses.text: The GCMP and the effectiveness of its implementation shall be formally reviewed at least annually and following significant geotechnical incidents, changes that could affect geotechnical risk, design assumptions or control effectiveness, or identification of previously unrecognized failure mechanisms.

clauses.heading: Geotechnical Design and Technical Governance
clauses.text: Geotechnical designs shall be based on current and validated technical data, credible failure mechanisms and recognized engineering methods, with documented design acceptance criteria proportionate to the risk.

clauses.heading: Geotechnical Design and Technical Governance
clauses.text: Designs shall consider relevant lifecycle factors, including mining sequence, blasting, groundwater, seismic loading, adjacent workings and changing mine geometry. Where deformation, yielding or failure of an engineered geotechnical component is intentionally accepted as part of the design, this shall be justified and supported by defined acceptance criteria, monitoring and response requirements.

clauses.heading: Geotechnical Design and Technical Governance
clauses.text: High risk or complex geotechnical designs shall be subject to independent technical review by a person who was not responsible for the original design. The extent of review shall be proportionate to the risk and complexity of the design.

clauses.heading: Geotechnical Design and Technical Governance
clauses.text: Mining activities shall be conducted within the geotechnical operating limits, design assumptions and control measures defined in the approved geotechnical design, Ground Control Management Plan and associated Trigger Action Response Plans.

clauses.heading: Surface Ground Control
clauses.text: Surface mine excavations and ground structures, including pit walls, highwalls, benches, slopes, dumps, stockpiles and embankments, shall be designed, constructed, operated and monitored to maintain stability consistent with the approved geotechnical design and GCMP. Bench, berm, face and slope geometry shall be appropriate to the geotechnical conditions, mining method and equipment used.

clauses.heading: Surface Ground Control
clauses.text: Dumping locations and other areas where mobile equipment may be exposed to unstable ground shall be assessed before use and as conditions change. Where ground stability cannot be assured, appropriate setbacks, restraints, operating restrictions or other controls shall be established.

clauses.heading: Surface Ground Control
clauses.text: Where surface mining is conducted above, adjacent to or through underground workings or other significant voids, their location and condition shall be determined and appropriate controls established. Controls shall address, as applicable, investigation and survey requirements, safe ground thickness, personnel and equipment access, blasting, infill or backfill, barricading, monitoring and response to previously unidentified voids.

clauses.heading: Underground Ground Control
clauses.text: Underground excavations and ground support systems shall be designed, installed and maintained to control ground where personnel work or travel. Ground support design shall define, as applicable, support capacity and deformation characteristics, loading conditions, support type and density, installation sequence, allowable unsupported advance, requirements for intersections and large spans, and testing and quality control requirements.

clauses.heading: Underground Ground Control
clauses.text: Systematic ground support shall, wherever practicable, be designed and installed without requiring personnel to enter unsupported ground beyond the last effective line of support. Where this cannot be achieved, the work shall be supported by a documented risk assessment, an approved safe method of work and independent technical review proportionate to the risk.

clauses.heading: Underground Ground Control
clauses.text: Underground geotechnical design shall address, where applicable, pillar and crown pillar stability, seismicity and rock burst risk, surface subsidence and interaction with natural or man-made voids. Where seismicity or rock burst represents a ground control risk, appropriate design criteria, mining sequence, ground support, monitoring, exposure controls and response arrangements shall be established.

clauses.heading: Geotechnical Inspection, Monitoring and Reconciliation
clauses.text: Inspection and monitoring arrangements shall be established to detect material changes in ground conditions in time to implement corrective action, work restriction or evacuation before loss of control occurs. They shall define applicable methods, locations, frequencies, responsibilities, trigger criteria, communication and data quality requirements. Monitoring equipment relied upon for critical geotechnical decisions or TARP activation shall be inspected, maintained, calibrated and validated.

clauses.heading: Geotechnical Inspection, Monitoring and Reconciliation
clauses.text: Following geotechnical, hydrological, seismic or operational events that could affect ground stability, affected areas shall be reassessed and any required controls implemented before normal activities resume.

clauses.heading: Geotechnical Inspection, Monitoring and Reconciliation
clauses.text: Ground conditions shall be examined by designated competent personnel before work begins, after blasting, when conditions change or indicate increased risk, and at any additional frequencies defined in the GCMP based on risk and applicable regulatory requirements.

clauses.heading: Geotechnical Inspection, Monitoring and Reconciliation
clauses.text: Actual ground performance and monitoring results shall be periodically compared with design assumptions and predicted behavior, with material deviations triggering review and, where necessary, revision of the applicable risk assessment, design, critical controls, GCMP or TARP.

clauses.heading: Trigger Action Response Plans
Trigger Action Response Plans
clauses.text: Monitoring information used to activate a TARP shall be sufficiently reliable and communicated in time to allow the required response.

clauses.heading: Trigger Action Response Plans
clauses.text: TARPs involving potential evacuation or other critical emergency response shall be tested through drills or simulations at least annually and after significant changes, and reviewed for effectiveness following drills, activation or significant geotechnical events.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Ground, Scaling and Fall of Material
clauses.text: Hazardous or potentially unstable ground shall be taken down, supported or otherwise made safe before work or travel is permitted, with affected areas restricted, warning signs posted or barricades installed until the hazard is controlled.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Ground, Scaling and Fall of Material
clauses.text: Damaged or ineffective ground support shall be repaired or replaced before work or travel resumes where its condition could create a hazard.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Ground, Scaling and Fall of Material
clauses.text: Scaling and removal of loose or unconsolidated ground shall be performed by competent personnel using suitable methods and tools from a safe position, with appropriate stand-off distances, exclusion zones and access controls established where people or equipment could be exposed to falling or sliding ground.

clauses.heading: Hazardous Ground, Scaling and Fall of Material
clauses.text: Changes that could affect the approved geotechnical design basis, ground control arrangements or credible failure mechanisms shall be managed in accordance with the applicable Maaden Management of Change requirements.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness and Mine Closure
clauses.text: Ground control emergency scenarios identified through risk assessment or TARPs shall be incorporated into applicable emergency response arrangements, including mine collapse or cave-in where relevant.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness and Mine Closure
clauses.text: Temporary closure, final closure and abandonment planning shall address geotechnical risks and ensure that remaining mine openings, excavations and other ground control hazards are secured, rehabilitated, monitored or otherwise controlled to prevent unacceptable residual risk.

clauses.heading: Competency, Assurance and Records
clauses.text: Personnel performing, supervising or technically approving geotechnical and ground control activities shall be competent for their assigned responsibilities in accordance with section 2.7 EHSS Competency, Awareness and Communication.

clauses.heading: Competency, Assurance and Records
clauses.text: Personnel exposed to ground control hazards shall receive appropriate information and training on hazard recognition, applicable controls and TARPs.

clauses.heading: Competency, Assurance and Records
clauses.text: Business Units shall periodically verify the implementation and effectiveness of geotechnical and ground control arrangements using risk-based performance measures, inspections, monitoring and assurance activities.

clauses.heading: Competency, Assurance and Records
clauses.text: Geological and geotechnical data, models, risk assessments and material design information necessary to understand and safely manage the long term geotechnical and ground control basis shall be retained for the life of the facility.

processes.title: Underground Mines Ventilation, Fire and Refuge Safety
processes.purpose: Underground mine ventilation, fire and explosion prevention, emergency egress and refuge arrangements are established and maintained to provide a safe underground working environment, prevent and control fires and explosions, and enable safe evacuation or refuge during emergencies.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden owned, managed or controlled underground mining operations and associated projects throughout their lifecycle. It applies, as relevant, to underground workplaces, ventilation systems, fire and explosion hazards, mobile and fixed equipment, combustible and flammable materials, refuge chambers, escapeways, atmospheric monitoring and emergency arrangements.

clauses.heading: Governance, Risk and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units shall define responsibilities and accountabilities for underground ventilation, fire and explosion controls, refuge arrangements and escapeways.

clauses.heading: Governance, Risk and Planning
clauses.text: Underground ventilation, fire protection, refuge and emergency-egress arrangements shall comply with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, including SAF-18 Mines and Mineral Processing Plants and applicable SAIS Safety and Fire Protection Directives, with relevant provisions of 30 CFR Part 57 used as technical guidance where consistent with Saudi requirements.

clauses.heading: Governance, Risk and Planning
clauses.text: Underground ventilation, fire, explosion, emergency egress and refuge hazards shall be assessed and managed in accordance with Section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management.

clauses.heading: Governance, Risk and Planning
clauses.text: Underground ventilation, fire, explosion, emergency egress and refuge hazards shall be assessed and managed in accordance with section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management, considering credible atmospheric, heat, flammable gas, combustible dust, ignition, equipment fire, smoke propagation, power loss, evacuation and refuge scenarios.

clauses.heading: Governance, Risk and Planning
clauses.text: Ventilation, fire, explosion, emergency egress and refuge risks requiring critical controls shall be managed in accordance with section 2.6 Critical Control Management.

clauses.heading: Ventilation Management
Ventilation Management
clauses.text: Underground ventilation shall maintain a safe and respirable atmosphere, control heat and humidity, and dilute or remove hazardous gases, diesel emissions (DPM), dust, fumes and other airborne contaminants.

clauses.heading: Ventilation Management
Ventilation Management
clauses.text: Critical ventilation systems shall incorporate monitoring, alarms, reliability and backup arrangements based on risk and applicable requirements.

clauses.heading: Ventilation Management
clauses.text: Loss or failure of required ventilation shall result in equipment shutdown, work stoppage, access restriction or personnel withdrawal until safe conditions are restored and verified.

clauses.heading: Ventilation Management
clauses.text: Atmospheric conditions shall be monitored at locations and frequencies defined by the Ventilation Plan, risk assessment and applicable requirements.

clauses.heading: Ventilation Management
clauses.text: Monitoring instruments used for critical decisions or TARP activation shall be maintained, calibrated and verified.

clauses.heading: Ventilation Management
clauses.text: Personnel shall be withdrawn and access restricted where atmospheric conditions exceed established safe limits, except for controlled entry specifically authorized for emergency response or recovery.

clauses.heading: Fire and Explosion Management
clauses.text: Each underground mine shall establish and maintain a Fire and Explosion Management Plan proportionate to its risk profile that addresses credible fire and explosion scenarios, fuel and ignition controls, detection and suppression arrangements, powered equipment, fixed plant, combustible materials, TARPs and emergency response interfaces.

clauses.heading: Fire and Explosion Management
clauses.text: Where required by SAF-18, fixed fire protection and suppression requirements shall be determined through a Fire Hazard Analysis performed or approved by an appropriately qualified engineer experienced in mining fire hazards.

clauses.heading: Fire and Explosion Management
clauses.text: Underground fire prevention and protection arrangements shall comply with applicable requirements of SAF-04, SAF-18, NFPA 122 and NFPA 520 and, where applicable, NFPA 30.

clauses.heading: Fire and Explosion Management
clauses.text: Underground operations shall control ignition sources, combustible materials, flammable and combustible liquids, equipment leaks, combustible waste, hot work and other credible sources of fire or explosion.

clauses.heading: Fire and Explosion Management
clauses.text: Where flammable gas, combustible dust, frictional ignition or spontaneous combustion hazards are credible, detection, monitoring, prevention and response controls shall be established.

clauses.heading: Fire and Explosion Management
clauses.text: Electrical and electronic equipment used where flammable atmospheres may occur shall be suitable for the applicable hazardous area classification and comply with SAF-12, applicable NFPA 70 requirements and Section 3.30 Electrical Safety.

clauses.heading: Fire and Explosion Management
clauses.text: Powered mobile equipment, fixed plant equipment and conveyor systems shall be assessed for fire risk and provided with fire prevention, detection, isolation, suppression and firefighting controls based on the identified hazards and applicable requirements. Self-propelled equipment used underground shall be provided with a Compressed Air Foam (CAF) fire suppression system and at least one portable multipurpose dry chemical extinguisher, with the fixed suppression system arranged to shut down the protected equipment upon actuation.

clauses.heading: Fire and Explosion Management
clauses.text: Fire detection, alarm, warning, suppression and firefighting systems shall be provided, inspected, tested and maintained in accordance with the Fire Hazard Analysis, SAF-04, SAF-18, NFPA 122, NFPA 520 and approved design requirements.

clauses.heading: Refuge, Escapeways and Emergency Egress
clauses.text: Underground mines shall provide and maintain refuge chambers or refuge areas where required by SAF-18, NFPA 520, risk assessment and the approved mine emergency strategy. Refuge capacity shall be at least twice the maximum number of persons expected to rely on the refuge. Where travel distance to an exit exceeds 400 m, one or more refuge areas or a separate means of egress shall be provided based on risk assessment. Refuge location, capacity and required operating duration shall account for credible emergencies, workforce distribution, escapeways, travel time and self-rescuer capability.

clauses.heading: Refuge, Escapeways and Emergency Egress
Refuge, Escapeways and Emergency Egress
clauses.text: Underground mines shall establish and maintain emergency escapeways in accordance with SAF-18, NFPA 520 and the approved mine emergency strategy.

clauses.heading: Refuge, Escapeways and Emergency Egress
clauses.text: Escapeways shall be protected, clearly identified, unobstructed and available under foreseeable emergency conditions.

clauses.heading: Refuge, Escapeways and Emergency Egress
clauses.text: Underground workplaces shall have independent means of evacuation where required by applicable legal, regulatory or adopted technical requirements.

clauses.heading: Refuge, Escapeways and Emergency Egress
clauses.text: Where independent evacuation routes cannot be provided, alternative egress or refuge arrangements shall be justified by risk assessment and approved through applicable mine design, emergency planning and Management of Change processes.

clauses.heading: Refuge, Escapeways and Emergency Egress
clauses.text: Refuge locations, capacities, escapeways, emergency routes and relevant ventilation circuits shall be shown on current mine emergency plans.

clauses.heading: Refuge, Escapeways and Emergency Egress
clauses.text: Travel time to safe egress or refuge shall be validated against workforce locations, credible emergency conditions and the capability and rated duration of the self-rescuers provided.

clauses.heading: Refuge, Escapeways and Emergency Egress
clauses.text: All personnel required to go underground shall be provided with an approved self-rescue device having a minimum one hour rated duration and suitable for the identified underground emergency hazards.

clauses.heading: Refuge, Escapeways and Emergency Egress
clauses.text: Personnel required to go underground shall receive training in mine emergency actions and the location, limitations and correct use of applicable self-rescue devices before undertaking underground work and at least annually thereafter.

clauses.heading: Refuge, Escapeways and Emergency Egress
clauses.text: Reliable emergency communications shall be available for underground personnel, refuge locations and other locations identified through risk assessment and emergency planning.

clauses.heading: Emergency Conditions and Re-entry
clauses.text: TARPs shall be established for critical ventilation, atmospheric, fire, explosion, refuge and escapeway conditions and define trigger levels, alarms, equipment shutdown, stop-work and withdrawal criteria, communication and escalation requirements, emergency activation, and conditions for re-entry or resumption of work.

clauses.heading: Emergency Conditions and Re-entry
clauses.text: Underground fire, ventilation failure, evacuation, refuge and communication arrangements shall be integrated with the applicable Emergency Response Plan and periodically tested through drills or simulations.

clauses.heading: Emergency Conditions and Re-entry
Review and Verification
clauses.text: Ventilation Plans, Fire and Explosion Management Plans, risk assessments, TARPs and emergency arrangements shall be formally reviewed at least annually and following relevant incidents, significant changes or evidence that required controls may be ineffective.

clauses.heading: Review and Verification
clauses.text: Changes affecting ventilation, fire and explosion controls, refuge arrangements or escapeways shall be managed in accordance with Section 3.52 Management of Change.

clauses.heading: Review and Verification
clauses.text: Business Units shall verify the implementation and effectiveness of critical underground ventilation, fire, refuge and escapeway controls.

clauses.heading: Review and Verification
clauses.text: Personnel performing underground ventilation, fire-protection, refuge or emergency-safety responsibilities shall be competent in accordance with Section 2.7 EHSS Competency, Awareness and Communication.

processes.title: Tire and Rim Management
processes.purpose: Maaden manages tires, wheels, rims and associated assemblies throughout their lifecycle to prevent uncontrolled release of stored energy, tire fires, bursts and explosions, separation or projection of components, vehicle loss of control, and crushing or struck-by incidents.
processes.scope: This process applies to tires, wheels and rims fitted to mining and other heavy mobile equipment throughout their lifecycle, including selection, use, inspection, maintenance, repair and disposal.

clauses.heading: Tire and Rim Management Governance
clauses.text: Business Units shall implement and maintain documented arrangements for managing tires, wheels, rims and associated assemblies throughout their lifecycle, from selection and procurement through disposal.

clauses.heading: Tire and Rim Management Governance
clauses.text: Roles, responsibilities, authorities and competency requirements shall be defined for people who perform, inspect, supervise or authorize tire and rim activities. Safety critical tire and rim work shall be performed only by people who have been assessed as competent and authorized for the assigned activities.

clauses.heading: Tire and Rim Management Governance
clauses.text: Contractor personnel and service providers shall comply with applicable Maaden tire and rim requirements.

clauses.heading: Risk Assessment and Critical Controls
clauses.text: Business Units shall identify and assess hazards and credible consequences associated with tires, wheels, rims and associated assemblies throughout their lifecycle in accordance with section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Risk Assessment and Critical Controls
clauses.text: Critical controls for applicable tire, wheel and rim fatal risk scenarios shall be identified and managed in accordance with section 2.6 Critical Control Management process.

clauses.heading: Selection and Procurement
clauses.text:
Tires, wheels, rims and associated components shall be selected in accordance with equipment manufacturer requirements and for the intended application, including load, speed, duty cycle, inflation pressure, haul profile, terrain, environmental conditions, operating temperature, wheel-end heat exposure and foreseeable abnormal operating conditions. Earth-mover tires and rims shall conform, as applicable, to ISO 4250-1, ISO 4250-2 and ISO 4250-3. Tires and rims for mobile cranes and similar specialized machines shall conform, as applicable, to ISO
10571.

clauses.heading: Selection and Procurement
clauses.text: Only compatible tires, wheels, rims and associated components identified through current OEM or manufacturer matching information shall be assembled and used together.

clauses.heading: Selection and Procurement
clauses.text: Current manufacturer specifications, compatibility information, operating limits, inspection and rejection criteria, tightening torques and maintenance requirements shall be available to people responsible for selection, procurement, acceptance or servicing.

clauses.heading: Selection and Procurement
clauses.text: Multipiece rim assemblies shall not be specified, installed or used on light vehicles. Light vehicles shall be fitted with single piece rims approved by the vehicle manufacturer or verified as compatible with the vehicle and tire application by a competent person using manufacturer information.

clauses.heading: Selection and Procurement
clauses.text: Tires, wheels, rims and associated components shall be inspected against defined acceptance criteria before initial use, with nonconforming items identified, segregated and prevented from use.

clauses.heading: Receipt, Identification and Traceability
clauses.text: Tires, wheels, rims and associated components shall be verified on receipt against specified acceptance criteria, including identity, specification, condition and compatibility.

clauses.heading: Receipt, Identification and Traceability
clauses.text: Tires, wheels, rims and associated components requiring traceability shall be uniquely identified, and records of their relevant inspection, testing, repair and service history and current status shall be maintained against that identification. Traceability requirements shall be determined by risk assessment, manufacturing requirements and applicable standards.

clauses.heading: Receipt, Identification and Traceability
clauses.text: Tires, wheels, rims and associated components that are damaged, defective, suspect or otherwise not approved for service shall be clearly identified, segregated where practicable and prevented from use until their serviceability is determined.

clauses.heading: Storage and Handling
clauses.text: Tires, wheels, rims and associated components shall be stored in designated areas that control rolling, toppling, fire, vehicle interaction, damage and deterioration risks. Rubber tires and related products shall be stored in accordance with applicable manufacturer requirements and ISO 2230.

clauses.heading: Storage and Handling
clauses.text: Tires, wheels, rims and assemblies shall be lifted, handled and transported using equipment designed or verified for the intended task and rated for the known load. Handling equipment shall be operated within its rated capacity and applicable manufacturer requirements, in accordance with section 3.26 Lifting Operations process.

clauses.heading: Storage and Handling
clauses.text: People shall not work, stand or pass beneath suspended or elevated tires, wheels, rims or assemblies.

clauses.heading: Storage and Handling
clauses.text: Tires and assemblies shall not be inflated or deflated while gripped or supported by tire-handling equipment unless the equipment manufacturer expressly permits that use and the equipment is designed and rated for the resulting loads.

clauses.heading: Maintenance, Inspection and Repair
clauses.text: Inspection, monitoring, testing and maintenance requirements for tires, wheels, rims and associated assemblies shall be established based on applicable manufacturer instructions, operating conditions, duty severity, service history and risk. These requirements shall include inspection of wheel and rim components when disassembled and at defined intervals for wear, corrosion, cracking, distortion, fatigue, damage and compatibility.

clauses.heading: Maintenance, Inspection and Repair
clauses.text: Tire repairs shall be performed within applicable tire manufacturer limits and shall be inspected and authorized before return to service. Earth mover tires shall be operated within the applicable load and inflation pressure limits specified by the equipment OEM and tire manufacturer and consistent with ISO 4250-2.

clauses.heading: Maintenance, Inspection and Repair
clauses.text: Safety related defects shall be assessed and corrected before they create a hazard. Equipment, tires, wheels, rims or associated components for which continued operation is hazardous shall be removed from service, identified against further use and verified as serviceable before return to service, consistent with MSHA 30 CFR 56.14100(b)– (c) and 57.14100(b)–(c).

clauses.heading: Maintenance, Inspection and Repair
clauses.text:
Pre-use inspections conducted in accordance with section 3.27 Mobile Equipment Safety process shall include externally visible tire, wheel and rim conditions, including damage, abnormal wear, signs of incorrect inflation and loose or missing fasteners, consistent with the pre-shift examination requirements of MSHA 30 CFR 56.14100(a) and
57.14100(a).

clauses.heading: Maintenance, Inspection and Repair
clauses.text: Tire service equipment and safety devices shall be designed or verified for their intended use, appropriately rated, inspected and maintained in accordance with applicable manufacturer requirements and relevant MSHEM processes. Measuring and torque equipment whose accuracy affects safety shall be calibrated or verified at defined intervals.

clauses.heading: Maintenance, Inspection and Repair
clauses.text: Changes that may affect tire, wheel or rim compatibility, operating limits, integrity, servicing or risk controls shall be managed in accordance with section 3.52 Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Tire and Rim Servicing
clauses.text: Tire and rim activities shall be performed under documented procedures that define authorized people, task sequence and critical controls. Servicing shall be conducted in a designated service area or controlled field work area with a load-bearing surface, controlled access, task lighting and applicable exclusion zones.

clauses.heading: Tire and Rim Servicing
clauses.text: Before wheel removal or servicing, equipment shall be isolated, immobilized and supported against rolling, articulation, falling or lowering. Controls shall comply with Section 3.23 Energy Isolation and Control of Stored Energy, and the applicable technical requirements of MSHA 30 CFR 56.14105, 57.14105, 56.14211 and 57.14211.

clauses.heading: Tire and Rim Servicing
clauses.text: Before demounting, repair or wheel removal, tires shall be completely deflated, the valve core removed and zero pressure verified from outside the potential trajectory. Tires that are damaged, suspected to be unsafe or significantly underinflated shall be completely deflated before wheel removal. Where either tire or wheel in a dual assembly is damaged or suspected to be unsafe, both tires shall be completely deflated. Controls shall meet the applicable technical requirements of OSHA 29 CFR 1910.177 and MSHA 30 CFR 56.14104 and 57.14104.

clauses.heading: Tire and Rim Servicing
clauses.text: Tires shall be inflated using a verified restraining device or engineered stand-off arrangement appropriate to the wheel type, size and inflation pressure. Inflation equipment shall permit pressure control and monitoring from outside the potential trajectory. Inflation shall be continuously attended and shall not exceed manufacturer or equipment OEM pressure limits. Controls shall meet the applicable technical requirements of OSHA 29 CFR 1910.177, including 1910.177(d)(4), and MSHA 30 CFR 56.14104 and 57.14104.

clauses.heading: Tire and Rim Servicing
clauses.text: Before inflation, components shall be inspected and verified as compatible, serviceable, correctly positioned, seated and locked using current OEM or manufacturer information. Pressurized components shall not be struck, adjusted or repositioned. Wheel fasteners shall be tightened and verified to OEM-specified torque, including re-torque where required.

clauses.heading: Tire and Rim Servicing
clauses.text: Heat shall not be applied to a tire, wheel, rim, associated component or fastener while a tire is mounted. Wheel and rim components shall not be welded, brazed, heated or reworked unless permitted by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.177(e), (f) and (g), authorized by the component manufacturer and completed under an approved repair specification. Components that cannot be safely repaired shall be removed from service.

clauses.heading: Tire and Rim Servicing
clauses.text: Equipment affected by tire overheating, fire, electrical contact, lightning exposure, suspected pyrolysis or another condition capable of delayed failure shall be stopped and isolated. Exclusion zones and restricted approach periods shall be established using documented OEM, tire manufacturer and emergency response criteria.

clauses.heading: Tire and Rim Servicing
clauses.text: The affected assembly shall not be approached, moved, deflated or serviced until the defined criteria have been met and an authorized competent person confirms that work may proceed. Emergency responders shall act under an approved emergency response plan in accordance with section 5.1 Emergency Response Preparedness and Planning.

clauses.heading: End of Life and Disposal
clauses.text: Tires, wheels and rims removed from service shall be identified and segregated to prevent unauthorized reuse pending repair, return to the supplier or disposal.

clauses.heading: End of Life and Disposal
clauses.text: Condemned tires, wheels and rim components shall be rendered unusable before disposal and managed in accordance with section 3.6 Waste Management, and applicable environmental requirements.

processes.title: Explosives and Blasting Management
processes.purpose: Explosives and blasting activities are authorized, planned, conducted and verified so that explosive materials remain secure and accounted for, unintended initiation is prevented, blast effects are controlled, and people, assets, underground workings, communities and the environment are protected.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Units, Corporate Functions and contractors that manufacture, store, transport, handle, use or dispose of explosive materials, conduct blasting, or may expose people, infrastructure, communities or the environment to blast effects.

clauses.heading: Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall comply with applicable explosives legislation and authority requirements and hold the required licenses, permits and approvals before explosive materials are manufactured, procured, stored, transported or used. SAIS SAF-14, including the Declaration of Compliance under Section 15, shall be met. NFPA 495 shall be the minimum technical basis, supported by NFPA 400 Chapter 11 and NFPA 498 where applicable.

clauses.heading: Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall appoint an accountable person for explosives and blasting, a custodian for each storage location and an authorized blaster for each blast. Only competent, authorized and appropriately licensed personnel shall conduct explosives or blasting activities.

clauses.heading: Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall implement an explosives and blasting management plan proportionate to their activities and risks. The plan shall define how applicable legal, authority, manufacturer, NFPA 495 and this process’s requirements are implemented, including controls for the explosives lifecycle, blasting, misfires and emergencies.

clauses.heading: Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish acceptance criteria and monitoring methods for ground vibration, air overpressure, flyrock and blast fumes that meet applicable permit and authority requirements and NFPA 495.

clauses.heading: Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Explosives and blasting hazards shall be managed under section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management process and, where a material unwanted event is identified under section 2.6 Critical Control Management process.

clauses.heading: Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Changes to explosive materials, initiation systems, blast designs, facilities or transport arrangements shall be managed under section 3.52 Management of Change.

clauses.heading: Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Contractors conducting explosives or blasting activities shall meet the requirements of section 4.1 Contractor EHSS Management and the applicable requirements of this section.

clauses.heading: Explosive Materials, Storage and Transport
clauses.text: Only explosive materials and initiation systems authorized by the applicable authority and accepted by Maaden shall be used. Products shall be classified, compatible and used within their approved conditions in accordance with SAIS SAF-14 Section 6, NFPA 495 and manufacturer requirements. Detonators and initiating devices shall be segregated from other explosives until required for priming or loading unless an authority approved alternative complies with NFPA 495.

clauses.heading: Explosive Materials, Storage and Transport
clauses.text: Explosive materials shall be stored only in licensed facilities authorized for their classification and quantity. Storage facilities shall be sited, separated, constructed, protected and maintained in accordance with SAIS SAF-14 Sections 8–10 and applicable NFPA 495 quantity-distance requirements.

clauses.heading: Explosive Materials, Storage and Transport
clauses.text: Continued use of a facility that does not meet applicable quantity-distance requirements shall require a quantitative risk assessment, compensating controls and written approval from SAIS.

clauses.heading: Explosive Materials, Storage and Transport
clauses.text: Permanent underground explosive storage shall be permitted only where expressly authorized by SAIS and where development, egress, siting, ventilation, fire risk, security and emergency arrangements have been assessed under section 3.36 Underground Mines Ventilation, Fire and Refuge Safety process.

clauses.heading: Explosive Materials, Storage and Transport
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain traceable explosives inventory, reconcile each issue and return, complete physical stock counts at least monthly and promptly return unused materials to authorized storage. Access, keys and initiation equipment shall be controlled under SAIS SAF-14 Section 12 and SAIS Security Directives. Losses, discrepancies or security breaches shall be reported under authority requirements.

clauses.heading: Explosive Materials, Storage and Transport
clauses.text: Transportation of explosive materials shall comply with SAIS SAF-14 Section 14 and NFPA 495, including requirements for authorization, compatibility, custody, security, routes, stops and emergency arrangements; applicable NFPA 498 requirements for safe havens and interchange lots; and, for off-site transport, section 3.43 Transportation of Dangerous Goods and Materials.

clauses.heading: Explosive Materials, Storage and Transport
clauses.text: Manufacture, sensitization or on-site production of explosives or blasting agents shall require specific government or authority approval under SAIS SAF-14 Section 5 and shall meet NFPA 495.

clauses.heading: Explosive Materials, Storage and Transport
clauses.text: Ammonium nitrate shall be stored, handled and used in accordance with SAIS SAF-14 Section 7 and NFPA 400 Chapter 11.

clauses.heading: Explosive Materials, Storage and Transport
clauses.text: Maintenance or modification involving potential ignition, impact or contamination shall not begin at an explosives facility or vehicle until explosive materials have been removed or protected under MSHEM sections 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment and 3.22 Hot Work and Ignition Source Control processes.

clauses.heading: Explosive Materials, Storage and Transport
clauses.text: Vehicles and equipment shall be confirmed free of explosive materials before maintenance.

clauses.heading: Blast Planning and Execution
clauses.text: Each blast shall have a documented design meeting NFPA 495 and applicable authority requirements and approved by a person authorized for the type and scale of blasting. Design assumptions, critical controls, field and hole conditions, exclusion requirements and monitoring needs shall be verified before loading or firing. Deviations beyond approved tolerances shall be assessed and authorized before work continues.

clauses.heading: Blast Planning and Execution
clauses.text: The blast site and risk-based exclusion zone shall remain controlled from the arrival of explosives until the authorized blaster issues the all-clear. Access shall be restricted and unrelated people, vehicles and activities excluded. Loaded blasts shall be fired without unnecessary delay; any delay shall be authorized and the blast secured, monitored, handed over and recorded.

clauses.heading: Blast Planning and Execution
clauses.text: Initiation systems shall be installed, connected and tested under the approved blast design, manufacturer instructions and NFPA 495, and shall remain under the authorized blaster’s control. Measures shall prevent unintended initiation from lightning, radio frequency energy, stray current, static electricity or other energy sources, with activities suspended and people withdrawn where required.

clauses.heading: Blast Planning and Execution
clauses.text: Before firing, the authorized blaster shall verify that warnings and notifications have been given, people and equipment are in safe locations, access points are effectively controlled, safe escape arrangements are available and affected facilities, underground workings and external parties have been notified where required.

clauses.heading: Blast Planning and Execution
clauses.text: Re-entry shall not occur until the applicable waiting period has elapsed, fumes and atmospheric conditions are acceptable, the area has been examined for misfires and other hazards, and the authorized blaster has issued the all clear. Waiting and re-entry criteria shall meet NFPA 495, manufacturer and applicable authority requirements.

clauses.heading: Blast Planning and Execution
clauses.text: Business Units and sites shall maintain a misfire procedure meeting NFPA 495 and applicable authority requirements. Any charge suspected of failing to initiate as designed shall be treated as a misfire; the area shall remain secured, access restricted and the required waiting period observed. Misfires shall be resolved under an authorized blaster, with drilling or disturbance prohibited until formal release, and shall be recorded and reported.

clauses.heading: Blast Planning and Execution
clauses.text: Recovered, damaged, deteriorated, contaminated or unidentifiable explosive materials shall be quarantined, secured and disposed of only by authorized specialists at an approved location in accordance with NFPA 495, manufacturer requirements, authority approvals and documented Business Unit or site procedures.

clauses.heading: Special Activities and Emergency Controls
clauses.text: Blasting in gassy, dusty, hot, oxidizing, reactive or sulfide bearing ground shall not proceed until the ground and material conditions have been tested and characterized and appropriate explosive selection, loading time limits, monitoring and withdrawal criteria have been approved. Testing shall occur before initial use, following relevant changes and at a periodic frequency established by the Business Unit or site based on the risk assessment, technical specialist advice and explosive manufacturer recommendations.

clauses.heading: Special Activities and Emergency Controls
clauses.text: Underwater, compressed air and other specialized blasting methods shall be supported by appropriate technical expertise, a documented risk assessment and an approved procedure meeting NFPA 495 and applicable authority requirements. The procedure shall address the method specific interaction with vessels, diving or swimming activities, communication signals, charge identification, misfire recovery, unintended electrical currents, pressure- lock controls, electrical bonding and grounding, personnel restrictions and breakthrough conditions, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Special Activities and Emergency Controls
clauses.text: Where a fire has reached, or cannot be prevented from reaching, explosive materials or ammonium nitrate, the area shall be evacuated immediately, and no attempt shall be made to fight the fire.

clauses.heading: Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish inspection, testing and maintenance requirements for explosives facilities, vehicles, bulk loading, blasting and initiation equipment and monitoring instruments. Defects affecting security, explosive condition, transport, loading, initiation or monitoring shall be corrected before further use.

clauses.heading: Verification and Improvement
clauses.text: Each blast shall have a traceable record meeting NFPA 495 and applicable authority requirements. Blast performance and control effectiveness shall be evaluated using blast records, inventory reconciliation, monitoring results, flyrock, fumes, misfires, deviations and complaints. Abnormal outcomes and repeated control failures shall be reported and investigated under MSHEM section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship, with corrective actions tracked to closure.
