processes.title: Drilling Operations Safety
processes.purpose: Establish and maintain safe systems of work for drilling operations, from planning and mobilization through drilling, maintenance, demobilization and rehabilitation, to prevent harm to people, the environment, assets and operations.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Business Units and Corporate Functions, employees, contractors, subcontractors, service providers and visitors involved in or exposed to drilling operations under Maaden’s operational control. Covers all drilling methods, including auger, RAB, air-core, reverse-circulation, diamond core, sonic and water-bore drilling, together with associated equipment, access roads and remote field support activities.

clauses.heading: Pre-Operational Planning and Readiness
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions planning or managing drilling operations shall establish a documented drilling plan addressing the work scope, drilling method, location, resources and operational interfaces.

clauses.heading: Pre-Operational Planning and Readiness
clauses.text: Applicable permits, licenses, approvals and authorizations shall be obtained before the relevant activities commence.

clauses.heading: Pre-Operational Planning and Readiness
clauses.text: The drilling location shall be assessed for environmental sensitivities, underground and overhead services, ground conditions, restricted areas and other site specific hazards.

clauses.heading: Pre-Operational Planning and Readiness
clauses.text: Drilling risks and critical controls shall be identified, communicated, implemented and verified before work commences.

clauses.heading: Pre-Operational Planning and Readiness
clauses.text: Personnel shall be competent, trained, inducted and authorized for their assigned duties before commencing work.

clauses.heading: Pre-Operational Planning and Readiness
clauses.text: Drilling and support equipment shall be available, inspected and confirmed fit for purpose before mobilization and use.

clauses.heading: Pre-Operational Planning and Readiness
clauses.text: Required materials, emergency response arrangements, communication systems and medical support shall be available before operations commence.

clauses.heading: Pre-Operational Planning and Readiness
clauses.text: Access routes and journey management arrangements shall be assessed before mobilization.

clauses.heading: Road Access and Drill Pad Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess road access, drill pad locations and associated earthworks before construction or drilling operations commence.

clauses.heading: Road Access and Drill Pad Requirements
clauses.text: Road access, drill pads and associated earthworks shall be designed or approved by a competent person in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements and engineering standards.

clauses.heading: Road Access and Drill Pad Requirements
clauses.text: Access roads shall be designed, constructed and maintained for the safe movement of personnel, drilling equipment, support vehicles and emergency response vehicles.

clauses.heading: Road Access and Drill Pad Requirements
clauses.text: Drill pads shall provide sufficient dimensions, stability, gradient and drainage for rig operations, rod handling, equipment storage, exclusion zones and emergency response.

clauses.heading: Road Access and Drill Pad Requirements
clauses.text: Geotechnical hazards, steep slopes, soft or unstable ground, flood-prone areas and other ground related hazards shall be identified and controlled before construction.

clauses.heading: Road Access and Drill Pad Requirements
clauses.text: Safe access, turning, parking, pedestrian movement, reversing controls and emergency escape routes shall be provided and maintained at drilling locations.

clauses.heading: Road Access and Drill Pad Requirements
clauses.text: Access roads and drill pads shall be inspected and verified as safe and fit for purpose before drilling equipment is mobilized or operations commence.

clauses.heading: Drilling Equipment and Operational Controls
clauses.text: Drilling operations shall be planned and conducted in accordance with approved operating procedures, risk assessments and applicable MSHEM requirements.

clauses.heading: Drilling Equipment and Operational Controls
clauses.text: Only competent and authorized personnel shall perform drilling activities or operate drilling equipment.

clauses.heading: Drilling Equipment and Operational Controls
clauses.text: Drill rigs, compressors and associated support equipment shall be inspected and maintained, and their safety critical functions shall be verified before use.

clauses.heading: Drilling Equipment and Operational Controls
clauses.text: Drill rigs, masts and supporting systems shall be positioned, erected, lowered, operated and moved on stable supporting conditions and within manufacturer or approved engineered limits. Personnel shall be protected from mast movement, instability, suspended components and other associated line of fire hazards.

clauses.heading: Drilling Equipment and Operational Controls
clauses.text: Personnel shall remain clear of rotating augers, drill stems, rods, feed mechanisms and other hazardous moving components. Personnel shall not pass under or step over a moving auger or drill stem. Rod and drill steel handling shall use mechanized handling where reasonably practicable and shall control crushing, pinch-point, caught- between and line of fire exposure.

clauses.heading: Drilling Equipment and Operational Controls
clauses.text: High pressure air, water and fluid systems shall be rated for the maximum operating pressure and provided with suitable restraints, locking devices or automatic protection where hose or connection failure could create a hazard. Pressure shall be isolated and safely released before connections are opened, equipment is maintained or blockages are cleared.

clauses.heading: Drilling Equipment and Operational Controls
clauses.text: Following loss of power or control energy, drilling controls shall be placed in a safe or neutral condition and equipment secured against unintended movement before power is restored. Drilling shall not resume until safe conditions and required controls have been verified.

clauses.heading: Drilling Equipment and Operational Controls
clauses.text: During movement or repositioning of drilling equipment, effective communication or continuous visual contact shall be maintained between the operator and personnel assisting the movement. Drill steel, tools and other loose equipment shall be secured and the mast placed in a safe position before movement.

clauses.heading: Drilling Equipment and Operational Controls
clauses.text: Drilling specific critical controls, including guarding, emergency stops, line of fire controls and exclusion zones, shall be implemented and verified before drilling commences and when conditions change.

clauses.heading: Drilling Equipment and Operational Controls
clauses.text: Pre-start inspections and work team briefings shall be completed before each shift, and affected personnel shall be informed of changes to hazards, conditions or controls before work continues.

clauses.heading: Drilling Equipment and Operational Controls
clauses.text: Drilling operations involving lifting or hazardous energy shall comply with applicable MSHEM lifting and energy isolation requirements, with unintended movement and the release of stored energy effectively controlled.

clauses.heading: Drilling Equipment and Operational Controls
clauses.text: Changes to drilling equipment, methods or operating parameters shall be assessed before implementation and shall be managed through the Management of Change process where its applicability criteria are met.

clauses.heading: Remote Operational Requirements
clauses.text: Where drilling operations are conducted in remote areas, the applicable requirements of 3.40 Exploration and Remote Field Safety shall also apply.

processes.title: Exploration and Remote Field Safety
processes.purpose: Define the controls for managing health and safety risks during exploration and remote field activities, including isolation, travel, difficult access, limited communication, environmental conditions and delayed emergency response.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden employees, contractors, subcontractors, service providers and visitors involved in exploration and remote field activities, including geological mapping, surveying, sampling, geophysics, drilling support, remote inspections, field camps, vehicle travel, equipment recovery and other work away from established operating facilities, from planning and mobilization through field operations, demobilization and rehabilitation.

clauses.heading: Pre-Commencement Requirements
clauses.text: Required land access approvals, environmental permits and restricted area authorizations shall be confirmed, and applicable stakeholder commitments shall be addressed before site entry or ground disturbance.

clauses.heading: Pre-Commencement Requirements
clauses.text: A joint pre-mobilization survey shall be completed and used to develop the field execution plan and site-specific risk assessment. The survey shall involve relevant Maaden, contractor and technical representatives where significant interfaces, unfamiliar locations or shared responsibilities require joint assessment.

clauses.heading: Pre-Commencement Requirements
clauses.text: Personnel shall be competent, inducted and authorized for their assigned field activities.

clauses.heading: Pre-Commencement Requirements
clauses.text: Vehicles, equipment, travel routes, accommodation, communication systems, medical support and emergency resources shall be verified against the approved field execution plan and risk assessment before mobilization.

clauses.heading: Pre-Commencement Requirements
clauses.text: Field work shall commence only after a documented readiness review confirms that safety critical requirements are complete.

clauses.heading: Field Site and Camp Requirements
clauses.text: Field sites, camps, shelters, accommodation and equipment shall be located on stable ground, away from flood paths, steep slopes, old workings and other uncontrolled hazards, and secured against foreseeable weather conditions.

clauses.heading: Field Site and Camp Requirements
clauses.text: Safe access, vehicle parking, pedestrian routes, muster points and emergency escape routes shall be established, identified and maintained.

clauses.heading: Field Site and Camp Requirements
clauses.text: Drinking water, protection from heat and weather, sanitation, lighting, first aid, fire protection, spill response and waste facilities shall be provided based on personnel numbers, work duration, environmental conditions and the site-specific risk assessment.

clauses.heading: Field Site and Camp Requirements
clauses.text: Open holes, excavations and fall hazards shall be protected against unintended access, clearly marked and secured before being left unattended.

clauses.heading: Remote Operational Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and implement a Remote Site Management Plan before commencing remote field activities. The extent and detail of the plan shall be proportionate to the activity risk, remoteness, duration, workforce, accessibility and available emergency response capability.

clauses.heading: Remote Operational Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain a personnel accountability system that covers buddy arrangements, personnel locations, planned movements, assigned vehicles and expected return times. The system shall define when buddy arrangements are mandatory, the required communication intervals, based on risk, and the escalation and emergency response actions for missed check-ins or overdue personnel.

clauses.heading: Remote Operational Requirements
clauses.text: Primary and backup communication systems shall be available, maintained and verified before personnel are deployed.

clauses.heading: Remote Operational Requirements
clauses.text: Remote field emergency response and medical evacuation arrangements shall be established, communicated and verified before deployment, in coordination with the applicable emergency preparedness and medical services processes.

clauses.heading: Remote Operational Requirements
clauses.text: Remote field activities shall not begin or continue when communication systems, emergency response capability or required critical controls are unavailable or ineffective.

clauses.heading: Journey Management Requirements
clauses.text: Remote journeys shall be supported by a documented route assessment and Journey Management Plan addressing route and terrain conditions, occupants, driver, vehicle, planned departure and return times, rest breaks, communications, check-ins and overdue escalation.

clauses.heading: Journey Management Requirements
clauses.text: Remote journeys shall be authorized before departure, with changes to the approved journey reassessed, communicated and reauthorized before continuing.

clauses.heading: Journey Management Requirements
clauses.text: Vehicles shall be legally compliant, inspected, maintained and suitable for the route, terrain and load.

clauses.heading: Journey Management Requirements
clauses.text: Drivers shall be competent, authorized and fit for work, and all occupants shall wear seat belts.

clauses.heading: Journey Management Requirements
clauses.text: Lone and night travel shall be avoided where practicable and shall be specifically risk assessed where required.

clauses.heading: Journey Management Requirements
clauses.text: Vehicle recovery shall be performed by competent personnel using approved methods, rated recovery points and suitable equipment.

clauses.heading: Health, Weather and Environmental Requirements
clauses.text: Health, environmental and weather related risks specific to remote field activities shall be assessed and controlled in accordance with the applicable MSHEM processes.

clauses.heading: Health, Weather and Environmental Requirements
clauses.text: Weather forecasts and warnings shall be monitored, and defined trigger actions shall be established for heat, flood, lightning, wind, dust and poor visibility.

clauses.heading: Health, Weather and Environmental Requirements
clauses.text: Personnel shall not enter or remain in wadis, drainage channels or flood prone areas when flash flooding is possible.

clauses.heading: Health, Weather and Environmental Requirements
clauses.text: Approved access tracks and work areas shall be used, and unnecessary vegetation clearing, off-road travel and land disturbance shall be avoided.

clauses.heading: Health, Weather and Environmental Requirements
clauses.text: Fuel, chemicals and waste shall be stored, handled, transported and disposed of using approved environmental and spill controls.

clauses.heading: Health, Weather and Environmental Requirements
clauses.text: Temporary facilities, waste and equipment shall be removed and disturbed areas rehabilitated following completion of work.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and approve a site- or project-specific Emergency Response Plan addressing credible emergencies before remote work commences, in accordance with section 5.1 Emergency Response Preparedness and Planning.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness
clauses.text: Emergency roles, contacts, GPS coordinates, access directions, maps, assembly points, evacuation routes and transfer locations shall be current and available.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness
clauses.text: Suitable first-aid, Emergency Communication Devices, fire equipment, spill kits and rescue equipment shall be available, inspected and ready for use.

processes.trigger: if work is performed in exploration or a remote field location

processes.title: Molten Metal Safety
processes.purpose: Molten metal activities are designed, operated and maintained to prevent uncontrolled contact between molten metal and people, water, incompatible materials or uncontrolled energy, and to prevent or mitigate spills, run-outs, splashes, fires, explosions and harmful exposure.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Business Units that melt, charge, retain, treat, tap, sample, pour, cast, granulate, transfer, transport, or otherwise handle metal in a molten state throughout design, construction, commissioning, operation, inspection, maintenance, modification, shutdown, and decommissioning, including activities performed by contractors.

clauses.heading: Risk Assessment and Controls
clauses.text: Business Units shall assess molten metal hazards and credible loss of control scenarios for normal operation, startup, shutdown, maintenance, abnormal conditions, and emergencies.

clauses.heading: Risk Assessment and Controls
Risk Assessment and Controls
clauses.text: Controls shall prioritize elimination, separation, mechanization, automation, remote operation, engineered containment, and safeguarding before reliance on administrative controls or personal protective equipment.

clauses.heading: Risk Assessment and Controls
clauses.text:
Controls required to prevent or mitigate credible molten metal events shall be managed in accordance with section
2.6 Critical Control Management requirements, including defined performance requirements and verification arrangements.

clauses.heading: Design and Engineered Safeguards
clauses.text: Molten metal facilities and equipment shall have a documented design basis that addresses the hazards and credible consequences identified through the applicable risk assessment process.

clauses.heading: Design and Engineered Safeguards
clauses.text: HAZOP or another structured hazard assessment technique shall be used where warranted by facility complexity or credible consequences. Changes affecting molten metal facilities, equipment, materials, operating conditions, safe operating limits, or controls shall be assessed before implementation and managed in accordance with section 3.52 Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Design and Engineered Safeguards
Design and Engineered Safeguards
clauses.text: Where foreseeable events could obstruct escape, emergency arrangements shall provide at least two independent escape routes that cannot be obstructed by the same event, or safe refuge where immediate evacuation cannot be achieved safely.

clauses.heading: Design and Engineered Safeguards
clauses.text: Molten metal equipment and areas shall contain or safely divert credible spills, run-outs, breakouts, excessive flows, overflows, foaming, and splashes away from people, occupied areas, escape routes, and equipment required for safety.

clauses.heading: Design and Engineered Safeguards
clauses.text: Water systems, drains, hoses, and locations where water could accumulate shall be separated from credible molten metal release paths or protected against molten metal contact.

clauses.heading: Design and Engineered Safeguards
clauses.text: Electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, fuel, oxygen, control, and compressed gas systems shall be separated or protected where exposure to molten metal could initiate or escalate a credible event.

clauses.heading: Design and Engineered Safeguards
clauses.text: Equipment and systems required for safety shall achieve or maintain a defined safe state following the loss or disturbance of energy, control, cooling, or other required utilities.

clauses.heading: Design and Engineered Safeguards
clauses.text: Where continuous cooling is required to prevent a credible high consequence event, an assured cooling supply shall be provided, and the required response to cooling interruption and restoration shall be defined.

clauses.heading: Materials, Tools and Moisture Control
clauses.text: Charge materials shall meet defined acceptance criteria for dryness, compatibility, contamination, and the presence of closed, hollow, sealed, or enclosed items that could retain moisture, liquid, gas, or pressure before introduction into molten metal.

clauses.heading: Materials, Tools and Moisture Control
clauses.text: Where the source, type, or history of charge materials indicates potential radioactive contamination, the materials shall be assessed and controlled in accordance with section 3.16 Radiation Management before acceptance and introduction into molten metal.

clauses.heading: Materials, Tools and Moisture Control
clauses.text: Tools, molds, sampling devices, and other equipment or surfaces that may contact molten metal shall meet defined requirements for dryness, cleanliness, compatibility, condition, temperature, and preparation before use to prevent moisture related, chemical, or exothermic reactions.

clauses.heading: Operating and Transfer Controls
clauses.text: Molten metal processes shall be operated within defined safe operating limits. Safety significant parameters, indicators of deviation, alarms, and required responses shall be defined and understood by affected personnel.

clauses.heading: Operating and Transfer Controls
clauses.text: Personnel exposure during tapping, pouring, casting, granulation, and other activities with credible molten metal exposure shall be minimized through mechanization, automation, remote operation, or engineered separation, as determined by the risk assessment.

clauses.heading: Operating and Transfer Controls
clauses.text: Entry into and presence within molten metal exposure zones shall be restricted to authorized people whose presence is required.

clauses.heading: Operating and Transfer Controls
clauses.text: Molten metal transfer equipment, containers, and lifting attachments shall be designed, selected, operated, and maintained to prevent loss of containment, uncontrolled movement, dropped loads, overflow, and personnel exposure to heat or splash.

clauses.heading: Operating and Transfer Controls
clauses.text: Molten metal transfer routes shall be defined and controlled to address credible collision, derailment, rollover, route obstruction, loss of control, and spill consequences.

clauses.heading: Integrity and Protective Systems
clauses.text: Equipment and protective systems required to prevent, detect, control, or mitigate a credible molten metal event shall be identified and managed in accordance with section 3.50 Asset Integrity Management, with defined inspection, testing, maintenance, and acceptance criteria. This shall include, where applicable, containment, refractory and cooling systems, supporting structures, lifting and transfer equipment, alarms, trips, interlocks, shutdown functions, emergency controls, and backup systems or services required for safety.

clauses.heading: Integrity and Protective Systems
clauses.text: Safety critical functions shall be tested at defined intervals and following any modification, repair, maintenance, or other intervention that could affect the required safety function.

clauses.heading: Integrity and Protective Systems
clauses.text: Equipment or protective systems that do not meet defined safety or integrity criteria shall be removed from service or placed in a safe condition. Continued operation with an impaired safety function shall be risk assessed, authorized, controlled, time-bound, and managed in accordance with section 3.51 EHSS Critical Systems Bypass process.

clauses.heading: Competency, Exposure Control and Emergency Readiness
clauses.text: People who operate, maintain, inspect, or supervise molten metal activities shall be competent and authorized for their assigned duties, including applicable emergency duties. Other people entering molten metal exposure areas shall receive relevant hazard information and emergency instructions before entry.

clauses.heading: Competency, Exposure Control and Emergency Readiness
clauses.text: Exposure to molten metal, heat, flame, hot surfaces, airborne contaminants, and noise shall be assessed and controlled in accordance with sections 3.13 Airborne Contaminants and Chemical Exposure Control, 3.14 Noise and Hearing Conservation, 3.15 Thermal Stress and Physical Hazards, and 3.31 Personal Protective Equipment, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Competency, Exposure Control and Emergency Readiness
clauses.text: Protective clothing and PPE for molten metal exposure shall be selected in accordance with Process 3.31 Personal Protective Equipment, comply with ISO 11612, and, where applicable, have molten metal performance evaluated using ASTM F955.

clauses.heading: Competency, Exposure Control and Emergency Readiness
clauses.text: Emergency arrangements for credible molten metal scenarios shall address warning, safe shutdown and isolation, evacuation or refuge, exclusion zones, fire response, casualty rescue, spill or release control and process stabilization, as applicable, and be established and tested in accordance with section 5.1 Emergency Response Preparedness and Planning.

processes.title: Laboratory Safety
processes.purpose: Laboratory activities are planned, conducted and verified to prevent injury, harmful exposure, fire, explosion, uncontrolled reaction, loss of containment, contamination and environmental harm, while maintaining conditions necessary for safe laboratory work.
processes.scope: This process applies to laboratories and associated sample receipt, preparation, chemical storage, instrument, compressed gas and waste areas under Maaden control.

clauses.heading: Laboratory Hazard and Risk Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify laboratories within their control and define their authorized activities, operating boundaries and access restrictions.

clauses.heading: Laboratory Hazard and Risk Management
clauses.text: Laboratory hazards shall be assessed before work begins and when changes to materials, equipment, facilities, methods, personnel, operating conditions or activities could affect risk.

clauses.heading: Laboratory Hazard and Risk Management
clauses.text: The assessment shall determine the required controls, operating limits, prohibited conditions, competency and authorization requirements, emergency arrangements, performance criteria and stop-work conditions.

clauses.heading: Laboratory Hazard and Risk Management
clauses.text: Where the composition or hazard of a material or sample is uncertain, controls shall be based on credible worst- case properties until the hazards have been characterized.

clauses.heading: Laboratory Hazard and Risk Management
clauses.text: Laboratory activities involving new materials, new methods, non-routine work or significantly changed conditions shall not proceed until associated hazards and controls have been evaluated.

clauses.heading: Laboratory Operations
clauses.text: Laboratory activities shall be conducted by competent and authorized personnel in accordance with approved Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that define operating limits, protective measures, abnormal condition response and safe shutdown requirements.

clauses.heading: Laboratory Operations
clauses.text: Laboratory access shall be restricted to authorized people or people under appropriate supervision.

clauses.heading: Laboratory Operations
clauses.text: Laboratory activities shall not begin or continue unless required controls are available, functional and meet their established performance criteria.

clauses.heading: Laboratory Operations
clauses.text: Unattended or after hours laboratory activities shall be assessed and authorized, with arrangements for monitoring, abnormal condition response and safe shutdown.

clauses.heading: Materials and Samples
clauses.text: Hazardous materials, samples and wastes shall be identified and controlled according to their hazards, compatibility, quantities, condition and intended use.

clauses.heading: Materials and Samples
clauses.text: Hazardous materials, samples, intermediates, wastes and secondary containers shall be identified to prevent misidentification, unintended use and incompatible interaction.

clauses.heading: Materials and Samples
clauses.text: Materials shall be stored, handled and segregated to prevent incompatible interaction, fire, explosion, uncontrolled reaction or hazardous release.

clauses.heading: Materials and Samples
clauses.text: Quantities and storage arrangements for flammable, combustible and other fire hazardous materials shall remain within the approved laboratory fire protection design and applicable fire protection requirements, including NFPA 45 requirements.

clauses.heading: Materials and Samples
clauses.text: Expired, deteriorated, unknown, leaking or otherwise unserviceable materials shall be isolated from use until their safety, fitness for use and disposition have been determined.

clauses.heading: Materials and Samples
clauses.text: Samples requiring legal, regulatory, contractual or quality traceability shall be controlled through documented receipt, custody, retention and disposition arrangements.

clauses.heading: Engineering and Equipment Controls
clauses.text: Ventilation, containment and other engineering controls shall be provided where hazardous exposure, airborne contamination or uncontrolled release could occur and shall be verified against documented performance criteria, including laboratory ventilation requirements based on ANSI/ASSP Z9.5.

clauses.heading: Engineering and Equipment Controls
clauses.text: Laboratory facilities, equipment, utilities, safeguards, alarms and protective systems shall be designed, selected and maintained to manage the applicable hazards and intended service conditions.

clauses.heading: Engineering and Equipment Controls
clauses.text: Equipment affecting laboratory safety or containment shall be removed from service or otherwise controlled when its condition could adversely affect safe operation.

clauses.heading: Engineering and Equipment Controls
clauses.text: Compressed gases, cryogenic substances, flammable liquids and reactive materials shall be controlled against release, incompatible interaction, fire, explosion, overpressure and hazardous exposure, with compressed-gas cylinders identified, secured against falling, protected from valve damage, stored in adequately ventilated locations, segregated according to compatibility, and clearly marked as full, in use or empty.

clauses.heading: Engineering and Equipment Controls
clauses.text: Environmental conditions and operating parameters that could affect laboratory safety, containment or the validity of laboratory results shall be controlled within defined limits.

clauses.heading: Engineering and Equipment Controls
clauses.text: Engineering controls, containment systems and safety critical laboratory equipment shall be inspected, tested, calibrated, maintained or otherwise verified at frequencies necessary to demonstrate their continued effectiveness.

clauses.heading: Engineering and Equipment Controls
clauses.text: A deficiency affecting a required laboratory control shall be corrected before the affected activity continues unless authorized interim controls reduce the risk to an acceptable level.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness
clauses.text: Laboratory emergency arrangements and equipment shall address credible exposure, spill, fire, uncontrolled reaction, loss of containment and control failure scenarios.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness
clauses.text: Emergency eyewash and shower equipment shall be provided where immediate flushing could be required and shall meet established location, accessibility and performance criteria, including ANSI/ISEA Z358.1 requirements.

clauses.heading: Waste and Decontamination
clauses.text: Laboratory waste, contaminated equipment and contamination hazards shall be identified, contained, decontaminated where required, and managed through applicable hazardous material, waste and environmental processes.

clauses.heading: Waste and Decontamination
clauses.text: Equipment, materials or containers leaving laboratory control for maintenance, transport, storage, disposal or reuse shall be assessed and decontaminated where required to prevent exposure, contamination or unintended release of hazardous substances.

processes.title: Transportation of Dangerous Goods and Materials
processes.purpose: Goods and materials transported for or on behalf of Maaden are classified, prepared, transported and delivered through controlled arrangements that prevent harm to people, the environment, assets, communities and transport infrastructure.
processes.scope: This process applies to the transport of dangerous goods, hazardous materials, waste and other regulated materials by or on behalf of Maaden. Passenger transport, stationary storage, waste treatment and disposal, radiation protection programs, lifting operations and general vehicle operation shall be managed through the applicable interfacing MSHEM processes.

clauses.heading: Transport Governance and Authorization
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify the materials, transport activities, transport modes, jurisdictions and supply chain roles under their responsibility or control.

clauses.heading: Transport Governance and Authorization
clauses.text: Responsibilities for classification, preparation, loading, transport, unloading, emergency response and transfer of custody shall be defined before transport begins.

clauses.heading: Transport Governance and Authorization
clauses.text: Transport activities shall comply with applicable legal, regulatory, permit, authority, contractual and formally adopted Maaden requirements, and all required licenses, permits, registrations, approvals and certificates shall be valid before transport begins.

clauses.heading: Classification and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Goods and materials shall be identified and classified by competent personnel before packaging, documentation, carrier selection or transport, with materials of unknown identity or uncertain classification prevented from transport.

clauses.heading: Classification and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: The transport determination shall identify applicable shipping descriptions, identifiers, hazard classifications, quantities, physical state, containment requirements, transport restrictions and emergency information requirements.

clauses.heading: Classification and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Transport risks shall be assessed before initial transport operations and when changes to the material, quantity, containment, mode, route, destination or applicable requirements may affect risk.

clauses.heading: Classification and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Risk assessments shall consider credible loss of containment, fire, explosion, exposure, incompatibility, cargo movement, collision, rollover, route conditions, weather, security threats, affected communities, environmentally sensitive areas and emergency response capability. Additional journey management, monitoring, tracking, escort, security or emergency controls shall be implemented where required by applicable obligations or risk assessments.

clauses.heading: Carriers, Personnel and Transport Equipment
clauses.text: Carriers and transport contractors shall be selected and monitored through a risk-based process that verifies, as applicable: legal authorization to operate; competent and authorized personnel; compatible and serviceable transport equipment; required insurance; emergency response capability; and control of subcontracted activities.

clauses.heading: Carriers, Personnel and Transport Equipment
clauses.text: All vehicles and containers used to transport hazardous materials shall be operated and maintained such that the release of liquids, litter, dust, solids or odor are prevented while in transit.

clauses.heading: Carriers, Personnel and Transport Equipment
clauses.text: Contracts shall define applicable EHSS, technical, competency, emergency response, reporting, verification and subcontracting requirements.

clauses.heading: Carriers, Personnel and Transport Equipment
clauses.text: Personnel performing regulated or safety critical transport activities shall be competent, authorized and, where required, licensed or certified.

clauses.heading: Carriers, Personnel and Transport Equipment
clauses.text: Vehicles, transport units and equipment shall be compatible with the cargo, maintained, inspected and operated within their design limits. Equipment with defects that could affect safe transport shall not be used.

clauses.heading: Containment, Loading and Cargo Control
clauses.text: Goods and materials shall be packaged or contained in approved, compatible and serviceable systems capable of maintaining integrity during foreseeable transport conditions. Damaged, leaking, contaminated, expired or otherwise nonconforming containment shall not be loaded or transported.

clauses.heading: Containment, Loading and Cargo Control
clauses.text: Cargo shall be segregated, distributed and secured to prevent incompatible interaction, movement, loss of stability or release of materials.

clauses.heading: Containment, Loading and Cargo Control
clauses.text: Loading, unloading, filling and transfer activities shall be performed by competent and authorized personnel using controls that prevent loss of containment, incompatible mixing, fire, explosion, exposure and environmental release.

clauses.heading: Containment, Loading and Cargo Control
clauses.text: Material identity, receiving containment, available capacity, connections, compatibility and applicable protective systems shall be verified before transfer operations commence. Applicable protective systems may include isolation, overfill prevention, emergency shutdown, ignition control, bonding, earthing and vapor control measures.

clauses.heading: Containment, Loading and Cargo Control
clauses.text: Containment systems, connections, closures, vehicles and transfer areas shall be inspected before release from loading or unloading locations.

clauses.heading: Hazard Communication and Custody
clauses.text: Packages, containers, vehicles and transport units shall display applicable hazard markings, labels, placards, identification numbers and warnings. Where applicable, facilities shall clearly placard the vehicle with the hazard classification of the material being transported in accordance with the United Nations chemical hazard classification system for the transport of dangerous goods.

clauses.heading: Hazard Communication and Custody
clauses.text: Regulated shipments shall be accompanied by complete, accurate and current transport documentation and emergency information.

clauses.heading: Hazard Communication and Custody
clauses.text: The receiving party shall verify shipment identity and condition, including any evidence of leakage, damage, tampering or discrepancy, before accepting custody.

clauses.heading: Hazard Communication and Custody
clauses.text: Rejected, returned or undeliverable shipments shall remain under controlled custody until managed through an authorized arrangement.

clauses.heading: Transport Readiness and Incident Management
clauses.text: Transport activities shall not commence until required transport controls have been verified.

clauses.heading: Transport Readiness and Incident Management
clauses.text: Arrangements shall be established to manage credible transport incidents and emergencies, including the reporting and management of spills, releases, theft, tampering and loss of custody in accordance with applicable legal, regulatory and Maaden requirements.

clauses.heading: Special Transport Requirements
clauses.text: Waste shall be classified before transport and transported only by authorized transporters to authorized receiving facilities using required approvals, compatible containment, placarding, tracking and transport documentation. Transfers of custody and final receipt shall be recorded and rejected, or undeliverable waste shall remain under controlled custody.

clauses.heading: Special Transport Requirements
clauses.text: Radioactive materials shall be transported only with required authorization, approved packages, competent and authorized personnel, transport documentation, radiation protection and security controls, continuity of custody, and any category specific tracking, communication, escort and incident reporting requirements.

clauses.heading: Special Transport Requirements
clauses.text: Explosives and blasting agents shall be transported under authorized arrangements that define controls for vehicles, routes, segregation, ignition sources, security, parking, communication and emergencies based on their classification and quantity.

clauses.heading: Special Transport Requirements
clauses.text: Cyanide shall be transported using verified competent carriers, compatible and secure containment, segregation from incompatible materials, route risk assessment, tracking, communication, emergency arrangements, security controls and delivery verification, with any claim of conformance with the International Cyanide Management Code supported by verification evidence.

clauses.heading: Special Transport Requirements
clauses.text: Flammable and combustible liquids, gases, cryogenic fluids, elevated temperature materials and other dangerous goods shall be transported in accordance with applicable classification, packaging, containment, segregation, transfer, competency, documentation, carrier acceptance, security and emergency requirements for the material and mode of transport.

processes.title: Building and Facility Safety
processes.purpose: Establish requirements for the lifecycle management of buildings and facilities to protect people, assets, the environment and business continuity through safe design, construction, occupancy, operation, maintenance, modification and decommissioning.
processes.scope: This process applies to permanent, temporary and portable buildings and occupied structures under Maaden operational control in process and non-process areas. It includes offices, control rooms, workshops, laboratories, utility and support buildings, warehouses, accommodation and welfare facilities, temporary cabins, occupied tents, contractor occupied facilities and buildings essential to operations even when not routinely occupied.

clauses.heading: Building and Facility Safety Governance
clauses.text:
Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain risk-based building and facility safety arrangements based on documented consideration of building type, location, occupancy, use, condition, hazard exposure and criticality. When establishing and reviewing these arrangements, Business Units and Corporate Functions shall consider relevant facility lifecycle and asset management principles described in ISO 41001 and ISO
55001.

clauses.heading: Building and Facility Safety Governance
clauses.text: Each building or facility shall have an identified owner or responsible function accountable for its approved use, occupancy, compliance, inspection, maintenance and management of identified deficiencies. The owner or responsible function shall ensure that current approvals, design and as-built information, occupancy limitations, safety critical systems, inspection records, modifications and condition status are maintained

clauses.heading: Building and Facility Safety Governance
clauses.text: Buildings and facilities shall comply with applicable legal, regulatory, permit, engineering, accessibility, fire and life safety requirements, including, where applicable, Saudi Building Code SBC 201, SBC 301, SBC 302, SBC 401, SBC 501, SBC 701 and SBC 801; Saudi Civil Defense requirements; SAIS Safety and Fire Protection Directives SAF-03, SAF-04, SAF-06 and SAF-09; and applicable SASO technical regulations.

clauses.heading: Building and Facility Safety Governance
clauses.text: Building and facility risks shall be managed in accordance with section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management.

clauses.heading: Facility Planning, Siting and Design
clauses.text: Buildings in process and non-process areas shall be sited considering intended use and occupancy, adjacent activities, process and non-process hazards, traffic, security, natural and environmental hazards, separation distances, evacuation and emergency access. Critical facilities shall meet applicable emergency response and business continuity objectives consistent with ISO 22301.

clauses.heading: Facility Planning, Siting and Design
clauses.text: Permanent buildings, portable buildings and occupied tents exposed to credible process fire, explosion or toxic release hazards shall be evaluated in accordance with section 3.47 Process Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment, SAIS SAF-03 and API RP 752, API RP 753 or API RP 756, as applicable, regardless of their designated area. Approved siting, occupancy limitations and required protective measures shall be implemented and maintained.

clauses.heading: Facility Planning, Siting and Design
clauses.text: New buildings and modifications to existing buildings shall be designed by appropriately qualified professionals using an approved design basis addressing intended use, occupancy, life safety, structural and environmental loads, foreseeable hazards and applicable codes. The design shall provide structural integrity, fire protection, fire resistance and compartmentation, safe access and egress, accessibility, electrical and mechanical safety, ventilation, drainage, emergency systems, applicable environmental protection measures and safe maintenance access.

clauses.heading: Facility Planning, Siting and Design
clauses.text: Floors, roofs, stairs, ramps, platforms, walkways, ladders, elevated edges and openings shall be designed, protected and maintained to support foreseeable loads and prevent slips, trips and falls, in accordance with applicable Saudi Building Code and SAIS SAF-06 requirements and, at mining operations, applicable provisions of MSHA 30 CFR Parts 56 and 57, Subparts J and P.

clauses.heading: Facility Planning, Siting and Design
clauses.text: Temporary and portable buildings, cabins and occupied tents shall not be occupied until their location, structural stability, anchoring, weather resistance, fire and electrical safety, ventilation, occupancy capacity, access and egress have been assessed and authorized in accordance with applicable codes, manufacturer requirements and site hazards.

clauses.heading: Construction, Commissioning and Occupancy
clauses.text: New buildings and modifications affecting building or facility safety shall be subject to documented design and construction compliance verification in accordance with applicable project and Management of Change requirements. Verification shall confirm conformance with the approved design, applicable safety requirements and regulatory obligations.

clauses.heading: Construction, Commissioning and Occupancy
clauses.text: Buildings shall not be occupied or placed into service until required commissioning, inspections, statutory approvals and readiness verification are complete. Safety critical systems shall be functionally tested, and current drawings, certificates, operating and maintenance information and occupancy limitations shall be accepted by the responsible owner before handover.

clauses.heading: Fire and Life Safety
clauses.text: Buildings shall have fire prevention, detection, alarm, suppression, portable firefighting, emergency lighting and emergency communication measures based on the approved occupancy classification and documented fire risk assessment. Design and installation shall comply with applicable SBC 801, Saudi Civil Defense, SAIS SAF-03 and SAF-04, and NFPA 1, NFPA 10, NFPA 13, NFPA 72 and NFPA 101 requirements.

clauses.heading: Fire and Life Safety
clauses.text: Means of egress, emergency exits and evacuation routes shall be sufficient for the approved occupancy, clearly identified, illuminated, unobstructed and maintained in serviceable condition in accordance with applicable codes and, where specified by Maaden for mining operations, MSHA 30 CFR 56.4530 and 57.4530.

clauses.heading: Fire and Life Safety
clauses.text: Fire protection and life safety systems shall be inspected, tested and maintained, and restored following impairment, in accordance with section 5.3 Emergency Response Equipment Maintenance, Testing and Interruption process.

clauses.heading: Fire and Life Safety
clauses.text: Emergency and standby power systems supporting fire and life safety shall comply with applicable NFPA 110 requirements. System impairments shall be subject to documented risk assessment, authorization and compensatory measures until restoration in accordance with section 5.3.

clauses.heading: Fire and Life Safety
clauses.text: Building occupancy, fire hazards, access, egress, fire protection systems and credible emergency scenarios shall be addressed in emergency response and pre-incident planning in accordance with section 5.1 Emergency Response Preparedness and Planning requirements.

clauses.heading: Operation, Inspection and Building Integrity
clauses.text: Buildings and facilities shall be operated, used and maintained within approved design, occupancy, contents, structural loading, building siting and risk assessment limits and assumptions.

clauses.heading: Operation, Inspection and Building Integrity
clauses.text: Building safety critical systems, services and utilities shall be identified, inspected, tested and maintained to control associated safety, health and environmental risks.

clauses.heading: Operation, Inspection and Building Integrity
clauses.text:
Workplaces, access routes, passageways, storerooms, service rooms and welfare facilities shall be maintained clean, orderly, sanitary and free from conditions that could affect safe use. Potable water, sanitary facilities and housekeeping at mining operations shall meet applicable MSHA 30 CFR 56.20002, 56.20003, 56.20008, 57.20002,
57.20003 and 57.20008 requirements.

clauses.heading: Operation, Inspection and Building Integrity
clauses.text: Buildings and structures shall undergo risk-based inspection and condition assessment by qualified personnel at defined intervals and following events, damage or deterioration that could affect structural integrity, in accordance with applicable Saudi Building Code requirements.

clauses.heading: Operation, Inspection and Building Integrity
clauses.text: Deficiencies affecting structural integrity, fire protection, emergency response capability, occupancy safety or environmental performance shall be risk assessed, controlled, tracked and corrected. Where structural integrity, fire safety or life safety may be compromised, the affected area or building shall be evacuated, isolated or occupancy restricted until confirmed safe by a qualified person authorized by the responsible owner.

clauses.heading: Environmental and Sustainability Controls
clauses.text: Buildings and facilities shall be designed, operated, maintained, modified and decommissioned to prevent pollution and minimize adverse environmental impacts. Applicable environmental controls arising from legal and regulatory requirements, permit conditions, approved environmental assessments and environmental risk assessments shall be incorporated, maintained and verified.

clauses.heading: Change Management and Decommissioning
clauses.text: Changes affecting a building or facility’s approved use, occupancy, design, structural loading, layout, fire protection, ventilation, utilities or emergency arrangements shall be assessed and authorized before implementation in accordance with Process 3.52 Management of Change and applicable code, permit and authority approval requirements.

clauses.heading: Change Management and Decommissioning
clauses.text: Buildings and facilities removed from service shall remain safe, isolated and secured against unauthorized access until their final disposition, in accordance with applicable regulatory and MSHEM decommissioning requirements.

processes.title: Warehouse Safety
processes.purpose: Establish requirements for the safe receipt, handling, storage, picking, packing, staging, loading, unloading and dispatch of materials within warehouses and storage facilities to protect people, assets, the environment and business continuity through effective warehouse design, operation, maintenance, inspection and control of storage and material handling risks.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden owned, leased, operated or managed warehouses, stores, laydown areas and other temporary or permanent indoor or outdoor storage facilities, including contractor operated warehouse and storage facilities under Maaden control.

clauses.heading: Governance, Planning and Competency
clauses.text:
Business Units and Corporate Functions shall manage warehouse related obligations, EHSS risks, material unwanted events and associated critical controls in accordance with sections 2.4 EHSS Legal and Regulatory Requirements,
2.5 EHSS Risk Management and 2.6 Critical Control Management.

clauses.heading: Governance, Planning and Competency
clauses.text: New warehouse projects and modifications to existing warehouses that may affect EHSS risk shall be managed in accordance with Process 4.2 Project EHSS Management.

clauses.heading: Governance, Planning and Competency
clauses.text: Personnel performing warehouse activities shall be competent and, where required, authorized. Powered industrial truck operators and people conducting formal storage system inspections shall meet applicable role-specific competency and authorization requirements.

clauses.heading: Governance, Planning and Competency
clauses.text:
Warehouse operations and maintenance activities requiring procedural control shall be conducted in accordance with Standard Operating Procedures or Standard Maintenance Procedures established under Processes 3.48 and
3.49, as applicable. Non-routine work and work requiring a permit shall be controlled in accordance with Process
3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment process.

clauses.heading: Warehouse Design and Operating Limits
clauses.text: Warehouse buildings, layouts, loading facilities, outdoor storage areas and associated infrastructure shall be designed, constructed and maintained for their intended use, approved occupancy where applicable, materials and quantities stored, structural loads, material handling methods, traffic arrangements, fire protection requirements and emergency access. Design and construction shall comply with applicable requirements, including SBC 201, SBC 801, SAIS SAF-03 Buildings for Industrial Facilities, SAIS SAF-04 Fire Protection Systems and Equipment and SAIS SAF-06 Plant Layout, Spacing and Access.

clauses.heading: Warehouse Design and Operating Limits
Warehouse Design and Operating Limits
clauses.text: Changes to stored materials, commodity classifications or quantities, storage heights or configurations, warehouse operating limits, storage systems, layouts, traffic routes, material handling equipment, ventilation, drainage, spill containment, fire protection systems or design assumptions, or emergency arrangements that may introduce or alter EHSS risk shall be managed in accordance with Process 3.52 Management of Change.

clauses.heading: Storage Systems and Material Control
clauses.text: Racking, shelving and other storage systems shall be designed, installed, commissioned, used, inspected, modified and maintained in accordance with applicable legal, manufacturer, engineering requirements, including applicable provisions of ANSI MH16.1 and BS EN 15635.

clauses.heading: Storage Systems and Material Control
clauses.text: Load capacities and configuration restrictions for floors, mezzanines and storage systems shall be displayed or readily available at the point of use and not exceeded.

clauses.heading: Storage Systems and Material Control
clauses.text: Storage systems exposed to foreseeable mobile-equipment impact shall have impact protection or equivalent controls, with damage or defects that could affect load stability or structural integrity assessed by a competent person, the affected area unloaded and restricted according to risk, and the system returned to service only after repair, replacement or confirmation that it is safe for its intended use.

clauses.heading: Storage Systems and Material Control
clauses.text: Pallets, containers and other unit load devices shall be selected and used based on the material, load, handling method, storage configuration and environmental conditions, with items that do not meet defined acceptance criteria identified, removed from use and repaired, replaced or confirmed safe before reuse.

clauses.heading: Storage Systems and Material Control
clauses.text:
Materials and unit loads shall be identified, segregated and arranged according to their physical and chemical characteristics, compatibility requirements and identified risks. They shall be stacked, blocked, interlocked, restrained or limited in height, as necessary, to prevent collapse, falling, rolling, sliding, deterioration, contamination or loss of containment, in accordance with applicable provisions of 29 CFR 1910.176 and MSHA 30 CFR 56.16001 and
57.16001 for mining operations.

clauses.heading: Storage Systems and Material Control
clauses.text: Materials and unit loads shall be inspected before acceptance or put away for damaged packaging, leakage, contamination, incorrect or missing identification, load instability and other conditions that could affect safe handling or storage. Unsafe materials or loads shall be segregated and controlled pending assessment and authorized disposition.

clauses.heading: Material Handling and Traffic Control
clauses.text: Material handling activities shall be planned and controlled to prevent injury, unstable or dropped loads, uncontrolled material movement and loss of load control. Manual handling and lifting operations shall comply with sections 3.17 Ergonomics and Work Design and 3.26 Lifting Operations, respectively.

clauses.heading: Material Handling and Traffic Control
clauses.text: Pedestrians shall be physically separated from powered industrial trucks and other mobile equipment where reasonably practicable. Warehouse traffic controls shall address routes, crossings, visibility restrictions, reversing, speed, parking, access and exclusion zones in accordance with sections 3.27 Mobile Equipment Safety and 3.29 Traffic and Journey Management. Where physical separation is not reasonably practicable, alternative controls shall be established based on the interaction risk.

clauses.heading: Material Handling and Traffic Control
clauses.text: Loading and unloading activities shall be controlled to prevent vehicle or trailer movement, premature departure, trailer instability, falls of people or materials and unauthorized access. Vehicle restraints, trailer supports and driver release controls shall be established based on risk. Dock levelers, ramps, dockboards and bridging devices shall be load rated, secured, inspected and maintained.

clauses.heading: Material Handling and Traffic Control
clauses.text: Conveyors, automated storage and retrieval systems and other warehouse machinery shall be safeguarded in accordance with section 3.33 Machine Safety and Guarding. Associated activities involving energy isolation, work at height or electrical hazards shall comply with sections 3.23, 3.24 and 3.30, respectively.

clauses.heading: Material Handling and Traffic Control
clauses.text:
Battery charging and equipment fueling areas shall be designated and controlled for equipment movement, ventilation, ignition sources, electrical hazards, spills and emergency response in accordance with sections 3.20,
3.22, 3.27 and 3.30, as applicable. Battery charging areas at mine facilities shall also comply with applicable provisions of MSHA 30 CFR 56.4502 and 57.4502.

clauses.heading: Hazardous and Regulated Materials
clauses.text: Hazardous materials stored or handled in warehouses shall be identified, controlled and managed according to their hazards, quantities, compatibility requirements, storage conditions and applicable obligations in accordance with section 3.20 Hazardous Material Management. Controls shall address containment, segregation, ignition sources, fire protection, spills, emergency arrangements and access, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Hazardous and Regulated Materials
clauses.text: Radioactive materials, explosives and dangerous goods shall be managed in accordance with sections 3.16 Radiation Management, 3.38 Explosives and Blasting Management and 3.43 Transportation of Dangerous Goods and Materials, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Housekeeping, Fire, Emergency and Security Controls
clauses.text:
Warehouses and storage areas shall be maintained to prevent stored materials, spills, waste, damaged packaging or other obstructions from affecting safe access, material containment, equipment operation, means of egress, fire protection or emergency response. Waste and hazardous materials shall be managed in accordance with sections
3.6 Waste Management and 3.20 Hazardous Material Management, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Housekeeping, Fire, Emergency and Security Controls
clauses.text: Stored materials, quantities, heights and configurations shall remain within the approved warehouse fire protection design and operating limits.

clauses.heading: Housekeeping, Fire, Emergency and Security Controls
clauses.text: Warehouse fire protection systems and emergency equipment shall be inspected, tested and maintained in accordance with section 5.3 Emergency Response Equipment Maintenance, Testing and Interruption.

clauses.heading: Housekeeping, Fire, Emergency and Security Controls
clauses.text: Warehouse emergency response, means of egress, emergency access, ignition source control and security arrangements shall be maintained based on the materials stored, warehouse activities, credible emergency scenarios and applicable obligations, in accordance with applicable MSHEM processes.

clauses.heading: Inspection and Improvement
clauses.text: Warehouses and storage systems shall undergo routine checks and periodic formal inspections by competent personnel at frequencies based on risk, condition, operating experience, manufacturer and engineering requirements, and applicable obligations.

clauses.heading: Inspection and Improvement
clauses.text: Inspections shall verify the condition and safe operation of warehouse storage systems, materials, load supporting equipment, traffic arrangements, loading facilities, hazardous-material controls, machinery, housekeeping, fire protection and emergency arrangements.

clauses.heading: Inspection and Improvement
clauses.text: Warehouse deficiencies, damage and deviations from established operating limits shall be recorded, risk assessed and controlled until corrective action is completed and verified.

processes.title: Process Safety Information Management
processes.purpose: Define the requirements for maintaining Process Safety Information concerning process hazards, process technology, process equipment, buildings and structures associated with applicable Maaden facilities and projects.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Units and Corporate Functions responsible for developing, receiving, maintaining or using Process Safety Information for processes and facilities with credible potential for a major process safety event. It also applies to contractor personnel performing these activities on behalf of Maaden.

clauses.heading: Governance and Information Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain a documented process to identify and maintain an inventory of required Process Safety Information, assign accountable ownership, create or obtain, review, approve and update the information, make current information accessible to authorized users, protect it from unauthorized alteration, damage or loss, maintain revision history, and prevent the unintended use of superseded information.

clauses.heading: Governance and Information Management
clauses.text: Process Safety Information shall be retained for the operating life of the facility and for any longer period required by applicable legal, regulatory, permit requirements.

clauses.heading: Process Hazard Information
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that applicable facilities maintain information sufficient to identify and understand the physical, chemical, toxicological, reactive, corrosive, thermal stability and incompatibility hazards of substances and materials associated with the process, including hazardous interactions arising from mixing, contamination, loss of segregation or abnormal process conditions. The information shall include current Safety Data Sheets where required and other technical information where Safety Data Sheets do not provide sufficient information.

clauses.heading: Process Hazard Information
clauses.text: Facilities handling or storing explosives shall maintain information on explosive properties, storage requirements, separation distances, compatibility and applicable legal, regulatory and permit requirements.

clauses.heading: Process Technology Information
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that applicable facilities maintain process technology information sufficient to understand the process and its hazards, including, as applicable, process descriptions, process flow diagrams, process chemistry, material and energy balances, design capacities, maximum intended inventories, safe operating limits, credible abnormal conditions and the consequences of deviation from those limits or conditions.

clauses.heading: Process Technology Information
clauses.text: Where required Process Safety Information is unavailable or incomplete, the applicable facility or project shall ensure that sufficient information is obtained, developed or reconstructed and technically validated by competent people before being used to support design, operation or other process safety activities.

clauses.heading: Facility and Equipment Information
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that applicable facilities maintain information necessary to demonstrate that process equipment is designed and constructed in accordance with applicable Saudi regulations and the engineering codes and standards specified in the approved design basis. This information shall include, as applicable, design specifications, materials of construction, piping and instrumentation diagrams, process control system architecture, instrumented protection functions, relief and vent system design bases, electrical area classification, ventilation system design, and applicable design codes and standards.

clauses.heading: Facility and Equipment Information
clauses.text: Process Safety Information shall identify equipment and controls classified as EHSS critical under the section 3.50 Asset Integrity Management process.

clauses.heading: Process Safety Critical Limits and Design Basis
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain documented safe operating limits for process safety critical parameters, including consequences of exceeding established safe operating limits.

clauses.heading: Process Safety Critical Limits and Design Basis
clauses.text: Each safety critical safeguard, including applicable relief systems, shutdown systems, alarms and interlocks, shall have a documented design basis defining its required function and performance criteria.

clauses.heading: Information Accuracy, Updating and Change Control
clauses.text: Changes affecting Process Safety Information shall be managed through the Management of Change process, including updating and verifying safety critical information before startup or restart.

clauses.heading: Information Accessibility and Use
clauses.text: Current Process Safety Information shall be accessible in a usable form to authorized personnel who require it for their assigned responsibilities.

clauses.heading: Information Accessibility and Use
clauses.text: Applicable Process Safety Information shall be used as an input to Process Hazard Analysis, Management of Change, Standard Operating Procedures, Standard Maintenance Procedures, Asset Integrity Management, Pre- Startup Safety Review, Emergency Response, Incident Management and Stewardship, and Training and Competency processes.

clauses.heading: Verification and Validation
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify at a risk-based frequency that required Process Safety Information is complete, technically accurate and consistent with actual facility conditions.

clauses.heading: Verification and Validation
clauses.text: Process Safety Information supporting hazard studies, major modifications or startup activities shall be validated by personnel competent in the applicable process, engineering discipline or operational area.

clauses.heading: Verification and Validation
clauses.text: Process Safety Information deficiencies shall be documented, prioritized and tracked to closure.

clauses.heading: Monitoring and Improvement
clauses.text: Facilities shall monitor the implementation and effectiveness of process safety information management and evaluate recurring deficiencies, discrepancies, and information quality issues.
