processes.trigger: if process design, chemistry, equipment, hazards or safe operating limits must be documented

processes.title: Process Hazard Analysis and Risk Assessment
processes.purpose: Establish effective systems to systematically identify, analyze and evaluate risks using appropriate methodology throughout the lifecycle of facilities, operations, projects, modifications, and decommissioning activities to ensure risks are reduced to ALARP and that critical controls remain effective.
processes.scope: This process applies to all the Business Units and Corporate Functions, including Process Plants, Non-Chemical Operations and Mining Risk Assessment (RA) studies related to new, existing and modified facilities.

clauses.heading: Governance and Applicability
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish, implement and maintain a Process Hazard Analysis program that defines the facilities, operations, processes and activities requiring PHA and provides for the identification and evaluation of process hazards and associated risk controls.

clauses.heading: Governance and Applicability
clauses.text: The PHA method and level of detail shall be commensurate with process complexity, hazard significance, credible consequences, lifecycle stage, proposed or implemented changes, and applicable legal, regulatory and permit requirements.

clauses.heading: Governance and Applicability
clauses.text: PHA studies shall evaluate credible environmental, health, safety and security consequences using the applicable criteria and methodology established by the EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Hazard Identification and Method Selection
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall select risk assessment methodologies based on process complexity, available information, lifecycle stage and risk significance.

clauses.heading: Hazard Identification and Method Selection
clauses.text: One or more of the following methodologies shall be applied where relevant Hazard Identification (HAZID), What-If, Structured What-If (SWIFT), Checklist, Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP), Failure Modes and Effects Analysis / Failure Modes, Effects and Criticality Analysis (FMEA / FMECA), Fault Tree Analysis (FTA), Event Tree Analysis (ETA), Layer of Protection Analysis (LOPA), Bowtie Analysis, Quantitative Risk Assessment (QRA) and Dust Hazard Analysis (DHA).

clauses.heading: Hazard Identification and Method Selection
clauses.text:
Methods selected shall be capable of identifying credible initiating events, hazard scenarios, escalation factors, consequences, prevention barriers, mitigation barriers and critical controls management.
[Table table-153-image.png]

Table 3.47-1. Applicable PHA methodologies

clauses.heading: Process Safety Information
clauses.text: PHA studies shall not commence until required Process Safety Information has been verified as current, complete and available to the assessment team in accordance with section 3.46 Process Safety Information Management.

clauses.heading: Process Hazard Analysis Execution
clauses.text: PHAs shall evaluate all lifecycle modes including, normal operation, start-up, shutdown, emergency operation, emergency shutdown, maintenance, temporary operations, commissioning and decommissioning.

clauses.heading: Process Hazard Analysis Execution
clauses.text: The analysis shall identify hazards, initiating events and credible failure scenarios, including equipment, utility and control system failures and human error; evaluate their consequences, safeguards and escalation factors; and define interim actions, mitigation measures, critical controls and additional risk reduction requirements.

clauses.heading: Process Hazard Analysis Execution
clauses.text: Maaden EHSS Risk Matrix shall be used for conducting the appropriate process hazard analysis methodology in accordance with the EHSS risk management process.

clauses.heading: Hazard Identification Study (HAZID)
clauses.text: A Hazard Identification Study (HAZID) shall be conducted during the early stages of projects, new facilities, major modifications, or where limited process design information is available.

clauses.heading: Hazard Identification Study (HAZID)
clauses.text: HAZID shall evaluate the potential consequences of identified hazards and determine the need for additional risk assessment studies, including HAZOP, LOPA, QRA, DHA, FMEA, FTA, ETA, or Bowtie analyses.

clauses.heading: Hazard Identification Study (HAZID)
clauses.text: HAZID shall identify existing and proposed safeguards, critical controls, and actions required to reduce risk to ALARP.

clauses.heading: What-If / Structured What-If (SWIFT)
clauses.text: A What-If or Structured What-If (SWIFT) study shall be used where broad hazard identification is required for processes, operations, maintenance activities, utilities, infrastructure or support systems.

clauses.heading: What-If / Structured What-If (SWIFT)
clauses.text: The study shall use structured questioning across relevant operating modes and activities within the defined scope to identify credible hazard scenarios, equipment failures, human errors, external events and deviations from intended operation, and evaluate their potential consequences, existing safeguards, critical controls and required additional risk reduction measures.

clauses.heading: Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP)
clauses.text: A Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP) shall be conducted for new or modified process facilities and existing facilities where process hazards require detailed and systematic analysis.

clauses.heading: Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP)
clauses.text: HAZOP shall systematically evaluate deviations from design intent across applicable operating modes, including start-up, normal operation, shutdown, emergency operation, maintenance and abnormal conditions, to identify credible causes, consequences, safeguards, operability issues and environment, health, safety and process safety risks.

clauses.heading: Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP)
clauses.text: Major or severe consequence scenarios identified by HAZOP shall be subject to further analysis using LOPA, QRA or another suitable method, as appropriate, to evaluate risk and the adequacy of protection layers.

clauses.heading: Hazard and Operability Study (HAZOP)
clauses.text: HAZOP recommendations shall define the actions required to eliminate hazards, improve operability, strengthen safeguards or reduce risk to ALARP.

clauses.heading: Layer of Protection Analysis (LOPA)
clauses.text: Layer of Protection Analysis (LOPA) shall be completed when major or severe consequences are identified, Safety Instrumented Functions are proposed, and PHA teams identify uncertainty regarding risk reduction adequacy in accordance with the applicable standards IEC61508 and IEC61511 or other relevant standards.

clauses.heading: Layer of Protection Analysis (LOPA)
clauses.text: LOPA studies shall define initiating events, quantify initiating event frequencies, identify independent protection layers, validate independence of IPLs, determine residual risk and determine required risk reduction.

clauses.heading: Layer of Protection Analysis (LOPA)
clauses.text: Safety Instrumented Systems identified as required risk reduction measures shall comply with IEC 61511 lifecycle requirements or other applicable standards.

clauses.heading: Layer of Protection Analysis (LOPA)
clauses.text: Protection layers claimed within LOPA shall be auditable and periodically verified.

clauses.heading: Quantitative Risk Assessment and Facility Siting
clauses.text: Facility Siting Assessments shall be completed for process facilities, occupied buildings, control rooms, laboratories, workshops, warehouses and other occupied structures exposed to process hazards.

clauses.heading: Quantitative Risk Assessment and Facility Siting
clauses.text: Industrial Building QRA shall be conducted when buildings are located within identified hazard impact zones, new occupied buildings are planned within process areas, significant facility modifications alter hazard exposure and facility siting studies identify potentially intolerable risk.

clauses.heading: Quantitative Risk Assessment and Facility Siting
clauses.text: QRA shall evaluate the following minimum requirements toxic impacts, fire radiation, explosion overpressure occupancy and vulnerability, adjacent facility impacts, domino effects and offsite consequences to the public, environment, and external infrastructure.

clauses.heading: Quantitative Risk Assessment and Facility Siting
clauses.text: Facility siting studies shall include but are not limited to the following administrative buildings, control rooms, maintenance facilities, emergency response facilities, warehouse, public exposure and nearby facilities in accordance with the SAIS SAF-03 Buildings for Industrial Facilities.

clauses.heading: Dust Hazard Analysis (DHA)
clauses.text: Facilities that manufacture, process, handle, convey, recycle or store combustible particulate solids shall conduct and document a Dust Hazard Analysis in accordance with applicable NFPA 660 requirements.

clauses.heading: Dust Hazard Analysis (DHA)
clauses.text: The DHA shall evaluate applicable buildings, process equipment, material handling systems, conveyors, bucket elevators, silos, dust collectors, workshops and storage facilities to identify combustible dust, fire, deflagration and explosion hazards; dust accumulation and migration pathways; potential ignition sources; and the adequacy of housekeeping, grounding and bonding, explosion prevention, isolation, venting and suppression controls.

clauses.heading: Dust Hazard Analysis (DHA)
clauses.text: The DHA shall be reviewed and, where necessary, updated following significant changes to materials, processes, equipment, facilities or combustible dust controls.

clauses.heading: Human Factors Assessment
clauses.text: Human factors shall be evaluated as part of all PHA studies and shall address staffing levels, workload, fatigue, ergonomics, procedures, human-machine interfaces, alarm management, Accessibility, maintenance error potential, training requirements and communication effectiveness.

clauses.heading: Critical Controls Management
clauses.text: Critical Control Management shall follow the requirements established in section 2.6.

clauses.heading: Recommendations and Action Management
clauses.text: PHA recommendations shall clearly identify the issue and required outcome, be assigned to a responsible owner with a target completion date and be tracked to verified closure through an approved action tracking process.

clauses.heading: Recommendations and Action Management
clauses.text: Residual risk following closure shall be documented and accepted by designated accountable management.

clauses.heading: Revalidation PHA studies
clauses.text: Each covered process shall undergo PHA revalidation at least every five years, unless a shorter interval is required by MOC's, RCA's, Audit Findings or applicable regulatory requirements.

clauses.heading: Revalidation PHA studies
clauses.text: Revalidation shall include review of management of change (MOCs), incidents, near misses, previous recommendations, updated risk information and updated facility information.

clauses.heading: Revalidation PHA studies
clauses.text: A new or updated PHA shall be completed when changes introduce new hazards or significantly modify existing risk.

clauses.heading: Competency
clauses.text: PHA teams shall be multidisciplinary and include personnel with knowledge of operations, engineering, maintenance, process safety, instrumentation and controls, safety and emergency response.

clauses.heading: Competency
clauses.text: Personnel leading or facilitating PHA studies including What-If, HAZOP, LOPA, QRA and DHA shall be competent in the selected methodology based on relevant training and experience, in accordance with section 2.7 EHSS Competency, Awareness and Communication.

clauses.heading: Documentation and Records
clauses.text: PHA records shall include the study scope, methodology, team members and roles, worksheets, findings, recommendations, action tracking and closure evidence, and applicable revalidation records, and be retained for the life of the facility.

processes.title: Standard Operating Procedures
processes.purpose: Establish the minimum requirements for developing, maintaining, and communicating accurate and clear written Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to manage EHSS risks and support the safe and consistent execution of operations.
processes.scope: This process applies to mining, processing, manufacturing, utilities, logistics, storage, material handling and associated support operations where documented operating procedures are required to control EHSS risks, including new, modified and existing facilities, equipment and processes, as well as temporary operating conditions and temporary process modifications requiring temporary operating procedures.

clauses.heading: SOP Identification and Coverage
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions responsible for operational activities shall identify operational activities that require documented standard operating procedures based on operational complexity, environment, health, safety, security and process safety risk, regulatory obligations and critical operating controls. Standard operating procedures shall be established where procedural control is necessary to achieve safe and consistent operation.

clauses.heading: SOP Identification and Coverage
clauses.text: The need for new or revised standard operating procedures shall be evaluated during Management of Change, project handover and Pre-Startup Safety Reviews, where applicable. Required standard operating procedures shall be developed, reviewed, approved, communicated and available before the applicable activity is performed or the facility, equipment or operational change is placed into operation.

clauses.heading: SOP Development and Approval
clauses.text: Standard operating procedures shall be developed by personnel who are competent in the activity and knowledgeable of the associated hazards, controls and operating requirements.

clauses.heading: SOP Development and Approval
clauses.text: Standard operating procedures shall be technically reviewed before approval and implementation to verify technical accuracy, consistency with current equipment and operating conditions, applicable regulatory requirements, identified hazards and controls and training implications.

clauses.heading: SOP Development and Approval
clauses.text: Responsibilities for development, review, approval and revision of standard operating procedures shall be defined and approved by the designated operational authority prior to use.

clauses.heading: Operating Procedure Content
clauses.text: Standard operating procedures shall define applicable operating modes, including start-up, normal operation, abnormal or upset operation, temporary operation where applicable, normal shutdown, emergency operation, emergency shutdown, and restart following shutdown, trip, maintenance or emergency conditions, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Operating Procedure Content
clauses.text: Standard operating procedures shall identify critical safeguards, interlocks, protective systems and required operating precautions.

clauses.heading: Operating Procedure Content
clauses.text: Standard operating procedures shall, where applicable, define operating limits, consequences of deviations from operating limits, actions required to prevent or correct deviations and conditions requiring escalation or shutdown.

clauses.heading: Operating Procedure Content
clauses.text: Standard operating procedures shall incorporate applicable process hazard assessment outcomes, risk assessment outcomes, lessons learned from incidents and investigations, relevant operational experience and regulatory requirements.

clauses.heading: Operating Procedure Content
clauses.text: Standard Operating Procedures applicable to start-up, shutdown and EHSS Critical SOPs shall incorporate documented checklists specifying the required sequence of actions for the safe and controlled operation of equipment or units.

clauses.heading: Operating Procedure Content
clauses.text: Standard operating procedures shall identify required actions when critical safeguards are bypassed, disabled or unavailable, where permitted by applicable bypass and management of change processes.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Standard Operating Procedures
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and designate as EHSS Critical Operating Procedures those procedures required to prevent Major or Severe consequence scenarios identified through PHA studies and verify their implementation and use through defined assurance activities.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Standard Operating Procedures
clauses.text: EHSS Critical Operating Procedures shall clearly identify critical actions with cautionary notes, holding points and stop conditions necessary to prevent unwanted events.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Standard Operating Procedures
clauses.text: Deviations from EHSS Critical Operating Procedures shall be assessed and authorized through applicable risk management and management of change processes.

clauses.heading: Temporary Operating Procedures
clauses.text: Temporary operating procedures shall be developed where temporary operational conditions introduce changes to normal operating practices.

clauses.heading: Temporary Operating Procedures
clauses.text: Temporary operating procedures shall define the temporary condition, identify associated risks and controls, specify validity periods, identify approval requirements and define conditions for return to normal operation.

clauses.heading: Temporary Operating Procedures
clauses.text: The validity period for any temporary procedure shall not exceed one year, after which the procedure shall be removed from use upon expiry.

clauses.heading: Communication, Competency and Use
clauses.text: Relevant personnel shall have access to current operating procedures applicable to their work.

clauses.heading: Communication, Competency and Use
clauses.text: Personnel shall be informed of new, revised and temporary operating procedures before use.

clauses.heading: Communication, Competency and Use
clauses.text: Personnel performing activities governed by standard operating procedures shall be trained and assessed as competent before performing the activity independently.

clauses.heading: Review and Continuous Improvement
clauses.text: Standard Operating Procedures shall be periodically reviewed to confirm that they remain current, accurate and effective. EHSS Critical Operating Procedures shall be reviewed at least every three years and other Standard Operating Procedures at least every five years, or earlier when triggered by operational changes, incidents or lessons learned, audit or assurance findings, risk assessment outcomes, regulatory changes or other conditions affecting the procedure.

clauses.heading: Review and Continuous Improvement
clauses.text: Obsolete, superseded or withdrawn operating procedures shall be removed from operational use and prevented from unintended use.

processes.title: Standard Maintenance Procedures
processes.purpose: Establish the minimum requirements for developing, maintaining, implementing and reviewing Standard Maintenance Procedures (SMPs) to support safe, reliable and consistent maintenance activities, preserve asset integrity, manage EHSS risks and maintain the effectiveness of critical controls and critical assets.
processes.scope: This process applies to maintenance of Maaden assets where documented maintenance procedures are required to manage EHSS risks or applicable legal, regulatory or permit requirements. It covers preventive, predictive, condition based and corrective maintenance, including inspection, testing, calibration, planned shutdown, integrity related and temporary maintenance activities.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Identification and Coverage
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions responsible for maintenance activities shall identify maintenance activities that require documented Standard Maintenance Procedures based on EHSS risk, process safety risk, asset integrity, equipment complexity, regulatory obligations and manufacturer requirements.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Identification and Coverage
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance Procedures shall be established where procedural control is required to ensure safe, reliable and consistent execution of maintenance activities.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Identification and Coverage
clauses.text: The need for new or revised Standard Maintenance Procedures shall be evaluated during management of change, project, commissioning, pre-startup safety reviews, incident investigations and asset integrity reviews where applicable.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Identification and Coverage
clauses.text: Required Standard Maintenance Procedures shall be approved by the designated authority and available to affected personnel before the applicable maintenance activity is performed or the asset is placed into service.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Development and Approval
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance Procedures shall be developed by personnel who are competent in the maintenance activity and knowledgeable of the associated hazards, controls, equipment, integrity requirements and regulatory obligations.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Development and Approval
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance Procedures shall be technically reviewed before approval and implementation to verify technical accuracy, consistency with current equipment and operating conditions, asset integrity requirements, identified hazards, controls, applicable regulatory requirements and competency and training implications.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Development and Approval
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define accountability, responsibilities and authorities for the development, technical review, approval and implementation of Standard Maintenance Procedures.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Development and Approval
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance Procedures affecting safety critical functions, critical controls or safety instrumented functions shall include appropriate technical review by relevant engineering disciplines.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Development and Approval
clauses.text: New or significantly revised Standard Maintenance Procedures shall be validated and approved to confirm that the procedure can be executed as intended and that identified controls are effective before implementation.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Content
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance Procedures shall define the minimum requirements, controls and acceptance criteria necessary to safely execute the maintenance activity.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Content
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance Procedures shall identify applicable equipment or asset types, maintenance boundaries and prerequisites, required integrity, reliability or safety objectives, applicable hazards and critical controls, conditions requiring escalation, specialist review or work stoppage and requirements for equipment restoration and return to service.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Content
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance Procedures shall incorporate applicable outcomes from process hazard analysis, risk assessments, asset integrity reviews, incident investigations, lessons learned and regulatory obligations.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Content
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance Procedures shall define activities requiring verification, inspection, testing, calibration, proof testing or validation necessary to maintain asset integrity or critical control effectiveness.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Content
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance Procedures shall define requirements for verification and return to service where maintenance activities can affect asset integrity, safety functions, critical controls, process safety or operational readiness.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Procedure Content
clauses.text:
Standard Maintenance Procedures shall reference applicable requirements of 3.51 EHSS Critical Systems Bypass,
3.52 Management of Change, 3.21 Permit to Work and Task Risk Assessment and 3.31 Personal Protective Equipment and other MSHEM processes required to execute the task safely.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Maintenance Procedures
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify all EHSS critical SMPs addressing Major or Severe consequence scenarios to maintain safe maintenance as identified through applicable Hazard Analysis.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Maintenance Procedures
clauses.text: Deviations from EHSS Critical Maintenance Procedures shall be assessed and authorized through applicable risk management and management of change processes.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Maintenance Procedures
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish assurance activities to verify the implementation and effectiveness of EHSS Critical Maintenance Procedures.

clauses.heading: Temporary Maintenance Procedures
clauses.text: Temporary Maintenance Procedures shall be developed where temporary maintenance strategies, temporary equipment arrangements or temporary repairs introduce changes to established maintenance requirements.

clauses.heading: Temporary Maintenance Procedures
clauses.text: Temporary Maintenance Procedures shall define the temporary condition, identify associated risks and controls, identify affected assets and controls, define approval requirements, specify validity periods and define requirements for return to the original condition.

clauses.heading: Temporary Maintenance Procedures
clauses.text: The validity period for any temporary procedure shall not exceed one year, after which the procedure shall be removed from use upon expiry.

clauses.heading: Temporary Maintenance Procedures
clauses.text: Temporary repairs that affect asset integrity, process safety, critical controls or regulatory compliance shall be managed through applicable 3.52 Management of Change and 3.50 Asset Integrity processes.

clauses.heading: Communication, Competency and Use
clauses.text: Current applicable Standard Maintenance Procedures, including new, revised and temporary procedures, shall be made available and communicated to affected personnel before use.

clauses.heading: Communication, Competency and Use
clauses.text: Personnel, including contractors, shall be trained and assessed as competent and, where required, authorized before independently performing maintenance activities governed by Standard Maintenance Procedures.

clauses.heading: Communication, Competency and Use
clauses.text: Maintenance activities shall be performed in accordance with the applicable approved Standard Maintenance Procedure and stopped for review where the procedure cannot be followed as written or does not address the conditions encountered.

clauses.heading: Review and Continual Improvement
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance Procedures shall be reviewed and updated as necessary to remain current, accurate, effective and consistent with applicable maintenance, asset integrity, EHSS, legal, regulatory and manufacturer requirements. EHSS Critical Maintenance Procedures shall be reviewed at least every three years, and all other Standard Maintenance Procedures at least every five years.

clauses.heading: Review and Continual Improvement
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance Procedures shall also be reviewed following changes, incidents or equipment failures, audit or assurance findings, critical control or asset integrity findings, changes to applicable legal or regulatory requirements, changes to manufacturer recommendations, or other relevant lessons learned that could affect the procedure.

clauses.heading: Review and Continual Improvement
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance Procedures shall be controlled so that only current approved versions are available for operational use and obsolete, superseded or withdrawn versions cannot be unintentionally used.

processes.title: Asset Integrity Management
processes.purpose: Establish requirements for managing the integrity of assets across all Business Units and Corporate Functions to prevent Environment, Health, Safety, and Security (EHSS) consequences and support safe, reliable, and sustainable operations.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Units and Corporate Functions that own, operate, maintain, inspect, test, monitor, modify or decommission assets requiring integrity management. These assets include, but are not limited to, pressure relief devices and relieving systems; EHSS critical instruments, alarms and protective functions; stationary and rotating equipment; electrical equipment and protection systems; civil and structural assets; cathodic and anodic protection systems; and utility and chemical hoses and flexible connections.

clauses.heading: Asset Integrity Governance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement and maintain an Asset Integrity Management system proportionate to their asset inventory, operating risks and applicable obligations.

clauses.heading: Asset Integrity Governance
clauses.text: Business Unit and Corporate Functions management shall be accountable for implementation and effectiveness of Asset Integrity Management and shall define applicable responsibilities and technical authorities.

clauses.heading: Asset Integrity Governance
clauses.text: Asset Integrity Management shall address applicable lifecycle stages from design and procurement through fabrication, installation, commissioning, operation, inspection, testing, maintenance, modification, preservation and decommissioning.

clauses.heading: Asset Integrity Governance
clauses.text: Asset Integrity Management shall be integrated with applicable operational, maintenance, reliability, EHSS Risk Management, Process Safety Information and Management of Change processes.

clauses.heading: Asset Register and Criticality
clauses.text: Assets within the scope of Asset Integrity Management shall be identified and maintained within controlled asset management or integrity registers.

clauses.heading: Asset Register and Criticality
clauses.text: The information maintained shall be sufficient to identify the asset, applicable service, criticality, technical basis and inspection, testing or maintenance strategy.

clauses.heading: Asset Register and Criticality
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish, implement and maintain documented criteria and a structured process for identifying and classifying EHSS Critical Assets.

clauses.heading: Asset Register and Criticality
clauses.text:
An asset shall be designated as an EHSS Critical Asset where:
a. Asset Criticality Assessments determine that failure or unavailability of the assets could potentially result in a Major or Severe EHSS consequences.
b. Applicable legal, regulatory, permit, approved engineering design or formally adopted technical standard requirements require the asset to perform a critical protection, monitoring, containment, prevention, mitigation or shutdown function. Examples include Pressure Safety Valves (PSVs), Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (CEMS), Safety Instrumented Functions (SIFs), Emergency Shutdown Systems (ESDs), and other assets with mandated critical functions.
c. A structured risk assessment determines that probability of failure or unavailability of the asset results in the associated scenario being assessed within the intolerable Risk Zone.

clauses.heading: Asset Register and Criticality
clauses.text: EHSS Critical Asset lists shall be controlled and maintained current. Changes to asset criticality or required protective function shall be technically justified and managed through the applicable Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Asset Integrity Strategy
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish an Asset Integrity Strategy defining how applicable degradation, failure and integrity risks are identified, assessed, controlled, monitored and reviewed throughout the asset lifecycle.

clauses.heading: Asset Integrity Strategy
clauses.text: Inspection, testing, monitoring and maintenance strategies shall be based on an approved technical basis appropriate to the asset and service.

clauses.heading: Asset Integrity Strategy
clauses.text:
Applicable methodologies shall include:
a. Risk Based Inspection; for stationary equipment in accordance with API 580 and 581.
b. Reliability Centered Maintenance; in accordance with SAE JA1011, SAE JA1012, IEC 60300-3-11, or other adopted standards, based on asset criticality and failure modes.
c. Reliability Instrumented System (RIS), for Safety Instrumented Systems (SIS) and critical process instruments in accordance with IEC 61508 and IEC 61511 standards.
d. Inspection and maintenance intervals established through applicable regulatory requirements, recognized codes and standards including API 580, API 581, API 510, API 570, API 653, ASME PCC-3 and API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 where relevant to the asset or manufacturer requirements.

clauses.heading: Asset Integrity Strategy
clauses.text: Asset Integrity strategies shall define applicable damage or failure mechanisms, required inspection or maintenance activities, methodologies, frequencies, acceptance criteria and actions where acceptance criteria are not achieved.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Monitoring
clauses.text: Inspection, testing, calibration, condition monitoring and other integrity verification activities shall be established for applicable assets and performed by competent personnel using approved standard operating and maintenance procedures and suitable equipment.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Monitoring
clauses.text: Inspection, testing and maintenance shall be completed within the frequency established by the approved Asset Integrity Strategy and applicable legal, technical or manufacturer requirements.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Monitoring
clauses.text: Results shall be documented and retained in a form that supports traceability, assessment of equipment condition, trend analysis and verification of continued suitability for service.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Monitoring
clauses.text: New, modified, repaired or replaced assets shall be subject to applicable inspection, testing, commissioning and acceptance requirements before being placed or returned into service.

clauses.heading: Pressure Relief Valves and or Devices
clauses.text: Pressure relief devices and relieving systems shall be designed, installed, inspected, tested, maintained and repaired in accordance with the applicable construction and in-service inspection codes and recognized standards, including API 520, API 521, API 576 and API 2000, where applicable.

clauses.heading: Pressure Relief Valves and or Devices
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define applicable pressure relief device service classifications, inspection and testing frequencies, acceptance criteria, and rules for extending or reducing inspection intervals based on service conditions, operating experience and applicable technical requirements.

clauses.heading: Pressure Relief Valves and or Devices
clauses.text:
Pressure relief valves, devices, appliances and vacuum breakers shall be classified as follows:
a. Class A: Pressure relief valves, devices and vacuum breakers installed in highly corrosive service, services susceptible to plugging or fouling, new or unknown service conditions, or fired boilers.
b. Class B: Pressure relief valves, devices and vacuum breakers not classified as Class A or Class C, including those installed in clean process service, non-corrosive service, and steam service excluding fired boilers.
c. Class C: Pressure relief valves, devices and vacuum breakers installed on non-process utility systems where the primary function is thermal expansion protection or utility system protection rather than process overpressure protection, including utility water, cooling water, dry compressed air and nitrogen systems.

clauses.heading: Pressure Relief Valves and or Devices
clauses.text: Unless shorter interval is required by an applicable obligation, adopted standard, manufacturer requirement, service condition or operating experience, the initial maximum scheduled inspection/test interval shall be 2 years for Class A, 3 years for Class B and 5 years for Class C.

clauses.heading: Pressure Relief Valves and or Devices
clauses.text: The inspection interval for Class A pressure relief valves and devices can be extended by up to 50% of the current interval if two consecutive inspections confirm satisfactory performance. However, the total interval shall not exceed a maximum of five (5) years.

clauses.heading: Pressure Relief Valves and or Devices
clauses.text: The inspection interval for Class B and Class C pressure relief valves and devices can be extended by up to 50% of the current interval if two consecutive inspections confirm satisfactory performance. However, the total interval shall not exceed a maximum of five (5) years.

clauses.heading: Pressure Relief Valves and or Devices
clauses.text: The inspection interval of Class A, Class B and Class C pressure relief valves and devices shall be reduced where the as-received opening pressure exceeds the applicable CDTP by more than 10%, or where inspection indicates that the pressure relief valve or device is heavily fouled or stuck. In such cases, the inspection interval shall be reduced to the previous successful interval or, as a minimum, 50% of the current interval.

clauses.heading: Pressure Relief Valves and or Devices
clauses.text: All pressure relief valves and or devices and rupture disk shall be periodically inspected to ensure that existing block valves are in fully open position and seals are intact. The inspection frequency shall be conducted as a minimum, on quarterly basis.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain a controlled register of EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices, Alarms and associated protective functions identifying the protected hazard or scenario, required function, applicable performance requirement, test method, approved test frequency and operating status.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: Safety Instrumented Functions shall be designed, verified, operated, proof tested, maintained and modified in accordance with IEC 61511, with IEC 61508 applied where required by the approved technical basis.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: Inspection, proof testing and functional testing shall demonstrate that the complete protective function, including applicable sensors, logic solvers, alarms, diagnostics and final elements, can achieve its required performance and design intent.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: EHSS Critical Alarms and non-SIS protective instruments shall be maintained, calibrated and functionally tested to demonstrate their required function. Alarm management arrangements shall follow the approved alarm philosophy and IEC 62682 or ISA 18.2.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: Any addition, removal, or modification of EHSS critical alarms shall be approved through the management of change process and protected from unauthorized suppression, shelving, or modification.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: Failed, bypassed, inhibited, overridden or otherwise degraded EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices, Alarms and associated protective functions shall be controlled through section 3.51 EHSS Critical Systems Bypass process.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: A failure that prevents the required critical function from operating on demand shall be reported in accordance with section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship criteria.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: Standard Maintenance and Operating Procedures shall define the requirements for proof testing and verification of Safety Instrumented Functions.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: Full functional testing of the EHSS Critical Instruments and Alarms loop (from initial to final element) shall be carried out if any change is made to the application program of logic solvers for that loop to ensure that Integrity level is not compromised.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: EHSS Critical Emergency Shutdown valves shall be leak tested to ensure that they meet the leakage requirement of the application of the valve based on applicable codes, standards and or manufacturer’s recommendations.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: Instrument equipment and system (complete loop or any individual component) or alarms shall not be taken out of service or tested during operation of the plant without prior approval, in accordance with section 3.51 EHSS Critical Systems Bypass process.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: Initial interval for testing of each component of EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms including loop shall be one year. Testing intervals of more than a year are acceptable for any or all the components or complete loop of EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms, if the documented result of quantitative analysis ensures integrity of the component and loop to perform as per design intent, and justifies testing interval of more than one year.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: The testing interval of component or complete loop EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms shall be reduced to ½ of the current interval, if they fail to function within the acceptable limits. However, the testing interval shall not be changed if the EHSS Critical Instrument, Device and Alarm failed to function as per the design intent and the RCA indicated that it is other than time based, if the root cause has been determined and rectified.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices, and Alarms shall be tested following any failure, suspected failure, demand event, relevant incident, or repair, replacement, or modification that could affect their required function, to verify that the required performance, reliability, and protective function have been restored.

clauses.heading: EHSS Critical Instruments, Devices and Alarms
clauses.text: Any deficiency found during the inspection and test that would have prevented the critical function to perform on demand, will result in inspection and test 'not satisfactory’ shall be reported in accordance with section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship process.

clauses.heading: Stationary Equipment
clauses.text: Pressure vessels, process piping, atmospheric and low pressure storage tanks, boilers, fired heaters and other stationary pressure containing equipment shall be designed, inspected, assessed, maintained, repaired and modified in accordance with the approved design basis, applicable legal requirements and recognized construction and in- service inspection codes. Applicable standards include API 510, API 570, API 653, API 573 and National Board Inspection Code (NBIC), as relevant to the equipment and service.

clauses.heading: Stationary Equipment
clauses.text: Inspection and integrity strategies for stationary equipment shall be based on credible damage and degradation mechanisms, equipment criticality, service conditions, operating history and applicable technical standards. Applicable methodologies and standards include API 571 for damage mechanism identification, API 970 for Damage Mechanism Reviews, API 580/581 where Risk-Based Inspection is used, API 579-1/ASME FFS-1 for fitness for service assessment, and API 584 for Integrity Operating Windows, where applicable.

clauses.heading: Stationary Equipment
clauses.text: Cryogenic piping, storage tanks, insulation systems and other cryogenic stationary equipment shall be included in the applicable Asset Integrity inspection and monitoring program, with inspection methods, frequencies and acceptance criteria established based on the approved technical basis, service conditions, manufacturer requirements, degradation mechanisms and operating experience. Evidence of leakage, moisture ingress, deterioration or loss of integrity shall trigger appropriate assessment and corrective action.

clauses.heading: Electrical Equipment and Protection Systems
clauses.text: Electrical equipment and systems shall be designed, installed, inspected, tested and maintained in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements, the approved design basis, manufacturer requirements and recognized technical standards. EHSS Critical Electrical Equipment and protective systems shall be identified and maintained in the EHSS Critical Asset List. Applicable standards include NFPA 70B, applicable IEC, IEEE and ANSI/NETA standards, and IEC 60079 for electrical equipment in hazardous areas, including IEC 60079-17 where applicable.

clauses.heading: Electrical Equipment and Protection Systems
clauses.text: Inspection, preventive maintenance and functional testing strategies for EHSS Critical Electrical Equipment and protective systems shall be based on equipment criticality, credible failure modes, required protective function, manufacturer recommendations, operating experience and the applicable technical basis. Protection relays, circuit- breaker trip functions, grounding and bonding systems, emergency generators, uninterruptible power supplies, batteries and other electrical systems credited as EHSS safeguards shall be tested or verified at frequencies sufficient to demonstrate their required availability and protective function.

clauses.heading: Electrical Equipment and Protection Systems
clauses.text: Failures, degraded performance or test results outside approved acceptance criteria for EHSS Critical Electrical Equipment or protective functions shall be evaluated and corrected in accordance with the applicable Asset Integrity findings and EHSS Risk Management requirements. Required changes to inspection or testing frequencies shall be determined based on the failure assessment, applicable NFPA 70B, ANSI/NETA or manufacturer requirements, and the approved technical basis.

clauses.heading: Civil and Structural Assets
clauses.text: Civil and structural assets shall be managed in accordance with applicable legal, design, inspection and maintenance requirements. Structures whose failure could cause or contribute to a critical EHSS event, loss of containment, failure of EHSS Critical control, obstruction of safe access or escape, or loss of emergency response shall be designated and managed as EHSS Critical Assets.

clauses.heading: Civil and Structural Assets
clauses.text: Applicable civil and structural assets shall comply with the Saudi Building Code, ISO 2394 General principles on reliability for structures, and ISO 13822 Bases for design of structures or other applicable design and assessment standards. Integrity strategies shall include baseline, recurring and event driven inspection or engineering assessment at frequencies based on criticality, material, environment, deterioration rate, design life and previous findings.

clauses.heading: Civil and Structural Assets
clauses.text: Where structural integrity or stability is uncertain, appropriate controls shall be implemented until fitness for service is confirmed by a competent structural engineer. Changes affecting structural loading, configuration, supports, foundations, or use shall be subject to engineering review and Management of Change, where applicable.

clauses.heading: Rotating Equipment and Mechanical Overspeed Protection
clauses.text: Rotating equipment shall be identified, operated, inspected and maintained in accordance with the approved design basis, manufacturer requirements and applicable recognized technical standards. EHSS Critical Rotating Equipment and associated protective functions, including Mechanical Overspeed Protection where applicable, shall be identified and maintained in the EHSS Critical Asset List. Applicable standards include API 610, API 611, API 612, API 616, API 617, API 618, API 670, API 686 and ISO 20816, where relevant to the equipment and approved technical basis.

clauses.heading: Rotating Equipment and Mechanical Overspeed Protection
clauses.text: Inspection, preventive and predictive maintenance, condition monitoring and functional testing strategies for rotating equipment shall be based on credible failure modes, equipment criticality, approved operating limits, manufacturer recommendations, applicable technical standards and operating and maintenance history. Standby equipment credited as an EHSS safeguard shall be periodically tested or operated to demonstrate its required availability.

clauses.heading: Rotating Equipment and Mechanical Overspeed Protection
clauses.text: Mechanical Overspeed Protection and other EHSS Critical protective functions shall be inspected, functionally tested and verified at frequencies established by the approved technical basis and applicable manufacturer or technical standard requirements, and following maintenance, modification or other activities that could affect their required function. Testing and return to service acceptance criteria shall be defined in accordance with API 611/ 612 or other applicable technical procedure or standard.

clauses.heading: Rotating Equipment and Mechanical Overspeed Protection
clauses.text: Abnormal vibration, temperature, lubrication condition, seal performance, alignment, overspeed protection performance or other condition indicators outside approved limits shall be evaluated before continued operation where they could indicate an integrity threatening condition. Continued operation shall be managed in accordance with the applicable Asset Integrity findings and EHSS Risk Management requirements.

clauses.heading: Cathodic and Anodic Protection Systems
clauses.text: Cathodic and Anodic Protection systems required to maintain the integrity of assets within the scope of this process shall be identified and managed with documented system boundaries, protected assets, design criteria, required operating parameters, acceptance criteria and inspection/test frequencies. A system protecting an EHSS Critical Asset shall be designated EHSS Critical.

clauses.heading: Cathodic and Anodic Protection Systems
clauses.text: Buried or submerged piping systems shall apply AMPP SP0169 or another approved system specific standard, and cathodic protection for applicable aboveground storage tank bottoms shall comply with API 651 and applicable AMPP requirements. Initial and recurring testing shall demonstrate that the approved protection criteria are achieved. Electrical measurement techniques shall use AMPP/NACE TM0497 or another approved method where applicable.

clauses.heading: Cathodic and Anodic Protection Systems
clauses.text: Anodic Protection systems shall receive functional inspection and verification at intervals not exceeding 12 months. The inspection shall include, as applicable, the protection monitoring panel, programmable or controlled DC power supply, test and bonding stations, reference and cathode electrodes, protection potential, grounding, meter accuracy, circuit integrity and other components required to demonstrate the approved protective function.

clauses.heading: Cathodic and Anodic Protection Systems
clauses.text: Loss of power, physical damage, excavation, suspected interference, failed reference electrodes or unexplained changes in protection level shall trigger evaluation, classification of any finding and corrective action.

clauses.heading: Utility and Chemical Hoses
clauses.text: Utility and chemical hoses, flexible connections and associated fittings whose failure could release hazardous material, pressure or stored energy, or impair an EHSS Critical function, shall be selected, installed, identified, inspected, tested, maintained and replaced in accordance with the approved service specific technical basis, manufacturer requirements and applicable recognized standards. Applicable standards include ISO 7751, ISO 8031, ISO 6134, ISO 2398, ISO 8331, ISO 1402, EN 1765, EN 12115 and SAE J517, as relevant to the hose type and service. Fire hoses shall be managed under the applicable Emergency Response Equipment requirements.

clauses.heading: Utility and Chemical Hoses
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish technical requirements for hose and flexible connection systems that address, as applicable, material and service compatibility, pressure rating, proof testing, electrical continuity or antistatic requirements, coupling and connection integrity, prevention of backflow and cross-connection, restraint against uncontrolled movement, safe depressurization, inspection and rejection criteria, and defined service life or replacement requirements.

clauses.heading: Utility and Chemical Hoses
clauses.text: Hoses and flexible connections shall be verified as fit for service before use and removed from service where inspection, testing, condition or service life criteria are not met. Temporary hose connections to live process or operational equipment shall be subject to the Management of Change process unless specifically covered by an approved standard operating or maintenance procedure.

clauses.heading: Findings, Defects and Risk Management
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish arrangements for personnel and contractors to report observed or suspected Asset Integrity deficiencies. Inspection, testing, monitoring or integrity assessment results that do not meet approved acceptance criteria shall be recorded and managed as Asset Integrity findings.

clauses.heading: Findings, Defects and Risk Management
clauses.text: Asset Integrity findings that may affect safe or reliable operation shall be evaluated before continued operation. The evaluation shall consider, as applicable, the asset condition, degradation or failure mechanism, credible consequences, effect on the required function, associated EHSS risk, operating restrictions, compensating controls, monitoring requirements and required corrective actions. Continued operation where the finding affects EHSS risk shall require documented technical assessment and authorization in accordance with section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management.

clauses.heading: Findings, Defects and Risk Management
clauses.text: Asset Integrity findings meeting applicable incident classification criteria shall be reported and managed in accordance with section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship. Corrective actions arising from findings, inspections, testing, failures or engineering assessments shall be prioritized, assigned, tracked and verified to closure.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Repair and Modification
clauses.text: Repairs and modifications affecting asset integrity shall comply with the applicable design, construction and in- service inspection codes and shall use approved procedures, qualified personnel and suitable quality assurance and quality control.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Repair and Modification
clauses.text: Preventive, predictive, corrective, and condition based maintenance activities affecting asset integrity shall be planned and managed through approved maintenance systems.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Repair and Modification
clauses.text: Asset integrity programs shall incorporate reliability information, failure history, degradation mechanisms, and operating experience.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Repair and Modification
clauses.text: Maintenance activities for preventive maintenance and corrective maintenance for test and inspection of assets shall be developed in accordance with Standard Operating and Maintenance procedure process. The procedure shall include the hazards during test/inspection and mitigation.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Repair and Modification
clauses.text: Changes affecting the approved design basis or integrity strategy shall be managed through Management of Change.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Repair and Modification
clauses.text: Temporary repairs shall be supported by an approved engineering assessment that defines applicable operating limits, monitoring, compensating controls and the timeframe for permanent resolution.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Repair and Modification
clauses.text: Materials and spare parts for EHSS Critical Assets shall be subject to controls necessary to verify conformity with approved specifications before installation.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Repair and Modification
clauses.text: Third party inspection, testing and maintenance activities shall be performed by suitably qualified and approved organizations and subject to appropriate Maaden verification and acceptances.

clauses.heading: Maintenance Repair and Modification
clauses.text: New or modified assets shall complete the applicable requirements of Pre-Startup Safety Review process before being placed into service.

clauses.heading: Asset Maintenance Deferment
clauses.text: A scheduled inspection, testing, calibration, monitoring, maintenance shall be completed by its approved due date unless an Asset Maintenance Deferment is approved before the due date.

clauses.heading: Asset Maintenance Deferment
clauses.text: An Asset Maintenance Deferment request shall identify the affected asset and function, scheduled activity, original due date, applicable technical standard and maximum allowable interval, reason for deferment, current condition and previous results, credible failure modes and consequences, proposed deferred date or expiry date, compensating controls, additional monitoring, operating restrictions and required technical and risk approvals.

clauses.heading: Asset Maintenance Deferment
clauses.text:
Asset Maintenance Deferments shall be supported by a documented technical assessment and EHSS Risk Assessment for all EHSS critical assets demonstrating the basis for continued operation in accordance with section
2.5 EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Asset Maintenance Deferment
clauses.text: The outcome of technical assessments for all deferred non-EHSS critical assets that highlight EHSS consequences shall trigger a risk assessment in accordance with section 2.5 EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Asset Maintenance Deferment
clauses.text: The deferment period shall not exceed the applicable preventive maintenance frequency interval, and approved deferments shall be recorded in the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) or equivalent system, communicated and monitored to closure.

clauses.heading: Asset Maintenance Deferment
clauses.text: Repeated deferments shall be analyzed for recurring causes and cumulative risk. An expired deferment shall be treated as an overdue Asset Integrity activity and escalated through the applicable Maaden risk management process. Postponement or extension of a turnaround or planned unit shutdown shall include assessment of the resulting impact on scheduled Asset Integrity activities, EHSS Critical Assets and associated risks.

clauses.heading: Asset Maintenance Deferment
clauses.text: A third consecutive deferment of the same scheduled Asset Integrity activity shall require a documented reliability study or equivalent technical study to determine whether the inspection, testing or maintenance strategy remains appropriate and to identify any required strategy changes.

clauses.heading: Critical Asset Status and Service Restoration
clauses.text: Removal, bypass, override, isolation or impairment of an EHSS Critical Asset or protective function shall be controlled under section 3.51 EHSS Critical Systems Bypass process. The approved bypass or impairment status shall be identifiable to Operations and recorded in the applicable operating or asset management system.

clauses.heading: Critical Asset Status and Service Restoration
clauses.text: Return to service verification following inspection, testing, maintenance, repair or modification shall confirm, as applicable, that the work is complete; Satisfactory/Acceptable Limits are met; protective devices are installed and active; temporary isolations and bypasses are removed or controlled; setpoints and configurations are correct; required functional testing is complete; and applicable Oracle/CMMS, asset and inspection records are updated.

processes.title: EHSS Critical Systems Bypass
processes.purpose: Define the minimum requirements and controls for the safe and controlled bypassing of EHSS Critical Systems across all Maaden operations, to prevent EHSS incidents and ensure operational integrity.
processes.scope: This process applies to the bypassing of EHSS Critical systems within Maaden Business Units, facilities, and plants. It does not apply to Emergency Response equipment, which is governed by the Emergency Response Equipment Maintenance, Testing and Interruption process. This process also does not apply to devices installed on equipment that remain isolated or out of service.

clauses.heading: Identification and Control of EHSS Critical Systems
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall determine the applicability of this process to their activities, facilities and operations and establish and maintain a process for controlling EHSS Critical System bypasses.

clauses.heading: Identification and Control of EHSS Critical Systems
clauses.text: Applicable facilities shall identify and maintain a register of EHSS Critical Systems. The register shall include, as applicable, the system and component identification, critical control or protective function, associated hazard or scenario, accountable function, and required performance criteria.

clauses.heading: Identification and Control of EHSS Critical Systems
clauses.text: The register shall be reviewed following relevant management of change activities and major hazard studies.

clauses.heading: Bypass Planning and Risk Assessment
clauses.text:
EHSS Critical Systems shall not be bypassed during all operation modes unless:
a. A formally approved bypass authorization form has been completed prior to initiating the bypass; and
b. Alternative risk controls have been incorporated into an approved Standard Operating Procedure (SOP); or
c. Alternative risk controls have been identified, assessed, and documented through a formal process safety risk assessment.

clauses.heading: Bypass Planning and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Where no approved Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) exists for the anticipated operating condition, the proposed bypass shall be evaluated and authorized through the Management of Change process before the bypass is implemented.

clauses.heading: Bypass Planning and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Risk assessments conducted to support EHSS Critical System bypasses shall use a quantitative or semi-quantitative process safety risk assessment methodology that considers the loss of the bypassed protection and any proposed alternative controls.

clauses.heading: Bypass Planning and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Alternative controls shall be implemented and verified before the bypass is initiated.

clauses.heading: Bypass Planning and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Where pressure relief protection is impaired, the technical adequacy of alternative overpressure protection arrangements and associated risk controls shall be verified before the bypass is initiated.

clauses.heading: Bypass Planning and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Bypass risk and alternative controls shall be reassessed when operating, equipment, environmental or other conditions materially differ from those considered in the approved bypass risk assessment.

clauses.heading: Bypass Authorization
clauses.text: EHSS Critical Systems bypass shall not commence without SOP or risk assessment and documented bypass authorization form in accordance with the EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Bypass Authorization
clauses.text: Bypass authorization shall specify affected system, justification, duration, alternative controls, approval requirements, communications and restoration details.

clauses.heading: Bypass Authorization
clauses.text: Shift Supervisor shall verify that the bypass authorization record and risk assessment is completed before authorizing implementation of the bypass.

clauses.heading: Bypass Authorization
clauses.text: If the Bypass Risk Level is higher than the Initial Risk Level (Design Risk), the bypass form shall be approved in accordance with the EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Bypass Authorization
clauses.text:
If the Bypass Risk Level is equal to or lower than the initial Risk Level (Design Risk), then the bypass risk form shall be approved according to the following conditions:
a. Shift Supervisor for bypass less than 8 hours.
b. Operation Manager for bypass more than 8 hours but less than one week.
c. Operations Director for bypass more than one week.

clauses.heading: Bypass Authorization
clauses.text: EHSS Critical Instruments, Alarms, Electrical Systems, and Pressure Relief Devices that remain bypassed for more than one week shall be evaluated through the Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Bypass Authorization
clauses.text: Bypasses associated with shutdowns and turnarounds shall be formally tracked until closure.

clauses.heading: Bypass Implementation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Personnel initiating a bypass shall verify that all required approvals and alternative controls are in place before implementation.

clauses.heading: Bypass Implementation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Active bypasses shall be clearly identifiable and communicated to affected personnel and included in shift handovers.

clauses.heading: Bypass Implementation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Active bypasses shall be periodically reviewed to confirm continued necessity, effectiveness of alternative controls, and compliance.

clauses.heading: Bypass Implementation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Duration of the EHSS Critical Instruments, Alarms, Electrical Systems, and Pressure Relief Devices bypass shall not exceed eight hours unless formally approved in accordance with the EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Bypass Implementation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Work on bypassed EHSS Critical Instruments, Alarms, Electrical Systems, and Pressure Relief Devices shall be completed continuously and in the shortest practicable time to minimize risk exposure.

clauses.heading: Bypass Implementation and Monitoring
clauses.text: Unexpected process conditions occurring during the bypass period shall be evaluated and escalated in accordance with the applicable EHSS risk management requirements.

clauses.heading: Restoration of EHSS Critical Systems
clauses.text: Bypassed EHSS Critical System shall be restored to service as soon as the purpose of the bypass has been completed.

clauses.heading: Restoration of EHSS Critical Systems
clauses.text: Prior to restoration, the person responsible shall verify that the system can perform its intended function.

clauses.heading: Restoration of EHSS Critical Systems
clauses.text: EHSS critical back-in service shall be documented including date and time of reinstatement, name and signature of the person performing the reinstatement, confirmation that the bypass has been removed and the device is operational.

clauses.heading: Assurance and Performance Monitoring
clauses.text: Business Units and applicable Corporate Functions shall, at planned intervals, verify compliance with this process and review active and completed bypasses, bypass duration and status, recurring causes, incidents, and assurance findings to identify adverse trends and required corrective actions.

clauses.heading: Assurance and Performance Monitoring
clauses.text: Business Units shall monitor bypass performance using key performance indicators that include, as a minimum, the number of active bypasses, bypass duration and aging, overdue bypasses, bypass-related incidents, and bypass- related assurance findings.

clauses.heading: Competency and Records
clauses.text: Personnel involved in bypass risk assessment, authorization, implementation, monitoring and restoration shall be competent for their assigned responsibilities.

clauses.heading: Competency and Records
clauses.text: Records of bypasses, approvals, risk assessments and restoration activities shall be maintained.

processes.title: Management of Change
processes.purpose: Changes throughout the facility and asset lifecycle are systematically identified, evaluated, authorized, implemented, verified, documented and closed to prevent the introduction of new hazards, escalation of existing risks, noncompliance, and unintended impacts on people, the environment, security, process safety, asset integrity or operational performance.
processes.scope: This process applies to all Business Units, Corporate Functions, Contractors, and Third-Party assets on Maaden premises. It covers permanent, temporary, and emergency changes affecting design, equipment, materials, technology, operations, products, EHSS critical services, procedures, organization, temporary repairs, and regulatory compliance. Changes in kind that do not alter design, function, or risk are excluded and managed through engineering, procurement, and quality assurance systems.

clauses.heading: Management of Change Governance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement and maintain a management of change process for the identification, assessment, authorization, implementation, verification and closure of applicable changes.

clauses.heading: Management of Change Governance
clauses.text: The management of change process shall define accountabilities, responsibilities, authorities and competency requirements for personnel involved in managing changes.

clauses.heading: Management of Change Governance
clauses.text: Proposed changes shall be screened against defined criteria to determine whether the management of change process applies. The criteria shall consider potential impacts on EHSS risks, asset integrity, operational performance, emergency management and response, competency requirements, and legal and regulatory compliance.

clauses.heading: Assessment and Authorization
clauses.text: Changes shall be assessed through appropriate technical and risk assessments before authorization. The assessment shall identify the purpose of the change, affected activities, assets or functions, hazards and risks, impacts on existing controls and barriers, compliance obligations, and required risk reduction and mitigation measures.

clauses.heading: Assessment and Authorization
clauses.text: MOC process requires that any permanent, temporary or emergency changes shall only be implemented once all authorizations have been obtained.

clauses.heading: Assessment and Authorization
clauses.text: Higher risk changes shall be approved in accordance with the EHSS Risk Management process.

clauses.heading: Implementation and Control
clauses.text: Approved changes shall be implemented in accordance with the defined approved requirements.

clauses.heading: Implementation and Control
clauses.text: Before implementation, affected personnel shall be informed of relevant impacts of the change.

clauses.heading: Implementation and Control
clauses.text: MOC process shall require that all documents, procedures and processes affected by the change are updated, communicated, and appropriate training provided prior to implementation of the change.

clauses.heading: Verification and Readiness
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify that requirements associated with the approved change have been completed before startup, operation and handover.

clauses.heading: Verification and Readiness
clauses.text: Verification activities shall confirm as applicable design requirements have been achieved, required actions have been completed, affected documents have been updated, required training has been completed and required testing and inspections have been completed.

clauses.heading: Verification and Readiness
clauses.text: Where applicable Pre-Start up Safety Review shall be completed before operation of a new, modified or reinstated facility, system or process.

clauses.heading: Temporary Changes
clauses.text: Temporary changes shall have a clearly defined scope and duration, not exceeding 6 months from the date of implementation. The duration shall be determined based on risk assessment, operational impact and regulatory requirements.

clauses.heading: Temporary Changes
clauses.text: Temporary changes shall be reviewed every 30 days and shall not be extended beyond their approved scope or duration without reassessment and authorization.

clauses.heading: Temporary Changes
clauses.text: Extension approval of temporary MOC from 6 months up to 1 year shall be risk-based in accordance with the EHSS risk management process.

clauses.heading: Temporary Changes
clauses.text:
Temporary changes shall not exceed one year from the implementation date. However, changes that are expected to be in place for longer than one year and cannot be converted into permanent change can be extended provided that:
a. The extension does not exceed the next scheduled turnaround or shutdown cycle.
b. Approved by Business Units or Corporate Functions department Vice President or N-3, ensuring that risk assessment and mitigation measures are systematically reviewed and documented.
c. Risk mitigation measures remain effective and additional safeguards are implemented.

clauses.heading: Temporary Changes
clauses.text: If temporary MOC remain open for more than 2 years without execution, then MOC cannot be executed unless revised with a new risk assessment confirming conditions are unchanged.

clauses.heading: Temporary Changes
clauses.text: Temporary changes shall be returned to their original condition or converted into permanent changes through the MOC process before closure.

clauses.heading: Temporary Changes
clauses.text: PSSR shall be conducted before normal operations are resumed following a temporary MOC.

clauses.heading: Temporary Changes
clauses.text: MOC process shall include a methodology to monitor the remaining duration of temporary MOCs and notify change owners for escalation as required.

clauses.heading: Emergency Changes
clauses.text: MOC process shall include a documented provision for managing emergency changes.

clauses.heading: Emergency Changes
clauses.text: The use of the emergency change process shall be strictly limited to situations where failure to make an immediate change could result in injury, asset damage, property damage, loss of containment, fire, explosion, legal non- compliance, environmental impact, major production loss, or major off-spec production.

clauses.heading: Emergency Changes
clauses.text: Any emergency MOC shall be converted into a permanent or temporary MOC as soon as it is safe to do so, and in all cases within 48 hours of implementation, ensuring that risk mitigation measures are in place and compliance is maintained.

clauses.heading: Emergency Changes
clauses.text: MOC process shall require an investigation to be carried out into the causes, requiring the emergency MOC to avoid the recurrence of the event.

clauses.heading: Emergency Changes
clauses.text: The approval levels for emergency changes shall be documented and business units shall ensure the correct competencies and training are implemented for designated approvers in emergency situations.

clauses.heading: Emergency Changes
clauses.text: Affected personnel shall be informed prior implementation of the emergency change and change shall be recorded in the shift logbook.

clauses.heading: Organizational and Personnel Changes
clauses.text: Organizational and personnel changes that may affect EHSS risk management, asset integrity, process safety or legal and regulatory compliance shall be evaluated through the management of change process, including changes to critical roles, responsibilities, organizational interfaces and competency requirements.

clauses.heading: Organizational and Personnel Changes
clauses.text: Competency gaps resulting from organizational or personnel changes shall be addressed before affected personnel undertake duties independently.

clauses.heading: MOC Closure
clauses.text: The management of change process shall require all MOC requests, including cancelled and rejected requests, to be recorded, documented and closed out within defined timeframes in a format accessible to affected stakeholders.

clauses.heading: MOC Closure
clauses.text: Changes shall not be closed until required actions have been completed or formally transferred to an approved action management process with assigned accountability and target completion dates.

clauses.heading: MOC Closure
clauses.text: Implemented changes shall be subject to post-implementation verification, proportionate to risk, to confirm that intended outcomes have been achieved and affected risk controls remain effective.

clauses.heading: Documentation, Performance and Learning
clauses.text: Management of change records shall be maintained from initiation through closure and retained for the life of the applicable facility or plant to support future process hazard analysis revalidation and assurance activities.

clauses.heading: Documentation, Performance and Learning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall periodically evaluate management of change performance, including relevant findings and trends from completed changes, incidents, audits and assessments.

clauses.heading: Documentation, Performance and Learning
clauses.text: Relevant lessons learned shall be communicated to affected Business Units, Corporate Functions and other stakeholders.
