processes.trigger: if a permanent or temporary technical, procedural, material or organizational change is proposed

processes.title: Pre-Startup Safety Review
processes.purpose: Establish the minimum requirements for conducting a Pre-Start Up Safety Review (PSSR) to verify the readiness of new or modified processes, equipment, and facilities before startup. The PSSR ensures that all safety systems, engineering controls, operational safeguards are implemented and effective, deficiencies are resolved, and EHSS risks are prevented.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Units and Corporate Functions, including their facilities, plants, sites, mines and buildings, as well as all Maaden and contractor employees involved in operation, maintenance and projects.

clauses.heading: PSSR Governance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define accountabilities, responsibilities, authorities and competency requirements for the initiation, execution, review and approval of PSSR activities.

clauses.heading: PSSR Governance
clauses.text:
Business Units and Corporate Functions shall conduct a PSSR before:
a. initial startup or commissioning of new facilities and major capital projects;
b. startup or restart following modifications subject to the Management of Change process; and
c. restart following major shutdowns or turnarounds where process conditions, equipment configuration or safeguards may have changed.

clauses.heading: PSSR Governance
clauses.text: PSSRs shall be performed by a competent multidisciplinary team and shall verify completion of applicable Management of Change and EHSS Risk Management requirements.

clauses.heading: PSSR Governance
clauses.text: Startup, restart, energization, pressurization, commissioning or introduction of hazardous materials shall not proceed until the PSSR has been completed and formally authorized by designated personnel.

clauses.heading: PSSR Planning and Preparation
clauses.text: The scope and level of detail of the PSSR shall be based on the nature, complexity and risk of the facility, process, equipment or modification.

clauses.heading: PSSR Planning and Preparation
clauses.text: The PSSR shall verify that applicable design, construction, installation, commissioning, testing, regulatory and inspection requirements have been completed and accepted before startup.

clauses.heading: Technical and Operational Readiness Verification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, maintain and implement documented procedures and checklists that comply with the requirements of this process to ensure a safe start-up of new projects, existing facilities, buildings, plants, equipment, or business units following modifications, major shutdowns, turnarounds or system idle more than 6 months.

clauses.heading: Technical and Operational Readiness Verification
clauses.text: The PSSR shall verify that facilities, equipment and systems conform to the approved design basis and are capable of operating within approved operating limits.

clauses.heading: Technical and Operational Readiness Verification
clauses.text: The PSSR shall verify before startup that applicable commissioning, functional testing, integrity verification and acceptance activities are completed and documented, and that equipment, systems, safeguards and EHSS critical controls are physically installed, available and functioning as intended.

clauses.heading: Technical and Operational Readiness Verification
clauses.text: The PSSR shall verify before startup that current approved operating, maintenance and emergency procedures, and other documentation required for safe operation and emergency response, are available to affected personnel.

clauses.heading: Risk and Change Verification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify that applicable Management of Change requirements, approvals and actions required before startup have been completed.

clauses.heading: Risk and Change Verification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify that changes made during construction, commissioning or modification have been incorporated into current documentation in accordance with section 3.46 Process Safety Information Management process.

clauses.heading: Risk and Change Verification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify that actions arising from applicable EHSS risk assessments that are required before startup have been completed and that identified critical controls are available and effective.

clauses.heading: Competence and Emergency Readiness
clauses.text: PSSR shall be led by a qualified PSSR Team Leader appointed by the Area Manager or designated authority. The PSSR Team Leader shall possess relevant operational experience and technical competence to effectively manage the review and ensure findings are addressed prior to startup.

clauses.heading: Competence and Emergency Readiness
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify that personnel responsible for operation, maintenance and emergency response have completed applicable training and demonstrated the required competence before startup.

clauses.heading: Competence and Emergency Readiness
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify that applicable emergency response and security arrangements are implemented and operationally ready before startup.

clauses.heading: Startup Authorization and Deficiency Management
clauses.text: The PSSR Team shall document completion of PSSR Checklist review, applicable supporting documents and approved PSSR Authorization form by Area Manager and Director prior to startup.

clauses.heading: Startup Authorization and Deficiency Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish criteria defining deficiencies that shall be resolved before startup and the PSSR outcome shall be documented.

clauses.heading: Startup Authorization and Deficiency Management
clauses.text: Any deficiencies identified during the PSSR shall be documented, assessed, classified, and tracked until resolved, either prior to start-up or through defined post start-up action plans in accordance with the EHSS risk management process.

clauses.heading: Records and Retention
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall retain PSSR records demonstrating completion, review and authorization of PSSR activities and make them available to support future risk assessments, incident investigations, audits and Management of Change activities.

processes.trigger: Use before initial startup or commissioning; startup/restart after an MOC modification; restart after a major shutdown or turnaround; and for the documented extended-idle case (>6 months).

processes.title: Blinds and Carseal Management
processes.purpose: Define the minimum requirements for managing blinds and carseals installed on valves to prevent inadvertent or unauthorized opening that could result in EHSS incidents across all Maaden operations.
processes.scope: This process applies to the management of all blinds and carseals installed on valves intended to remain car seals open, locked open, car seals closed or locked closed for EHSS considerations in process areas and facilities across all Maaden. Blinds and car seals installed for emergency response equipment are not covered under the scope of this process and are managed according to the requirements of emergency management and response process.

clauses.heading: Identification and Register
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify permanent and temporary blinds, and valves required to be car sealed or locked in a defined position, based on their role in managing EHSS risks.

clauses.heading: Identification and Register
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain current registers of identified blinds and carseal or locked valves, including the required valve position and the basis for inclusion.

clauses.heading: Identification and Register
clauses.text: Registered blinds and carseal or locked valves that their deviation can result in Major or Severe EHSS consequences shall be defined as EHSS critical blinds and carseal registered list.

clauses.heading: Blinds Management
clauses.text: Blinds list shall be developed, approved and maintained for normal operation, shutdown and startup based on review of as-built P&IDs and physical field verification. All installed blinds shall be clearly indicated on the as-built P&IDs and maintained throughout the asset lifecycle.

clauses.heading: Blinds Management
clauses.text: Documented procedure, including necessary forms, approval authority, and precautions, shall be developed and implemented for the installation or removal of blinds in accordance with the standard operating or maintenance procedures.

clauses.heading: Blinds Management
clauses.text: All blinds shall be selected, rated and installed for the design conditions of the service.

clauses.heading: Blinds Management
clauses.text: Documented verification shall be conducted prior to equipment or plant startup to confirm that blinds are in the approved operating configuration, any discrepancies shall be documented and resolved before startup proceeds.

clauses.heading: Blinds Management
clauses.text: Temporary blinds installed for maintenance, shutdown, startup, commissioning or similar activities shall be controlled throughout their installation and removal.

clauses.heading: Blinds Management
clauses.text: Addition or deletion of any blinds from the blinds list for normal operation, shutdown or startup shall be done in accordance with section 3.52 Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Carseal Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall develop, approve and maintain a master list of carseals that are kept Car Seals Open, Locked Open, Car Seals Closed or locked Closed for EHSS consideration during normal operation, shutdown and startup in each operating plants.

clauses.heading: Carseal Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain an up to date list of car seals valves. The list shall include the serial number of the car seals installed and the date of the installation.

clauses.heading: Carseal Management
clauses.text: Documented procedure, including necessary forms, approval authority, and precautions, shall be developed and implemented for the installation or removal of car seals to operate valves, in accordance with the standard operating or maintenance procedures.

clauses.heading: Carseal Management
clauses.text: Car Seals lists shall include all valves sizes on relief valves, rupture disc, flare lines, battery limit, bypass valves on EHSS critical control valves and any other valves which if closed or opened during the normal operations, shutdown and startup can result in Major or Severe consequences.

clauses.heading: Carseal Management
clauses.text: Risk assessments, Process Hazard Analysis studies, engineering review, P&ID review and physical verification in the field shall be carried out in developing and reviewing the list of car seals valves.

clauses.heading: Carseal Management
clauses.text: Carseals valves shall be maintained in their designated position, and their position shall be indicated on the as-built P&IDs.

clauses.heading: Carseal Management
clauses.text: Carseals shall be weatherproof, robust and strong enough to prevent inadvertent or accidental removal. They shall be attachable by hand or self-locking and non-releasable, with a minimum unlocking strength of no less than 50 pounds.

clauses.heading: Carseal Management
clauses.text: Addition or deletion of any car seals from the car seals list for normal operation, shutdown or startup shall be done in accordance with section 3.52 Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Carseal Management
clauses.text: All removed carseals during shutdown and startup shall be tagged and stored securely, with records maintained for traceability and future audits.

clauses.heading: Carseal Management
clauses.text: Pre-startup checklist shall include verification of all carseals positions as per the master list to ensure compliance with EHSS requirements before initiating any startup activities.

clauses.heading: Verification and Monitoring
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall quarterly verify the status of the carseals valves and blinds list in the plant, with results documented and discrepancies addressed promptly.

clauses.heading: Verification and Monitoring
clauses.text: Verification shall include reconciliation against engineering documentation, blind and carseal registers, and physical field conditions, with damaged, missing or incorrectly installed carseals immediately replaced and all findings documented.

clauses.heading: Verification and Monitoring
clauses.text: Unauthorized removal, installation or alteration of blinds or car seals valves shall be reported and investigated in accordance with the Incident Management and Stewardship process.

clauses.heading: Verification and Monitoring
clauses.text: Corrective actions arising from inspections, audits, incidents or reviews shall be tracked to closure.

clauses.heading: Competency
clauses.text: Personnel responsible for identifying, installing, removing or verifying blinds or carseal valves shall be competent for their assigned responsibilities, including applicable process hazards, isolation and overpressure risks, configuration control, and management of change requirements.

clauses.heading: Documentation and Records
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall retain records of inspections, surveys, startup verifications and corrective actions.

clauses.heading: Documentation and Records
clauses.text: Changes involving blinds or carseal valves shall be incorporated into affected engineering documents in accordance with the Management of Change and Process Safety Information Management processes.

processes.trigger: if positive isolation, line breaking, blinds, spades, spectacles or carseals are used

processes.title: Physical Security
processes.purpose: Facilities establish and maintain risk-based physical security measures that protect people, assets, critical infrastructure, information and operations from unauthorized access, intrusion, theft, sabotage and other credible security threats.
processes.scope: This process applies to facilities and locations owned, operated, leased or controlled by Maaden where physical security measures are required based on the facility security classification, security risk assessment or applicable authority requirements.

clauses.heading: Physical Security Governance and Risk Basis
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall conduct a Business Criteria Analysis (BCA) as specified in SEC-01 and assign a Facility Security Classification (FSC) based on the BCA.

clauses.heading: Physical Security Governance and Risk Basis
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall determine and implement the physical security requirements applicable to facilities and locations within their control based on the facility security classification and security risk assessment recommendations.

clauses.heading: Physical Security Governance and Risk Basis
clauses.text: The Security Risk Assessment (SRA) shall be conducted by a qualified SAIS-approved security consultant, and the resulting physical security measures defined from the approved SRA recommendations implemented by a SAIS- approved and qualified security contractor.

clauses.heading: Physical Security Governance and Risk Basis
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and implement a tracking system to monitor and manage Security Risk Assessment (SRA) recommendations and corrective actions until completion.

clauses.heading: Perimeter Protection
clauses.text: Facility perimeter protection shall be designed, implemented, and maintained based on the facility security classification and security risk assessment recommendations, and in accordance with SEC-01 and SEC-02 Security Fencing Systems.

clauses.heading: Perimeter Protection
clauses.text: Security fencing systems shall be selected based on the facility security classification and shall comprise, as applicable, an external interface area, anti-personnel fence area, and internal interface area. The system shall include, as applicable, clear zones, patrol roads, gates, sensors, surveillance, and lighting in accordance with SAIS directives.

clauses.heading: Perimeter Protection
clauses.text: Where a facility contains explosives magazines, the perimeter fencing system shall comply with the requirements of a Category 1 fencing system.

clauses.heading: Security Gates
clauses.text: Security gates shall be designed and implemented based on the facility security classification, security risk assessment recommendations and in accordance with SEC-03 Security Gates.

clauses.heading: Security Gates
clauses.text: Gate and design shall integrate the required access control system, inspection, surveillance, lighting, communication, alarm and anti-vehicle protection measures.

clauses.heading: Security Gates
clauses.text: Power to the gatehouse and all security devices shall comply with the requirements of SEC-07 Power Supply.

clauses.heading: Security Gates
clauses.text: Security gates, emergency gates, heavy-equipment gates and other controlled access points shall maintain perimeter integrity during normal, degraded and emergency conditions.

clauses.heading: Security Lighting
clauses.text: Security lighting shall be designed and implemented based on the security risk assessment recommendations and in accordance with SEC-04 Security Lighting.

clauses.heading: Security Lighting
clauses.text: Security lighting shall be integrated with surveillance and intrusion-detection systems to prevent lighting conditions from impairing their required performance.

clauses.heading: Access Control and ID Management System
clauses.text: Facilities shall establish access control arrangements that verify identity and authorization and restrict access to authorized people.

clauses.heading: Access Control and ID Management System
clauses.text: Electronic access-control systems shall be designed, implemented and integrated in accordance with SEC-05 Security Systems at Industrial Facilities and applicable authority requirements.

clauses.heading: Access Control and ID Management System
clauses.text: Personal Identification Verification cards and other regulated security credentials shall be issued, protected, suspended, revoked and recovered in accordance with SEC-11 Personal Identification Verification Cards.

clauses.heading: Security Systems, Surveillance and Intrusion Detection
clauses.text: Electronic physical security systems shall be designed, installed, integrated and modified based on the facility security classification and security risk assessment and in accordance with SEC-05 Security Systems at Industrial Facilities.

clauses.heading: Security Systems, Surveillance and Intrusion Detection
clauses.text: Physical security systems shall incorporate the availability, resilience, backup, tamper protection and failure protection required to maintain their intended security functions.

clauses.heading: Security Systems, Surveillance and Intrusion Detection
clauses.text: Intrusion detection and surveillance systems shall detect and localize security events and provide information sufficient for alarm assessment and security response within designated areas.

clauses.heading: Security Systems, Surveillance and Intrusion Detection
clauses.text: Surveillance and intrusion detection coverage shall address designated perimeters, gates, access points, critical assets and other areas identified through the security risk assessment.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Screening and Security Devices
clauses.text: Inspection, screening, personnel protection, anti-vehicle and other security devices shall be selected and implemented based on the facility security classification and security risk assessment and in accordance with SEC- 06 Security Devices.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Screening and Security Devices
clauses.text: Security devices requiring certification, testing or specialist safety controls shall be appropriately certified and operated by competent and authorized personnel.

clauses.heading: Security Control Centers and Protected Security Structures
clauses.text: Where required by the facility security classification and security risk assessment recommendations, Security Control Centers shall provide the facilities and systems required for integrated security monitoring, alarm management, surveillance, communications and coordination of security response.

clauses.heading: Security Control Centers and Protected Security Structures
clauses.text: Security Control Centers and other structures, rooms and enclosures housing security systems or equipment shall be designed and protected in accordance with SEC-09 Structures Housing Security Equipment.

clauses.heading: Security Control Centers and Protected Security Structures
clauses.text: Structures housing security systems and equipment shall provide controlled access, environmental protection and resistance to unauthorized entry, interference and tampering.

clauses.heading: Security Control Centers and Protected Security Structures
clauses.text: Keys and other physical access devices for security facilities, rooms, and equipment shall be securely managed and controlled to prevent unauthorized access or misuse.

clauses.heading: Power, Communication and System Integration
clauses.text: Physical security systems shall be provided with power continuity and backup arrangements required to maintain their intended security functions in accordance with SEC-07 Power Supply.

clauses.heading: Power, Communication and System Integration
clauses.text: Physical security systems requiring communication or network connectivity shall be integrated in accordance with SEC-08 Security Communications and Networks and Process 3.60 Security Communication and Networks.

clauses.heading: Physical Security Integrity and Impairment Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and implement a Maintenance and Support Program (MSP) for physical security infrastructure, systems, and equipment to ensure they are installed, inspected, tested, maintained, repaired, and commissioned by competent personnel in a manner that preserves their intended protective function.

clauses.heading: Physical Security Integrity and Impairment Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess failures, degradation and deviations affecting physical security measures and implement corrective actions or compensating controls until the required protection is restored.

clauses.heading: Management of Change
clauses.text: Business Units shall manage changes that may affect the facility security classification, security risk assessment, approved physical security basis or physical security measures in accordance with applicable SAIS approval requirements and Process 3.52 Management of Change.

processes.title: Facilities with Marine Interface
processes.purpose: Industrial facilities with marine interfaces are assessed, designed, operated and maintained in accordance with applicable marine security requirements to protect people, assets, operations and business continuity.
processes.scope: This process applies to Maaden owned, operated, leased or controlled industrial facilities that have a marine interface, including coastal industrial facilities with access to coastal waters, seawater intakes, marine approaches, discharge channels or other marine side facility boundaries.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Governance and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units shall identify facilities with marine interfaces and determine the applicability of SEC-13 and other applicable SAIS SEC requirements.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Governance and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units shall assess marine security risks through the facility security risk assessment process, considering marine side threats, vulnerabilities and access routes affecting critical assets, infrastructure, seawater intakes, discharge channels, marine approaches and other areas requiring protection.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Governance and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish marine-security requirements based on the security risk assessment, facility security classification and applicable authority requirements.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Design and Implementation
clauses.text: Business Units shall implement marine security measures to protect vulnerable marine areas, critical assets and critical infrastructure identified through the security risk assessment process.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Design and Implementation
clauses.text: Business Units shall design, implement and modify marine security infrastructure, systems and protective measures in accordance with SEC-13.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Design and Implementation
clauses.text: Marine security arrangements shall address, where required marine surveillance and intrusion detection; exclusion zones and restricted marine areas; marine barriers and protective measures; security monitoring and alarm integration; marine side access control; and marine security communications.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Design and Implementation
clauses.text: New facilities and modifications affecting marine security arrangements shall be submitted to SAIS for the required review or approval and comply with any conditions imposed.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Operations and Coordination
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish and maintain marine security arrangements that are consistent with the facility security classification, security risk assessment and applicable security requirements.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Operations and Coordination
clauses.text: Access to marine areas shall be restricted to authorized personnel and authorized activities.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Operations and Coordination
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish and maintain response arrangements for marine security events.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Operations and Coordination
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish coordination arrangements with relevant government agencies where required by applicable authority requirements or security risk assessment outcomes.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units shall maintain marine security infrastructure, systems and protective measures in a condition capable of achieving their intended protective function.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units shall assess failures, impairments and deviations affecting marine security measures and implement corrective actions or compensating controls where required.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units shall maintain documented evidence demonstrating compliance with SEC-13 requirements.

clauses.heading: Marine Security Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units shall submit required regulatory compliance documentation where required by SAIS.

processes.keywords: Facilities with Marine Interface; marine, port, jetty, ship, vessel; Marine Security Governance and Risk Assessment; Marine Security Design and Implementation; Marine Security Operations and Coordination; Marine Security Compliance
processes.trigger: if the facility or activity has a port, jetty, vessel or other marine interface

processes.title: Residential Compounds for Industrial Facilities
processes.purpose: Residential compounds associated with Maaden industrial facilities are located, designed, operated and maintained in accordance with applicable security requirements to protect residents, personnel and assets.
processes.scope: This process applies to residential compounds owned, operated, leased or controlled by Maaden that are associated with an industrial facility.

clauses.heading: Design Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify residential compounds within their control and determine the applicability of SEC-19 Residential Compounds for Industrial Facilities.

clauses.heading: Design Requirements
clauses.text: Residential compounds associated with industrial facilities shall be located outside the industrial facility operational area and security perimeter, with separation distances established in accordance with SEC-19 and its referenced requirements.

clauses.heading: Design Requirements
clauses.text: New residential compounds and modifications to existing compounds shall be submitted to SAIS where required and shall address any additional security conditions imposed by the authority.

clauses.heading: Design Requirements
clauses.text: Residential compounds shall be designed and modified in accordance with SEC-19, including its requirements for perimeter protection and clear zones, vehicle and pedestrian gates, gatehouses and access control facilities, anti- vehicle protection, traffic, inspection and rejection arrangements, security lighting, video surveillance and analytics, security communications, and fire protection.

clauses.heading: Security Operations
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish security arrangements for controlling access by residents, employees, visitors, contractors, service providers, vehicles and deliveries in accordance with SEC-19.

clauses.heading: Security Operations
clauses.text: Residential compounds shall maintain documented security procedures, post orders, patrol arrangements, alarm response arrangements and emergency security scenarios in accordance with SEC-19.

clauses.heading: Security Operations
clauses.text: Security communications for residential compounds shall be integrated with relevant Maaden security assets and emergency response arrangements in accordance with SEC-19.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Verification and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that required security infrastructure, systems and arrangements are inspected, tested and maintained to demonstrate continued conformity with SEC-19.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Verification and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall manage security system failures, impaired controls and deviations from SEC-19 until compliance is restored.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Verification and Compliance
clauses.text: New or modified residential compounds shall not be occupied until required security controls have been verified against the approved design, SEC-19 and SAIS conditions.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Verification and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain documented evidence of compliance with SEC-19 and shall submit the required Proof of Compliance through the prescribed regulatory workflow where required by SAIS.

processes.keywords: Residential Compounds for Industrial Facilities; residential compound, accommodation, camp; Design Requirements; Security Operations; Inspection, Verification and Compliance
processes.trigger: Use for residential compounds associated with an industrial facility, according to applicable design, operating and security requirements.

processes.title: Passive Defense Measures at Industrial Facilities
processes.purpose: Industrial facilities under Maaden control identify, assess and protect critical assets and security critical infrastructure against credible drone and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) threats through risk-based passive defense measures.
processes.scope: This process applies to industrial facilities owned, operated, leased or controlled by Maaden where passive defense measures are required to protect critical assets, security critical infrastructure or single points of failure from credible drone or unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) threats.

clauses.heading: Passive Defense Governance and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall determine the applicability of SEC-21 requirements based on facility security classification, security risk assessment outcomes and SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Passive Defense Governance and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess drone and UAV threats through the facility security risk assessment process.

clauses.heading: Passive Defense Governance and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that security risk assessments identify critical assets, security critical infrastructure and single points of failure that can require protection from drone or UAV threats.

clauses.heading: Passive Defense Governance and Risk Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and document passive defense requirements based on the security risk assessment, facility security classification, credible threat scenarios and SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Passive Defense Design and Implementation
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall implement passive defense measures where required to protect critical assets, security critical infrastructure and single points of failure from identified drone or UAV threats.

clauses.heading: Passive Defense Design and Implementation
clauses.text: Passive defense measures shall be designed and implemented in accordance with SEC-21 and SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Passive Defense Design and Implementation
clauses.text: New facilities and modifications affecting passive defense measures shall be submitted to the SAIS where required and shall address any additional conditions imposed by the authority.

clauses.heading: Passive Defense Design and Implementation
clauses.text: Where security risk assessments recommend the use of electronic anti-drone measures, Business Units and Corporate Functions shall evaluate and implement such measures in accordance with SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Passive Defense Operations and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain passive defense measures in a condition capable of achieving their intended protective function.

clauses.heading: Passive Defense Operations and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess failures, impairments and deviations affecting passive defense measures and implement corrective actions or compensating controls where required to maintain their intended protective function.

clauses.heading: Passive Defense Operations and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain documented evidence demonstrating compliance with SEC- 21 requirements.

clauses.heading: Passive Defense Operations and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall submit required regulatory approvals, compliance documentation and completion records where required by SAIS.

processes.keywords: Passive Defense Measures at Industrial Facilities; passive defense, hardening, standoff, protective design; Passive Defense Governance and Risk Assessment; Passive Defense Design and Implementation; Passive Defense Operations and Compliance
processes.trigger: if passive-defense, standoff, hardening, zoning or protective-design measures are required

processes.title: Security Operations at Industrial Facilities
processes.purpose: Industrial facilities establish and maintain risk-based security operations that protect people, assets, information and operations from credible security threats and enable effective response to security events.
processes.scope: This process applies to industrial facilities owned, operated, leased or controlled by Maaden.

clauses.heading: Security Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall determine the applicability of SEC-15 Security Management at Industrial Facilities and SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain a facility security organization with the accountability, authority, capability, staffing and resources required by the facility security classification and SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall conduct and maintain a facility specific security risk assessment in accordance with applicable security directives and SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall review and approve security risk assessment recommendations and track their implementation.

clauses.heading: Security Governance and Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, document and maintain a Facility Security Plan based on the security risk assessment, facility security classification and SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Governance and Planning
clauses.text: The Facility Security Plan shall define the security organization, physical and procedural controls, operating arrangements, required capabilities, and support and maintenance requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Operating Arrangements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain documented security procedures and post orders for security activities performed at the facility.

clauses.heading: Security Operating Arrangements
clauses.text: Security operating arrangements shall address, as applicable personnel, visitor, contractor and vehicle access; identification, credential, key and material control; gate, patrol and Security Control Center operations; security screening and prohibited items; security alarm assessment and response; security threat and incident response; coordination with emergency response activities; protection of security sensitive information; and temporary or degraded security arrangements.

clauses.heading: Security Operating Arrangements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish security arrangements for controlling contractors’ presence and activities within industrial facilities.

clauses.heading: Security Operating Arrangements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that security personnel are competent, authorized and fit for their assigned general, post specific and equipment specific duties.

clauses.heading: Security Operating Arrangements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall communicate applicable security threats, rules of conduct, reporting expectations and security awareness requirements to employees, contractors and visitors.

clauses.heading: Security Operating Arrangements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall control the possession, storage, issue and use of firearms and ammunition in accordance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Operating Arrangements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall provide security personnel with the vehicles, communication capability, protective equipment and other resources required to perform their assigned security duties.

clauses.heading: Security Operating Arrangements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall integrate applicable EHSS requirements and safe work practices into security operations, procedures and post orders.

clauses.heading: Construction, Commissioning and Operational Readiness
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define and control security responsibilities and interfaces during construction, commissioning, startup, operation, modification and decommissioning.

clauses.heading: Construction, Commissioning and Operational Readiness
clauses.text: Construction activities affecting an operating facility shall be controlled to prevent unauthorized access and adverse impacts on the facility security posture.

clauses.heading: Construction, Commissioning and Operational Readiness
clauses.text: Security responsibility for facilities or areas entering commissioning shall be formally transferred to the operating security organization.

clauses.heading: Construction, Commissioning and Operational Readiness
clauses.text: New or modified industrial facilities shall not begin operation until required security infrastructure, systems, personnel, equipment, procedures, post orders and Security Control Center capabilities are operational or approved compensating controls have been implemented.

clauses.heading: Operational Control and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain security infrastructure, systems and equipment, including required technical support arrangements, in a condition capable of achieving their intended protective functions.

clauses.heading: Operational Control and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess security system failures, impaired controls and deviations from applicable security requirements and implement corrective actions or compensating controls where required.

clauses.heading: Operational Control and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall manage changes that can affect the facility security posture, security risk assessment or Facility Security Plan in accordance with Process 3.52 Management of Change.

clauses.heading: Operational Control and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall review and update the Facility Security Plan and security operating arrangements following changes to the security risk assessment, facility changes, security incidents or changes in applicable requirements.

clauses.heading: Operational Control and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall conduct an annual assessment of compliance with applicable security directives and implement corrective actions for identified deficiencies.

clauses.heading: Operational Control and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall ensure that security incidents can be reported without retaliation and are investigated and addressed in accordance with Process 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship and SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Operational Control and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall integrate credible security scenarios, responsibilities and response arrangements into facility emergency plans and shall test them through training, drills or exercises.

clauses.heading: Operational Control and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain documented evidence demonstrating implementation of SEC-15 and SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Operational Control and Assurance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall submit required security risk assessments, Facility Security Plans, compliance documentation and completion records where required by SAIS.

processes.keywords: Security Operations at Industrial Facilities; guarding, patrol, security control room, dispatch; Security Governance and Planning; Security Operating Arrangements; Construction, Commissioning and Operational Readiness; Operational Control and Assurance
processes.trigger: Use for risk-based security operations at an industrial facility, including guarding, access control, patrol, dispatch, readiness and security response.

processes.title: Security Communication and Networks
processes.purpose: Security communication systems and networks provide secure, reliable and resilient voice, data and video communications for security, firefighting and emergency response activities.
processes.scope: This process applies to facilities owned, operated, leased or controlled by Maaden where wired or wireless communication systems or data networks are used to support security, firefighting or emergency response activities.

clauses.heading: Security Communication and Network Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify security communication systems and networks within their control and determine the applicability of SEC-08 Security Communications and Networks and other SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Communication and Network Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and document security communication and network requirements based on the facility security classification, security risk assessment recommendations, emergency response requirements and applicable authority requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Communication and Network Requirements
clauses.text: Security communication systems and networks shall be designed, implemented and modified in accordance with SEC-08, and applicable National Cybersecurity Authority (NCA) requirements.

clauses.heading: Communication Capability and Coverage
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall provide wired and wireless voice, data and video communication capabilities required for security, firefighting and emergency response activities.

clauses.heading: Communication Capability and Coverage
clauses.text: Security communication systems shall provide the coverage and capacity required across locations and operating conditions identified through the facility security risk assessment and emergency response planning processes.

clauses.heading: Communication Capability and Coverage
clauses.text: Security communication systems shall support communication and coordination between security facilities, emergency responders, relevant command and control locations and external response agencies where required.

clauses.heading: Communication Capability and Coverage
clauses.text: Wireless communication equipment used in hazardous areas shall be selected, approved and used in accordance with SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Communication Capability and Coverage
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall obtain required regulatory approvals for radio frequencies, wireless communication equipment and related installations before use.

clauses.heading: Network Security and Resilience
clauses.text: Security systems requiring network connectivity shall use security networks segregated from other networks and protected from unauthorized users in accordance with SEC-08 and applicable National Cybersecurity Authority (NCA) requirements.

clauses.heading: Network Security and Resilience
clauses.text: Security voice, data and video communications shall be protected against unauthorized access, interception, alteration and disruption, including through encryption where transmitted over wireless, shared, backbone, wide area or public networks.

clauses.heading: Network Security and Resilience
clauses.text: Security communication systems and networks shall incorporate redundancy, power continuity and alternative communication capability based on the facility security classification, credible failure scenarios and emergency response requirements.

clauses.heading: Network Security and Resilience
clauses.text: Security communication systems and networks shall be monitored for failures, loss of connectivity, unauthorized access and attempts to compromise communication services.

clauses.heading: Operation and Support
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall control the authorized use, administration and access to security systems, networks, equipment, configurations and encryption credentials.

clauses.heading: Operation and Support
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain security communication systems, network infrastructure and supporting power supplies in a condition capable of achieving their intended communication and protective functions.

clauses.heading: Operation and Support
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess failures, impairments and deviations affecting security communication systems or networks and implement corrective actions or compensating controls where required to maintain essential communication capability.

clauses.heading: Verification and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify the coverage, capacity, connectivity, integration, cybersecurity and resilience of security communication systems before operational use and following material modification.

clauses.heading: Verification and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain documented evidence demonstrating compliance with SEC- 08 and applicable authority requirements.

clauses.heading: Verification and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall submit required regulatory approval, compliance and completion documentation where required by the applicable authority.

processes.keywords: Security Communication and Networks; security communications, network, protected information; Security Communication and Network Requirements; Communication Capability and Coverage; Network Security and Resilience; Operation and Support; Verification and Compliance
processes.trigger: Use when wired or wireless voice, data or video communication systems or networks support security, firefighting or emergency response.

processes.title: Security for Non-Industrial Facilities
processes.purpose: Non-industrial facilities under Maaden control are classified, assessed, designed, operated and maintained in accordance with applicable security requirements to protect people, assets, operations and business continuity.
processes.scope: This process applies to non-industrial facilities owned, operated, leased or controlled by Maaden.

clauses.heading: Security Governance and Classification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify non-industrial facilities within their control and determine the applicability of SEC-100, associated non-industrial security directives and other applicable SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Governance and Classification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, document and maintain the facility security classification and supporting basis for applicable non-industrial facilities in accordance with SEC-100 and applicable SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Governance and Classification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish security requirements for non-industrial facilities based on the facility security classification, security risk assessment, applicable security directives and SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Risk Assessment and Design Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall conduct and maintain security risk assessments for applicable non- industrial facilities in accordance with SEC-100 and applicable SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Risk Assessment and Design Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall review and update security risk assessments following material facility changes, operational changes, significant security incidents, significant changes in threat conditions or other circumstances that can affect the facility security posture.

clauses.heading: Security Risk Assessment and Design Requirements
clauses.text: New non-industrial facilities and modifications to existing facilities shall be submitted to the SAIS where required and shall address any additional security conditions imposed by the authority.

clauses.heading: Security Risk Assessment and Design Requirements
clauses.text: Security infrastructure and security systems for non-industrial facilities shall be designed, implemented and modified in accordance with SEC-100, applicable security directives and other applicable SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Operations and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain security arrangements that are consistent with the facility security classification and security risk assessment recommendations.

clauses.heading: Security Operations and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall implement and maintain security operations to control access, respond to security events and monitor the effectiveness of security controls at non-industrial facilities.

clauses.heading: Security Operations and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall assess security system failures, impaired controls and deviations from applicable security requirements and implement corrective actions or compensating controls where required.

clauses.heading: Security Operations and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall maintain documented evidence of compliance with applicable security directives and SAIS requirements.

clauses.heading: Security Operations and Compliance
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall submit required regulatory compliance documentation where required by SAIS.

processes.keywords: Security for Non-Industrial Facilities; non-industrial facility, corporate office; Security Governance and Classification; Security Risk Assessment and Design Requirements; Security Operations and Compliance
processes.trigger: if a corporate office or other non-industrial facility is involved

processes.title: Contractor EHSS Management
processes.purpose: The purpose of this process is to establish Maaden wide requirements for managing contractor and subcontractor EHSS risks throughout the contracted work lifecycle.
processes.scope: This process applies to contracted work and services requiring contractor specific controls to manage EHSS risks or comply with applicable Maaden EHSS obligations, with those controls proportionate to the nature, complexity and risk of the contracted work.

clauses.heading: Contractor EHSS Governance and Coordination
clauses.text: Accountability for integrating and verifying applicable EHSS requirements throughout the contracted work lifecycle shall be assigned through the applicable contractor management process and approved authority arrangements.

clauses.heading: Contractor EHSS Governance and Coordination
clauses.text: Business Units/Corporate Functions and the contractor shall define and communicate their EHSS responsibilities, authorities and interfaces before affected work begins.

clauses.heading: Contractor EHSS Governance and Coordination
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish coordination arrangements where contractors, subcontractors, Maaden personnel or other employers perform interacting work or share a workplace.

clauses.heading: Contractor EHSS Governance and Coordination
clauses.text: The contractor accountable to Maaden shall manage its subcontractors and shall verify implementation of the applicable contract and EHSS requirements.

clauses.heading: Contractor EHSS Governance and Coordination
clauses.text: Business Units/Corporate Functions and contractor personnel shall have authority to stop affected work when a mandatory EHSS requirement or required control is absent, ineffective or not implemented.

clauses.heading: Contracted Work EHSS Planning and Risk Profiling
clauses.text: Before contractor selection or engagement, Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define the contracted scope and assess its applicable EHSS risks and obligations, including the work locations, interfaces, resources and equipment; EHSS risks and credible emergencies; critical controls; subcontracting; and applicable legal, regulatory, permit and Maaden requirements.

clauses.heading: Contracted Work EHSS Planning and Risk Profiling
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish a contracted work EHSS risk profile that determines the required capability assessment, contract controls, readiness verification, monitoring, assurance and closeout arrangements in accordance with the Contractor Management Manual.

clauses.heading: Contracted Work EHSS Planning and Risk Profiling
clauses.text: Where the contracted work EHSS risk profile identifies that the minimum Contractor Management Manual arrangement are insufficient, Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish additional or enhanced controls proportionate to the risk.

clauses.heading: Contracted Work EHSS Planning and Risk Profiling
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall review the risk profile when a change may affect the risks, obligations, interfaces, critical controls or management arrangements.

clauses.heading: Contractor EHSS Capability and Selection
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and apply contractor EHSS pre-qualification, capability and selection criteria in accordance with the contractor management manual.

clauses.heading: Contractor EHSS Capability and Selection
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify the capability of the contractor that will perform the work to a level proportionate to the EHSS risks of the contracted activities.

clauses.heading: Contractor EHSS Capability and Selection
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall not select or award work to a contractor that has not demonstrated compliance with applicable mandatory EHSS qualification and selection criteria established through the contractor management manual.

clauses.heading: Contractor EHSS Capability and Selection
clauses.text: Contractor EHSS capability shall be reassessed where an incident, nonconformity, ownership or organizational change, scope change or other material event may affect the contractor's capability. Findings that could affect contractor qualification or supplier status shall be managed through the applicable Procurement or contractor management process.

clauses.heading: Contract EHSS Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall include applicable EHSS requirements in procurement and contract documents before contract award.

clauses.heading: Contract EHSS Requirements
clauses.text: Contract documents shall define the applicable MSHEM and other EHSS requirements, obligations, controls, restrictions and performance expectations and shall identify required EHSS deliverables, responsible parties, acceptance criteria and required submission or completion points.

clauses.heading: Contract EHSS Requirements
clauses.text: The contractor shall communicate applicable EHSS requirements to its personnel and subcontractors in a form they can understand and shall verify implementation.

clauses.heading: Contract Transition, Mobilization and Readiness
clauses.text: Contract transition, handover, mobilization, onboarding and readiness verification shall be managed through the applicable Contractor Management Manual arrangements, with additional EHSS controls established where required by the contracted work EHSS risk profile.

clauses.heading: Contract Transition, Mobilization and Readiness
clauses.text: Contractors shall not mobilize or begin affected work until the applicable contractor management readiness process has verified that required EHSS conditions are satisfied, including competent and authorized personnel, required inductions, equipment readiness, applicable work controls and authorizations, and emergency arrangements.

clauses.heading: Work Execution, Coordination and Change Control
clauses.text: Contractors and subcontractors shall implement applicable contract requirements, MSHEM requirements and scope specific EHSS controls throughout work execution.

clauses.heading: Work Execution, Coordination and Change Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall provide contractors with information under its control that is necessary to understand relevant hazards, interfaces, emergency arrangements and critical controls.

clauses.heading: Work Execution, Coordination and Change Control
clauses.text: Changes affecting the contracted work EHSS risk, scope, personnel, competence, equipment, subcontracting, controls or management arrangements shall be assessed and controlled through the applicable Contractor Management Manual contract change arrangements and applicable MSHEM Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Performance Monitoring, Assurance and Escalation
clauses.text: Contractor EHSS performance shall be monitored and assured through the Contractor Management Manual and the applicable requirements of sections 6.2 and 6.3, with reporting, corrective action and escalation proportionate to the EHSS risks, exposure and actual performance of the contracted work.

clauses.heading: Performance Monitoring, Assurance and Escalation
clauses.text: Monitoring and assurance shall be increased where contractor performance deteriorates, the risk profile increases or an EHSS nonconformity is identified. Material matters requiring contractual, qualification, supplier status or other commercial action shall be referred through the applicable Contractor Management Manual, Procurement or Legal process.

clauses.heading: Worker Engagement, Welfare and Raising Concerns
clauses.text: The contractor shall provide its personnel and subcontractors with the EHSS information necessary for their work and shall enable their participation in risk assessment and improvement of controls relevant to their activities.

clauses.heading: Worker Engagement, Welfare and Raising Concerns
clauses.text: Contractor personnel shall be able to report hazards, unsafe conditions, welfare concerns and EHSS nonconformities through HEMAYA without retaliation. Business Units and Corporate Functions shall communicate applicable reporting and escalation arrangements and ensure that material concerns are assessed and tracked to verified closure.

clauses.heading: Worker Engagement, Welfare and Raising Concerns
clauses.text: Where the contract includes accommodation, catering, sanitation, transport or other welfare services, Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define the applicable requirements in the contract and shall verify readiness before the service begins.

clauses.heading: Work Restriction, Suspension, Termination and Continuity of Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall restrict, suspend or stop contracted work where a mandatory EHSS requirement or required control is absent or ineffective, or where the work presents uncontrolled EHSS risk.

clauses.heading: Work Restriction, Suspension, Termination and Continuity of Control
clauses.text: Suspended work shall not resume until the cause is assessed, required corrective actions and controls are implemented, affected personnel are informed, and applicable authorizations and critical controls are reverified.

clauses.heading: Work Restriction, Suspension, Termination and Continuity of Control
clauses.text: During suspension, termination, transfer, demobilization or closeout, Business Units/Corporate Functions and the contractor shall maintain applicable critical controls, emergency arrangements, site security, environmental protection, permit conditions and required records until the work is made safe and responsibility is formally transferred or closed. Suspension, termination or commercial closeout shall not remove outstanding incident, corrective action, remediation, restoration or EHSS record handover obligations.

clauses.heading: Land Use Permit (LUP)
clauses.text: Where contracted work may occupy, use or change the use of Maaden controlled land, Business Units and Corporate Functions shall determine during scope definition whether a Land Use Permit or other land, environmental, security, building, excavation, access or work approval is required.

clauses.heading: Land Use Permit (LUP)
clauses.text: The contractor shall not establish or occupy a camp, temporary facility, laydown area, workshop, store, access route, utility corridor or other land use area until required approvals are granted and pre-use conditions are verified.

clauses.heading: Land Use Permit (LUP)
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall incorporate applicable approval boundaries, duration, permitted use, responsibilities, controls, change conditions, restoration obligations and closeout criteria into the contract and readiness arrangements.

clauses.heading: Land Use Permit (LUP)
clauses.text: The contractor shall not transfer, share, expand or materially change an approved land use without prior authorization.

clauses.heading: Land Use Permit (LUP)
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall review and, where required, amend, renew or reissue the approval before a change to the approved use, boundary, size, structure, route, duration, responsible party or approval basis.

clauses.heading: Land Use Permit (LUP)
clauses.text: Before approval expiry, handover or transfer, the contractor shall remove temporary facilities, materials, chemicals, equipment and waste, resolve outstanding obligations, and restore or remediate the affected land to the defined acceptance criteria.

clauses.heading: Land Use Permit (LUP)
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify compliance during readiness, execution and closeout and shall retain the approval, amendments, material findings, restoration evidence and final acceptance record.

clauses.heading: Contractor EHSS Records and Information Handover
clauses.text: The contract shall define the EHSS records and information that the contractor is required to create, maintain, protect, submit and hand over. Such records shall meet applicable legal, permit, contract records management requirements.

clauses.heading: Contractor EHSS Records and Information Handover
clauses.text: Before closeout, Business Units and Corporate Functions shall verify through the applicable Contractor Management Manual arrangements that required EHSS records and information have been received and accepted.

clauses.heading: Demobilization, EHSS Closeout and Learning
clauses.text: Demobilization and closeout shall be managed through the applicable Contractor Management Manual arrangements and shall include verification of applicable EHSS closeout conditions and required EHSS clearance before the contracted scope is closed.

clauses.heading: Demobilization, EHSS Closeout and Learning
clauses.text: Incomplete EHSS actions remaining at demobilization or closeout shall have an assigned accountable party, due date, interim controls where required and a defined verification requirement.

clauses.heading: Demobilization, EHSS Closeout and Learning
clauses.text: Contractor and subcontractor EHSS performance and relevant lessons learned shall be captured through the applicable contractor management closeout arrangements and used to inform future EHSS capability assessments, contractor selection and contracted work planning.

clauses.heading: Demobilization, EHSS Closeout and Learning
clauses.text: Contractor EHSS incidents shall be reported, investigated, communicated and closed in accordance with section 6.1 Incident Management and Stewardship.
