processes.title: Project EHSS Management
processes.purpose: Projects integrate and assure applicable EHSS requirements throughout the project lifecycle so that EHSS risks are managed, requirements are incorporated into project design and execution, and assets are safely transitioned to operations.
processes.scope: This process applies to greenfield and brownfield projects owned, managed or controlled by Maaden, including capital, enhancement, exploration and development projects, expansions, modifications and upgrades, and mine closure from early project definition through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, operational readiness, handover and closeout.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Governance
clauses.text: Projects shall define and communicate EHSS accountabilities and interfaces among the project team, relevant Corporate and Business Unit functions, contractors and the receiving operating organization.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Governance
clauses.text: The Project Manager shall be accountable for integrating applicable EHSS requirements, resources, deliverables and assurance activities into project planning, decisions and stage gate arrangements.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Governance
clauses.text: Projects shall integrate EHSS input from the earliest applicable project stage and before decisions are made that could affect site selection, technology selection, design or execution strategy.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Governance
clauses.text: Projects shall establish EHSS governance and assurance arrangements appropriate to the applicable project delivery and governance model.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Planning and Risk Management
clauses.text: Each project shall determine its EHSS risk profile based on the project scope, location, lifecycle stage, activities, technology, interfaces, credible consequences and applicable obligations.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Planning and Risk Management
clauses.text: Project EHSS requirements and assurance activities shall be proportionate to the resulting EHSS risk profile.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Planning and Risk Management
clauses.text: Projects shall establish and maintain an EHSS Management Plan or equivalent controlled arrangements defining applicable EHSS requirements, responsibilities, deliverables, assurance activities and stage gate criteria.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Planning and Risk Management
clauses.text: Projects shall identify and integrate applicable EHSS legal, regulatory, permit and approval requirements throughout the project lifecycle in accordance with Process 2.4 EHSS Legal and Regulatory Requirements.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Planning and Risk Management
clauses.text: Projects shall apply Process 2.5 EHSS Risk Management throughout the project lifecycle and maintain the risk and hazard information necessary to support project decisions and transfer to operations.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Planning and Risk Management
clauses.text: Projects shall determine and complete the EHSS studies, assessments and reviews required by the project risk profile, applicable requirements and relevant MSHEM processes.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Planning and Risk Management
clauses.text: Projects shall document EHSS decisions, assumptions, findings and recommendations and track resulting actions to verified closure or controlled transfer.

clauses.heading: EHSS in Project Design
clauses.text: Project design shall incorporate applicable MSHEM, legal, regulatory and approved Maaden technical requirements and apply the hierarchy of controls. All capital projects shall incorporate environmental and sustainability requirements addressed in MCIS_TK_0387.

clauses.heading: EHSS in Project Design
clauses.text: Projects shall identify EHSS critical assets, critical controls and required performance criteria during design and incorporate them into procurement, construction, commissioning and handover.

clauses.heading: EHSS in Project Design
clauses.text: Project design shall consider safe construction, commissioning, operation, inspection, maintenance, emergency response, decommissioning, closure and rehabilitation throughout the asset lifecycle.

clauses.heading: EHSS in Project Design
clauses.text: Facility siting and the location and design of permanent, temporary and occupied buildings shall be assessed, where applicable, for credible fire, explosion, toxic release and other major hazards that could affect occupants or emergency functions.

clauses.heading: EHSS in Project Design
clauses.text: Cybersecurity risks associated with Operational Technology systems shall be identified and addressed during project design and applicable hazard and risk assessments in accordance with Maaden cybersecurity requirements.

clauses.heading: EHSS in Project Design
clauses.text:
Projects shall control changes that could affect the approved EHSS basis through project change control and section
3.52 Management of Change process.

clauses.heading: Environmental and Health Assurance
clauses.text: Projects shall complete and integrate environmental and social baseline studies, impact assessments studies, project categorization and permitting deliverables and mitigation requirements in accordance with applicable legal requirements and relevant MSHEM environmental processes.

clauses.heading: Environmental and Health Assurance
clauses.text: Projects shall identify and control occupational health and industrial hygiene risks arising during project execution and future operation in accordance with applicable MSHEM health processes.

clauses.heading: Exploration Projects
clauses.text: Exploration projects shall establish environmental management arrangements before exploration activities commence, addressing applicable risks associated with locations, access routes, camps and temporary facilities, land disturbance, drilling, trenching and sampling, soil, water, waste, air quality, biodiversity, fuels and hazardous materials.

clauses.heading: Exploration Projects
clauses.text: Exploration areas and temporary facilities shall be progressively rehabilitated, where practicable, and when no longer required shall be appropriately decommissioned, remediated or restored in accordance with applicable legal, regulatory, permit obligations, and MSHEM requirements.

clauses.heading: Project Security Assurance
clauses.text: Projects shall identify applicable physical and industrial security requirements during early project development and integrate them into the project scope, design basis, schedule, procurement, construction, commissioning and operational-readiness arrangements.

clauses.heading: Project Security Assurance
clauses.text: Where applicable under Supreme Authority for Industrial Security (SAIS) requirements, the Facility Operator shall complete the required Business Criteria Analysis to determine the facility security classification and applicable security requirements.

clauses.heading: Project Security Assurance
clauses.text: Projects subject to SAIS requirements shall complete the applicable security approval stages and obtain required approvals before dependent design, procurement, construction, commissioning or operation proceeds.

clauses.heading: Project Security Assurance
clauses.text: Security Risk Assessments, security design and other activities requiring SAIS approval shall be performed by appropriately qualified and SAIS approved consultants or contractors, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Project Security Assurance
clauses.text: Corporate Security shall provide the applicable governance review and act as Maaden's interface with SAIS for required submissions and regulatory correspondence.

clauses.heading: Project Security Assurance
clauses.text: Security requirements shall be coordinated with civil, electrical, communications, information technology, infrastructure and other project packages necessary for effective implementation and commissioning of security systems.

clauses.heading: Project Security Assurance
clauses.text: Projects shall classify, control access to and protect security sensitive project information in accordance with applicable information protection and authority requirements.

clauses.heading: Project Security Assurance
clauses.text: Projects shall obtain required authority and Maaden approvals for proposed deviations from applicable security requirements before implementation.

clauses.heading: Contractor and Construction EHSS Management
clauses.text: Applicable EHSS requirements shall be incorporated into project procurement, contractor evaluation, contract documents and contractor management arrangements in accordance with Section 4.1 Contractor EHSS Management.

clauses.heading: Contractor and Construction EHSS Management
clauses.text: Before construction begins, the project shall verify that required construction EHSS plans, competent resources, risk assessments, emergency arrangements, work controls, temporary facilities and other applicable readiness conditions are established.

clauses.heading: Contractor and Construction EHSS Management
clauses.text: Projects shall manage construction EHSS risks, changing conditions and interfaces throughout execution.

clauses.heading: Contractor and Construction EHSS Management
clauses.text: Projects shall apply quality assurance, inspection, testing, preservation and verification controls to EHSS critical assets, systems and controls during procurement, construction and commissioning.

clauses.heading: Commissioning, Operational Readiness and Handover
clauses.text: Projects shall initiate operational readiness planning in time for the receiving organization to influence design and establish the people, competency, procedures, maintenance and emergency arrangements required for operation.

clauses.heading: Commissioning, Operational Readiness and Handover
clauses.text: Projects shall verify commissioning EHSS readiness before commissioning or the introduction of hazardous materials or energy.

clauses.heading: Commissioning, Operational Readiness and Handover
clauses.text: A Pre-Startup Safety Review shall be completed before startup or introduction of hazardous materials or energy in accordance with section 3.53 Pre-Startup Safety Review process.

clauses.heading: Commissioning, Operational Readiness and Handover
clauses.text: Projects shall verify that required EHSS critical assets and operational arrangements meet approved design, performance, regulatory and readiness requirements before operation.

clauses.heading: Commissioning, Operational Readiness and Handover
clauses.text: Before operational handover, the project and receiving organization shall verify that applicable EHSS requirements, critical controls, safety critical systems, approvals, procedures, competencies and outstanding actions are complete or subject to an approved controlled transfer arrangement.

clauses.heading: Commissioning, Operational Readiness and Handover
clauses.text: Residual EHSS risks and outstanding actions shall be understood and formally accepted by the receiving organization through applicable governance arrangements.

clauses.heading: Commissioning, Operational Readiness and Handover
clauses.text: Project handover shall provide the receiving organization with the controlled EHSS information required to operate, maintain, modify, decommission and close the asset.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Assurance, Closeout and Records
clauses.text: Projects shall conduct risk-based EHSS assurance at defined lifecycle stages to verify conformance with applicable project, design, MSHEM, legal, regulatory and stage gate requirements.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Assurance, Closeout and Records
clauses.text: Project closeout shall verify completion or controlled transfer of outstanding EHSS obligations, actions, commitments and required records.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Assurance, Closeout and Records
clauses.text: Projects shall capture and communicate relevant EHSS lessons from design, execution, commissioning and assurance activities.

clauses.heading: Project EHSS Assurance, Closeout and Records
clauses.text: Projects shall control, retain and transfer EHSS records in accordance with applicable legal, regulatory and project requirements.

processes.trigger: Use across applicable greenfield and brownfield project lifecycles, from early definition and design through construction, commissioning, readiness, handover and closeout.

processes.title: Emergency Response Preparedness and Planning
processes.purpose: Establish minimum requirements for identifying credible emergency scenarios and maintaining effective plans, capabilities, resources, and coordination arrangements to protect people, the environment, assets, operations, and affected communities.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Units and Corporate Functions, employees, contractors, and relevant stakeholders involved in emergency preparedness and planning for Maaden controlled operational, administrative, project, mining, processing, and remote locations.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement, and maintain documented emergency preparedness and response arrangements based on their activities, facilities, hazards, credible emergency scenarios, and potential consequences.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness Management
clauses.text: Emergency preparedness and response arrangements shall comply with applicable legal, regulatory, permit, and authority requirements. Facilities comply with SAIS SAF-20, Pre-Incident Planning and Management of Emergencies, including applicable notification and coordination requirements.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness Management
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define accountability, roles, responsibilities, authorities, and interfaces for implementing and maintaining emergency preparedness and response arrangements.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness Management
clauses.text: Emergency preparedness and response arrangements shall address people who may be affected and coordination with applicable internal functions, neighboring operations, emergency services, authorities, mutual aid organizations, and other response partners.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness Management
clauses.text: Emergency preparedness requirements shall be integrated into the design, construction, modification, operation, and decommissioning of facilities and activities.

clauses.heading: Emergency Preparedness Management
clauses.text: Changes that can affect emergency scenarios or response capability shall be assessed, and affected emergency plans, Pre-Incident Plans, resources, training, and coordination arrangements shall be updated.

clauses.heading: Emergency Scenario Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall identify and assess credible emergency scenarios arising from their activities, facilities, hazards, infrastructure, and surrounding conditions.

clauses.heading: Emergency Scenario Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Scenario assessments shall be conducted by competent personnel with collective knowledge of the applicable activities, hazards, potential consequences, and emergency response requirements.

clauses.heading: Emergency Scenario Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Scenario identification shall consider internal and external events and be informed by applicable risk assessments, Process Hazard Analyses, incidents, emergency responses, exercises, and relevant lessons learned.

clauses.heading: Emergency Scenario Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Credible scenarios shall include, where relevant, fire, explosion, loss of containment, hazardous material or radiological release, structural failure, rescue and medical emergencies, natural hazards, utility failure, transportation and security events, mine emergencies, and other events with potential major consequences.

clauses.heading: Emergency Scenario Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Assessments shall consider exposed people, hazardous material inventories and release paths, facility layout and access, geographic and climatic conditions, neighboring activities, environmental receptors, and potential off-site consequences.

clauses.heading: Emergency Scenario Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Credible scenarios shall be prioritized using the Maaden EHSS Risk Matrix and considering potential consequences, escalation, response complexity, required resources, and available response capabilities.

clauses.heading: Emergency Scenario Identification and Assessment
clauses.text: Assessment results shall be documented and used to define emergency planning, capability, training, and exercise requirements.

clauses.heading: Emergency Strategies, Plans and Pre-Incident Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement, and maintain an Emergency Response Plan based on identified credible scenarios and assessed consequences, including applicable environmental emergencies and spills.

clauses.heading: Emergency Strategies, Plans and Pre-Incident Planning
clauses.text: Emergency response strategies shall prioritize the protection and rescue of people, including responders and affected communities; stabilization of the incident and prevention of escalation; protection of the environment and property; and transition to recovery.

clauses.heading: Emergency Strategies, Plans and Pre-Incident Planning
clauses.text: Pre-Incident Plans shall be developed and maintained for prioritized credible scenarios requiring scenario specific tactics, resources, coordination, or protective actions.

clauses.heading: Emergency Strategies, Plans and Pre-Incident Planning
clauses.text: Emergency plans shall define arrangements for emergency notification and activation; incident command, coordination, and escalation; protection and accountability of affected people; operational and protective response actions; control of the incident area; and transition to re-entry and recovery.

clauses.heading: Emergency Strategies, Plans and Pre-Incident Planning
clauses.text: Emergency plans shall establish a scalable Incident Command System, including command authority, transfer of command, coordination interfaces, and escalation arrangements.

clauses.heading: Emergency Strategies, Plans and Pre-Incident Planning
clauses.text: Required emergency response personnel, competencies, equipment, systems, facilities, and external support shall be determined from the credible scenarios and response strategies.

clauses.heading: Emergency Strategies, Plans and Pre-Incident Planning
clauses.text: An Emergency Operations Center or equivalent coordination facility shall be established and maintained where required by assessed consequences, response complexity, or applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

clauses.heading: Emergency Strategies, Plans and Pre-Incident Planning
clauses.text: Emergency plans shall define coordination and communication interfaces with applicable internal functions, contractors, neighboring facilities, authorities, emergency services, mutual-aid organizations, and other response partners.

clauses.heading: Emergency Strategies, Plans and Pre-Incident Planning
clauses.text: Where credible scenarios can result in off-site consequences, emergency plans shall define arrangements for warning, protective action communication, and coordination with affected facilities, communities, authorities, and authorized public-communication functions.

clauses.heading: Emergency Strategies, Plans and Pre-Incident Planning
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define the hierarchy and approval authority for Emergency Response Plans and Pre-Incident Plans and integrate them with applicable crisis management and business continuity arrangements.

clauses.heading: Emergency Strategies, Plans and Pre-Incident Planning
clauses.text: Current information required to support emergency command and response, including location, access, hazard, utility, isolation, resource, and contact information, shall be readily accessible to authorized internal and external responders.

clauses.heading: Emergency Capabilities, Resources and Coordination
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall determine the emergency capabilities and resources required for identified credible scenarios, considering their nature, scale, location, potential consequences, escalation potential, and response complexity.

clauses.heading: Emergency Capabilities, Resources and Coordination
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain documented readiness requirements for emergency personnel, equipment, facilities, communication systems, medical support, and internal and external response resources based on identified credible scenarios.

clauses.heading: Emergency Capabilities, Resources and Coordination
clauses.text: Emergency personnel and response coverage shall be sufficient for identified credible scenarios across operating shifts, remote locations, periods of reduced staffing, contractor activities, and foreseeable resource unavailability.

clauses.heading: Emergency Capabilities, Resources and Coordination
clauses.text: Responsibilities, communication arrangements, resource commitments, and response interfaces with contractors, authorities, external emergency services, neighboring facilities, and mutual aid organizations shall be documented.

clauses.heading: Emergency Capabilities, Resources and Coordination
clauses.text: The availability and mobilization of external and mutual aid resources, including communication interoperability and equipment compatibility, shall be verified through applicable drills or exercises.

clauses.heading: Emergency Capabilities, Resources and Coordination
clauses.text: Emergency capability gaps shall be assessed, and interim controls shall be implemented until the required capability is restored or an alternative providing equivalent risk control is established.

clauses.heading: Emergency Competency, Training and Awareness
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define role specific competency and training requirements for personnel with emergency responsibilities, based on assigned roles, credible scenarios, hazards, response strategies, and equipment.

clauses.heading: Emergency Competency, Training and Awareness
clauses.text: Personnel shall demonstrate the required competency before assignment to an emergency role and shall be formally appointed or authorized where required by the role or applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

clauses.heading: Emergency Competency, Training and Awareness
clauses.text: Employees, contractor personnel, visitors, and other people at Maaden controlled workplaces shall receive information and instructions relevant to their expected actions during an emergency, including alarm recognition, emergency reporting, evacuation, assembly, and shelter arrangements.

clauses.heading: Emergency Competency, Training and Awareness
clauses.text: Competency for personnel with emergency response duties shall be assessed against defined role specific criteria at established intervals and following circumstances that can affect their ability to perform the role. Assessments shall include practical demonstration where the role requires applied response skills.

clauses.heading: Emergency Competency, Training and Awareness
clauses.text: Emergency competency, training, and awareness requirements shall be reviewed and updated following changes affecting emergency arrangements, identified competency deficiencies, or relevant findings from drills, exercises, incidents, and assurance activities.

clauses.heading: Exercises and Preparedness Verification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish, implement, and monitor an annual risk-based drill and exercise program covering prioritized credible emergency scenarios. The program shall address applicable legal and regulatory requirements, emergency risks, operational changes, previous exercise and emergency performance, and identified competency needs.

clauses.heading: Exercises and Preparedness Verification
clauses.text: Each drill or exercise shall have documented objectives, scope, participants, performance criteria, and evaluation arrangements established before it is conducted.

clauses.heading: Exercises and Preparedness Verification
clauses.text: Drills and exercises shall reflect the applicable scenario, response arrangements, location, operating conditions, and external interfaces. Each drill or exercise shall be subject to a documented safety review, and hazardous response actions shall be simulated where their physical execution would introduce unacceptable risk.

clauses.heading: Exercises and Preparedness Verification
clauses.text: The exercise program shall verify applicable emergency command, communication, notification, personnel accountability, protective actions, operational response, response capability, resource availability, external coordination, and initial recovery arrangements.

clauses.heading: Exercises and Preparedness Verification
clauses.text: Employees, contractors, emergency personnel, support functions, and external response parties shall participate in drills and exercises relevant to their assigned roles.

clauses.heading: Exercises and Preparedness Verification
clauses.text: Mining operations shall include mine specific emergency arrangements within the exercise program, where applicable. Each mine shall conduct at least two evacuation drills annually, covering representative work areas and operating conditions.

clauses.heading: Exercises and Preparedness Verification
Exercises and Preparedness Verification
clauses.text: Exercise performance and findings shall be evaluated and documented, and resulting corrective actions and lessons learned shall be communicated, tracked to closure, and used to improve emergency preparedness and response arrangements.

clauses.heading: Preparedness Monitoring and Plan Review
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall evaluate the effectiveness of applicable emergency preparedness and response arrangements at defined intervals using results from exercises, actual emergencies, audits, and other relevant performance information.

clauses.heading: Preparedness Monitoring and Plan Review
clauses.text: Emergency Response Plans and Pre-Incident Plans shall be formally reviewed, updated as necessary, and reapproved at least once every three years.

clauses.heading: Preparedness Monitoring and Plan Review
clauses.text: Emergency plans and arrangements shall be reviewed and updated as necessary following exercises, actual emergencies, relevant changes, audits, or findings that may affect their adequacy or effectiveness.

clauses.heading: Preparedness Monitoring and Plan Review
clauses.text: Lessons and deficiencies identified through exercises, emergencies, audits, and other evaluations shall be used to improve applicable emergency arrangements, with required actions managed through the applicable corrective- action process.

clauses.heading: Preparedness Monitoring and Plan Review
clauses.text: Documented evidence of emergency plan reviews, exercises, preparedness evaluations, lessons learned, and resulting actions shall be retained in accordance with applicable record-control requirements.

processes.title: Emergency Response Team Selection and Training
processes.purpose: Establish minimum requirements for determining Emergency Response Team needs and for selecting, training, qualifying, equipping, authorizing and maintaining competent personnel capable of performing assigned emergency response duties safely and effectively.
processes.scope: This process applies to Business Units and Corporate Functions that establish, provide, manage, or rely upon internal, contractor, mutual aid, or external Emergency Response Teams for firefighting, rescue, medical, hazardous material, mine emergency or other specialized emergency response functions.

clauses.heading: ERT Management and Capability Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain documented arrangements for managing Emergency Response Teams in accordance with applicable legal, regulatory, and adopted technical requirements.

clauses.heading: ERT Management and Capability Requirements
clauses.text: Required ERT functions and capabilities shall be determined through a documented and approved capability assessment considering credible emergency scenarios, response plans, risk assessments, operating conditions, and the capability requirements established under section 5.1 Emergency Response Preparedness and Planning.

clauses.heading: ERT Management and Capability Requirements
clauses.text: ERT capabilities shall address firefighting, rescue, medical, hazardous-material, mine-emergency, and other specialized response functions identified through the emergency capability assessment.

clauses.heading: ERT Management and Capability Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall define the ERT organization, operational capability level, authority, responsibilities, command arrangements, and response limitations in accordance with NFPA 600 and the applicable provisions of NFPA 1550.

clauses.heading: ERT Management and Capability Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish role specific criteria for selecting ERT members, addressing the knowledge, skills, experience, qualifications, availability, and medical and physical suitability required for their assigned emergency duties.

clauses.heading: ERT Management and Capability Requirements
clauses.text: ERT candidates and members shall be medically evaluated and cleared by a competent occupational health physician before assignment, at least annually thereafter, and before returning to emergency duties following an illness, injury, condition, or absence that could affect their capability. Medical information shall remain confidential, with only fitness status and necessary work restrictions communicated to management, in accordance with Process 3.19 and NFPA 1580, as applicable.

clauses.heading: ERT Management and Capability Requirements
clauses.text: ERT members shall only be assigned or authorized for functions for which they are medically and physically fit, trained, assessed as competent, qualified, equipped, and capable of performing the assigned duties safely.

clauses.heading: ERT Management and Capability Requirements
clauses.text: Minimum ERT staffing, availability, backup coverage, and personnel distribution shall be defined and maintained for the required response capabilities, operating shifts, locations, and foreseeable emergency conditions.

clauses.heading: ERT Management and Capability Requirements
clauses.text: Internal ERT arrangements shall be coordinated with relevant contractors, neighboring facilities, mutual-aid organizations, external emergency services, and authorities. Their roles, interfaces, resource commitments, communication arrangements, and limitations shall be defined.

clauses.heading: ERT Management and Capability Requirements
clauses.text: Activities or facilities shall not commence or continue operation unless the required ERT capability is available or approved interim controls and alternative response arrangements have been established. Changes affecting ERT capabilities or arrangements shall be assessed and managed through Process 3.52 where the Management of Change applicability criteria are met.

clauses.heading: ERT Training and Qualification
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain an ERT training and qualification program based on credible emergency scenarios, required response capabilities, assigned roles, and applicable legal and adopted technical requirements.

clauses.heading: ERT Training and Qualification
clauses.text: ERT members shall complete approved initial training and demonstrate the required competency before authorization to perform emergency response duties.

clauses.heading: ERT Training and Qualification
clauses.text: ERT members shall demonstrate the safe use of assigned apparatus, equipment, communication systems, respiratory protection, and PPE before independent assignment.

clauses.heading: ERT Training and Qualification
clauses.text: Training and qualification requirements shall be defined for each assigned operational level and function, including ERT leader, incident commander, incident safety officer, instructor, assessor, and other specialist roles, where applicable. An annual training, certification, and competency assessment plan shall be maintained. Minimum role specific qualification, initial training, refresher training, certification renewal, and competency reassessment requirements shall be defined in an approved ERT Training and Competency Matrix.

clauses.heading: ERT Training and Qualification
clauses.text: ERT training shall address, as applicable to assigned roles, facility hazards, credible emergency scenarios, emergency-response plans, Pre-Incident Plans, fixed fire-protection and detection systems, assigned response procedures, command arrangements, communications, personnel accountability, responder safety, and the inspection, use, care, and limitations of assigned equipment and PPE.

clauses.heading: ERT Training and Qualification
clauses.text: Facility fire-brigade members, firefighters, and fire-apparatus driver/operators shall be trained and qualified for their assigned operating levels and duties in accordance with NFPA 600, NFPA 1081, and NFPA 1010, as applicable. Live fire training shall be planned, delivered, and controlled in accordance with NFPA 1400.

clauses.heading: ERT Training and Qualification
clauses.text: Personnel assigned technical-rescue duties shall be trained and qualified for the applicable rescue discipline and operational level in accordance with NFPA 1006.

clauses.heading: ERT Training and Qualification
clauses.text: Personnel assigned hazardous-material response duties shall be trained and qualified for their assigned awareness, operations, technician, or incident-command level in accordance with NFPA 470. ERT members shall maintain valid CPR/AED certification and any first aid, bloodborne pathogen, or other medical response certification required by their assigned roles.

clauses.heading: ERT Training and Qualification
clauses.text: ERT instructors and assessors shall be competent and authorized for the subjects, functions, and qualification levels they deliver or assess. Formal certifications identified in the approved ERT Training and Competency Matrix shall be issued through Pro Board, IFSAC, or another accreditation or certification system formally approved by Maaden.

clauses.heading: ERT Training and Qualification
clauses.text: ERT competency shall be maintained through refresher training, certification renewal, and competency reassessment. Each ERT member shall complete a documented practical competency evaluation at least annually. Additional training or reassessment shall be completed following relevant changes, extended absence, incidents, exercises, unsatisfactory assessment results, or identified competency deficiencies.

clauses.heading: Operational Readiness and Competency
clauses.text: Where an underground mine ERT capability is required, assigned members shall complete at least 80 hours of mine- emergency training annually, covering breathing-apparatus operations, mine fires and explosions, ventilation and controls, mine gases and atmosphere evaluation, exploration, search and rescue, emergency planning, and command integration. Practical underground training shall be conducted at least once every six months and shall include search, navigation, and rescue under smoke or controlled smoke-equivalent conditions.

clauses.heading: Operational Readiness and Competency
clauses.text: ERT members shall maintain current operational familiarity with facility-specific access and egress routes, response-equipment locations, communication systems, staging and command locations, and external response interfaces applicable to their assigned functions.

clauses.heading: Operational Readiness and Competency
clauses.text: ERT members shall have access to suitable and serviceable PPE, respiratory protection, apparatus, tools, communication systems, and other equipment required for their assigned functions and credible response conditions.

clauses.heading: Operational Readiness and Competency
clauses.text: Each ERT member shall participate in at least four scenario-based ERT drills annually, covering scenarios applicable to their assigned functions and identified through the emergency capability assessment. Drill planning and evaluation shall be coordinated through Process 5.1. Participation in an actual emergency response shall not substitute for required training unless an approved equivalency has been established and the member’s performance has been documented and assessed against the applicable competency requirements.

clauses.heading: Operational Readiness and Competency
clauses.text: Where SCBA or supplied-air respiratory protection is used, incident-scene controls shall provide for wearer identification, location and task tracking, entry and air-duration monitoring, emergency withdrawal, and PASS or equivalent devices. Incident-scene arrangements shall include an Incident Safety Officer and controls for responder rescue, rehabilitation, and infection prevention, based on the incident complexity and risk.

clauses.heading: Operational Readiness and Competency
clauses.text: Authorization to perform emergency-response duties shall be suspended when an ERT member no longer maintains the required medical or physical fitness, competency, qualification, certification, participation, or operational readiness and reinstated only after the applicable requirements are satisfied, supporting evidence is documented, and formal clearance is obtained.

clauses.heading: ERT Performance Monitoring and Improvement
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and periodically review performance measures for ERT staffing and coverage, training, competency, qualification, authorization, medical and physical fitness, participation, equipment readiness, and internal and external response arrangements, using relevant results from training assessments, drills, exercises, actual responses, inspections, and compliance reviews.

clauses.heading: ERT Performance Monitoring and Improvement
clauses.text: ERT training and qualification requirements and programs shall be periodically reviewed for continued alignment with assigned duties, credible emergency scenarios, applicable legal requirements, adopted standards, certification conditions, and the approved ERT Training and Competency Matrix.

clauses.heading: ERT Performance Monitoring and Improvement
clauses.text: The availability and capability of internal and external response resources and arrangements shall be periodically verified, including the continued validity of applicable mutual-aid and external-service commitments.

clauses.heading: ERT Performance Monitoring and Improvement
clauses.text: Deficiencies affecting ERT capability shall be controlled and managed through the applicable corrective action process until the required capability is restored or an approved alternative response arrangement is established. Identified actions shall be assigned, tracked, and verified for effective closure, and findings and lessons learned shall be used to improve ERT management, selection, training, qualification, resources, readiness, and response arrangements.

clauses.heading: ERT Performance Monitoring and Improvement
clauses.text: Records demonstrating ERT capability, staffing, selection, medical and physical fitness, assignment, authorization, qualification, certification, training, competency reassessment, participation, equipment readiness, external- response arrangements, performance monitoring, and corrective action closure shall be maintained and retained in accordance with applicable legal and record control requirements in accordance with Process 3.19.

processes.title: Emergency Response Equipment Maintenance, Testing and Interruption
processes.purpose: Establish minimum requirements for maintaining emergency response equipment and systems throughout their lifecycle in a reliable and ready condition, including the control of inspection, testing, maintenance, interruption, restoration, decommissioning, disposal and readiness monitoring.
processes.scope: This process applies to emergency response equipment, materials, vehicles, fire protection systems, detection and alarm systems, communication systems, medical and rescue equipment, environmental response equipment, and other emergency resources provided or controlled by Maaden Business Units and Corporate Functions.

clauses.heading: Emergency Equipment Management and Asset Control
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain documented arrangements for managing emergency equipment and systems under their control throughout their lifecycle, including acquisition, acceptance, operation, maintenance, modification, decommissioning and disposal.

clauses.heading: Emergency Equipment Management and Asset Control
clauses.text: Emergency equipment and systems shall be identified from credible emergency scenarios, response plans, Pre- Incident Plans, legal requirements, and required response capabilities.

clauses.heading: Emergency Equipment Management and Asset Control
clauses.text: All emergency response equipment and systems shall be classified as EHSS critical assets, designated as AC0. This categorization ensures that such equipment receives the highest priority in terms of preventive maintenance, testing, and overall management.

clauses.heading: Emergency Equipment Management and Asset Control
clauses.text: Roles and authorities for equipment specification, approval, procurement, acceptance, custody, inspection, testing, maintenance, impairment control, and disposal shall be defined.

clauses.heading: Emergency Equipment Management and Asset Control
clauses.text: Emergency equipment and systems shall comply with applicable legal, regulatory, permit and authority requirements, including applicable SAIS Safety and Fire Protection Directives.

clauses.heading: Emergency Equipment Management and Asset Control
clauses.text: Emergency equipment shall be suitable for its intended function, operating environment, users, and identified emergency scenarios. Fire protection equipment and systems shall be approved, listed or certified, as applicable, by SASO or another competent Saudi authority and, where required by approved specifications, UL, FM or equivalent.

clauses.heading: Emergency Equipment Management and Asset Control
clauses.text: Emergency equipment and systems shall be recorded in an approved emergency-equipment register or maintenance-management system and managed against approved equipment-specific inspection, testing and maintenance schedules. Records shall include, as applicable, asset identity, location, ownership, criticality, technical requirements, service status, service life and applicable certification. Equipment shall be inspected and accepted before initial service, following replacement or modification, and after significant maintenance.

clauses.heading: Emergency Equipment Management and Asset Control
clauses.text: Contractor-provided, leased, mobile, shared and externally maintained emergency equipment shall meet the same applicable approval, readiness and asset-control requirements. Contractors performing inspection, testing, maintenance or certification shall meet applicable Saudi accreditation or authorization requirements.

clauses.heading: Emergency Equipment Management and Asset Control
clauses.text: Unauthorized modification, substitution, relocation, removal, or non-emergency use of emergency equipment shall be prevented. Changes affecting equipment type, quantity, location, capacity, performance, availability or supporting infrastructure shall be assessed and authorized before implementation and managed through Management of Change where they could affect required emergency capability.

clauses.heading: Emergency Equipment Management and Asset Control
clauses.text: Obsolete, expired, recalled, damaged, nonconforming or decommissioned emergency equipment shall be identified, controlled, removed from service and disposed of through approved arrangements that prevent unauthorized reuse. Business Units and Corporate Functions shall periodically verify that equipment inventories and asset information remain complete, accurate and aligned with required emergency capabilities. Required specifications, approvals, certificates, asset changes and disposal records shall be maintained in accordance with applicable record control requirements.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Maintenance Requirements
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish and maintain an approved inspection, testing and preventive maintenance program for emergency equipment and systems.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Maintenance Requirements
clauses.text: Inspection, testing and maintenance requirements shall be based on equipment criticality, credible emergency scenarios, applicable legal and regulatory requirements, manufacturer instructions and adopted technical standards, including NFPA 10, NFPA 25, NFPA 72, NFPA 110 and other applicable equipment specific standards.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Maintenance Requirements
clauses.text: Emergency equipment and systems shall be inspected, tested and maintained at defined intervals to confirm their availability, integrity and required performance against equipment-specific acceptance criteria.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Maintenance Requirements
clauses.text: Inspection, testing and maintenance activities shall be performed by competent and authorized personnel using approved methods and, where required, calibrated or functionally verified measuring and test equipment, with independent testing or certification conducted by an appropriately accredited or Saudi authorized organization.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Maintenance Requirements
clauses.text: Maintenance, replacement parts, consumables and modifications shall comply with approved specifications and manufacturer requirements.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Maintenance Requirements
clauses.text: Overdue or missed inspection, testing or maintenance activities shall be managed through the applicable Asset Maintenance Deferment requirements. The deferment shall identify the affected equipment and system components, assess the resulting risk, establish compensating controls and escalation requirements, assign an accountable owner and completion date, and require completion at the earliest practicable opportunity.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Maintenance Requirements
clauses.text: Inspection and testing activities shall not reduce emergency capability unless an approved impairment arrangement and suitable compensating controls are established.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Maintenance Requirements
clauses.text: Defective, damaged, expired, contaminated or noncompliant equipment shall be identified and removed from service until repaired or replaced and successfully inspected and tested for return to service. Equipment with expired mandatory certification or unresolved legal noncompliance shall not be approved for continued use.

clauses.heading: Inspection, Testing and Maintenance Requirements
clauses.text: Inspection, testing, maintenance, defects, repairs, replacements and return-to-service results shall be recorded in the approved maintenance management system. Business Units and Corporate Functions shall periodically verify compliance with the approved program and completion of required corrective actions.

clauses.heading: Equipment Interruption and Compensating Controls
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish documented arrangements to assess, authorize and control planned and unplanned interruptions of emergency equipment and systems. An interruption shall not be initiated without prior assessment and authorization, except where immediate action is necessary to protect personnel or prevent escalation of an emergency or equipment damage.

clauses.heading: Equipment Interruption and Compensating Controls
clauses.text: The interruption shall be classified and assessed based on equipment criticality, the affected emergency capability, credible emergency scenarios, operating conditions, expected duration and potential consequences, and the assessment shall define the compensating controls and operating conditions required during the interruption.

clauses.heading: Equipment Interruption and Compensating Controls
clauses.text: Compensating controls shall be implemented before a planned interruption and as soon as practicable following an unplanned interruption. The controls shall be maintained and periodically verified for effectiveness during the authorized interruption period and reassessed when the interruption duration, operating conditions or emergency risks change.

clauses.heading: Equipment Interruption and Compensating Controls
clauses.text: Relevant affected parties shall be notified of the interruption, compensating controls and restoration of the equipment or system. External responders and authorities shall be notified where their response arrangements or applicable notification requirements are affected.

clauses.heading: Equipment Interruption and Compensating Controls
clauses.text: Activities or facilities shall be restricted, suspended or shut down where the interruption assessment determines that the required emergency capability cannot be maintained.

clauses.heading: Equipment Interruption and Compensating Controls
clauses.text: Interrupted equipment and systems shall be restored according to priorities and target completion requirements established based on equipment criticality, the affected emergency capability and assessed risk. Return to service shall be verified and authorized before the applicable compensating controls are removed.

clauses.heading: Equipment Interruption and Compensating Controls
clauses.text: Interruption records shall include assessment, authorization, compensating controls, required notifications, interruption duration, restoration verification and return to service authorization. Significant or recurring interruptions shall be investigated to identify underlying causes and required improvements, and resulting actions shall be managed through the applicable corrective action process.

clauses.heading: Equipment Interruption and Compensating Controls
clauses.text: Non-emergency use of firewater, hydrants or fire hoses shall be avoided where practicable and shall only occur following documented justification, risk assessment and authorization, with the required quantity and duration recorded. Such use shall not reduce the firewater storage tank level below the approved minimum fire service operating level necessary to maintain the required fire protection design demand, duration and system performance. Where the required fire protection capability cannot be maintained, the condition shall be managed as an interruption in accordance with this process.

clauses.heading: Restoration and Return to Service
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall establish documented arrangements for the controlled restoration and return to service of emergency equipment and systems.

clauses.heading: Restoration and Return to Service
clauses.text: Required maintenance, repair, replacement or corrective work shall be completed before the equipment or system is inspected and functionally tested to verify its condition, configuration, functionality and required performance. The verification shall include settings, connections, power supplies, controls, alarms and supporting systems, as applicable.

clauses.heading: Restoration and Return to Service
clauses.text: Restoration inspection and testing shall be performed by competent and authorized personnel against approved equipment specific acceptance criteria, and return to service shall be authorized by the designated approval authority.

clauses.heading: Restoration and Return to Service
clauses.text: Emergency equipment and systems shall not be returned to service, and associated compensating controls or operating restrictions shall not be removed, until the acceptance criteria have been met and return to service has been verified and authorized.

clauses.heading: Restoration and Return to Service
clauses.text: Equipment or systems that fail restoration testing or do not meet the applicable acceptance criteria shall remain out of service, and the applicable compensating controls and operating restrictions shall remain in place. Repeated restoration test failures shall be investigated and managed through the applicable corrective action process.

clauses.heading: Restoration and Return to Service
clauses.text: Relevant affected parties shall be notified when emergency capability has been restored and associated compensating controls or operating restrictions have been removed. Asset status, applicable equipment inventories, maintenance records, inspection and test results, return-to-service authorization and affected emergency plans shall be updated and retained in the applicable approved systems.

clauses.heading: Readiness Monitoring and Performance Review
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall monitor and review defined indicators of emergency-equipment readiness and maintenance performance. Monitoring shall address equipment availability, completion of required inspection, testing and maintenance, overdue critical maintenance, interruption closure, restoration-testing results, repeated defects, corrective-action completion and relevant findings from drills, exercises and actual emergency responses. Applicable indicator ownership, reporting frequency, targets and escalation thresholds shall be defined.

clauses.heading: Readiness Monitoring and Performance Review
clauses.text: The continuing suitability, sufficiency, location and availability of emergency equipment and systems shall be verified at planned intervals and following material changes to credible emergency scenarios, facilities, operations or response arrangements. The review shall include equipment and services provided, leased, shared or maintained by external parties where they contribute to the required emergency capability. Risk-based independent assurance or competent third-party assessment shall be conducted where required by regulatory obligations, adopted technical standards, equipment criticality or identified performance concerns.

clauses.heading: Readiness Monitoring and Performance Review
clauses.text: Monitoring results, trends, findings and lessons learned shall be used to improve equipment specifications, maintenance strategies, resource and spare-part arrangements, and emergency-response capability. Identified deficiencies and improvement actions shall be risk-prioritized and managed through the applicable corrective-action process.

processes.title: Incident Management and Stewardship
processes.purpose: EHSS incidents, Near Misses, High Potential Incidents (HPIs) and EHSS Observations are consistently reported, classified, investigated, analyzed, communicated, recorded and used to drive effective risk reduction and continual improvement across Maaden.
processes.scope: This process applies to work-related EHSS incidents, occupational injuries and illnesses, near misses, High Potential Incidents, Life Saving Rule violations and EHSS observations involving Maaden employees, contractors or visitors arising from activities under Maaden operational control, including Maaden-managed transportation and work performed on behalf of Maaden outside Maaden-managed facilities. For joint ventures and other activities not under Maaden operational control, the applicable Business Unit shall establish documented arrangements for incident reporting, investigation information sharing, recordkeeping and performance reporting.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Reporting and Notification
clauses.text: Employees, contractors and visitors shall report EHSS events that they are involved in or witness by recording them in the Maaden incident reporting system (HEMAYA). Where the event involves an occupational injury or illness, the incident shall also be reported to the designated medical and EHSS function.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Reporting and Notification
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish and maintain arrangements that encourage EHSS event reporting without fear of retaliation and communicate reporting expectations through EHSS inductions and awareness activities.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Reporting and Notification
clauses.text: EHSS events shall be reported and recorded within the Business Unit, department, project or activity responsible for the affected operation or work activity. Event reports shall contain the information to support notification, classification, investigation, recordkeeping and performance reporting.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Reporting and Notification
clauses.text: EHSS event reporting accountability shall be assigned to the Business Unit, project or activity responsible for the work activity, including transportation activities and project to operation transitions.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Reporting and Notification
clauses.text: The Business Unit EHSS function shall notify Corporate EHSS of Class 1, Class 2, Class 3 incidents and High Potential Incidents (HPIs). Class 1 incidents shall be immediately escalated to the highest Business Unit EHSS authority and to Corporate EHSS.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Reporting and Notification
clauses.text: EHSS incidents shall be reported to applicable government and regulatory authorities in accordance with applicable legal, regulatory and permit requirements.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Reporting and Notification
clauses.text: Facilities under SAIS supervision shall immediately notify SAIS of incidents occurring within the facility boundary through approved SAIS emergency communication channels. Where full incident information is not available at the time of notification, available information shall be reported and updated when additional information is available.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Reporting and Notification
clauses.text: Facilities under SAIS supervision shall submit incident reports and investigation reports to SAIS in accordance with applicable SAF-25 requirements.

clauses.heading: Incident Response and Evidence Preservation
clauses.text: The responsible supervisor, line manager or designated incident lead shall ensure immediate actions are taken to protect people, the environment, assets and information following an incident.

clauses.heading: Incident Response and Evidence Preservation
clauses.text: Incidents requiring emergency response or site control shall be managed in accordance with applicable emergency management arrangements.

clauses.heading: Incident Response and Evidence Preservation
clauses.text: Following stabilization of the incident, relevant evidence, records and information shall be identified, collected, preserved and protected from unauthorized alteration or removal.

clauses.heading: Incident Response and Evidence Preservation
clauses.text: Where a fatality involving an employee or contractor is confirmed, the Business Unit shall secure and preserve the incident scene, including restricting access to authorized personnel, maintaining an entry and exit log, suspending related operations as required, and immediately notifying applicable government authorities, until the scene is released by the relevant authority.

clauses.heading: Incident Response and Evidence Preservation
clauses.text: Business Units shall provide cooperation and access to government authorities when required for incident response, investigation or regulatory review.

clauses.heading: Incident Response and Evidence Preservation
clauses.text: Where a contractor employee is involved in a reportable occupational injury or illness, the responsible Business Unit shall notify the contractor organization and obtain documented confirmation that applicable legal and regulatory reporting obligations have been addressed by the contractor employer.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Classification
clauses.text: The EHSS events subject to reporting, classification and management under this process shall include incidents, near misses, Life Saving Rule (LSR) violations and EHSS observations (unsafe acts and unsafe conditions).

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Classification
clauses.text:
EHSS incidents shall be classified and categorized in accordance with Table 6.1-1:
[Table table-207-1.png]

[Table table-208-1.png]

Table 6.1-1. EHSS Incident Classification Categories.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Classification
clauses.text:
Occupational injuries and illnesses shall be further classified using Table 6.1-2:
[Table table-208-2.png]

Table 6.1-2. Occupational Injury and Illness Classification.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Classification
clauses.text: EHSS incidents shall be classified based on the initiating event that resulted in the incident, rather than solely on the resulting consequence(s).

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Classification
clauses.text: EHSS incidents shall be assigned a severity classification based on the most severe consequence resulting from the incident and classified as Class 1, Class 2, Class 3 or Class 4 in accordance with the Maaden EHSS Incident Severity Classification Matrix.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Classification
clauses.text:
Process Safety Events shall be classified as Tier 1, Tier 2 or Tier 3. Tier 1 and Tier 2 Process Safety Events shall be classified in accordance with API Recommended Practice 754, Process Safety Performance Indicators for the Refining and Petrochemical Industries. A Process Safety Event that does not meet Tier 1 or Tier 2 criteria shall be classified as a Tier 3 Process Safety Event where one or more of the criteria in Table 6.1-3 apply.
[Table table-208-3.png]

Table 6.1-3. Process Safety Event Tier 3 Classification Criteria.
Note: LOPCs not meeting Tier 1, Tier 2 or Tier 3 criteria shall be classified as Process Safety Near Miss.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Classification
clauses.text: Occupational injury and illness recordability, work-relatedness and classification shall be determined in accordance with OSHA 29 CFR 1904 recordkeeping requirements, considering applicable medical and work activities assessments.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Classification
clauses.text: Business Units shall maintain records supporting injury and illness classification decisions, including medical assessments, work-relatedness determinations and recordability evaluations.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Classification
clauses.text: For Fire, Explosion and Property Damage incidents occurring within Maaden facilities, direct damage costs shall be considered when determining incident severity, regardless of liability or ownership of the damaged asset. The only exception shall be incidents involving personal vehicles (vehicle damage) in parking areas.

clauses.heading: EHSS Event Classification
clauses.text: Near misses shall be classified as Safety, Health, Environment, Security or Process Safety events based on the most credible potential consequence that could reasonably have occurred.

clauses.heading: Reclassification of Incidents
clauses.text: Incident classifications shall be reviewed and revised when new information, medical confirmation or investigation findings justify a change in classification or severity.

clauses.heading: Reclassification of Incidents
clauses.text: Reclassification of occupational injuries and illnesses from a higher classification to a lower classification shall be supported by a medical assessment and approved by the designated corporate doctor.

clauses.heading: Reclassification of Incidents
clauses.text: All other incident reclassifications shall be reviewed and approved by the designated appointing authority.

clauses.heading: Reclassification of Incidents
clauses.text: Approved incident reclassifications shall be documented, supported by appropriate evidence, and updated in the Maaden incident reporting system (HEMAYA), with corresponding updates reflected in applicable EHSS performance records and statistics.

clauses.heading: High Potential Incidents (HPIs)
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish and maintain a process to assess the credible worst-case consequences of EHSS incidents and near misses to identify High Potential Incidents (HPIs).

clauses.heading: High Potential Incidents (HPIs)
clauses.text:
As a minimum, the scenarios listed in Table 6.1-4 shall be considered during HPI assessment.
[Table table-209-1.png]

Table 6.1-4. High Potential Incident Assessment Scenarios.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: EHSS incidents and near misses shall be investigated. The level of investigation shall be commensurate with the classification, complexity and credible potential consequences of the event.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: The Business Unit, site, department or project responsible for the affected operation or activity shall be responsible for investigating the incident.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: Incident investigations shall be initiated as soon as practicable and no later than 48 hours after the incident has been stabilized or the emergency has been declared over.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: Investigation requirements shall be determined based on the highest credible potential consequence of the incident. Class 1, Class 2 and Class 3 incidents, and High Potential Incidents (HPIs), shall be investigated by a formally appointed investigation team.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: The appointing authority shall appoint the investigation team and define the investigation scope, objectives, deliverables and completion requirements.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text:
The appointing authority and investigation team leader shall be, as a minimum, the levels specified in Table 6.1-5.
[Table table-210-1.png]

Table 6.1-5. Team Investigation Leadership Levels.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: Where an incident is reclassified during the investigation, the appointing authority responsible for the revised classification shall review the investigation team composition and make any changes necessary to ensure alignment with the incident classification and investigation requirements.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: Investigation team leaders shall be competent in incident investigation and causal analysis methodologies in accordance with section 2.7 EHSS Competency, Awareness and Communication requirements, and shall not have a conflict of interest that could compromise the independence, objectivity, or credibility of the investigation findings.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: Investigation teams shall include personnel with knowledge relevant to the incident, including management or supervision, employees, subject matter experts and, where applicable, contractor representatives. Corporate EHSS representation shall be included in the investigation team for all Class 1 incidents.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: Class 1, Class 2, Class 3 incidents and High Potential Incidents (HPIs) shall be investigated using Fault Tree Analysis. Class 4 incidents investigated by an individual shall use the 5 Whys methodology.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: For incidents requiring a team investigation, the Investigation Team Leader shall issue a preliminary investigation report to the appointing authority within 48 hours of the investigation team being formed. The preliminary report shall summarize the incident, investigation status, information collected and immediate actions required to control risk prior to resumption of normal operations.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: Investigations shall identify causes, contributing factors, control failures and actions necessary to prevent recurrence, taking account of relevant previous incidents and lessons learned.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text:
Investigation findings shall be documented in a written investigation report, reviewed and approved by the designated appointing authority, and shall include, as a minimum:
a. Executive Summary.
b. Description of the incident.
c. Observations and Evidence (Brief Analysis).
d. Direct Causes, Root Causes, Contributing Factors and Latent Failures.
e. Conclusions.
f. Required corrective and preventative actions to address the findings, conclusions and recommendations.
g. Lessons Learned.
h. Report Appendices

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: Investigation reports shall be completed within 30 calendar days of the incident date for incidents requiring a team investigation, unless an extension is approved by the appointing authority, and within 10 working days of the incident date for incidents not requiring a team investigation.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: Investigation reports for incidents subject to regulatory reporting shall satisfy applicable regulatory reporting requirements.

clauses.heading: Incident Investigation
clauses.text: Investigation reports shall be managed in accordance with applicable privacy, confidentiality, and legal requirements, including the protection of personal and medical information and the review and approval of any external release.

clauses.heading: Investigation Actions and Follow-Up
clauses.text: Business Units shall assign, track, implement and verify the implementation and effectiveness of corrective and preventive actions arising from incident investigations, and shall close such actions only where documented evidence demonstrates that the actions have been implemented, the identified causes and control deficiencies have been addressed, and action effectiveness has been verified.

clauses.heading: Investigation Actions and Follow-Up
clauses.text: Each corrective and preventive action shall be assigned to a single accountable owner and target completion date by the appointing authority.

clauses.heading: Investigation Actions and Follow-Up
clauses.text: Changes to the recommendation, accountable owner, target completion date or cancellation of the recommendation shall be justified, documented and approved by the appointing authority before implementation of the change.

clauses.heading: Investigation Actions and Follow-Up
clauses.text: Management shall review the status of corrective and preventive actions arising from incidents at least quarterly to verify timely and effective closure.

clauses.heading: EHSS Alerts and Lessons Learned
clauses.text: Corporate EHSS shall establish and maintain arrangements to communicate significant external and internal lessons learned from EHSS incidents and High Potential Incidents (HPIs) across Maaden.

clauses.heading: EHSS Alerts and Lessons Learned
clauses.text: Lessons learned shall be developed for Class 1, Class 2 and Class 3 incidents and High Potential Incidents (HPIs), and shall identify key findings, causes, failed or missing controls, and actions necessary to prevent recurrence.

clauses.heading: EHSS Alerts and Lessons Learned
clauses.text: Business Units shall establish and maintain an incident learning process to identify, evaluate, communicate and apply lessons learned from internal and external incidents, near misses and High Potential Incidents (HPIs), including the communication of applicable EHSS Alerts and lessons learned to affected personnel and relevant stakeholders.

clauses.heading: EHSS Alerts and Lessons Learned
clauses.text: Lessons learned shall be considered in the review and improvement of procedures, training, risk assessments, operational controls and emergency preparedness arrangements.

clauses.heading: EHSS Alerts and Lessons Learned
clauses.text: Facilities under SAIS supervision shall submit lessons learned from incidents, near misses and High Potential Incidents (HPIs) to SAIS in accordance with applicable SAF-25 requirements.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Data and Recordkeeping
clauses.text: EHSS incident records, including occupational injury and illness records for employees , contractors and visitors, shall be maintained.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Data and Recordkeeping
clauses.text: Business Units shall maintain records of worked man-hours for employees and contractors for EHSS performance measurement, incident statistics and reporting purposes.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Data and Recordkeeping
clauses.text:
Actual worked man-hours obtained from electronic timekeeping systems shall be used as the preferred basis for EHSS performance reporting. Where electronic timekeeping systems are not available, worked man-hours shall be calculated in accordance with Table 6.1-6.
[Table table-212-1.png]

Table 6.1-6. Worked man-hours calculation methods.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Data and Recordkeeping
clauses.text: Occupational injuries, illnesses and worked man-hours for contractor personnel performing work activities on Maaden premises shall be recorded and included in Maaden contractor injury and illness statistics and incidence rate calculations, including project personnel, transportation personnel, drivers and personnel involved in loading and unloading activities.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Data and Recordkeeping
clauses.text: Occupational injuries and illnesses involving students participating in internship programs on Maaden premises shall be recorded and included in contractor injury and illness statistics and incidence rate calculations.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Data and Recordkeeping
clauses.text:
Visitor incidents shall be recorded and maintained as a separate category from employee and contractor incidents. Injuries, worked man-hours and incidence rates for the following categories of personnel shall not be included in Maaden EHSS performance statistics:
a. Mail and courier personnel.
b. Office equipment service personnel.
c. Incidental delivery service personnel (e.g., convenience store deliveries, vending machine deliveries, Incoming material deliveries).
d. Casual visitors (e.g., Customers, Regulatory Authorities, Raw material/Utilities companies’ officials, port official, suppliers, Government /public officials, tours).
e. Government Security staff assigned at the BUs.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Data and Recordkeeping
clauses.text: Where work is performed under a Permit to Work system, the issuing Maaden entity shall be responsible for recording and reporting the incident.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Data and Recordkeeping
clauses.text: Expansion projects and construction activities shall maintain EHSS performance statistics separate from operational statistics where required by approved Maaden reporting arrangements.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Statistics and Reporting
clauses.text: Business Units and Corporate Functions shall designate responsible people for maintaining worked man-hours, EHSS incident statistics, performance data, and performance reporting records for employees and contractors.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Statistics and Reporting
clauses.text: EHSS incident statistics shall be maintained and reported on a monthly and annual basis.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Statistics and Reporting
clauses.text: EHSS performance reporting shall include the applicable incident performance indicators required by SAF-25.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Statistics and Reporting
clauses.text: Corporate EHSS shall consolidate EHSS performance information and periodically report EHSS performance to Senior Management.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Statistics and Reporting
clauses.text: Business Units shall periodically analyze EHSS incidents, trends and performance data to identify recurring causes, emerging risks, opportunities for improvement and actions necessary to reduce risk and improve performance.

clauses.heading: EHSS Incident Statistics and Reporting
clauses.text: Corporate EHSS shall periodically review Business Unit EHSS incident and performance analyses to identify Maaden- wide trends, systemic issues and opportunities for continual improvement.
